Any other outcome (another Slack error, a network, HTTP or rate-limited error, a success, a synchronous throw) is ignored. After the latch every Web API method called through the wrapper is refused locally: the original is not called, and the call rejects with `WebApiCallRefusedLocallyError` (code `persona_web_api_refused_locally`, `data.error` the latched Slack error, so a caller's handling reads it as Slack's answer). The client's other methods still run; `paginate` is neither observed nor refused (unused in `src/`). The latch belongs to one wrapper: a new client starts unlatched. Pure: nothing at import, and a watch holds only its wrappers and its latch.
    ├── persona-notifier.ts     b.av2 SR-7.1 / SR-7.2 per-persona server notices. `createPersonaNotifier({ getPersona, clientFor, destinations?, destinationHold?, isDryRun, log, recordStartupError? })` returns `notify(key, text, options?)`, `flush(key)`, `forget(key)` and the persona teardown's window entries `submitTeardown(key)`, `settleTeardown(key)`, `openTeardownWindow(persona)`, `closeTeardownWindow(key)` and `teardownWindowState(key)` (b.jg5 SRJ-1003); none throws or rejects. A notice goes only to the persona's destination (its `permission_prompts` channel, or its DM with `dm.contact`), posted through the persona's own Web client from `clientFor(key)` as one top-level message with only channel and text, so it appears under the persona's identity. The post is handed to the destination hold (`destinationHold`, `persona-destination-hold.ts`; when none is injected the notifier builds its own over `destinations`, or over a resolver of its own), which posts through the destination resolver (`persona-destination.ts`); the resolver opens the DM for a `dm` destination. The notifier prefixes every body with `Persona "<name>" (key=<key>): `, so callers pass the key and the body only. Routing, in order (first match wins): while the key's teardown window is open (`openTeardownWindow(persona)` at the start of the persona teardown's serializer turn, given the persona's name and key so a key no longer applied is still named, until `closeTeardownWindow(key)` when it completes; counted, so a nested open needs its own close), every notice for it is one startup-errors entry through `recordStartupError` and one log line, never a Slack call, never queued, held or dropped (b.jg5 SRJ-1003, SRJ-1013), its text with Slack's control-character escapes undone (`unescapeSlackControlCharacters`, so `&amp;`, `&lt;` and `&gt;` in a notice built for Slack are written as `&`, `<` and `>`): the entry is `personaTeardownNoticeEntryText(ref, text, occasion?)`, `<ref>, <occasion>: <text>` with `<ref>` `persona "<name>" (key=<key>)` and the occasion `PERSONA_TEARDOWN_NOTICE_RAISED` (`raised during its teardown`), of class `PERSONA_TEARDOWN_NOTICE_LABEL` (`persona-teardown-notice`, defined in `kill-failure-alert.ts` and re-exported here, the one constant) or the options' `teardownEntryClass` (`persona-kill-survivor`, the kill-failure alert's survivor version), and the line is `[slack] persona-notifier: notice for <ref> raised during its teardown — written to the server log and startup-errors.log (<class>), not posted: <first line>`; an outage notice's options (`PersonaNoticeOptions.outage`: `phase` `PERSONA_NOTICE_OUTAGE_ONSET` or `PERSONA_NOTICE_OUTAGE_ALL_CLEAR` and its `classes`) let an onset the window writes mark its classes for the key, so the all-clear listing a marked class takes the same route whenever it comes, after the window has closed included, with the occasion `PERSONA_TEARDOWN_NOTICE_ALL_CLEAR_AFTER` (`the all-clear of an outage raised during its teardown`) and the line `[slack] persona-notifier: all-clear for <ref> of an outage raised during its teardown — written to the server log and startup-errors.log (persona-teardown-notice), not posted: <first line>`, while an onset of a marked class raised outside any window starts a new outage and drops that class's mark; an all-clear listing a marked class and an unmarked one is split when its options carry `allClearOf` (the outage state's renderer of the all-clear of a subset of its classes, over the same bad-stretch snapshot): the marked classes' all-clear is written that way, and the rest's all-clear, listing only the unmarked classes, routes on as any notice (with no `allClearOf`, or one that throws, the whole all-clear is written); next, from a teardown's submit until its window opens, the onset of an outage class in `PERSONA_NOTICE_SUBMIT_MUTED_OUTAGE_CLASSES` (`ad-config-malformed`, a notice-episode kind of its own, b.jg5 SRJ-1016) for an applied key is muted, one line `[slack] persona-notifier: onset for <ref> of <classes> not posted — muted, its persona teardown was submitted; its all-clear is written, never posted: <first line>`, no post and no entry, and its classes are marked, so that outage's all-clear is written as above; a missing or throwing recorder changes the line's tail to `not posted, and its startup-errors entry was not written: <reason>` and still posts nothing; then an unknown key logs one line and drops the notice; dry run logs the persona reference and the notice's first line, with no Slack call; a persona with no serving client (`clientFor` returns undefined: not up yet, not brought up, or broken), whether its destination is a channel or `dm`, is held in that persona's own queue in raised order (the pre-validation hold); otherwise it is handed to the destination hold with `deliver`. For a `dm` destination the DM is opened (or taken from the resolver's cache) only when the notice is attempted, so a notice in the pre-validation queue opens it when flushed after the client is validated, never before. A queue holds at most `MAX_HELD_NOTICES_PER_PERSONA` (20) notices (defined in `persona-destination-hold.ts` and re-exported here), because a broken or retrying persona can go without a client for a long time: past the bound each new notice drops the oldest held one, which is logged (`[slack] persona-notifier: more than 20 notices held for <ref> — oldest held notice dropped, not posted: <first line>`) and never posted. `flush(key)` posts that persona's held notices in raised order once its client is validated and never touches another persona's queue, and posts nothing while its teardown window is open; a notice raised for a validated persona that still has held notices posts after them. A notice whose open or post fails at the destination is kept by the destination hold and retried with the persona's prompts, under one `persona-destination-failed` line per episode; the notifier logs nothing for it (see Permission Relay, [Destination hold](#destination-hold-bav2-sr-71-failures)). A notice whose post fails for the message itself (`MESSAGE_PAYLOAD_ERRORS`, such as `invalid_blocks` or `msg_too_long`) is dropped with one token-safe line, `[slack] persona-notifier: failed to post notice for <ref> to <channel>[ (reason=<reason>)]: <describeThrownValue>`. Either way the notice's `onPostFailure` callback is called once, at its first failed attempt, with the resolver's `DestinationFailure` (the step, the error code and the thrown value when there is one); later retries of the same notice don't call it again. A `dm` destination the resolver refuses (DMs off or no contact) is logged by the resolver and not posted, and `onPostFailure` is not called. Also exports `formatPersonaNotice` (also used by the permission poller for its stuck-prompt warning, which needs the post's outcome and so does not go through `notify`, except inside the persona's teardown window, where the poller hands it to `notify`), `firstNoticeLine` and `notifySafely` (calls an injected notify sink so that a throw or rejection goes to an error callback). Pure (b.av2 SR-13.1): no module-scope state, no I/O of its own, nothing at import; each instance holds its own queues. `server.ts` builds one instance over `clientFor`, the shared destination resolver and the shared destination hold and installs it in outage state, the session manager, the JSONL safeguard and the persona routing (the lost-message notice, `persona-routing.ts`). The connection manager's status listener (`createPersonaUpFlushListener`) calls `flush(key)` each time a persona reports up, after its bring-up or a reopen, so a persona's held notices post once its own client is validated. `forget(key)` (a persona teardown) drops that persona's pre-validation queue unposted, so a persona added later with the same key never posts them; it leaves the destination hold alone and logs one line when notices were dropped, `[slack] persona-notifier: persona=<key>: dropped <n> held notice(s), not posted — the persona was torn down`. Only notices queued before the window opened are in that queue, so `forget` drops none raised in the window. `submitTeardown(key)` and `settleTeardown(key)` (counted) bracket a teardown from its submit to its completion: `teardownWindowState(key)` (`PersonaTeardownWindowState`) answers `open` while a window is open, `submitted` from the submit until the window opens, and `none` otherwise; the notifier's own routing reads only the open window, and the notice episodes read the state (`persona-episodes.ts`). `server.ts` passes the one instance to the persona lifecycle, the notice episodes' teardown query and the permission poller's `teardownNotices`.
    ├── persona-destination.ts  b.av2 SR-7.1 / SR-5.1 where a persona's permission prompts and server notices go, and the post there. A persona's destination is read from `permission_prompts`: a channel with its ID, or `dm`. `createPersonaDestinations({ log })` returns `{ post(persona, client, message), forget(personaKey) }`; `post` never rejects and returns `posted` (with the conversation and `ts`), `refused` or `failed`. A channel destination is the configured channel. A `dm` destination is the persona's DM conversation with `dm.contact`, obtained with `conversations.open` (`users` = the contact) on the persona's own client: Slack returns the existing conversation, or opens one when none exists, so a DM-only persona's first post needs no earlier DM. Posts name the returned `D…` conversation ID, never the contact's user ID, and carry only channel, text and optional blocks (no username or icon override), so they appear under the persona's identity. The resolved DM is cached per persona key, tied to the contact it was opened for: the same persona and contact reuse it with no second open; concurrent posts share the one in-flight open; a different contact opens afresh; a failed open, or one that returns no conversation ID, is not cached; a post to the cached conversation failing with `channel_not_found` drops, as soon as the post fails, the entry that post used and never a newer one opened meanwhile; `forget(personaKey)` clears the persona's entry; a persona teardown calls it, and so do an in-place update that changed `permission_prompts`, `dm.enabled` or `dm.contact`, a confirmed credentials change once the new connection is in use, and a recovery bring-up of a credentials-broken persona (the new credentials may belong to another app, with another DM conversation). The cache holds one entry per persona, so one persona's failed open never affects another's destination (b.av2 SR-3.3). Defensive refusal: a `dm` destination with `dm.enabled` not true or no `dm.contact` (the loader already rejects both) makes no Slack call, logs `[slack] persona-destination: <ref> has permission_prompts set to "dm" but <dm.enabled is not true|dm.contact is not set> — no DM opened and nothing posted` and returns `refused`; it does not go through the MCP tool-scope check (`checkPersonaTarget`). A failed open or post is returned as `failed` (a `DestinationFailure`) with the step (`conversations.open` or `chat.postMessage`), the error class (`classifySlackError`; `no_conversation_id` for an open with no ID) the thrown value when there is one (for a token-safe description only) and, for a post, the conversation; `describeDestinationFailure` renders its token-safe log tail. Also exports `dmDestinationRefusal` and `describeDmDestinationRefusal` (the poller checks the refusal first, to log it per request), `describeDestinationFailureCause` (the token-safe cause the session manager's `spawn-failure-post` record carries), `classifySlackError` (the trail's `error` class, used by the poller and the click handler), `safeFailureCode` (a failure's code when it is a short identifier, else `unknown_error`: the form a log line or trail `error` field carries), `DM_OPEN_SCOPE` (`im:write`) and `MISSING_SCOPE_ERROR` (used by `registry.ts` and the destination hold). The resolver never retries: a failed open or post is returned once, and holding and retrying it is the destination hold's job (next entry). Pure (b.av2 SR-13.1): no module-scope state, no timers, nothing at import; each instance holds its own cache.
    ├── persona-destination-hold.ts  b.av2 SR-7.1 (failure part) / SR-3.2 / SR-3.3 / SR-10.3 hold and retry of a persona's permission prompts and server notices while its destination fails. `createPersonaDestinationHold({ destinations, getPersona, clientFor, clock?, log })` returns `begin(key)`, `deliver(persona, client, notice)`, `cancel(key)`, `cancelAll()` and `view(key)`. It owns each persona's failure episode, retry schedule, FIFO of held notices, timer and in-flight guard, and the `persona-destination-failed` lines. See Permission Relay, [Destination hold](#destination-hold-bav2-sr-71-failures).
    ├── persona-event-router.ts  b.av2 SR-3.1 / SR-4.1 / SR-7.1 / SR-13.1 the handler every persona connection forwards its events to. `createPersonaEventRouter({ routing, clientFor, getPersona, log, handleClick?, emitTrail? })` returns the connection manager's `onEvent` handler, called with the receiving persona's key, the event name and the library's listener argument. `message` and `app_mention`: one RAW line, `[slack] RAW <event> event persona=<key>: <first 300 chars of the event JSON>`, then the event and its `ack` go to persona-routing's `receive` with the receiving persona as the only receiver. `interactive`: the payload's channel, message `ts` and clicking user are read once; for each action `cscb.block_action.received` is emitted and `handlePermissionClick` runs with `receivingPersonaKey` set to the receiving persona's key, stopping at the first handled action. A throw while handling one action is logged as `[slack] persona=<key>: interactive action <i> of <n> handling failed: <describeThrownValue>` and the remaining actions still run. The payload is acked exactly once, after handling, on every path: when an action is handled, when none is, and when an action throws. Any other event name is logged, acked and ignored. A throw while handling one event is logged as `[slack] persona=<key>: <event> event handling failed: <describeThrownValue>` and never reaches the manager. No other persona's key, connection or client is consulted. Nothing runs at import.
    ├── persona-start.ts        b.av2 SR-6.1 / SR-3.1 / SR-3.4 / SR-7.2 / SR-13.1 the per-persona start procedure and the connection seams the server reads. The procedure's steps, in order: (1) the local credentials check and (2) the working-directory check, both evaluated before either stops the bring-up so both causes are reported (`checkPersonaLocalBringUp`; in dry run only `checkPersonaWorkingDirectory` runs and no credentials file is read); (3) Slack validation and connection through the connection manager's `bringUp(persona, tokens)` (no tokens in dry run); (4) the launch, only when step 3 reports the persona `up`. This module exports steps 1–3 as separate functions and runs none of them itself: `checkPersonaLocalSteps` (steps 1–2, returning each failure, the tokens read and the credentials digest (`credentialsDigest`, whatever step 1's outcome, a real-path collision included; none in dry run), logging only when given a logger), `connectPersonaSlack` (step 3, handing the persona and the tokens it is given to the manager) and `personaSlackStatusFailure` (the step-3 failure for a status other than `up`). A failure's step (`PersonaBringUpStep`) is `credentials`, `working-directory`, `slack` or `claude-config-dir`, the last for a persona held because its `claude_config_dir` cannot be resolved (bug b.g57), before its Slack step or at a later launch. The bring-up controller (`persona-bringup-controller.ts`) runs the server's start through them and keeps each persona's outcome; the start pass launches a persona that is `up` at start, and the controller launches one that reaches `up` through a retry. Steps 1–2 log through E2's checks and step 3 through the manager; a throw from `bringUp` is the only line `connectPersonaSlack` adds (`[slack] persona <ref> not brought up: Slack bring-up threw: <describeThrownValue>`), and it resolves a `slack` failure of class `error`. Nothing here posts to Slack, records a startup error or counts a failed spawn. Seams, built over the manager and the applied-config getter: `isPersonaClientServing(status)` (true for `up`, `lost` and `retrying` in its `reopen` phase; false while connecting, retrying its bring-up, broken, stopped or unmanaged), `createPersonaClientLookup` (`clientFor`: the manager's long-lived Web client for a serving applied persona, else nothing, and always nothing in dry run), `createPersonaIdentityLookup` (the serving persona's bot identity; the placeholder identity in dry run) `createPersonaUpFlushListener(notifier)` (a status listener: flush exactly that persona's held notices on every transition to `up`), `composePersonaStatusListeners(...listeners)` (several status listeners as the manager's one; each is called even when an earlier one throws), `createPersonaUpPredicate(connections, outcomes)` (`isPersonaUp(key)`, b.av2 SR-6.4: true only while `isPersonaClientServing` holds for the persona's status and its bring-up outcome is `up`; false for a persona the manager or the controller does not know; logs nothing; the one "is this persona up" check behind MCP session admission (Session Lifecycle, Connection), the permission poller's skip (Permission Relay, Per-tick flow) and `/interject`'s 503) and `createPersonaRelaunchGate(connections, log, outcomes?)` (`canRelaunch(key)`: decides through the same private check as `createPersonaUpPredicate` (`isPersonaUpGiven`), over one status read it also uses to word its log line, so the gate and the predicate can't drift: true only while `isPersonaClientServing` holds for the persona's status and, when `outcomes` is given, its bring-up outcome is `up`; false for a persona the manager does not know, such as one that failed its credentials or working-directory check; every brought-up persona is `up` in dry run). The server passes the bring-up controller as `outcomes` and hands the gate to restart (`RestartDeps.canRestart`), the restart launch and the health check's work list; see Auto-Restart. When it answers false it logs one of two lines, once per persona per reason: a repeat for the same reason is silent, and being eligible again re-arms it. While the connection is not serving: `[slack] persona=<key>: not relaunched — its Slack connection is <state>; eligible again once it is up`, with `<state>` one of `not brought up` (the manager does not know the persona), `connecting`, `retrying its bring-up`, `retrying`, `broken` or `stopped`. While the connection is serving but the bring-up outcome is not `up`: `[slack] persona=<key>: not relaunched — its bring-up has not succeeded; eligible again once it is up`. A key outside the applied set (`PersonaUpQuery.isApplied`, production: the bring-up controller's `isApplied`; b.av2 SR-8.6) is refused first, whatever its status: `[slack] persona=<key>: not relaunched — it is no longer in the applied configuration`; the up predicate answers false for it too. Each line carries only the key and the reason. Tokens exist only in memory: for the call, in the manager, and in the bring-up controller's entry for the persona (kept from the first read for later directory retries; see the next entry). Nothing runs at import.
    ├── persona-bringup-controller.ts  b.av2 SR-6.1 (outcomes) / SR-6.4 / SR-7.2 (part) / SR-10.3 (part) / SR-13.1 per-persona bring-up outcomes and retries. `createPersonaBringUpController({ connections, launch, dryRun, log, clock?, ... })` (`connections` is the connection manager's `bringUp`, `status` and `stop`, all required; `stop` closes a persona's connection when a `claude_config_dir` hold starts for it) returns `bringUp(persona, applied)`, `onConnectionStatus(key, status)` (the manager's status listener), `isUp(key)`, `isApplied(key)` (whether the key is in the applied set now, from the optional injected `appliedPersonas()` getter, which production binds to `personaConfig`'s personas; true for every key without it; see the applied-set guard under Server-Managed Startup step 5), `state(key)` (outcome and causes, never a token), `credentialsDigest(key)`, `changeCredentials(persona, applied, connections, hooks?)`, `holdForConfigDir(persona, failure)`, `cancel(key)` and `cancelAll()`. `credentialsDigest(key)` (b.av2 SR-8.3) is the read-only query behind the reload detection tick's credentials comparison: the digest or marker of the bytes the persona's bring-up read, or of its last confirmed credentials change, which is what it connected with, is retrying with or broke with. No retry re-reads the file, so it changes only at a confirmed credentials change. `changeCredentials` is apply step 4's per-persona body (see [Credentials change](#credentials-change-bav2-sr-86-step-4)). Beside the held content, each entry keeps the content its own connection uses (`live`: tokens and digest), set at bring-up, at every swap of a credentials reconnect (at once or later) and when a retrying persona takes a change; a refused change holds `live` again, so the change is pending. `isCredentialsBroken(state)`, exported here, is the SR-6.4 rule it, the change plan and the apply steps share. A persona broken by a credentials file another applied persona shares holds the digest of its own path's bytes (read only to be hashed, never parsed). It is undefined in dry run (no file is read) and for an unknown or cancelled persona. It is never logged. `bringUp` logs the persona's `persona-start` line, runs steps 1–2 (`checkPersonaLocalSteps`), then step 3 (`connectPersonaSlack`) when both pass, and resolves once the persona has an outcome: `up`, `broken` or `retrying` (see Server-Managed Startup step 5 for the cause mapping). It launches nothing itself at start. Causes are kept apart (credentials, directory, Slack, config dir). A directory-broken persona is re-checked on its own timer with its own `createPersonaRetrySchedule` (5 s doubling to 300 s, no cap), never through `backoff.ts`; a re-check is scheduled only once the previous one has finished. The tokens read at the persona's bring-up (or at its last confirmed credentials change) are held in its entry and handed to the manager when a directory retry reaches Slack; no retry re-reads the credentials file. A persona that reaches `up` through a retry is launched once through the injected `launch` (the server's `spawnForPersona`): when a directory retry's Slack step leaves the persona's outcome `up` (the manager's status is `up`, `lost` or `retrying` in the `reopen` phase), or when `onConnectionStatus` sees `up` right after `retrying` in the `bring-up` phase. An `up` after `lost` or a reopen launches nothing. The `claude_config_dir` hold (bug b.g57): the injected `checkConfigDir` (production: `checkLaunchConfigDir`) runs once steps 1 and 2 pass, right before step 3, at bring-up and when a directory retry reaches Slack; an unresolvable directory opens the hold there, so the persona never connects. `holdForConfigDir` (the session manager's hook, installed with `setConfigDirUnresolvableHook`) opens it for a persona whose later launch found the directory unresolvable, and closes its Slack connection (the manager's `stop` with the end reason `the persona's Slack connection was closed while its claude_config_dir cannot be resolved`, so an open lost, unreachable or refused episode ends with one cleared line; a failure logs `closing its Slack connection for its claude_config_dir failed: <error>`), so the persona leaves up (below) and its MCP session is dropped. Either way its outcome is `retrying` with a `configDir` cause and no connection, its instance and row are kept, and its notices are held by the notifier. The failure line is logged once when the episode starts, and the directory is re-checked on the persona's own timer and `createPersonaRetrySchedule`, outside the restart counter and cap, each attempt through the serializer. Once it resolves: one cleared line (`…; continuing the bring-up`), Slack validation and connection with the held credentials, then the launch (`up after its claude_config_dir resolved — launching`), which resumes the row through the collision ladder; Slack-unreachable then retries and launches on `up`. A persona Slack had refused when the hold started keeps that refusal as its cause and stays `broken` after the cleared line. A confirmed credentials change while held takes the new content (held and live) and opens no connection; the persona connects with it on its return. It returns false for a persona the controller does not know or has cancelled, and the caller then logs the line itself. An `up` right after `broken` (a pending credentials reconnect swapped in for a connection Slack had refused meanwhile) launches the persona the same way, logging `up after its confirmed credentials change — launching`. Each retry attempt, through to the launch it triggers, runs through the optional injected `serialize` (the server's lifecycle serializer, b.av2 SR-6.6): a directory re-check with its Slack step and launch, and the launch after a Slack retry reached `up`. Their checks (cancelled, no longer applied, already launched) run when the attempt starts, and the launch is awaited inside the attempt. `launchAfterRetry` also waits for up: it launches nothing unless the persona's outcome is `up` when its turn comes, so a Slack launch queued behind an operation that held the persona for its `claude_config_dir` (closing its connection) does nothing, even if the directory resolved by then; the hold's recovery launches it after the reconnect. The controller never submits `bringUp` itself; the apply bring-up does. `cancel(key)` (a persona teardown, or shutdown's `cancelAll()`) forgets the persona's entry and clears its timer, so retry work still queued for it does nothing. Each persona's state, timer and in-flight flag live in its own entry; nothing spans two personas. Lines go through the injected logger only (never `startup-errors.log`), and nothing here posts to Slack. Dry run reads no credentials file and makes no Slack call, but the directory check and its retry run as in a real start. Leaving up (b.av2 SR-6.3, SR-6.4): each time a persona's outcome changes from `up` to `broken` or `retrying` (a refused reopen of a running persona, or a Web API call refused for its bot token, bug b.ujn, both of which make it `broken`; or a `claude_config_dir` hold, which makes it `retrying` and closes its connection), the optional injected `onLeftUp(persona, state)` is told once; a persona that was never up is not reported, and a lost connection being reopened (`lost`, `retrying` in the `reopen` phase) stays `up` and is not reported. A throw or rejection from the listener is logged as `[slack] persona "<name>" (key=<key>): handling its change from up to <outcome> failed: <error>`. The module also exports `describePersonaNotUp(state)`, the token-free reason a persona is not up used by the refusal and drop lines (`<outcome>: <first cause>`, credentials before directory before Slack before config dir; `its bring-up has not run` with no state; `its Slack connection is not serving` when the outcome is `up` but the connection is not), and `createNotUpSessionDropper({ drop, log })`, the `onLeftUp` listener the server installs (Session Lifecycle, Disconnection). Clock, logger, checks, file-system seam, manager, launch, serializer and leaving-up listener are injected; nothing is created, read or scheduled at import or at construction.
    ├── persona-serializer.ts   b.av2 SR-6.6 / SR-13.1 per-persona lifecycle serialization. `createPersonaSerializer()` returns a `PersonaSerializer`: `run(key, operation)` (`PersonaSerialize`) starts the operation only once every operation already submitted for that key has settled, and resolves or rejects with the operation's own result; `whenIdle(key)` resolves (never rejects) once everything submitted for the key before the call has settled. Per key it holds one promise chain and nothing spans two keys, so one persona's operation never waits on another's. A rejected operation doesn't stop the next one for its key; its rejection goes to its submitter. Re-entrancy rule: an operation running for a key must never await `run` or `whenIdle` for the same key. What goes through it: Session Lifecycle, [Per-persona serialization](#per-persona-serialization-bav2-sr-66). No dependencies. Importable without side effects: importing it or calling the factory creates no timer, and an instance holds nothing until the first `run`. `server.ts` builds the one production instance at module scope.
    ├── persona-lifecycle.ts    b.av2 SR-6.1 / SR-6.2 / SR-6.5 / SR-6.6 / SR-8.6 / SR-13.1; b.jg5 SRJ-715 / SRJ-1507 the per-persona operations a confirmed apply runs. `createPersonaLifecycle(deps)` returns a `PersonaLifecycle`: `teardown(persona)`, the persona teardown of apply step 2 (b.av2 SR-6.5 as amended by b.jg5 SRJ-1507: it stops the approver, the live-row sequence and the retry timer first, kills the row with the bounded retry and keeps it, with no delete), which never rejects; `bringUp(persona, applied, options?)`, the bring-up at apply of step 6, which resolves with the bring-up outcome once an `up` persona's launch has settled, and with `{ recovery: true }` is the recovery bring-up of a credentials-broken persona whose credentials file changed; `reconnectCredentials(persona, applied)`, the credentials change of step 4, which resolves with the controller's `PersonaCredentialsChangeResult` once an up persona's first reconnect attempt has settled; `updateInPlace(change)`, the in-place update of step 3 (an `InPlaceApplyInput`), which never rejects; and `refreshTemplate(applied)`, the template refresh of step 5 (`refreshSlackChannelBotTemplate`, `agent-director-template.ts`), which never rejects and, belonging to no persona, is not serialized. The four per-persona operations are submitted through the injected serializer and never submit to it again from inside; none touches another persona. Every `teardown` cancels the persona's launch wait for a `working` row as soon as it is submitted (`cancelLaunchWait`, b.f2b). `teardown` also serves the old half of a destructive modify (its key still applied): it then also cancels the persona's bring-up retries and restart timer, and stops its UNAVAILABLE retry timer, at submit, before its serializer turn; `bringUp` serves the new half. Every `teardown` registers its submit with the notifier (`submitTeardown`, ended once by `settleTeardown`), and its serializer turn forgets the key's outage flags and opens the notifier's teardown window (`openTeardownWindow`) before its first step, closing it (`closeTeardownWindow`) when it completes, whatever a step throws, so every notice raised for the key meanwhile is written to the server log and a startup-errors entry (b.jg5 SRJ-1003); each CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answer its kill reports is raised through the notifier's `notify` with the text `teardownKillRefusalNoticeText(instanceId, refusal)` (exported; b.jg5 SRJ-1002, SRJ-1003), and a standing non-success that no kill-failure alert, try-time refusal notice or outage onset written in the window records is raised the same way with the text `teardownKillNotSucceededNoticeText(instanceId, outcome, tries)` (b.jg5 SRJ-110; both builders live in `checked-kill.ts`). A persona with only next-launch changes gets no operation. Injected dependencies (`PersonaLifecycleDeps`, all required): `serialize`; the bring-up controller's `bringUp`, `cancel`, `state` and `changeCredentials`; the connection manager's `stop`, `reconnectCredentials` and `replaceRetryTokens`; the routing's `forget`; `forgetAcks` (`forgetPersonaAcks`, the teardown); the destination resolver's `forget` (teardown, an in-place update that moves the DM destination, a credentials change right before its new connection comes into use, and a recovery bring-up); the destination hold's `cancel`; the notifier (`forget`, and, optional in the type so hand-built fixtures stay valid, `notify`, `submitTeardown`, `settleTeardown`, `openTeardownWindow` and `closeTeardownWindow`; production passes the one notifier); `appliedPersonas()` (the teardown's Stop-hook pass, whether a teardown's key is still applied, and whether an in-place update's key is still applied); `dryRun`; `isShuttingDown` (the server's `shuttingDown` flag, read at each use); `log`; `stopApprover` (optional in the type, always passed by production as `stopDialogApprover(key, APPROVER_STOP_TEARDOWN)`, b.jg5 SRJ-404, SRJ-715: called first when a teardown is submitted and awaited as its first step); `stopLiveRowSequence` (optional in the type, always passed by production as `stopLiveRowSequence(key, LIVE_ROW_STOP_TEARDOWN)`, b.jg5 SRJ-706, SRJ-715: called right after `stopApprover` when a teardown is submitted, and awaited as its second step, labelled `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_STOP_STEP` (`stopping its live-row sequence`), before the wait for the launch in flight; and awaited again once that launch settled, labelled `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_STOP_AGAIN_STEP` (`stopping its live-row sequence again, after its launch in flight settled`), since that launch can have started a sequence at a collision ladder replacement site after the first stop); `whenLaunchSettled`, `cancelLaunchWait` (`cancelWorkingRowWait`) and `forgetNotConnectedEpisode` (both optional in the type, always passed by production; b.f2b), `forgetNoticeEpisodes` (the episodes instance's `forget`, b.jg5 SRJ-1016), `forgetConflictLatch` (the latch instance's `forget`, b.jg5 SRJ-504), `forgetInvalidFlagsHold` (the `ErrInvalidFlags` hold's `forget`, b.jg5 SRJ-207, SRJ-715), `cancelRestartTimer`, `stopRetryTimer` (the retry controller's `stop` with the torn-down reason, b.jg5 SRJ-305), `forgetFailures`, `forgetDisconnectedStreak`, `resetOutageState` (`resetAllToHealthy`, once per teardown, right before its window opens), `forgetPersonaPrompts`, `dropSession` (the server's `dropPersonaSessionAndKeepAlive`), `killInstance` (`killPersonaInstanceForTeardown` with `KILL_RETRY_SYSTEM_CLOCK`, answering a `PersonaTeardownKillResult`: the bounded retry's result and the CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answers met, b.jg5 SRJ-715) and `raiseKillFailureAlert` (the one kill-failure alerts instance's `raise`, unlatched, with the context `KILL_FAILURE_CONTEXT_PERSONA_TEARDOWN`, b.jg5 SRJ-704) and the optional `outageFlags` (production `getOutageFlags`, read once after the kill, b.jg5 SRJ-110); there is no delete dependency; `replyGuard` (`PersonaTeardownReplyGuard`: `launchedWithDir`, `teardown` and `launchPass`, with the state directory bound); `storageCheck` (`runPersonaStorageCheck` with the notifier); `launch` (`spawnForPersona` with the start-time server-wide values); and `templateRefresh` (`installed`, the params the boot install wrote, and `getClient`). See Session Lifecycle, [Bring-up at apply](#bring-up-at-apply-bav2-sr-61), [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65), [In-place update](#in-place-update-bav2-sr-86) and [Credentials change](#credentials-change-bav2-sr-86-step-4); its lines are under Logging, [Persona lifecycle lines](#persona-lifecycle-lines-bav2-sr-65-sr-61). Importable without side effects: nothing is created, read or scheduled at import or at `createPersonaLifecycle`, so tests build it without importing `server.ts`.
    ├── delivery-decision.ts    b.av2 SR-4.2 / SR-4.3 / SR-4.4 / SR-13.1 the one place inbound delivery is decided. `decideDelivery(event, persona, applied)` takes one raw `message` / `app_mention` event, the receiving persona P (key, bot user ID, bot ID, channel entries and `dmEnabled`, P's `dm.enabled`) and every applied persona's key and channel entries, and returns deliver with `via`, or drop with a reason (`non-message`, `no-author`, `own`, `dm-disabled`, `group-dm`, `channel-not-configured` with an `unclaimed` flag, `not-mentioned`). What it covers: the deliverable subtypes (none, `file_share`, `bot_message`, `thread_broadcast`, `me_message`); an author must be present (`user` or `bot_id`); self-exclusion by P's bot user ID or P's bot ID, where an author with no `user` (a webhook or integration) is identified by its bot ID; the conversation kind (a DM is `channel_type` `im`, or, as a defensive fallback for an event without `channel_type`, a conversation ID starting with `D`; a group DM is recognised only by `channel_type` `mpim`), where a DM delivers with `via` `dm` when `dmEnabled` is on and is `dm-disabled` when it is off, an `mpim` event is always `group-dm`, and neither reaches the channel rules (an `app_mention` in a group DM has no `channel_type` and a `G…`/`C…` ID, so it takes the channel rules); channel membership; `delivery: all`; and `delivery: mentions`, which delivers on P's own user mention (`<@P>` or `<@P|label>`) or on `<!here>` / `<!channel>`, with or without a label. `<!everyone>` and user-group mentions do not count. An empty or unknown bot user ID or bot ID never matches. Self-exclusion is the only filter on the author: nothing arbitrates, counts or throttles exchanges between personas. `via`, first match wins: `dm`, `mention`, `broadcast`, `receive_all_shared`, `receive_all`. `receive_all_shared` needs at least one other applied persona with `delivery: all` in that channel, whether or not that persona is up; only a DM produces `dm`. Also exports `stripPersonaMention`, which removes P's own mention token (both forms) from the text and leaves other mentions and broadcasts. Pure: imports types only, keeps no state and has no side effects on import. Its only caller is the persona pipeline in `persona-routing.ts`.
    ├── persona-routing.ts      b.av2 SR-4.1 / SR-4.2 / SR-4.3 / SR-4.4 / SR-4.6 / SR-7.3 / SR-10.3 / SR-13.1; b.jg5 SRJ-1011 / SRJ-1501 / SRJ-1509 inbound delivery per persona. `createPersonaRouting(deps)` returns `receive(event, ack, personaKeys)` (one key or a list; the event router passes the receiving persona's key alone) and `forget(key)`: intake acks the event first, then, for each receiving persona key, writes the archive through the injected archive seam and runs that persona's pipeline, each run isolated (a throw is logged naming the persona and never stops another persona's run). It owns the per-persona dedupe: one `inbound-dedupe.ts` store per persona key, created on first use and kept until `forget(key)` drops it (a persona teardown, which stops the persona's connection first, since another event for the key would create a new store); the key is the event's (channel, ts), or (channel, ts, edited.ts) when the event carries a top-level `edited.ts` (read by the private `editedTs`; a `message_changed` event nests its edit under `message` and keeps the two-part key), and a duplicate key stops after the archive write with no decision and no log line. The pipeline asks `decideDelivery` (`delivery-decision.ts`) once per event whether the receiving persona gets it, passing the persona's bot identity (bot user ID and bot ID) from the injected `getBotIdentity` and the persona's `dm.enabled`; see Data Flow, Inbound for the rule order. The pipeline logs the drop lines (`unclaimed-channel`, `persona-dm-dropped`, and a plain dropped line for the other reasons, none carrying message text), resolves the author label, looks up the persona's session with `getSessionByPersona(key)` and probes its stream, sends `notifications/claude/channel` to that session only, with meta that adds the author's `user_id` (or `bot_id`) and the decision's `via`, and only once that send has succeeded records the persona's ack-tracker entry and adds the `ack_reaction` through the persona's own client (b.av2 SR-4.5). It also owns the b.kvq no-session branch and the b.9cj streamless branch (the private `handleLostMessage`): it feeds `decideLostMessageState` (`lost-message.ts`) the persona's inputs, each asked with its key at that time, and fires the human-triggered `scheduleRestart` only when `firesHumanTriggeredRestart` says so (`starting-now`). The inputs are optional `PersonaRoutingDeps` members, an absent one answering false: `isPersonaUp` (production: the server's one predicate), `isLatched` (production: the one conflict latch's `isLatched`), `isTmuxUnresponsive` (production: the `tmux-unresponsive` condition's `holds`), `isLaunchOrApproverRunning` (production: `isLaunchInFlight(key) || isDialogApproverRunning(key)`, a launch call or the dialog approver that runs after it returned; kept apart from `main()`'s "in flight for P" binding), `isKillFailed` (production: the kill-failure alerts' `isOpen`, read at call time through the holder `main()` sets, `personaKillFailureAlerts`, so false before `main()` builds them; b.jg5 SRJ-1011 state 4), `isSequenceOrWaitRunning` (b.jg5 SRJ-706, SRJ-1011; production: the session manager's running query `isLiveRowSequenceRunning`, read at call time, so false before `main()` installs the live-row sequence registry), and `isHeldOnInvalidFlags` (b.jg5 SRJ-207, SRJ-1011 state 3; production: the server's `ErrInvalidFlags` hold's `isHeld`, `invalid-flags-hold.ts`, read at call time, so false before `main()` builds the hold). Two more optional members serve the one lost-message row read (b.jg5 SRJ-1011, SRJ-1501): `isWorkInFlight(key)` (absent: nothing is in flight; production: `main()`'s "in flight for P" binding, `isPersonaWorkInFlight`, the one the health tick and the `tmux-unavailable` retry check use: anything that blocks a retry (a launch call or a running live-row sequence), or a running dialog approver) and `readRowLiveness(key)` (absent: no read is made; production: the liveness adapter `main()` builds, `_buildIsSessionAliveAdapter`, the same instance the restart path and the health tick receive, held in the module holder `personaRowLiveness` that `main()` sets right after building it and read at call time, so before then the routing's read answers `unknown` with no `status` call). Its answer is read with `livenessKindOf`, so a value that is not a reading counts as `unknown`. The read's gate, its answers and the decision after it are in Data Flow, Inbound step 7. One more optional member, `armRetryTimerIfMissing(key)` (b.jg5 SRJ-311; absent: nothing is armed; production: `server.ts`'s `armMissingTmuxUnavailableRetry` over `tmuxUnavailableRetryDeps`, the check the session-disconnect handler decides through, doing nothing while the server is shutting down), is asked before the decision (the private `armStoppedRetryBeforeDecision`: before the read gate's check, and again after the row read when one was awaited), only when none of states 1 to 4 applies, state 5's condition holds, P's `tmux-unavailable` flag is raised and P is below the restart cap (`isAtCap(key, RESTART_FAILURE_CAP)`); it is never a restart. One more optional member, `isRetryArmed(key)` (b.jg5 SRJ-1011 as amended; production: `unavailableRetry?.isArmed(key) === true`, read at call time through the holder `main()` sets, so false before the controller exists; absent, in hand-built fixtures: the armed-timer part of state 5 is not asked), gates state 5. State 5 (`not-answering`, the private `isNotAnswering`) holds only when its condition holds (the private `notAnsweringConditionHolds`: `isTmuxUnresponsive` or P's `tmux-unavailable` or `ad-config-malformed` flag read from `outage-state.ts` (`getOutageFlags`); no other outage class and no unclassified-error episode counts), P is below the restart cap (asked whether or not `isRetryArmed` is bound) and `isRetryArmed` answers exactly true: its notice says CSCB is retrying, so a P at the cap, even with a timer still armed that stops at its next retry, or with no timer armed, falls through to the later states. The restart guards come from the real restart and backoff state. It raises one lost-message notice (`buildLostMessageNotice`) through the injected `notify`, which goes to the persona's destination. Nothing else is posted in the source conversation (when the destination is that conversation, the notice is the one post there), and a lost message gets no ack reaction or ack-tracker entry. The notice is awaited; a failing `notify` logs `[slack] persona-routing: lost-message notice for persona <ref> failed: <describeThrownValue>` and is never thrown. `hasSessionStream(key)` is the one `_GET_stream` probe shared by dispatch, the restart guard and the health check. Every Slack client, the persona config, the bot identity, the name resolver, the archive writer, the ack-reaction source, the notice sink (`notify`), the logger and (optionally) the dedupe clock, the up predicate and the lost-message state inputs are injected; the session lookup, restart guards and outage flags use the real registry, restart, backoff and outage state. Side-effect free: no client, token, file, environment read, timer or log at import. The module holds no agent-director client: its one agent-director call is the injected lost-message row read, and a rejection of that read is caught and logged as `[slack] persona-routing: lost-message row read for persona <ref> failed — session-starting left out: <describeAgentDirectorFailure>` (redacted), never thrown. Slack-call failures are logged through `describeSlackCallFailure`.
    ├── lost-message.ts         b.av2 SR-4.6 / SR-7.3 / SR-13.1; b.jg5 SRJ-1011 / SRJ-1509 the lost-message recovery state and notice text. `LOST_MESSAGE_STATES` is the frozen, closed list of the ten `LostMessageState` values in SRJ-1011's order: `not-up`, `held-for-human`, `cannot-launch`, `kill-failed`, `not-answering`, `session-starting`, `restarting`, `auto-restart-disabled`, `restart-limit-reached`, `starting-now`. `decideLostMessageState(queries)` asks injected queries in order and stops at the first true: states 1 to 5 through `decideEarlyLostMessageState` (the optional `isNotUp`, `isLatched`, `isHeldOnInvalidFlags`, `isKillFailed`, `isNotAnswering`; the caller's `isNotAnswering` carries state 5's restart-cap and retry-timer gates, see `persona-routing.ts`), then the optional `isSequenceOrWaitRunning` (`restarting`, so a running live-row sequence reports `restarting` ahead of state 6; see `persona-routing.ts` for its binding), then the optional `isRowPending` (`session-starting`), then the three required queries: a restart already pending or running (`restarting`), auto-restart disabled (`session_restart_delay` 0), the persona at the restart-failure cap; otherwise `starting-now`. An absent optional query answers false (an absent `isNotUp` counts the persona as up), so with none given the decision is the four-query one. `decideEarlyLostMessageState` is exported so a caller that must know whether states 1 to 5 apply asks the same code. `firesHumanTriggeredRestart(state)` is true only for `starting-now` (b.jg5 SRJ-1501). `STATE_WORDING` is the frozen, exported map of each state's one `Recovery:` line; tests import it and the order and keep no copy. `buildLostMessageNotice(senderLabel, state)` builds the one-line notice body: a message from the sender was lost, not delivered, not saved and won't be delivered later, plus the recovery state. It escapes `&`, `<` and `>` in the label through `escapeSlackControlCharacters` (`slack-text-escape.ts`), so a bot `username` such as `<!channel>` notifies no one, and folds line breaks. The body carries no message text, no mention and no persona name; the notifier adds the persona reference. Pure: no state, I/O, timers or logging, nothing at import. Its only caller is `persona-routing.ts`, which feeds the queries (see that entry) and raises the notice through the per-persona notice sink.
    ├── slack-text-escape.ts    the one escaping of Slack's control characters in text CSCB posts but did not write. `escapeSlackControlCharacters(text)` replaces `&` (first, so no entity it writes is escaped again), `<` and `>` with `&amp;`, `&lt;` and `&gt;` and changes nothing else, so `<!channel>`, `<@U…>` or a `<…>` placeholder renders as itself and notifies no one. It is not idempotent: escaped text is escaped again. Its callers are `lost-message.ts` (the sender label) and `outage-state.ts` (agent-director's description quoted in the `ad-config-malformed` onset). `unescapeSlackControlCharacters(text)` undoes it (`&lt;` and `&gt;` first, `&amp;` last, so `&amp;lt;` becomes `&lt;`) and changes nothing else; its caller is `persona-notifier.ts`, whose persona teardown window writes text built for Slack to the server log and `startup-errors.log` instead (b.jg5 SRJ-1003). Pure: no imports, no module-scope state, nothing runs at import.
    ├── inbound-dedupe.ts       b.av2 SR-4.1 / SR-13.1 one persona's inbound dedupe store. `createInboundDedupeStore(now?)` returns a store whose `record(conversationId, ts, editedTs?)` answers `new` (and records the key), `duplicate`, or `unkeyable` (`conversationId` or `ts` missing, empty or not a string; nothing recorded, and the caller treats the event as new). The key is (`conversationId`, `ts`, `editedTs`) when `editedTs` is a non-empty string, and (`conversationId`, `ts`) otherwise; the parts are joined with a separator no Slack ID or ts contains, so a two-part and a three-part key never collide. A key is remembered for `INBOUND_DEDUPE_RETENTION_MS` (10 minutes) from its first sighting; a duplicate does not extend it. Each `record` first prunes expired keys, so memory stays bounded with no timer. It knows nothing about personas, Slack or config and limits nothing: distinct keys are always new. State is in memory only. Clock injected (default `Date.now`); nothing at import. Its only caller is `persona-routing.ts`, which keeps one store per persona.
    ├── registry.ts             Persona-keyed MCP session registry (b.av2 SR-6.3), per-session MCP Server factory with the persona-scoped Slack tools, transport routing. A session is identified by its `roots/list` working directory, compared by real path; `matchPersonaByRootsPath` maps it to exactly one applied persona (a directory matching more than one persona matches none, with one log line). `decideSessionAdmission(rootsPath, personas, { isPersonaUp, describeNotUp?, ... })` wraps the match and answers `admitted`, `unmatched` or `not-up` (b.av2 SR-6.4); it logs the refusal line for `not-up` and registers, removes or closes nothing itself (see Session Lifecycle, Connection). `closePendingSession(pendingId, transport, { removePending, stopKeepAlive })` disconnects a pending session that won't be registered: it removes the pending entry, stops the SSE keep-alive, then closes the transport and ignores a close error; `server.ts` uses it for every such branch (see Session Lifecycle, Connection). `dropPersonaSession(key)` drops the session registered for a persona: it removes the persona's MCP session-ID mappings and registry entry first, marks the entry not connected, then closes its transport, so the close restarts nothing; it resolves whether a session was registered and logs nothing (see Session Lifecycle, Disconnection; a persona teardown drops the session the same way). The registry holds one session per persona key (`getSessionByPersona`); a newer session for a persona replaces the older one, and a stale close of the replaced session leaves the newer one registered. A pending session's entry stub is promoted in place, so its tool handlers read the persona key it was matched under. The posting-scope check `checkPersonaTarget(persona, target, action)` sorts the target with the module-private `classifyPersonaTarget` (a configured channel `id`, a `D…` DM conversation ID, a `U…`/`W…` user ID, or other) and allows a configured channel always, a `D…` conversation only while the persona's `dm.enabled` is on, and a user ID only for a `post` action (`reply`) while `dm.enabled` is on; each tool's target argument and action are in the private `TOOL_TARGET` map (see Outbound). A pure check: no Slack call, log or state. The MCP instructions (`MCP_INSTRUCTIONS`, exported as the exact string `createSessionServer` hands every instance, which the shipped-description audit in `tests/shipped-docs.test.ts` covers) describe the `<channel>` tag (their example tag carries `source="slack-channel-router"`, the MCP server name the harness renders) (including the author's `user_id`, or `bot_id` for an author without a user, and the `via` values), say that `<@ID>` in text mentions a Slack user or another persona and is how to address another persona, say that a message without `via` is an injected prompt, state where the tools may act (configured channels, and with DMs on a DM conversation or, for `reply`, a user ID), and describe the tools. No session-id discovery (AD owns it).
    ├── lib.ts                  Pure utilities — chunking (`chunkText`), sanitization, the `_GET_stream` probe `hasGetStreamKey`, and the file exfiltration guard `assertSendable(filePath, stateDir, inboxDir, protectedPaths)` (see Security Model).
    ├── logging.ts              Log file setup — overrides console.error/console.log with timestamped writeSync to a log file. Size-based rotation on every write (b.brv): rotates server.log/clean_restart.log at CSCB_LOG_MAX_BYTES (default 10 MiB), keeps CSCB_LOG_KEEP generations (default 5; 0 = truncate).
    ├── agent-director-logger.ts  b.brv verbosity filter for the agent-director Client's diagnostic logger. `makeFilteredAdLogger(base)` drops routine `SubprocessClient: <verb> ok` per-poll success dumps at info/log level; warn/error always pass through. CSCB_AD_VERBOSE (truthy: 1/true/yes/on) returns the base logger unwrapped. Injected into `Client.create()` by `agent-director-startup.ts`.
    ├── startup-errors.ts       SR-5.1a startup-errors log — append-only to ~/.claude/channels/slack/startup-errors.log + stderr. Mostly written at start; these kinds of entry are written while the server runs: the runtime version re-check's stop entry (`ad-version-gate.ts`), `persona-unclassified-error` (b.jg5 SRJ-313), an unclassified-error alert for a persona no longer in the applied configuration, and `persona-kill-failed` and `persona-kill-survivor` (b.jg5 SRJ-704, SRJ-1013), the kill-failure alert's two versions for such a persona, and, for a stopped retry of a persona removed during its tries, `persona-kill-failed` carrying the stop's log line with no alert text (all written by `persona-episodes.ts`); and `persona-teardown-notice` (b.jg5 SRJ-1003, SRJ-1013), every notice raised for a persona while its teardown's notice window is open (its kill's ordinary kill-failure alert, a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME its kill met, an outage onset and that outage's later all-clear, an unclassified-error alert, the notices of the launch in flight, a stuck-prompt warning), with `persona-kill-survivor` for the kill-failure alert's survivor version raised then (written by `persona-notifier.ts`'s window through `recordStartupError`). The start sweep writes `persona-kill-survivor` at start too, and its `orphan-cleanup` entry can carry the alert's ordinary text (`session-manager.ts`).
    ├── agent-director-client.ts   SR-0.1 singleton Client wrapper. `getClient()` is a sync cached accessor returning the Client installed through the production `setClient()` setter, which only `agent-director-startup.ts` calls: by the startup gate, and in the server once more by the persona-client builder (`buildPersonaClient`, b.jg5 SRJ-213), which replaces the gate's client; every call site reads the singleton at call time, so none keeps a replaced client; calling `getClient()` before the gate runs throws a CSCB-internal "called before startup gate" error. The module holds no version check: AD's `Client.create()` enforces the client's minimum from `dist/version-floor.json`, and the startup gate applies CSCB's Phase 1 floor (`ad-version-gate.ts`) before it calls `setClient()`. Exposes `decideWithToken` (SR-7.2 — single source of truth for the snake-case `request_token` field on the decide wire) and `getPermission` + `isErrPermissionRequestNotFound` (SR-7.1 — wraps the paired AD release's `get-permission --request-token <uuid>` verb).
    ├── agent-director-errors.ts   SR-0.2 import surface for the agent-director client error classes it re-exports; `src/session-manager.ts`, among other modules and tests, imports them from here. Some modules and tests import error classes from `agent-director` directly. Re-exports `AgentDirectorError` and a subset of the 0.10.0 client's typed Err* classes, `ErrTmuxSessionCreate`, `ErrTmuxSendKeys`, `ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`, `ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed` and `ErrUnknownErrorName` among them. Others are not re-exported, among them `ErrPauseTimeout` (omitted by design) and `ErrInvalidFlags`, `ErrPermissionRequestNotFound` and `ErrAmbiguousRequest`, which CSCB recognises by `errName` on an `AgentDirectorError`. The module decides no class: an agent-director error gets its class from the classifier (`ad-error-class.ts`). The three Phase-1-only errors (`ErrTmuxKillFailed`, `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`, `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`) are recognised by name only: exported once as plain strings (`ERR_TMUX_KILL_FAILED_NAME`, `ERR_TMUX_UNRESPONSIVE_NAME`, `ERR_TMUX_SESSION_CONFLICT_NAME`, collected in `PHASE1_ONLY_ERR_NAMES`) and never imported or re-exported as classes until the Phase 1 client is adopted (E37), because a named import of an export the 0.10.0 client lacks fails every module that loads it.
