They are not in `PHASE1_ONLY_ERR_NAMES`, whose names the startup gate requires as classes in the client (`REQUIRED_ERR_NAMES`). `ERR_SPAWN_NOT_FOUND_NAME` (`'ErrSpawnNotFound'`) is kept as a string too, for the sites that tell that name apart through `hasAdErrorName` (`ad-error-class.ts`); its class is still re-exported. `ERR_SYSTEM_INSTALL_DISAPPEARED_NAME` (`'ErrSystemInstallDisappeared'`) is kept the same way for the liveness adapter, which reads that error `dead`. Also defines the CSCB-synthetic `ErrSpawnCapReached` (never emitted by the AD library; minted by the restart cap path — remediation hint "restart the server to retry — automatic restarts are suspended for this persona").
    ├── ad-description-phrases.ts  b.jg5 SRJ-1303 agent-director's description words that CSCB matches (ADSRD SR-1.4). No imports. String constants: the unusable recorded session name (`UNUSABLE_RECORDED_NAME_PHRASE`), the nine CONFLICT case words (`CONFLICT_*_PHRASE`, "another agent-director store" (`CONFLICT_ANOTHER_STORE_PHRASE`) among them), the description words that ride beside a case phrase or on a kill failure and are not case phrases (the plain spawn's label wordings `PLAIN_SPAWN_LABEL_NAMES_THIS_ID_PHRASE` and `PLAIN_SPAWN_LABEL_NOT_THIS_ID_PHRASE`, `NEW_ROW_ENDED_PHRASE`, `NOTHING_WRITTEN_PHRASE`, `PANE_NOT_ADOPTED_PHRASE`, `NO_KILL_SENT_PHRASE`, and every kill failure's `RETRY_KILL_LATER_PHRASE` and `NEVER_DELETE_ROW_PHRASE`), the different tmux server (`DIFFERENT_TMUX_SERVER_PHRASE`), the launch timeout (`LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_PHRASE`) and a row still stopping or still starting (`STILL_STOPPING_PHRASE`, `STILL_STARTING_PHRASE`). Besides the words it holds one pattern and its helper, the only definition of a kill failure's survivor-naming form (b.jg5 SRJ-702): `SURVIVOR_PID_PATTERN` (the word "pid", a space, then a number; no `g` flag) and `survivorPids(description)`, every pid a description names in that form, in order. The words are copied from agent-director so CSCB matches exactly what it writes; CSCB only looks for them in a description it has received and never uses one to build a command. The module sets no order in which the CONFLICT case words are checked, and the order of its declarations means nothing. The test stub's error builders take their descriptions from here; the error classifier (`ad-error-class.ts`) matches `UNUSABLE_RECORDED_NAME_PHRASE` and `DIFFERENT_TMUX_SERVER_PHRASE` from here; and the conflict latch (`conflict-latch.ts`) is the consumer of the nine CONFLICT case words, which it checks in the order it defines. No other module matches the other words.
    ├── ad-error-class.ts       b.jg5 SRJ-104 the one classifier of agent-director errors, and the `ErrInvalidFlags` step beside it. `classifyAdError(value)` maps any value thrown by an agent-director call to exactly one of ten classes (`AD_ERROR_CLASSES`, labels `AD_ERROR_CLASS_*`, type `AdErrorClass`), recognising errors by name; pure and never throws. `hasAdErrorName(value, name)` is the one never-throwing by-name check a site uses to tell one agent-director error name from another (a STATE name's meaning is set per site): true when `value` is an agent-director error whose `errName` is `name`, passed as a name constant from `agent-director-errors.ts`. `isInvalidFlagsError(value)` is its use for `ErrInvalidFlags`, and narrows the value to `InvalidFlagsError`. `isDifferentTmuxServerError(value)` (b.jg5 SRJ-1021) answers whether a value is the re-bound-socket form of ENVIRONMENT: true only when `classifyAdError` gives ENVIRONMENT and its `errDescription` contains `DIFFERENT_TMUX_SERVER_PHRASE` from `ad-description-phrases.ts`; a missing or non-string description answers false. Recognition is by class and phrase only, with no `instanceof`; it never throws. `outage-state.ts`'s `raiseTmuxUnavailable` uses it to pick the onset. `describeAdErrorClassification(c)` renders a classification for a log line. `conflictDescriptionOf(value)` (b.jg5 SRJ-501, SRJ-507) answers the raw `errDescription` of a value that `classifyAdError` classes CONFLICT, read by name, and `undefined` for a value of any other class (an `ErrUnknownErrorName` included, whatever its `unknownName`), for a missing or non-string description and when a read throws; it never throws. The CONFLICT classification itself carries no description, so `describeAdErrorClassification` never logs that raw text; the reader (`conflict-latch.ts`) redacts it before it is stored or logged. `killFailedDescriptionOf(value)` (b.jg5 SRJ-110) answers the raw description of a value that is an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` by name (its own `errDescription`, or the envelope's `err_description` of an `ErrUnknownErrorName` whose `unknownName` is `ErrTmuxKillFailed`), and `undefined` for any other value, a non-string description or a read that throws; the kill outcome (`checked-kill.ts`) carries it raw and every log line renders it redacted. `unclassifiedClassificationOf(value)` is the UNCLASSIFIED classification, reported name and rendered message included, of a value a site takes as UNCLASSIFIED although the classifier gives it another class (at a kill, a class SRJ-110 has no row for); it is pure and never throws. `CSCB_UNKNOWN_ERROR_NAME` (`'UnknownError'`) is the `errName` of CSCB's own `UnknownError` wrapper, which classifies UNAVAILABLE. `classifyWithInvalidFlagsRecheck(value, trigger?)` is the `ErrInvalidFlags` step: one immediate version re-check through `triggerAdVersionRecheck` (`ad-version-gate.ts`), then UNCLASSIFIED; it answers an `AdErrorStepAnswer`, or for an `InvalidFlagsError` argument an `AdInvalidFlagsStepAnswer` whose `recheck` is not optional. `describeAgentDirectorFailure(err)` renders a failed call for a log line (a safe `errName`, then the redacted description; `permission-poller.ts` re-exports it). **Verbs (b.jg5 SRJ-307, SRJ-310).** `AD_VERBS` (type `AdVerb`) lists every agent-director verb a wrapped call declares. A wrapped call declares an `AdCall`: its verb, or for `kill` an `AdKillCall` (`{ verb: 'kill', rowReadLive }`; `AD_CALL_KILL_ROW_READ_LIVE`, `AD_CALL_KILL_ROW_NOT_READ_LIVE`, `adKillCall(rowReadLive)`), since only the site knows whether it kills a row it read live. The tmux-touching set is `TMUX_TOUCHING_VERBS`: `spawn` (plain or reuse), `resume`, `read-pane`, `send-keys`, `pause`, and `kill` of a row read live. `isTmuxTouchingCall(call)` answers for a declared call (a `kill` only when `rowReadLive` is exactly true) and `adCallVerb(call)` gives its verb; both never throw. `AD_LAUNCH_VERBS` is `spawn` and `resume`, and `isLaunchCall(call)` answers for a declared call: a successful launch call leaves its row `pending`, which the wrapper passes as the condition end's reading. `AD_READ_VERBS` is `status`, `get` and `list`, the arming predicate's read verbs. `find-missing`, `delete`, `get-permission` and `decide` are in none of these sets. See [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104).
    ├── checked-kill.ts         b.jg5 SRJ-110 / SRJ-701 / SRJ-703 a kill's outcome, its class, whether the caller's next step may run, one checked kill and its log rendering. No server-only import (no notifier, outage state, Slack client, latch, episodes or server module), no state and no version re-check of its own, so a CLI process can use it too. `KillOutcome` is a success (`KillSuccess`) or a non-success (`KillFailure`). The successes: `killed` (`KILL_OUTCOME_KILLED`, the call resolved; `killSent` is the result's `kill_sent`, true or false, absent from a result with no boolean `kill_sent`, read through `ad-phase1-types.ts`'s `Phase1KillResult`), `row-gone` (`ErrSpawnNotFound`), `session-gone` (a GONE answer, `ErrTmuxSendKeys` or `ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`, its name kept: for `kill`, gone is success, b.jg5 SRJ-104) and `row-finished` (`KILL_OUTCOME_ROW_FINISHED`, with its `read`), which only the bounded retry (`kill-retry.ts`) gives, when a `status` read between tries finds the row finished. The non-success is `not-killed` with one of `KILL_FAILURE_CLASSES`: UNAVAILABLE (`killFailed` true for `ErrTmuxKillFailed`, by name, with its raw `killFailedDescription` from `killFailedDescriptionOf`), CONFLICT, UNUSABLE_NAME, CONFIG, ENVIRONMENT or UNCLASSIFIED; the thrown value is kept as `error` and never logged raw. A class SRJ-110 has no row for (`KILL_UNLISTED_CLASSES`: LAUNCH FAILURE, a STATE name other than `ErrSpawnNotFound`, `ErrInvalidFlags` included, and DIRECTORY) is UNCLASSIFIED with that class kept as `unlistedClass`; `recheck` is the answer kind of the `ErrInvalidFlags` version re-check a caller made, never set here. `killOutcomeOf(settled)` maps a settled kill (`{ result }` or `{ thrown }`) to its outcome by name through `ad-error-class.ts` (`classifyAdError`, `hasAdErrorName`); it is pure and never throws. `checkedKill(instanceId, kill)` makes exactly one call of the injected `kill` with `{ claude_instance_id }` alone (`PlainKillParams`, a plain kill) and answers its outcome; it never throws, rejects or retries. `killLetsNextStepRun(outcome)` is the next-step predicate: true only for a success form, false for every non-success and for any value that is not a kill outcome. `isKillOutcome(value)` and `killOutcomeStopsServer(value)` (a non-success whose `recheck` is `stop`) never throw. `describeKillOutcome(outcome)` renders one log line's fragment: `outcome=killed kill_sent=<true|false|absent>`, `outcome=row-gone (ErrSpawnNotFound)`, `outcome=session-gone (<GONE name>)`, `outcome=row-finished read=<read>` or `outcome=not-killed class=<class> …` (with `from=<class>` and `recheck=<kind>` for an unlisted class), every description through the shared redaction and no raw thrown value. Beside it, the two notice texts built from a kill's outcome where nothing latches on it (b.jg5 SRJ-1002, SRJ-1003, SRJ-110), both unescaped and never throwing: `teardownKillRefusalNoticeText(instanceId, refusal)` (a `KillRefusal`: `at` `KILL_REFUSAL_AT_KILL` or `KILL_REFUSAL_AT_READ`, a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE_NAME `errorClass`, the thrown value), `agent-director kill of <id> refused at a try: <outcome>` or `… refused at a status read between its tries: <outcome>`, and `teardownKillNotSucceededNoticeText(instanceId, outcome, tries)`, `agent-director kill of <id> did not succeed after <n> kill(s); the row is kept: <outcome>`. Its callers: `killPersonaInstance` and the start sweep's `sweepKill` (`session-manager.ts`), the bounded retry (`kill-retry.ts`), the restart work (`restart.ts`), the restart kill adapter (`server.ts`) and the persona teardown (`persona-lifecycle.ts`).
    ├── kill-retry.ts           b.jg5 SRJ-702 / SRJ-110 the bounded retry of a live row's kill. No server-only import (no notifier, outage state, Slack client, latch, episodes or server module) and no state, so a CLI process can use it too; every wait is injected (`KillRetryWait`: a clock with `setTimeout`, the shape `createFakeClock` satisfies, or a sleep function; `KILL_RETRY_SYSTEM_CLOCK` is the production clock), and every wait is awaited, so no timer is left pending once a call settles. `runKillRetry(options)` (`KillRetryOptions`: `instanceId`, the site's single-try `kill`, its between-try `read`, `wait`, the seed `lastRead`, optional `keepGoing` and `budget`, `log` and `logPrefix`) makes up to `KILL_RETRY_TRIES` (3) tries `KILL_RETRY_SPACING_MS` (2 s) apart, never throws or rejects, and answers a `KillRetryResult`: the `outcome` that stands, how the tries ended (`end`: `settled`, `exhausted`, `budget-spent`, `row-finished`, `read-config`, `read-latched` or `stopped`), the counts of `tries` and `reads`, and the `alert` decision (`KillRetryAlert`: `none`, `survivor` with `survivorDescription`, or `ordinary` with `lastKillFailedDescription` and/or `earlierSurvivorDescription`, each raw for the caller to redact). The seed (`KillRetrySeed`: `killRetrySeedOfState(state)`, `KILL_RETRY_SEED_LIVE_UNREAD`, `KILL_RETRY_SEED_NOT_LIVE_VALUE`) is the row state the path last read; `killRetrySeedIsLive` is true for a known-live seed or a state other than `ended` and `missing`. A read answers a `KillRetryRead` (`state`, `no-row`, `latched` or `failed` with its error). `createKillRetryPassBudget()` is the start sweep's pass budget; `killRetryStopped(result)` is true when a latching read or the keep-going check ended the tries; `namesSurvivor(description)` is `survivorPids` (`ad-description-phrases.ts`) found non-empty, the only survivor detector. Its lines come from `killRetryTryLine`, `killRetryReadLine`, `killRetryStopLine` and `killRetryEndLine`, every description redacted. Behaviour: [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The bounded kill retry**.
    ├── kill-failure-alert.ts   b.jg5 SRJ-704 / SRJ-1007 / SRJ-1013 the kill-failure alert's texts and its route selection. Pure: no module-scope state, no environment or file access, no server-only import (no notifier, Slack client, latch, episodes, outage state or server module) and nothing at import, so any process that kills a row can build the same texts. Two versions (`KILL_FAILURE_VERSION_ORDINARY`, `KILL_FAILURE_VERSION_SURVIVOR`): `killFailureOrdinaryBody` (*Kill failed*) quotes the descriptions the bounded retry's `ordinary` decision carries (the last kill failure's, the latest survivor-naming one, or both in SRJ-1007's two-description form, the last kill failure's first) and leaves the "agent-director said" sentence out when it has none; `killFailureSurvivorBody` (*Process outlived kill*) quotes the latest survivor-naming description and lists its pids (`killFailureSurvivorPidList`, which reads them only through `survivorPids`, `ad-description-phrases.ts`), and names no command. Every quoted description, the session and the instance id go through `renderLogMessageText` (redacted, one line, capped at 300 characters, b.jg5 SRJ-1001); a text built `forSlack` is then escaped once (`escapeSlackControlCharacters`), and a log line or entry is not. The closing sentences are the `KILL_FAILURE_*_CLOSING` constants, picked by `killFailureClosingSentence(version, closing)` from the rows `destination`, `destination-latched` (ordinary only; the survivor version takes its destination sentence), `cli-teardown` and `log-only`. `killFailureAlertText(content, closing, forSlack)` is the body, a space and the closing sentence; `killFailureAlertEntryText(ref, context, text)` is the log-line and entry form `<ref> (<context>): <text>`. The contexts are `KILL_FAILURE_CONTEXTS`, in SRJ-1007's order: `start sweep`, `CLI teardown`, `persona teardown`, `old-life wait`, `stuck-launch abort`, `recovery`. `selectKillFailureAlertRoute({ version, context, configured, latched })` answers SRJ-704's route, first match wins, with its class (`PERSONA_KILL_FAILED_LABEL`, `persona-kill-failed`; `PERSONA_KILL_SURVIVOR_LABEL`, `persona-kill-survivor`, for the survivor version on every route that writes an entry; `PERSONA_TEARDOWN_NOTICE_LABEL`, `persona-teardown-notice`, the persona teardown's, exported as the one constant that `persona-notifier.ts` imports and re-exports, since this pure module may load no notifier), whether the text is printed, whether it opens the persona's episode and its closing sentence; it is pure and never throws. Its callers: the kill-failure alerts (`persona-episodes.ts`) and the start sweep (`session-manager.ts`). Behaviour: [The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007).
    ├── live-row-sequence.ts    b.jg5 SRJ-705 / SRJ-706 / SRJ-717 / SRJ-710 the live-row sequence: the one way a persona's live row `cscb_<key>` (`pending` included) is replaced. `runLiveRowSequence(request, deps, stop)` runs one sequence and answers its outcome (`LiveRowSequenceOutcome`); it never throws or rejects and leaves no timer of its own pending once it settles. The request (`LiveRowSequenceRequest`) carries the key, the instance id, the state the starter last read, the entry step (`LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_ENTRY_KILL`, 1, or `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_ENTRY_GET`, 2, for a starter that made the first kill itself), the keep-conversation and retired-key flags, whether it ends in a launch (false is the no-launch form) and the kill-failure alert's context (one of `KILL_FAILURE_CONTEXTS`). `createLiveRowSequenceStop()` builds the stop signal (reasons `latched`, `teardown`, `shutdown`, `not-up`). The pure `decideLiveRowLaunchKind` decides step 6's kind and reason; `liveRowLaunchSucceeded` reads a launch result against `LIVE_ROW_LAUNCH_SUCCESS_ACTIONS` (`fresh-retired` among them, b.jg5 SRJ-806); the pure `liveRowSequence*Line` builders build every line it logs, under `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_LOG_PREFIX` (`[slack] live-row-sequence:`). The pace and caps are exported: `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_RUN_SPACING_MS` (5 s), `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_STEP4_PAUSE_MS` (5 s), `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_STEP3_RUNS` (3), `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_MAX_RUNS` (4), `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_MAX_KILLS` (2). Every agent-director call, the latch, the alerts, the retry arm and the clock come through `LiveRowSequenceDeps`, which the session manager's `buildLiveRowSequenceDeps` binds: the checked kill inside the bounded retry (`retryPersonaKill`), the kill-failure alerts and their episodes, the shared own-row `get` and `status` reads, the bypassing `find-missing` entry, E6's G accessor and the sequence-launch entry; the wait arms through `armNeverEarlyWait` on the injected clock, and the launch start comes from `parseLaunchStart` (`pending-row.ts`). It holds no module-scope state, runs nothing at import, and loads neither the session manager, the server, the notifier nor any Slack module; it arms through its own cause names (`LIVE_ROW_ARM_NOT_JUDGED`, `LIVE_ROW_ARM_ENDED`, `LIVE_ROW_ARM_REUSE_COLLISION`, `LIVE_ROW_ARM_LOST_RACE`), which the dependency builder maps to `unavailable-retry.ts`'s labels. Step 6's not-launched reasons include three for a `resume` that answered `ErrSpawnNotResumable`, after the entry's one re-read of the row (b.jg5 SRJ-710, never a second sequence): `not-resumable` (`LIVE_ROW_NOT_LAUNCHED_NOT_RESUMABLE`, a lost race, arming `LIVE_ROW_ARM_LOST_RACE`), `not-resumable-pending` (`LIVE_ROW_NOT_LAUNCHED_NOT_RESUMABLE_PENDING`, a launch in progress, arming `LIVE_ROW_ARM_ENDED`) and `not-resumable-latched` (`LIVE_ROW_NOT_LAUNCHED_NOT_RESUMABLE_LATCHED`, which the sequence ends as stopped for the latch, nothing armed). The registry, `createLiveRowSequenceRegistry({ deps, runAttempt })` (b.jg5 SRJ-706, SRJ-811), is one per server and holds its state in the returned object: entries keyed by instance id, each recording its persona key. `start(request)` starts a sequence without awaiting it and answers `started` (`LIVE_ROW_START_STARTED`; the sequence's first call comes after the answer), `already-running` (`LIVE_ROW_START_ALREADY_RUNNING`: a sequence already runs on that instance id or for that persona; nothing started) or `closed` (`LIVE_ROW_START_CLOSED`, after `close`), a refusal logging `liveRowSequenceNotStartedLine`; it never throws. `stop(key, reason)` sets that persona's sequence's stop signal before it returns, logs `liveRowSequenceStopAskedLine`, and resolves true once the sequence has settled (its call in flight returned, its end line logged), false at once when none runs; `stopAll(reason)` stops every one; `close()` stops every one with `shutdown` and refuses every later start; none rejects. `isRunning(key)` is true from the start's answer until the sequence settles, its step-6 launch included. Each sequence runs inside the injected attempt runner (`LiveRowSequenceAttemptRunner`; production `runDetachedRecoveryAttempt`, `unavailable-retry.ts`), its own recovery attempt for the persona, detached from its starter's. An entry is removed when its sequence settles, whatever the outcome. Its production starters, both in `session-manager.ts` and both through `startLiveRowSequence`, answer `sequence-waiting`: the collision ladder's replace step (`replacePersonaRow`, b.jg5 SRJ-707): at a ladder site whose row cannot be kept (`resume_enabled` false, a `cwd` mismatch, a `config_dir` mismatch) and whose last-read state is live (`pending` and an unreadable state included), and at a retired key's old life (b.jg5 SRJ-805), it starts a sequence with that state as its seed, entry at step 1, the conversation not kept, the retired-key flag set for a retired key, ending in a launch, alert context `recovery`; and the ladder's not-resumable step (`spawnNotResumableAtLadder`, b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-611): a `resume` that answered `ErrSpawnNotResumable` on a path holding dead evidence, whose re-read finds the row in a known live state other than `pending` (`AGENT_DIRECTOR_LIVE_STATES`), starts the same request seeded with the re-read state and with the conversation kept, so its step 6 is a `resume` when the row allows one. Behaviour: [The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717).
    ├── pane-read.ts            b.jg5 SRJ-117 the outcome of one `read-pane` of a persona's own row and its class. `FULL_PANE_READ_LINES` (40) is a full read's `n_lines`, and `PROBE_PANE_READ_LINES` (1) a one-line probe's, the count b.jdc's two prompt-row paths read with (`promptRowReconnectVerdict` in `server.ts`, `launchOnPromptRow` in `session-manager.ts`; b.jg5 SRJ-606, SRJ-607). `PaneReadOutcome` is a pane (`PANE_READ_PANE`, with its text), a failure (`PaneReadFailure`: kinds `PANE_READ_FAILURE_KINDS`, `gone`, `absent`, `unavailable`, `conflict`, `unusable-name`, `config`, `environment`, `unclassified`; each carries the classifier's `errorClass` and the redacted one-line `description` from `describeAgentDirectorFailure`, and a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME also keeps the thrown value as `error`; an UNCLASSIFIED is a `PaneReadUnclassified`, whose optional stop mark `stopping: true` only the shared reader sets, when its `ErrInvalidFlags` version re-check decided that the server stops) or latched (`PANE_READ_LATCHED`, `PaneReadLatched`, with an optional `cause`: the CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answer that latched the persona, absent when it was latched before and so not read; `PANE_READ_NOT_READ_LATCHED`). `paneReadFailureOf(value)` maps a value `read-pane` threw to exactly one failure, by class and by name through `ad-error-class.ts` (`classifyAdError`, `hasAdErrorName` for `ErrSpawnNotFound`); `paneReadClassNote(failure)` renders a failed read's class for the end of a caller's log line (`read-pane class=<class>`). Pure: no agent-director call, latch, module state or log line; never throws. The reader that calls agent-director and latches is `readPersonaOwnPane` (`session-manager.ts`). See [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The shared read-pane**.
    ├── ad-phase1-types.ts      b.jg5 SRJ-1303 CSCB-side, type-only declarations of the Phase 1 agent-director result and parameter fields the 0.10.0 client does not declare. No runtime code; its only import is a type import of the 0.10.0 client's own result and parameter types, which its interfaces extend. `Phase1KillResult` adds `kill_sent` (optional, absent from a binary older than Phase 1); `Phase1StatusResult`, `Phase1GetResult` and `Phase1ListRow` add `launch_started_at` (a `pending` row only), and `Phase1ListResult` carries `Phase1ListRow` rows; `Phase1SpawnResult` (plain or reuse spawn) and `Phase1ResumeResult` add `pre_trust` (`PreTrust`: `ok`, `skipped` or `failed`; optional, absent from a binary older than Phase 1). `Phase1SpawnParams` adds `reuse_finished` to a spawn's parameters (`SpawnParams`): the reuse spawn's flag (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-708), set only by the session manager's reuse spawn and absent on every plain spawn; the 0.10.0 client neither declares nor emits it, and the test stub records the parameters as given. `liveness_note` is the 0.10.0 client's own `get` and `list` field (free text, `string | null`), kept as that type; `LivenessNote` names the notes CSCB tells apart: `provenance_conflict` latches a persona, and `tmux_server_changed`, `process_not_seen_session_present` and `tmux_session_name_rewritten` must never latch one. The test stub's canned results take the types from here, never from `agent-director`. Four `src/` readers exist: `liveness-reading.ts` reads a `status` result's `launch_started_at` raw (`pendingLaunchStartOf`); `pending-row.ts` parses the `launch_started_at` of a `status` result or a `get` result through it (`parseLaunchStart`, `isPendingWithNoLaunchStart`), for the row-read rule's launch-start decision; the session manager's own-row read (`readPersonaOwnRow`, deciding through `row-read-rules.ts`, whose `LATCHING_LIVENESS_NOTE` satisfies `LivenessNote`) reads a `get` result's `liveness_note` (see [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)); and the session manager's after-launch step reads a spawn or `resume` result's `pre_trust` (`Phase1SpawnResult`, `Phase1ResumeResult`) only to log it (`preTrustLogLine`, b.jg5 SRJ-413). The kill outcome (`checked-kill.ts`) reads a kill result's `kill_sent` (`Phase1KillResult`, b.jg5 SRJ-701). No `src/` reader of the `launch_started_at` of a `list` row exists yet. Once the Phase 1 client is adopted its own types replace this module (b.jg5 E37).
    ├── agent-director-startup.ts  SR-5.1 startup gate — async `Client.create()` injection / SR-4.2 system-install typed-error branches / CSCB's Phase 1 floor check on `binaryVersion` before `setClient()` (b.jg5 SRJ-203) / SR-6.1 API surface probes / same-user stat. `runStartupGate(deps?, options?)` returns a `StartupGateOutcome` whose failure arm carries `refusalKind` (`StartupGateRefusalKind`: `client-too-old`, `below-phase1-floor`, `other`) so callers branch on which check refused, never on the class label or message text. `StartupGateOptions.skipPhase1Floor` (default false) leaves only the floor check out; it is reserved for `stop --stop-bots`'s client initialization. `runAgentDirectorStartupGate(deps?)`, the server's exiting entry point, always runs the floor and sets no call timeout. **Client options (b.jg5 SRJ-213).** `buildAdClientOptions(callTimeoutMs?)` is the one place client options are built: the store path, `createIfMissing`, the filtered logger (b.brv), and `callTimeoutMs` only when one is given (otherwise the key is absent and the client uses its own default). `StartupGateOptions.callTimeoutMs` passes it through; the CLI sets it, the server's gate does not. **The persona client (b.jg5 SRJ-213).** The 0.10.0 client fixes `callTimeoutMs` at construction, and the server's gate builds its client before the configuration holding `agent_director_call_timeout_ms` is read, so its version probe uses the client's default. Once the start has resolved its configuration, `buildPersonaClient(callTimeoutMs, deps?)` (`PersonaClientDeps`: `createClient`, `closeClient`, `recordStartupError`, `exit`) builds a second client with the configured value through the gate's own construction step and catch ladder (`constructClient`, `constructFailure`) and the same Phase 1 floor check (`refuseBelowPhase1Floor`), so both fail with one label, message and outcome shape per cause. It repeats no API-surface probe and no same-user stat: they cover the installed package and the store, which the gate has checked in this process. On success it closes the installed (gate's) client once, through the client module's `closeClient()`, and installs the new client with `setClient()`, with no await between the two. On a construct failure or floor refusal it installs nothing, closes the client it built (if any, through the `closeClient` seam) and answers the gate's failure outcome (`StartupGateFailure`); the gate's client stays installed. `buildPersonaClientOrExit(callTimeoutMs, deps?)`, the server's form, makes one `recordStartupError(classLabel, message)` call and exits 1 on failure, as the gate does.
    ├── ad-version-gate.ts      b.jg5 SRJ-201 / SRJ-202 / SRJ-208 / SRJ-204 / SRJ-205 / SRJ-206 / SRJ-211 / SRJ-212 CSCB's own Phase 1 floor for the agent-director binary, the two version refusal messages, the runtime version re-check and the host-version decision. No value import from `agent-director` (errors are classified by their `errName`, else `name`, read as a string; fields are read structurally), no child process and no file read of its own (the install-skill block comes from `install-skill-pointer.ts`); nothing is armed, read or logged at import. `PHASE1_FLOOR_VERSION` is the floor (currently 0.11.0), the Phase 1 agent-director release's version; code and tests read it from the constant, never a literal. `meetsPhase1Floor(version)` parses the version with the same strict rule as the installed client's parser (`major.minor.patch` with an optional `-prerelease`, no leading `v`, no `+build` metadata, no whitespace trimming), refuses a version that does not parse (fail closed), and compares major, minor and patch numerically against the floor's; the pre-release suffix is ignored, so `<floor>-rc.N` counts as `<floor>`. There is no development override: the client's `0.0.0-dev` sentinel compares as `0.0.0` and is refused. `PHASE1_RUNBOOK_SECTION_TITLE` is the title of the README runbook section for switching over to agent-director Phase 1; every message, test and doc that names the section takes the title from it. `PHASE1_SWITCH_OVER_INSTRUCTION` is the operator instruction every `ad-below-phase1-floor` entry carries (b.jg5 SRJ-1013). `buildBelowPhase1FloorMessage({ foundVersion, binaryPath }, foundBy?)` and `buildSystemInstallTooOldMessage({ foundVersion, binaryPath, requiredVersion }, foundBy?)` build the `ad-below-phase1-floor` and `ad-system-install-too-old` messages; their startup form (the default, `FOUND_BY_STARTUP_CHECK`) is described under [Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 1. The runtime form (`FOUND_BY_RUNTIME_RECHECK`) replaces the floor message's "found by the startup check" with `RUNTIME_RECHECK_PHRASE` ("found by a runtime re-check while the server was running") plus ", so the server stopped", and adds the same clause after the too-old message's binary path; the startup forms never contain the phrase. **Host-version decision (SRJ-211).** `decideHostAdVersion(result, clientMinimum)` is the one decision on the host's agent-director binary against the installed client's minimum. Both callers settle their one call with `settleHostVersionCall(resolve)`, which returns the resolved value or the thrown value (a synchronous throw counts as a rejection) and never rejects. The decision is pure and never throws. Rejections are read by name (`errName`, else `name`): `ErrSystemInstallNotFound` fails `not-found`; `ErrSystemInstallTooOld` fails `below-client-minimum` from the error's `actualVersion`, `requiredVersion` and `binaryPath`; `ErrSystemInstallUnreachable` (any reason) fails `version-unreadable`, carrying a `reason` word: the error's own reason when it is a short safe word (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens), else `unknown` (`UNREACHABLE_REASON_UNKNOWN`, not one of agent-director's reasons); any other named error or non-error throw fails `other` with the re-check's token-free description. The first refused read after start or after an accepted read writes one log line (`buildAdSettingsRefusedReadLine`, see [Logging](#agent-director-settings-lines-bjg5-srj-209)); the rest of the run writes nothing. No reason carries the parser's message, the file's text or a string value: a parse failure is reported by line and column, a read failure by its errno code (or `not a regular file`), a wrong-typed value by its kind. The startup gate appends this block to the three `ad-system-install-*` typed-error failure messages only — never to `ad-below-phase1-floor`, `ErrBunVersionTooOld`, the three `ad-shim-*` branches, or the same-user check. The skill walks the operator through installing agent-director; for `ad-system-install-too-old` it names the README switch-over runbook section and runs nothing — it offers no upgrade or install command (b.jg5 SRJ-208).
    ├── install-check.ts           b.jg5 SRJ-212 the agent-director install check. `runInstallCheck(deps?)` reads the installed client's minimum with `readClientMinVersion()`, makes one call to the injected resolver (`InstallCheckDeps.resolveSystemBinary`, default the client's own `resolveSystemBinary`; tests pass a stub) and applies the host-version decision `decideHostAdVersion` from `ad-version-gate.ts`, shared with `/publish`'s check; it classifies agent-director errors by name through that decision, never `instanceof`, and never throws. Outcomes: a binary that meets CSCB's Phase 1 floor passes; one at or above the client's minimum but below the floor (`0.10.0`, the client's `0.0.0-dev` sentinel) passes with the success result's optional `note` (`buildInstallCheckPhase1Note`, naming the runbook section); any other outcome fails with one of four class labels: `ad-system-install-not-found`, `ad-system-install-too-old` (below the client's minimum, message from `buildSystemInstallTooOldMessage`, which names the runbook section and advises no upgrade), `ad-system-install-unreachable` (an `ErrSystemInstallUnreachable` of any reason, with the decision's reason word, so a reason that is absent or not a short safe word reports `unknown`; a resolved version that does not parse as reason `unparseable-version`; or any other failure as reason `other`, described by its name or type and never its own message) and `ad-version-floor-unreadable` (the client's `dist/version-floor.json` cannot be read, or its `min_binary_version` is missing or not a version). A failure's `detail` keeps the thrown error's structural fields, each text as one token-free line through `redactToOneLine`: an unreachable error's `diagnostic` and `signal` (`null` when not a string; `exitCode` kept only when a number, else `null`), a not-found error's `checkedLocations` (each entry copied as `{ kind, detail }`, both texts redacted; an empty list when the field is not a list) and a failed floor read's `underlying` (the thrown value's message, else `null`). A binary that passes with the note is still refused by the startup gate (`ad-below-phase1-floor`). Side-effect-free: no `process.exit`, no disk writes, no stdout/stderr. Consumed by `scripts/install-check.ts` (the `bun run install-check` diagnostic, which prints the note as the last line of its OK block), the install-cscb skill and the npm postinstall probe (`postinstall.ts`). `readClientMinVersion(deps?)` returns the installed client's `min_binary_version` (or the `ad-version-floor-unreadable` failure, one per failure mode: the subpath cannot be resolved, the file cannot be read, it does not parse as JSON, or the field is missing or not a non-empty string). Its optional `ClientMinVersionDeps` are `resolveFloorUrl` (default `import.meta.resolve` of `agent-director/dist/version-floor.json`; a throw is the resolve failure, a non-`file:` URL a read failure) and `readFile` (default `readFileSync` as UTF-8; a throw is the read failure). With no deps, or an empty deps object, the value or the failure is cached (`resetCacheForTests` / `setFloorForTests` reset and seed the cache in tests); a call with any dep injected bypasses the cache, neither returning the cached value nor storing its own result; `/publish`'s preflight check `scripts/ad-version-check.ts` reads it too. The class-label constants and the `InstallCheckClassLabel` type live in `install-check-labels.ts` and are re-exported here. The startup gate does not call `runInstallCheck()`: it builds the client with `Client.create()` and applies the Phase 1 floor itself, and imports only the class-label constants, so both emit the same strings.
    ├── install-check-labels.ts    The agent-director class labels (`AD_SYSTEM_INSTALL_NOT_FOUND`, `AD_SYSTEM_INSTALL_TOO_OLD`, `AD_SYSTEM_INSTALL_UNREACHABLE`, `AD_VERSION_FLOOR_UNREADABLE`, `AD_BELOW_PHASE1_FLOOR`, `AD_SHIM_CATALOG_INCOMPLETE`) and the `InstallCheckClassLabel` type (the first four, which the install check writes; the not-found, too-old and unreachable labels are shared with the startup gate, and the last two only the startup gate writes). A leaf module with no imports, so `ad-version-gate.ts` takes its labels from here and never imports `install-check.ts` (which imports `agent-director`); `install-check.ts` re-exports all of it.
    ├── agent-director-template.ts SR-3.1 / SR-3.2 / b.av2 SR-8.6 step 5 — builds the slack-channel-bot MakeTemplateParams and calls client.makeTemplate({ overwrite: true }). `installSlackChannelBotTemplate(personaConfig, deps?)` is the boot install: fatal on any rejection (records `ad-template-install` and exits 1), and it resolves `InstalledTemplate`, agent-director's result plus the `params` it installed. `refreshSlackChannelBotTemplate(applied, installed, { getClient, log, home? })` is the apply-time refresh: `installed` with its memory-read `allow` rules derived afresh from `applied` (`deriveMemoryReadAllowRules`, the boot derivation, so never a config-dir root) and every other field, `claude_args` included, as the boot install wrote it. It never rejects and never exits: it logs one `[slack] template refresh:` line and resolves `{ kind: 'refreshed', path }` or `{ kind: 'failed' }`; nothing retries it. Importable without side effects.
    ├── session-manager.ts      SR-1 in full — startupSessionManager (one bring-up and one spawnForPersona per persona), spawnForPersona (SR-1.4 collision-then-act, persona-keyed; its first spawn is plain, with no reuse flag, b.jg5 SRJ-711, and an `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` at any launch is one counted launch failure that kills nothing and makes no spawn in its place, b.jg5 SRJ-602; its `resume`'s outcomes follow b.jg5 SRJ-113 and its `ErrSpawnNotResumable` b.jg5 SRJ-710), launchSession (restart relaunch by persona key), reconcileOrphans (the persona-keyed start sweep, b.av2 SR-6.3, b.jg5 SRJ-116: one `list`, its latch pass `latchFromListedRows`, the `absent-at-start` recording `recordAbsentPersonaKeys`, then the kills of live strays, each checked and none followed by a delete (`killStartSweepRow`), one post-kill findMissing over every row given a kill (`runStartSweepPostKillFindMissing`) and the summary line (`startSweepSummaryLine`); b.jg5 SRJ-714, SRJ-1506; Server-Managed Startup step 4), reconnectMcp/waitForWaitingAndReconnect. The reconnect (`reconnectMcpWithCause(key, lastRead, ref?)`, with the row state its caller last read; `reconnectMcp` answers its outcome alone) makes exactly one `send-keys` of `/mcp reconnect`, never retries, starts no tmux server and makes no tmux call of its own (b.jg5 SRJ-118, SRJ-609). It decides its answer by class and name through `ad-error-class.ts`: `ReconnectOutcome` is `ok`, `dead-session` with a `DeadSessionCause` (`tmux-gone`, `row-not-interactive` or `row-absent`), or `transient` (nothing typed, never counted, no spawn-failure notice; marked `latched` when it latched or found the persona latched, `stopping` when its `ErrInvalidFlags` re-check stopped the server). Its lines come from exported builders (`reconnectStartLine`, `reconnectLatchedLine`, `reconnectGoneLine`, `reconnectNotInteractiveLine`, `reconnectRowAbsentLine`, `reconnectConflictLine` with `RECONNECT_NOT_THIS_LAUNCH_NOTE`, `reconnectUnusableNameLine`, `reconnectInvalidFlagsLine`, `reconnectTransientLine`), and the ladder's line for a `transient` one from `transientReconnectLine`; `escalateDeadVerdictOfCause` gives the escalate-dead verdict for each cause (see Server-Managed Startup step 5, the `waiting` branch). Dead evidence (b.jg5 SRJ-611; [Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)): `DEAD_SESSION_CAUSES` and `ESCALATE_DEAD_VERDICTS` list every `DeadSessionCause` (the reconnect's three, plus `row-read-finished` for the launch wait's finished-row read and `prompt-row-ladder-gone` for the ladder's prompt-row GONE) and every `EscalateDeadVerdict`; `isDeadEvidence(source)` decides each by an exhaustive switch, true only for the GONE-based ones and false, fail safe, for any other value, `undefined` and `DEAD_EVIDENCE_NONE`; `carriedDeadEvidenceOf` builds the `CarriedDeadEvidence` (`{ source, evidence }`) a path carries, `CARRIED_DEAD_EVIDENCE_NONE` for none (the type carries a type-only brand that only these two supply, so a value built by hand fails the typecheck, and `evidence` is always `isDeadEvidence(source)`); `describeDeadEvidence` renders it for the lines; `waitForWaitingAndReconnectWithCause` gives the launch wait's `dead-session` with its cause (`WaitDeadSession`); `launchSession(key, config, { canLaunch?, deadEvidence? })` and `spawnForPersona(persona, config, isStartup?, hooks?, deadEvidence?)` take the escalate-dead verdict the restart path's relaunch carries, which the ladder keeps for its run; the line builders are `deadSessionRouteLine`, `waitRowFinishedLine`, `waitRowAbsentLine`, `promptRowSweepFinishedLine` and `joinedLaunchDropsDeadEvidenceLine`. At start, `startupSessionManager(config, { bringUp })` runs each persona through the b.av2 SR-6.1 procedure: steps 1–3 (the bring-up controller's `bringUp`, `persona-bringup-controller.ts`) for every persona at once, then the launch (`spawnForPersona`) for each persona that is `up`, through a first-in, first-out launch pool of at most `concurrency` (default 3; a value below 1 is treated as 1), in the order the personas become ready, so no persona's Slack connection waits behind another persona's launch; `bringUp` is the controller, and the server always passes it (without it each persona is launched directly, in config order through the same pool, which only launch-ladder unit tests do). A `broken` or `retrying` persona takes no pool slot and is counted in `notBroughtUp` and as a `not-brought-up` entry with its `outcome` and failures in `perPersona`; it records no startup error, raises no notice and is not a failed spawn. `launchSession(key, config, { canLaunch?, deadEvidence? })` (restart) runs the launch only; it asks `canLaunch` (the server passes the relaunch gate) before looking the persona up, and when that answers false (not up, or a key no longer applied) it launches nothing, runs no trust patch or reply-guard step and returns `'skipped'`. `spawnForPersona` is the one launch entry point and allows one in-flight launch per persona key: a second call for a key whose launch is still running joins it and gets its result, and `isLaunchInFlight(key)` reports whether one is running (a launch call only: it answers false while only the launch's dialog approver runs); `whenLaunchSettled(key)` resolves once that launch has settled, whatever its outcome (never rejects, starts nothing, does not wait for the approver), for a persona teardown. `readPersonaRowState(key)` is the UNAVAILABLE retry timer's row read (b.jg5 SRJ-303, SRJ-115): one `status` call for `cscb_<key>` through `withOutageDetection`, with no findMissing sweep and no other call; it answers an `UnavailableRetryRowRead` (`unavailable-retry.ts`): `state`, the row's state as agent-director reports it, or `absent` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_ROW_ABSENT`) for `ErrSpawnNotFound` (by name, `hasAdErrorName`), and, on a `pending` row only, `launchStartedAt`, the result's raw launch start (`pendingLaunchStartOf`; absent when it shows none). The registry installer `setLiveRowSequenceRegistry(registry)` (b.jg5 SRJ-706; production: `main()`'s one registry, installed before the start pass; test seam `_resetLiveRowSequenceRegistry()`) holds the server's registry. Its start entry, `startLiveRowSequence(request)`, the one way a starter reaches it (a step-2 entry is the same call with entry step 2), answers the registry's answer, or `not-installed` (`LIVE_ROW_START_NOT_INSTALLED`) with one line when none is installed; the running query `isLiveRowSequenceRunning(key)` and `stopLiveRowSequence(key, reason)` forward to it (false, and nothing stopped, with none installed). With both a registry and a latch with `addSetObserver` installed, one more set observer on the latch, `stopSequenceOnLatch`, stops a latched persona's running sequence with the reason `latched`, whichever installer ran second. While a sequence runs for a persona that is not latched, `spawnForPersona` answers `sequence-waiting` right after its held gate, before the in-flight join, with one line and no agent-director call, trust patch, reply-guard step, record or arm; `launchSession` maps it to the uncounted `'refused'`, and the start pass counts it neither as failed nor as succeeded. Its production starters are the collision ladder's replacement sites, through the replace step (b.jg5 SRJ-707): a live row there (`pending` included) starts a sequence entering at step 1, with the conversation not kept, the retired-key flag set for a retired key's old life, a launch at the end and the alert context `recovery`; and the ladder's not-resumable step (`spawnNotResumableAtLadder`, b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-611), which starts the same request with the conversation kept when the path holds dead evidence and the re-read finds the row in a known live state other than `pending` (a state CSCB does not know, an unreadable one included, is the lost race). `killPersonaInstanceForTeardown(key, { clock, ref? })` is the persona teardown's kill (b.jg5 SRJ-715, SRJ-110, SRJ-702): `runKillRetry` over one `killPersonaInstance` with `KILL_CONTEXT_TEARDOWN` per try, seeded `KILL_RETRY_SEED_LIVE_UNREAD`, its read between tries one `status` through `withOutageDetection` arming nothing with no own-row step (`readTeardownKillRow`), so it latches nothing, applying only the retired-key entry clear (`decideRetiredEntryClear`, site `persona teardown kill: status read between tries`); no keep-going check, nothing reported after the tries, its lines prefixed `[slack] persona teardown kill for <ref>`. It answers a `PersonaTeardownKillResult`, the retry's result plus `refusals` (`PersonaTeardownKillRefusal`: each CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answer met, `at` `KILL_REFUSAL_AT_KILL` or `KILL_REFUSAL_AT_READ`, `src/checked-kill.ts`), never throws, and makes no delete: no export of the session manager deletes a persona's row; the ladder itself is the private `runPersonaLadder`. The ladder's row guards and the sweep's `cwd` condition go through `compareRowToPersona` (see Server-Managed Startup steps 4 and 5). It also reports `workingDirectoryResolved` (the persona's working directory has a real path, `tryResolveRealPath`) and `cwdCheckDeferred`: the working directory has no real path and the row's `cwd` has none either (absent, missing, a dangling symlink's old target) or equals the configured `working_directory` lexically. For such a row neither the sweep nor the ladder acts on `cwd` grounds (b.av2 SR-6.4): the sweep keeps the row and defers the check to the launch, and the ladder keeps the row and fails the launch. A row whose `cwd` resolves to an existing directory elsewhere isn't deferred: it is still swept or replaced as a `cwd` mismatch, so a persona can't adopt another persona's directory.
