Keyed by persona key (b.av2 SR-6.3): every dependency, the pending-timer map and the in-flight launch set take the key, and log lines name it as `persona=<key>`. `scheduleRestart` takes `opts.humanTrigger`, which clamps the computed delay down to `HUMAN_TRIGGER_DELAY_CEILING = 5` s for explicit inbound-message triggers (never up; counter/cap unchanged) (b.kvq). `RestartDeps.canRestart(key)` (the server passes the relaunch gate) keeps a persona that is not up from being restarted; Auto-Restart step 1 lists when it is asked. `RestartDeps.isSessionAlive(key)` answers a liveness reading (`liveness-reading.ts`), not a boolean: only `dead` reaches the kill and the launch, and on `unknown` (a thrown probe included), at the probe or b.d61's re-probe, the work returns `liveness-unknown` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_LIVENESS_UNKNOWN`) with nothing done or counted and calls the optional arm hook `RestartDeps.armRetryTimer(key)` (b.jg5 SRJ-314; see Auto-Restart step 3). On `pending` at the first probe, whatever the session's connection shows, the work calls the optional `RestartDeps.deferPendingRow(key, reading)` once, with the `pending` reading and its launch start, and returns `pending-deferred` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_PENDING_DEFERRED`) with no reconnect, kill, launch or accounting; a member that throws is logged and changes nothing else. `RestartDeps.launchSession` returns a `LaunchSessionResult`: `true`, `false`, `'skipped'` or `'refused'`; a `'skipped'` launch (the persona is not up, or no longer applied, or a resume's version re-check decided the stop) and a `'refused'` one (its UNAVAILABLE retry timer was armed for it, b.jg5 SRJ-301, SRJ-302) count as neither success nor failure (see Auto-Restart step 5). `RestartDeps.killSession(key, lastRead)` (required; b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-701) is the kill before a relaunch, with `lastRead` the run's last `dead` reading: it answers a `KillSessionResult`, the kill's `KillOutcome` (`checked-kill.ts`, `kill_sent` included) or `KILL_SESSION_NOT_KILLED_GUARD` (`not-killed-guard`) when a guard of the adapter's made no call. The work launches only after a success form or that guard answer; any other answer, a value that is not an outcome and a throw included, ends the work with `latched`, `shutting-down` or `refused` and nothing counted (see Auto-Restart step 4); `latched` answers a CONFLICT or an UNUSABLE NAME and any other non-success after which the persona is latched (b.jg5 SRJ-702; the latched query asked after the kill, a throw counting as latched). Its lines are built by `relaunchAfterKillLine`, `killNotSucceededLine` and `killStopsServerLine`. A fired timer's work runs as one recovery attempt for the persona (`runInAttempt`, `unavailable-retry.ts`). `RestartDeps.serialize` (optional; production passes the lifecycle serializer's `run`) runs a fired timer's work through the per-persona serializer (b.av2 SR-6.6). `cancelRestartTimer(key)` cancels one persona's pending timer for a persona teardown, logging `[slack] Cancelled restart timer for persona=<key>` only when one was pending; work that has already started is left to finish. The restart work answers an outcome (`RestartWorkOutcome`, one of the `RESTART_OUTCOME_*` labels), which the restart timer ignores. `runRestartRetry(key, cwd, isInFlight)` is the UNAVAILABLE retry timer's entry (b.jg5 SRJ-303): the same work through the same serializer, as the same recovery attempt, with `isInFlight(key)` as its first step, the restart cap as its second (at the cap it answers `capped` with no call), and without the restart delay or a restart timer; it answers `RestartRetryOutcome` (the work's outcome, `in-flight` or `not-initialised`). The optional `RestartDeps.isLatched(key)` (b.jg5 SRJ-502; production: the server's latch's `isLatched`) is asked first in the serialized work of a fired timer and of a retry, before every other check and the liveness read: a latched persona gets `latched` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_LATCHED`) with no agent-director call and nothing recorded (a query that throws counts as latched). Right after it, and wherever the work asks the latched gate again, the optional `RestartDeps.isHeld(key)` (b.jg5 SRJ-207, SRJ-303; production: the server's `ErrInvalidFlags` hold's `isHeld`) answers `held` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_HELD`) the same way for a persona held on `ErrInvalidFlags` (a query that throws counts as held), and `scheduleRestart` arms no timer for one. Right after the held gate the work asks the optional `RestartDeps.isLiveRowSequenceRunning(key)` (b.jg5 SRJ-706, SRJ-303; production: the session manager's running query): while it answers true, or throws (taken as running), the work makes no agent-director call, records nothing, adds nothing toward the cap and answers `sequence-waiting` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_SEQUENCE_WAITING`), for a fired timer, a retry and a human-triggered restart alike; the retry entry's in-flight check, which counts a running sequence, answers first there. The work asks the latch again after the liveness read (right after the second up check; the probe's own read can latch the persona, b.jg5 SRJ-512, SRJ-513), right after an escalate-dead reconnect answer (`ReconnectEscalateDead`, `{ outcome: 'escalate-dead', deadEvidence }`, carrying the verdict the adapter swept with as a `CarriedDeadEvidence`, a type-only import, whose `evidence` flag is all the restart module decides the kill from (its `source` only names the verdict in `relaunchWithoutKillLine`), and only the session manager's builder makes such a value; a bare `'escalate-dead'` carries none; after a `dead` re-probe the persona is killed before the relaunch only after a verdict that is dead evidence, and any other verdict relaunches with no kill and logs `relaunchWithoutKillLine`; the relaunch passes the verdict to `RestartDeps.launchSession(key, cwd, sessionId?, deadEvidence?)`; b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611) before its re-probe (that reconnect's findMissing sweep can latch the persona, b.jg5 SRJ-120), right after the re-probe (whose own read can latch it too), and once more immediately before the kill, answering the same with the same line, so a persona that latched during the work's own awaits gets no reconnect and no kill; it asks the sequence gate again at each of those points, right before the launch and after a launch that answered `'refused'`, answering `sequence-waiting` when a sequence runs (a launch outside the serializer can start one at a collision ladder replacement site); and so does a launch that answers `'skipped'` because the persona latched at it (see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)). The optional `RestartDeps.slowRecovery` (`RestartSlowRecoveryObserver`: `noteLive`, `noteDead`, `noteInstallGone`, `noteOther(key, reason)` with `RESTART_SLOW_RECOVERY_OTHER_VERDICT`, `RESTART_SLOW_RECOVERY_OTHER_PENDING_PROBE` or `RESTART_SLOW_RECOVERY_OTHER_PENDING_REPROBE` (`SlowRecoveryOtherReason`); b.jg5 SRJ-610; production: the slow-recovery tracker) is told each run's readings and verdicts once the gates after each probe pass; it changes nothing in the run, and a note that throws is logged (see Auto-Restart step 3, **Slow recovery**). The re-probe's lines are exported (`reprobeDeadLine`, `reprobeLiveLine`, `reprobePendingLine`, `reprobeUnknownLine`, and `reprobeUnhandledLine` for the fallback on a reading kind none of the cases names). The key counts as active (`isRestartPendingOrActive`) while a fired timer's or a retry's work runs or waits for its turn; `activeLaunches` keeps a count per key, so one work that ends never hides another. `recordLaunchResultOutsideRestartWork(key, launched)` (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-113, SRJ-602) records the result of a launch that does not come back through `launchSession` (the live-row sequence's final launch) as the restart work records its own: a success resets the persona's failure count and cap latch; a failure is counted, with the line `[slack] Launch failed for persona=<key> — counted (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-113, SRJ-602)` and, once per episode at the cap, the cap line and the installed `onCapReached` (none before `initRestart`). Its caller decides which results count; it answers `launched`, `counted-failure` or `capped`. See Auto-Restart, UNAVAILABLE retry.
    ├── liveness-reading.ts     b.jg5 SRJ-314 (C12) the four liveness readings and the row-state mapper. Pure: no I/O, clock, module state or log line. `LIVENESS_LIVE`, `LIVENESS_PENDING`, `LIVENESS_DEAD`, `LIVENESS_UNKNOWN` (`LIVENESS_KINDS`, type `LivenessKind`); a reading (`LivenessReading`) is an object whose `kind` names it, with the frozen values `LIVENESS_READING_*`. `livenessReadingForState(state)` maps a row state: `pending` → `pending`, another state in `AGENT_DIRECTOR_LIVE_STATES` → `live`, one in `AGENT_DIRECTOR_DEAD_STATES` (`ended`, `missing`) → `dead` carrying that state, anything else → `unknown`. `livenessKindOf(reading)` answers a reading's kind, and `unknown` for any value that is not a reading; it never throws. A `pending` reading (`PendingLivenessReading`) carries `launchStartedAt`, the row's launch start raw as agent-director wrote it, when the `status` result showed one (b.jg5 SRJ-115); nothing here parses or ages it. `pendingLaunchStartOf(result)` reads it from a `status` result (a non-empty `launch_started_at` on a `pending` row only, else absent); `pendingLivenessReading(launchStartedAt?)` builds the frozen reading (`LIVENESS_READING_PENDING` when there is none); `livenessReadingForStatus(result)` is `livenessReadingForState` over the result's state, with a `pending` reading carrying the launch start; `launchStartOfReading(reading)` answers the launch start a probe's answer carries. A `dead` reading (`DeadLivenessReading`) may carry `source` `LIVENESS_DEAD_SOURCE_INSTALL_GONE` (`install-gone`): `LIVENESS_READING_DEAD_INSTALL_GONE` is the `dead` reading from `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, which reads no row, and `isInstallGoneDeadReading(reading)` tells it apart from a row read's `dead`, for the slow-recovery count (b.jg5 SRJ-610). A row read's `dead` reading carries what it read as `rowRead` (`DeadRowRead`: `ended`, `missing`, or `no-row` for `ErrSpawnNotFound`; `LIVENESS_READING_DEAD_ENDED`, `LIVENESS_READING_DEAD_MISSING`, `LIVENESS_READING_DEAD_NO_ROW`), so the restart path's kill can record the state its run last read in a latch (b.jg5 SRJ-501); `LIVENESS_READING_DEAD` is the `dead` reading with no row state read. `deadRowReadOf(reading)` answers a `dead` reading's `rowRead` (none for any other answer) and `deadLivenessReading(rowRead?)` builds the frozen reading. None of them throws. The `status` result is typed through `ad-phase1-types.ts` (a type-only import). `AGENT_DIRECTOR_LIVE_STATES` and `AGENT_DIRECTOR_PENDING_STATE` live here; `session-manager.ts` re-exports the live set. Only `dead` leads to a kill and a launch; see Auto-Restart step 3.
    ├── backoff.ts              SR-25 pure per-persona session-restart failure counter, keyed by persona key — `nextBackoffDelay` (min(base·2^n, 900 s)), `isAtCap`, `shouldNotifyCap` once-per-episode latch, `recordFailure`/`recordSuccess`, and `forgetFailures(key)` (the same reset as `recordSuccess`, for a persona teardown; not a success). No imports, no timers/I/O; in-process state, lost on server restart by design. Also exports the stateless `doublingBackoffDelay(base, priorAttempts, ceiling)` = min(base·2^priorAttempts, ceiling), unit-agnostic and finite for any attempt count; `nextBackoffDelay` delegates to it with the 900 s ceiling and returns the same values as before. The persona Slack-unreachable policy (`persona-retry-schedule.ts`) is also per persona but reuses only the arithmetic: it counts different failures and shares no state with the session-restart counters. The UNAVAILABLE retry timer (`unavailable-retry.ts`) is the other caller of `doublingBackoffDelay` outside this module: it keeps its own refusal count and never reads or writes the failure counter or the cap latch.
    ├── unavailable-retry.ts    b.jg5 SRJ-302 to SRJ-306 (and SRJ-301's code line) per-persona retry timer for a persona that agent-director refuses (UNAVAILABLE). `createUnavailableRetryController({ log, action, clock?, onRetryFire? })` builds one controller (`onRetryFire(key, firedAt)` observes every retry before its action, a skipped one included; production binds the `tmux-unresponsive` onset check at a retry. `onStopped(key, reason)` observes every real stop of a timer, after its stopped line and before its hand-off, a timer dropped because its re-arm failed included (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_RUN_FAILED`), but not a no-op stop, a failed first arm or a pending-only stop that yielded; production binds the condition's `cancelAlert`, then the unclassified-error episodes' `retryStopped` (b.jg5 SRJ-313), each isolated so one that throws does not skip the other. `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_TERMINAL_STOPS` names the stop reasons after which that alert check is never armed again: torn down, not applied, shutdown), which keeps at most one timer per persona key; clock and timers are injected (`SYSTEM_PERSONA_CONNECTION_CLOCK` by default), each controller holds its own entries, and no persona state is kept at module scope (the attempt context below holds only running attempts), so nothing spans two personas or two controllers. Nothing is armed, read or logged at import or creation. The controller's exports: `arm(key, cause)` (full mode; answers true when the persona has a timer after the call, false after `close` or when the first timer could not be set), `armPendingOnly(key)`, `conditionEnded(key, condition, reading?)` (called by the `tmux-unresponsive` condition's end and by each real clear of the `tmux-unavailable` outage, through the outage state's cleared-flag observer; both bound in `main()`), `stop(key, reason)`, `stopAll(reason)`, `close(reason)` (the server's shutdown: stops every persona and refuses every later `arm`), and the read-only `view(key)` (its phase, due time, wait, refusal count, causes, `mode` and `lastRow`), `isArmed`, `armedKeys` and `whenRunSettled`. `createFullModeRetryAction(deps)` is the server's retry action for both modes, over `runRestartRetry` and `readPersonaRowState` (`FullModeRetryDeps.readRow`, answering an `UnavailableRetryRowRead`: the row's `state` and, on a `pending` row, its raw `launchStartedAt`; the action acts on the state only). Its optional `isLatched(key)` (b.jg5 SRJ-303, SRJ-305; production: the server's latch's `isLatched`) stops a latched persona's timer before any call, in either mode, with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED` (`the persona is latched`, not a terminal stop), the same stop the latch's hold uses; a query that throws counts as latched (one line naming what it threw). Its optional `isHeld(key)` (b.jg5 SRJ-207, SRJ-303, SRJ-305; production: the server's `ErrInvalidFlags` hold's `isHeld`), asked right after it, stops a held persona's timer the same way with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_HELD` (`the persona is held on ErrInvalidFlags`, not a terminal stop), the stop the hold's set reaction uses, and a full-mode retry whose work answers `held` stops with it; a query that throws counts as held (one line naming what it threw). Its optional `isSessionConnected`, `hasSessionStream` and `endTmuxUnresponsive(key, reading)` let a retry that finds the persona healthy end its `tmux-unresponsive` condition ([The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310)) and, as `main()` binds the hook, clear its `tmux-unavailable` outage with the same reading (b.jg5 SRJ-311, SRJ-312); absent, a retry ends and clears nothing. `main()` builds the controller with it on the system clock and installs it as the outage state's trigger sink before the start pass. The waits come from `doublingBackoffDelay` over `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_BASE_S` (30 s) and `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CEILING_S` (300 s); stop reasons and again-reasons are the `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_*` and `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_AGAIN_*` labels. The live-row sequence arms with its four causes, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_SEQUENCE_NOT_JUDGED` (`sequence-not-judged`), `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_SEQUENCE_ENDED` (`sequence-ended-without-launch`), `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_REUSE_COLLISION` (`reuse-collision`, a reuse spawn's collision at its final launch) and `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_LOST_RACE` (`spawn-not-resumable-lost-race`, its final `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotResumable` whose re-read found a lost race), none ever counted ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)). The collision ladder arms `reuse-collision` too, on a reuse spawn's second collision (in the one re-run of get-then-act the first gave), and `spawn-not-resumable-lost-race` on a lost race: a resume's `ErrSpawnNotResumable` whose re-read found no reason to act, or a resume site's replacement whose re-read found the row in a known live state other than `pending`, or in a state CSCB does not know, on a path with no dead evidence (b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-609), both through the outage state's site entries (`reportReuseCollisionAtSite`, `reportLostRaceAtSite`) and never counted. Behaviour (modes, the retry action, the outcome map, stop rules, condition ends) is in Auto-Restart, [UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305) and [Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306); every line it logs is in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages. **What arms a timer (b.jg5 SRJ-301).** A launch attempt (a run of a persona's collision ladder, whoever starts it) and a recovery attempt (a run of its restart work, adapters included) run through `runInAttempt(key, 'launch' | 'recovery', fn)`, an attempt context carried on `AsyncLocalStorage` across the attempt's awaits and timers; it holds only the running attempts, never a persona's state between them. Attempts nest (a restart's relaunch is a launch attempt inside the recovery attempt), and the innermost one for the key records the error. A new attempt links to the nearest attempt still running, and a continuation that outlives its attempt (a timer the attempt set) is outside it, so an attempt started after another has closed is not nested in it. `fn` is handed an `AttemptView` of its own attempt (`key`, `kind`, and a live `lastError`: the last agent-director error met in that attempt, not in one nested in it, with its verb, its cause kind and whether it armed); `isInsideAttempt(key)` reads the context. `runOutsideAttempts(fn)` runs `fn`, and everything it starts, outside every attempt (`AsyncLocalStorage.exit`): the registry starts the dialog approver through it, so the approver is part of no launch or recovery attempt (b.jg5 SRJ-401). `runDetachedRecoveryAttempt(key, fn)` runs `fn` as a recovery attempt of its own for the persona, outside the caller's (`runOutsideAttempts`, then `runInAttempt`): the live-row sequence registry's attempt runner (b.jg5 SRJ-706), so an error a sequence meets arms by the attempt rule there and never marks its starter's launch refused. `reportAttemptError(key, value, verb, sink)` is the one reporting step, reached through `reportAgentDirectorError` in `outage-state.ts`; its second half, `reportAttemptCause(key, cause, verb, sink)`, takes a cause the caller decided itself, under the same context rule (the outage state's site entry `reportUnclassifiedAtSite` passes the `unclassified` cause for the resume path's `ErrInvalidFlags`, the reconnect's, and a kill's outcome of a class the kill has no row for inside an attempt). The arming predicate `unavailableRetryCauseFor(value, verb)`, over the classifier, answers the cause, in this order: `unavailable` for an UNAVAILABLE outcome from any verb, `kill-failed` when that outcome is `ErrTmuxKillFailed` (told apart by name through `hasAdErrorName`), `environment` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_ENVIRONMENT`) for an ENVIRONMENT answer (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`) from any verb, `kill` and the read verbs included, `config` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_CONFIG`) for a CONFIG answer (`ErrConfigMalformed`) from any verb, `kill` and the read verbs included, `unclassified` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_UNCLASSIFIED`, b.jg5 SRJ-313) for an UNCLASSIFIED answer from any declared verb but `status`, `get` and `list` (a call with no known verb arms nothing; `ErrInvalidFlags` is STATE here), `read-error` for any other error from `status`, `get` or `list` except `ErrSpawnNotFound` (each site keeps its meaning) and an UNUSABLE_NAME answer, and nothing otherwise. The `environment` and `config` causes (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_ANY_CONTEXT_CAUSES`) arm in any context (b.jg5 SRJ-311, SRJ-316), so a persona that met a CONFIG answer is retried whatever `session_restart_delay` and `health_check_interval` are: inside an attempt for `key`, inside another persona's attempt, or outside every attempt (the health tick, the permission poller and click handler, the JSONL safeguard, the dialog approver). A persona teardown's kill, each try and each `status` read between its tries, is the one call outside an attempt that arms nothing: it passes the wrapper's `armsNothing` option (`outage-state.ts`; b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-715, hatch A3). The start sweep (`reconcileOrphans`) calls agent-director outside the outage wrappers, so it reports nothing and arms nothing. A bounded kill retry inside an attempt (b.jg5 SRJ-702, `retryPersonaKill`) arms once per retry, not once per try: each try's UNAVAILABLE answer is held back (the wrapper's `deferUnavailableReport`), and only the outcome that stands is reported, once, through `reportDeferredUnavailable` (so `kill-failed` for an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` that stands); a try's other answers are reported at once, as they stand at once. Every other cause arms only inside an attempt for `key`; outside one it arms nothing. A stray `environment` or `config` arm (a torn-down persona, one not in the applied configuration or not up) stops at its first retry through the pre-call checks, with no agent-director call. One armed during a persona teardown (by a launch in flight, or an earlier call) does not wait for that: the teardown stops the persona's timer again once its launch in flight settled and once more after its kill ([Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65) steps 3 and 8; the kill itself arms none), which matters for a destructive modify's old half, whose key stays applied and would pass those checks. A cause goes once to the trigger sink (`UnavailableRetryTriggerSink`, which the controller implements through `arm`, and through `armPendingOnly` for the sink's optional member of that name), so a trigger while armed keeps the due time. Inside an attempt for `key` the innermost attempt records the error as its last. It is recorded as armed only when the sink answers true, that is when the persona has a timer after the call; a sink that answers anything else, or throws, armed nothing, and the step never throws. A launch is marked `refused` (session-manager entry) only from an error recorded as armed. A second arming path is the restart work's arm hook, `RestartDeps.armRetryTimer` (wired in `main()`): it arms the persona's timer with the `read-error` cause (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_READ_ERROR`) on every `unknown` liveness reading at the restart work, the re-probe's included, whatever made it `unknown` (a probe that throws included, which the arming predicate does not arm on; a probe whose own read latched the persona, an UNUSABLE_NAME answer or its own row reading `pending` with no launch start, stops at the work's latch check first and never reaches the hook, b.jg5 SRJ-512, SRJ-513; a CONFIG `status` has already armed the `config` cause through the reporting point, and a trigger while armed keeps the due time); see Auto-Restart, step 3. A third is the health tick's arm hook, `HealthCheckDeps.armRetryTimer` (wired in `main()`): a persona held off on its raised `tmux-unavailable` outage that the tick reads but does not find healthy, with no timer armed (`isRetryArmed` answers false), is armed with the `environment` cause, since a retry that stopped as not up, on a declined launch or on a failed run leaves the flag raised with no timer (see [Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 1). A fourth is the outage state's launch-failure arm (`armPendingOnlyAfterLaunchFailure`, `outage-state.ts`): inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona, a launch's `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` (a plain spawn's, a reuse spawn's or a `resume`'s, in the collision ladder and the live-row sequence alike) arms its timer at once in pending-only mode through the sink's `armPendingOnly` (cause `pending-row`), recording no attempt error, so the counted failure stays counted (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-113, SRJ-301, SRJ-409).
    ├── outage-state.ts         Persona-scoped outage-flag state machine — tracks four orthogonal classes (`ad-unreachable`, `cwd-unreachable`, `tmux-unavailable`, `ad-config-malformed`; the last added by b.jg5 SRJ-316) per persona, keyed by persona key (b.av2 SR-6.3), and emits onset / all-clear notices through an injected `notify(key, text, options?)` hook. Production wires the hook to the per-persona notifier, so each notice goes to that persona's destination and names the persona; the `cwd-unreachable` detail is the persona's working directory. Each notice carries `OutageNoticeOptions` (b.jg5 SRJ-1002, SRJ-1003): `{ outage: { phase: 'onset', classes: [<its class>] } }` or `{ outage: { phase: 'all-clear', classes: [<every class it lists>], allClearOf } }` (`allClearOf(classes)` renders the all-clear of a subset of those classes over the same bad-stretch snapshot, so the notifier can split it), which `main()` passes on to the notifier, so the all-clear of an outage whose onset a persona teardown's window wrote is written the same way, whenever it comes (the `persona-notifier.ts` entry). `server.ts` calls `initOutageState` at boot and, outside dry run, `resetAllToHealthy` with the applied persona keys before any persona is brought up, and a persona teardown calls it with that persona's key alone, once, right before its notice window opens (silent: no all-clear notice; a flag raised in the window is kept past the teardown); AD verb calls run inside `withOutageDetection` / `withSpawnDetection`, which raise a flag on a typed error (`tmux-unavailable` for class ENVIRONMENT, `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`, and `ad-config-malformed` for class CONFIG, `ErrConfigMalformed`, both decided through the classifier) and clear flags by these rules (b.jg5 SRJ-312): `ad-unreachable` and `ad-config-malformed` clear on any successful wrapped call (no error answer clears `ad-config-malformed`, `ErrSpawnNotFound` and GONE included); `tmux-unavailable` clears only when the declared call is tmux-touching (`isTmuxTouchingCall`, see [The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310), Declared verbs) and it succeeded or threw a GONE error, so a successful `status`, `get`, `list`, `find-missing`, `delete`, `get-permission`, `decide` or kill of a row not read live never clears it, because tmux did not answer them; `cwd-unreachable` clears on a successful `withSpawnDetection` call only. A GONE error is still rethrown unchanged. The all-clear is still one per bad stretch: it posts only when a clear empties the persona's flag set. `clearOutageFlag(key, cls, reading?)` tells the optional cleared-flag observer (`OutageStateDeps.onFlagCleared(key, cls, reading?)`) of each real clear, a flag that was raised, after the state change and any all-clear; a throwing observer is swallowed, and `resetAllToHealthy` (boot, teardown) never calls it. `main()` binds it so a `tmux-unavailable` clear calls the retry controller's `conditionEnded(key, 'tmux-unavailable', reading)` (see [Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306), Condition ends). The `reading` is the row reading the clear brought: `pending` from a successful launch call (`isLaunchCall`), the live reading of a health tick or retry that found the persona healthy, and none from any other tmux-touching success or a GONE error. Outside the wrappers, `tmux-unavailable` is cleared only by the health tick's healthy branch ([Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 4) and a retry that finds the persona healthy (the `unavailable-retry.ts` entry); the liveness adapter clears `ad-unreachable` and `ad-config-malformed` only. Every error a wrapped call throws is then reported once, before the rethrow, through `reportAgentDirectorError(key, err, call)` (b.jg5 SRJ-301), which two other places also call: the liveness adapter in `server.ts`, for its bare `status`, and a persona that joined a shared `find-missing` sweep another caller started (`session-manager.ts`), under its own key. The wrappers take the call's verb as a declared argument, `withOutageDetection(key, dir, call, fn)` and `withSpawnDetection(key, dir, call, fn)`, with `call` an `AdCall` (`ad-error-class.ts`: the verb, and for `kill` whether the site kills a row it read live), so typecheck makes every wrapped call site declare it; `fn` gets the plain client. `withOutageDetection` takes an optional fifth argument (`OutageDetectionOptions`): with `armsNothing: { personaConfigured }`, used only by a persona teardown's kill (b.jg5 SRJ-110; hatch A3), the error is not reported (no retry timer is armed, no `tmux-unresponsive` condition is started, nothing reaches the unclassified sink), and an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer raises `tmux-unavailable` or `ad-config-malformed` only when `personaConfigured()` answers true (a throw counts as false); the `ad-unreachable` raise and the clears are unchanged. With `deferUnavailableReport: true`, used only by one try of a bounded kill retry inside an attempt (b.jg5 SRJ-702), an UNAVAILABLE error (by class, `ErrTmuxKillFailed` included) is not reported: it arms no retry timer, starts no `tmux-unresponsive` condition and is not recorded as the attempt's last error; every other value, and a success, is handled as without it. The retry's caller then reports the outcome that stands once through `reportDeferredUnavailable(key, err, call)`, which reports an UNAVAILABLE value through `reportAgentDirectorError` with the kill's declared call and does nothing for any other value (its try reported it); it never throws. The report goes to the optional `triggerSink` in `OutageStateDeps` (see the `unavailable-retry.ts` entry): production installs the server's UNAVAILABLE retry controller there, and with none installed nothing is armed. An ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG error arms the persona's timer in any context (except under `armsNothing`); every other cause arms only inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona. The same step starts or continues the persona's `tmux-unresponsive` condition through the optional `conditionSink` (`TmuxUnresponsiveSink`, production the condition built in `main()`): inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona, for a tmux-touching call whose error the arming predicate answers with the `unavailable` cause (never ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG). The wrappers also end the condition, in any context, when a tmux-touching call succeeds or throws a GONE error, with the reading `pending` when the call was a successful launch (`isLaunchCall`) and no reading otherwise. With no condition sink installed nothing starts or ends. The same step also reports an UNCLASSIFIED error (b.jg5 SRJ-313) once to the optional `unclassifiedSink` (`UnclassifiedErrorSink`, production the unclassified-error episodes built in `main()`, see `persona-episodes.ts`): inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona, from any declared verb, the reads included; outside an attempt, or from a call with no known verb, nothing is reported. `reportAgentDirectorError(key, err, call, { reportUnclassified: false })` keeps a value from that sink with its arming unchanged: the liveness adapter passes it for `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, which keeps its `dead` reading. `reportUnclassifiedAtSite(key, err, call, classification)` is the site entry for an outcome a site classifies itself (the resume path's `ErrInvalidFlags` after its re-check, the reconnect's `send-keys` answering `ErrInvalidFlags`, and a kill in an attempt whose outcome is of a class the kill has no row for, `ErrInvalidFlags` after a re-check that did not stop included: `killPersonaInstance`, b.jg5 SRJ-110): inside an attempt it arms the persona's timer with the `unclassified` cause (`reportAttemptCause`) and reports the outcome with the site's classification; outside one it does nothing. The reuse spawn uses it too, for a name it gives no meaning; its `ErrInvalidFlags` reports nothing here (unless the re-check stops the server, it holds the persona, b.jg5 SRJ-207). `armPendingOnlyAfterLaunchFailure(key)` (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-113, SRJ-409) is the launch-failure arm: for a launch's `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` (a plain spawn's, a reuse spawn's or a `resume`'s; the session manager's `launchFailureResult` calls it) it arms the persona's retry timer at once, with no `get` first, in pending-only mode through the trigger sink's optional `armPendingOnly`, only inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona (a timer already in full mode stays in full mode); it records no attempt error, so the counted failure is never marked refused, answers whether the sink was asked, and never throws. An UNCLASSIFIED outcome touches no flag (`ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` still raises `ad-unreachable` in the wrappers). Flags, notices and the rethrown error are unchanged by any sink. `tmux-unresponsive` is not one of its classes: see [The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310). State mutates before every emit (SR-V-2.x state-before-emit); no timestamps by design. **The `tmux-unavailable` onset (b.jg5 SRJ-1021).** Every site that raises `tmux-unavailable` on an ENVIRONMENT answer (the wrappers, the liveness adapter's bare `status` in `server.ts`, and a joiner of a shared `find-missing` sweep in `session-manager.ts`) raises it through the one entry `raiseTmuxUnavailable(key, err)`, never through `setOutageFlag`. The onset has two forms, chosen there at raise time from the raising error `err`: `tmuxServerChangedOnset()` (the *tmux server changed* text, which sends a human to agent-director's README "Operator actions", says no bot acts on it, and carries no tmux install or repair advice) when `isDifferentTmuxServerError(err)` (`ad-error-class.ts`) holds, and `ONSET_TEMPLATES['tmux-unavailable']` (*tmux unavailable*) otherwise. The choice is not stored: no detail is recorded for the flag, so the bad-stretch history and the all-clear (`ALL_CLEAR_TEMPLATE`, naming `tmux-unavailable` with no detail) are the existing ones, and agent-director's description never reaches Slack. The same-flag dedupe holds: the first raising error of a bad stretch picks the onset, and a second error of either form while the flag is raised posts nothing. Either form changes nothing else: no kill, delete or launch follows from it, and the flag clears by the rules above. `setOutageFlag` and `raiseTmuxUnavailable` share one private raise step (`raiseFlag`), so state still mutates before the emit. **The `ad-config-malformed` outage (b.jg5 SRJ-316, SRJ-1018).** agent-director refuses its config file: a CONFIG answer (`ErrConfigMalformed`, recognised by name under the interim rule, see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)) from any wrapped call, in or out of an attempt, from the liveness adapter's bare `status`, or from a joiner's shared `find-missing` sweep raises it through the one entry `raiseAdConfigMalformed(key, err)`, never through `setOutageFlag`. It is handled as `ad-unreachable` is: the same destination, one onset per episode and the one all-clear. The flag is set first, then one raise line is logged (built from the classification's fields only, `describeAdErrorClassification`), then the onset (`adConfigMalformedOnset(err)`, `ONSET_TEMPLATES['ad-config-malformed']`) is posted, quoting the classifier's rendered message (redacted, one line, capped at `MAX_LOGGED_MESSAGE_LENGTH`) with Slack's control characters escaped after the cap (`escapeSlackControlCharacters`, `slack-text-escape.ts`), so a description cannot mention `@channel` or a user and no entity is cut; the raise line quotes the same message redacted but unescaped. A value with no description drops the quoting sentence. The onset goes out through a private isolating step (`notifyIsolated`): a `notify` that throws, or returns a promise that rejects, is logged once (`[slack] outage-state: onset notice for persona=<key> failed: <error> — the flag stays raised; the notice counts as posted`) and the onset counts as posted, so it is not posted again this episode and `raiseAdConfigMalformed` never throws. A wrapper raising it from its catch block therefore still reports the CONFIG value through `reportAgentDirectorError` (arming the retry timer) and rethrows that value, not the notify failure. No detail is ever recorded for the class, so the all-clear lists it bare and agent-director's text appears only in the onset. A second CONFIG answer while the flag is raised logs and posts nothing. It clears on any successful wrapped call and, at the liveness adapter, on a `status` success or `ErrSpawnNotFound` (each shows agent-director loaded its config and read its store); a real clear logs one line before any all-clear. `version` and `help` never clear it: CSCB never wraps them, and the version re-check touches no flag. Its clear stops no timer: the cleared-flag observer is told of it, but `main()` passes only `tmux-unavailable` clears to the retry controller. No action follows the outage: the site that met the answer refuses (see [Refusals at the launch and recovery sites](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)), and the retry timer retries the persona. CSCB's own read of `~/.agent-director/config.toml` (`ad-settings.ts`) never raises it; only agent-director's answers do. **Class order.** `OUTAGE_CLASS_ORDER` is the exported, frozen stable order (`ad-unreachable`, `cwd-unreachable`, `tmux-unavailable`, `ad-config-malformed`) in which the all-clear lists the resolved classes; tests iterate it. `_resetOutageState` is test-only. Its classes are outage flags only: the once-per-episode latches of the per-persona notice kinds live in `persona-episodes.ts`, which holds no `OutageClass`, except that the `ad-config-malformed` kind's latch is this module's `ad-config-malformed` flag.

The reason (`LatchRecoveryReason`, one `LATCH_RECOVERY_REASON_KIND_*` kind each) is one of five: the row reads a state (`latchRecoveryReasonRowReads(state)`), the row is gone, a retry of the refused operation was not refused, the row finished and a relaunch was not refused, or cleared by hand (the frozen `LATCH_RECOVERY_REASON_*` values); `latchRecoveryReasonText(reason)` renders it from `LATCH_RECOVERY_REASON_ROW_READS_HEAD` and `LATCH_RECOVERY_REASON_TEXTS`, the state rendered and escaped as a quoted description is. The post goes through the episodes' sink, never straight to Slack, and the observer reads no other notice's latch, so no not-connected notice already posted (b.f2b's `unproven-idle` or `blocked-on-prompt`, under `notConnectedNoticeRaised`) holds it back. A same-case set runs them too, since a refusal met while the persona was already latched may have armed its timer again. `bindConflictLatchHolds(latch, holds, log)` adds it to a latch and answers its removal. Observers run in the order they were added, and `main()` binds the holds before the notice, so every hold is done before the notice is posted (see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)). No module-scope state, no agent-director call and nothing run at import or creation, so a test builds a fresh instance and needs no reset seam. `main()` in `server.ts` builds the server's one instance, binds its holds and then its CONFLICT notice to it, and installs it in the session manager (`setConflictLatch`) and as the latched query of the restart work, the retry action and the health tick (see [Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1)), keeping no module-scope handle to it. The persona teardown (`runTeardown`, `persona-lifecycle.ts`) calls `forget` for its key through the injected `forgetConflictLatch`, after the launch in flight settled and right before it forgets the persona's notice episodes, which ends the CONFLICT episode too (b.jg5 SRJ-504); a process that ends drops every latch. Nothing else re-checks or clears a latch. See [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104).

    ├── row-read-rules.ts       b.jg5 SRJ-114 / SRJ-501 / SRJ-513 / SRJ-807 the pure row-read rule over one read of a persona's own agent-director row: one rule, two latch decisions and one entry-clear decision. `LATCHING_LIVENESS_NOTE` (`provenance_conflict`, satisfies `LivenessNote`) is the one note that latches; `isLatchingLivenessNote(note)` is exact equality with it (no prefix, substring or case-folded match); `isPersonaOwnRow(row, key)` is true when the row's `claude_instance_id` is exactly `cscb_<key>`. `decideOwnRowRead({ key, row, configured, retiredMarked })` (`OwnRowReadInput`, `retiredMarked` optional and absent counting as false; `RowReadRow`: `claude_instance_id`, `state`, optional `liveness_note` and `launch_started_at`, the fields a `get` result, a `list` row and a `status` result given the id `cscb_<key>` by its caller carry) answers a `RowReadDecision` whose optional `latch` (`RowReadLatchDecision`) is set only when `configured` is true and the row is the key's own, and then the first that holds decides: a row that reads `pending` with no launch start (`isPendingWithNoLaunchStart`, `pending-row.ts`) answers `ROW_READ_LAUNCH_START_NOT_RECORDED` (case `launch-start-not-recorded`, refused operation `none`, state `pending`), a latching note included; a row whose note is exactly the latching one answers case `conflicting-labels`, refused operation `bring-up` and the row's state through `latchRowStateRead`.     ├── crontable.ts            cscb_cron parser — `parseCrontable(text)` turns crontable text (5-field cron expression + prompt-file path + optional comma-separated persona list, each entry a persona name or key, space-delimited) into in-memory `{schedules, errors}` records. Pure module, no I/O, no timers (backoff.ts precedent); expression validity is delegated to the bundled zero-dependency `croner` library. Tolerant parse (PD-6): `#` comments and blank lines are skipped silently, each bad line becomes a structured parse-error record `{lineNumber, rawLine, reason class}` for the caller to log while sibling lines survive, and it never throws for content reasons. Duplicate lines are both kept; targets are kept verbatim, duplicates included, and are neither resolved nor validated here — name-to-key resolution and deduplication happen at fire time in `cron-dispatch.ts`. Each schedule carries identity `cscb-cron:<prompt-file-basename-without-extension>` (PD-1), the verbatim prompt path, and a `targets` union (all-bots marker vs. explicit list of targets as written). Parse-error reason classes keep their channel-list names (`wildcard-channel-list` for a literal `*`, `malformed-channel-list`, `path-with-spaces`).
    ├── cron-bootstrap.ts       cscb_cron boot-time crontable creator — `ensureCrontableExists(path)` guarantees a crontable file exists, returning `created` / `already-exists` / `failed(cause)`. Exclusive-create only: writes the template header with `{ flag: 'wx' }` when the path is absent, never write-then-rename and never mkdir's a missing parent. EEXIST is swallowed as `already-exists` (a human or another bot winning the create race is normal, not an error); a pre-existing file is left untouched byte-for-byte. Non-EEXIST errors surface as a `failed` outcome — never thrown, never `process.exit` — so a bad path can't crash boot. The module itself never logs; callers own log level and wording — `cron-scheduler.ts` uses it on both paths: an INFO line for the first-install create at `start()`, and, after a runtime deletion, a distinct re-created INFO line following the latched vanish WARN. D-Q1 invariant: this create is the server's ONLY write to the crontable, ever — the server never rewrites, reorders, normalizes, or prunes its content. The `#`-comment template header is exported as the shared constant `CRONTABLE_TEMPLATE_HEADER` (consumed by E6 bot discoverability); its documented line format tracks `crontable.ts`'s parser.
    ├── cron-log.ts             cscb_cron log writer — append-only writer for the dedicated cron log at `cron_log_path`. `createCronLog(path)` returns a handle whose `outcome`/`summary`/`info`/`warn` methods funnel through one internal append: per-(fire,target) outcome entries whose target field holds the target as written in the crontable, per-fire summary lines, info lines, and warn lines (the latter two are line kinds, not outcome classes). Write failures are swallowed (one `[slack] cron-log` console.error, fd dropped, self-heals next append) — they never propagate into dispatch. See [cron.log](#cronlog-cron_log_path). Pure half (record types + line formatting) is I/O-free.
    ├── cron-dispatch.ts        cscb_cron fire/delivery path — `createCronDispatcher({port, cronLog, cronTablePath, resolveTarget})` returns a handle whose `fire(schedule)` delivers ONE matched schedule; it logs every outcome and never throws. The scheduler's tick (`cron-scheduler.ts`) is the only caller — it hands the minute's matches to the dispatcher. The module imports nothing from server.ts, holds no timer, and reads no crontable. Each schedule delivers independently: every match becomes its own `/interject` POST and its own outcome line, so N schedules matching the same minute produce N separate messages. Fixed internal shape (E4's seam, do not collapse): resolve-targets → all-bots deferral branch → target-origin-agnostic per-target delivery. Targets resolve from the schedule's explicit persona list at FIRE time (`resolveDeliveryTargets`, pure): each written target goes through the injected `resolveTarget` (name or key → persona key, so a changed persona set applies at the next fire), then targets are deduplicated on the value to be POSTed in first-seen order — a persona named twice, by name or key, is delivered once; a target that resolves to nothing is POSTed as written, once per distinct text, so the handler answers 404. Each delivery target keeps the first-written text as its log target field. The all-bots marker is deferred to E4 — no read, no POST, one `fanout-deferred` outcome (target `-`) plus a `delivered=0 failed=0` summary (the target set is undefined until E4, and a no-match minute logs nothing, so 0/0 cannot read as quiet success). The prompt file is resolved and fresh-read every fire (never cached): leading `~` via `config.ts` `expandTilde`, absolute as-is, relative anchored to the CRONTABLE's directory — a deliberate divergence from system cron's $HOME convention so a prompt can colocate as `prompts/foo.md` and stay stable (E6's format reference carries this rationale). Missing → `prompt-missing`, unreadable → `prompt-unreadable` (errno), each target `-`, then a `failed=<targets>` summary and no POST. D-Q5 skip-never-truncate: the oversize predicate is UTF-8 byte length of the EXACT serialized `{persona, message, sender}` body > 32768 (`INTERJECT_BODY_CAP_BYTES`, imported from `interject.ts`), byte-identical to the /interject handler's own check — the measured string IS the sent string, so a 413 is structurally impossible; over-cap targets log `prompt-oversize` (size, cap) and are skipped, never truncated, never POSTed. Under-cap targets POST the measured body to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/interject` AS-IS (decision 7 — no extraction, no internal call) with `sender` = schedule identity (D-Q4 — else senderLabel defaults to `interject` and fires are indistinguishable from peer-bot traffic). Status → outcome: 200 `delivered`, 503 `no-session` (decision 1 — NO retry, no queue, no scheduleRestart), 404 `unknown-persona`, else/network error `http-error`. Sequential loop attempts every target; exactly one outcome line per (fire,target) plus one per-fire summary (`failed` = targets whose intended delivery did not happen). Known limitation (recorded, unsolved): a single non-loopback `bind` leaves no loopback listener, so every fire fails connection-refused → `http-error`; no loopback detection is added.
    ├── cron-scheduler.ts       cscb_cron once-per-minute dispatch tick — `createCronScheduler({dispatcher, cronLog, cronTablePath, clock?})` returns a `start`/`stop`/`tick` handle whose single self-re-arming minute-aligned `setTimeout` chain (NOT `setInterval` — ticks are serialized so the hot-reload step mutates the table only between whole passes) is the ONLY code path that dispatches schedules (decision 8). `start()` runs the crontable bootstrap FIRST (this `start()` is the sole `ensureCrontableExists` caller), performs the initial read + parse through the same shared load path the tick's reload uses (parse errors → `parse-error` outcome lines, target `-`), compiles each schedule's croner pattern once per load (queried, never started — no callback, so it schedules nothing itself), writes exactly ONE `scheduler started, N schedules loaded` info line (PD-4 outage-window marker), then arms the tick; `start()` is failure-isolated and never throws out to the server. Each tick first re-loads the crontable if its `(mtimeMs, size)` differs from the last successful load — no watcher, no dirty flag — then stamps the current wall-clock minute and skips the whole pass unless it is strictly after the last-ticked minute (monotonic guard — a backwards clock jump must not re-fire fired minutes), matches every in-memory schedule against that minute in server-local time via croner (DST is the library's, D-Q3), and hands each match, in crontable line order, to the dispatcher. No catch-up: a tick fires only the minute observed at its start; an overrun minute is simply skipped, and a no-match minute does nothing and logs nothing. The at-most-once `Map<schedule instance, epoch minute>` is a LOGGED ASSERTION, not the mechanism (decision 8): keyed on the compiled-schedule instance (NOT raw line text), so two identical operator lines are distinct schedules that EACH fire (PD-6) — only the SAME loaded schedule reappearing twice in one pass is skipped and shouted as a `SCHEDULER BUG` info line (an info line kind, deliberately NOT an outcome class, so it never pollutes the `grep http-error` triage view). NO rate cap / backlog cap / busy-detection / queue-depth check of any kind (owner gate answers 1-2). `stop()` is idempotent and cancels the pending timer.
    ├── health-check.ts         Periodic liveness poller — checks every applied persona on a timer via client.status. The work list comes from `HealthCheckDeps.getPersonas()` (production: the pure `buildPersonaWorkList(config, include?)`, persona key → working directory, one entry per persona however many channels it lists, filtered by `include`; the server passes the relaunch gate, so a persona that is not up, whether its Slack connection is not serving or its bring-up is broken or retrying, is left out of the tick); streaks, guard calls and the `cwd-unreachable` flag are keyed by persona key (b.av2 SR-6.3), and log lines name it as `persona=<key>`. `HealthCheckDeps.isSessionAlive(key)` answers a liveness reading (`liveness-reading.ts`), not a boolean: `dead` schedules a restart at once, and `unknown` (a thrown probe included) skips the persona for the tick, clearing its streak and arming nothing (b.jg5 SRJ-314). It schedules recovery for dead sessions AND for sessions that are alive (`live` or `pending`) but not deliverable — either MCP-disconnected (b.9a7) OR connected-but-streamless (b.9cj — `connected === true` in the registry while the SDK has silently dropped the `_GET_stream` map entry, probed via `HealthCheckDeps.hasSessionStream`). Only `live` is ever counted healthy: a `pending` row connected with its stream takes the not-deliverable path too, with no not-connected notice (b.jg5 SRJ-314). Both non-deliverable cases require two consecutive failing ticks before acting, a shared false-positive guard for the freshly-launched window; routes all through `scheduleRestart` (restart.ts then reconnects vs. relaunches per case); skips personas at the failure cap via `HealthCheckDeps.isAtCap` (SR-25.3/25.4), including the reconnect path. A persona with a no-attempt reason (`noAttemptReason`: it is latched, through the optional `isLatched`, wired in production to the server's latch, b.jg5 SRJ-502; it is held on `ErrInvalidFlags`, through the optional `isHeld`, wired in production to the server's hold, b.jg5 SRJ-207; work in flight; or its `tmux-unavailable` outage raised; b.jg5 SRJ-315) is still read, but the tick never calls `scheduleRestart` or `notifyNotConnected` for it; `latched` is asked again right after the tick's own read, which can latch the persona (b.jg5 SRJ-512). b.f2b adds five optional dependencies, all wired in production: `isLaunchInFlight` (true while anything is in flight for the persona, such as a parked start launch, a running live-row sequence or a running dialog approver; production binds the server's "in flight for P" binding `isPersonaWorkInFlight`, which the lost-message routing's read gate shares and which is built from the retry timer's "blocks a retry" binding; a no-attempt reason), `hasPendingWorkingRowEvidence` (schedule on the first undeliverable tick while the reconnect adapter gathers idle evidence for a `working` row), `isAutoRestartDisabled` with `notifyNotConnected(key, cause)` (with `session_restart_delay` 0, report an alive persona it would reconnect through the not-connected notice, worded for a `disconnected` or a `streamless` session), and `endNotConnectedEpisode` (end the persona's episode on every tick that finds it deliverable). b.jg5 SRJ-310 adds a sixth, wired in production: `endTmuxUnresponsive(key)`, called on the same healthy branch, which ends the persona's `tmux-unresponsive` condition with the tick's `live` reading. That branch then clears the persona's `tmux-unavailable` outage itself (`clearOutageFlag` with the `live` reading, no new dep; b.jg5 SRJ-312). b.jg5 SRJ-308 adds two more, wired in production: `now()`, the clock the tick's start time is read from as its body starts (production: the notice episodes' clock; absent, `Date.now`), and `onTickEnd(tickStartedAt)`, called once when each tick body ends, after all of its per-persona work and however the body ends, bound to the condition's `onsetAtTick(tickStartedAt)` (a throw is logged and changes nothing else). b.jg5 SRJ-311 adds two more, wired in production: `isRetryArmed(key)` (the retry controller's `isArmed`) and `armRetryTimer(key)` (the controller's `arm` with the `environment` cause). For a persona held off on `tmux-unavailable` that the tick reads but does not find healthy (`dead`, `pending`, disconnected or streamless), the tick arms its retry timer when `isRetryArmed` answers exactly `false`, with one line, and still makes no attempt of its own (`armMissingRetryTimer`; see [Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 1); with either member absent it arms nothing. b.jg5 SRJ-610 adds one more, wired in production: `resetSlowRecoveryCount(key)` (the slow-recovery tracker's `noteHealthy`), called last on the healthy branch, which resets the persona's slow-recovery count and leaves an open episode open. `forgetDisconnectedStreak(key)` drops one persona's disconnected streak at once, for a persona teardown.

Write (the exact text `true` or `false`, atomic, creating the directory), read (`true` only for `true` with at most one trailing newline; missing or unreadable is `absent`) and delete (a missing record is success). A key outside `PERSONA_KEY_RE` is refused before any filesystem call. Side-effect-free; every path comes from the caller's state directory.
    ├── atomic-write.ts         Atomic file writes. `atomicWriteFileSync(path, contents)` — write `<path>.tmp`, then rename it over `path`; on failure the `.tmp` file is removed and the error rethrown. Used by `stop-hook-bootstrap.ts` and `reply-guard-record.ts`. `durableWriteFileSync(path, bytes, fs?)` (b.av2 SR-8.1) is the atomic and durable write of the reload files: it creates a temporary file beside `path` named `<name>.<pid>.<random hex>.tmp` (opened exclusively, so each write has its own), writes every byte as given, fsyncs and closes it, renames it over `path`, then fsyncs the directory so the rename survives a crash. A failure before the rename leaves `path` as it was, removes the temporary file (best effort) and rethrows the error as raised. A failure to open or fsync the directory, after the rename, throws `DurableWriteUnsyncedError` (`path`, `code`, `syncError`): the new bytes are at `path` but may not survive a crash. A failure to close the directory after a successful fsync is ignored. The `fs` seam (`DurableWriteFs`) lets tests observe the call order or fail one call. `durableUnlinkSync(path, fs?)` is the durable delete: unlink, then fsync the directory. It returns true when a file was removed and false when `path` was already absent (ENOENT or ENOTDIR, with no directory sync). Any other failure is rethrown: an unlink failure is thrown as raised and leaves `path` as it was; a failure to open or fsync the directory comes after the unlink and throws `DurableUnlinkUnsyncedError` (`path`, `code`, `syncError`): `path` is gone, but the removal may not survive a crash. A failure to close the directory after a successful fsync is ignored, as for the write. Both are used by `reload.ts`, the delete for `config.json.pending`, and by `retired-keys.ts` for the retired-key record. Nothing here logs. Side-effect-free.

## Data Flow

### Inbound (Slack → Claude Code)

Inbound delivery lives in `src/persona-routing.ts`. Each persona has its own Socket Mode connection (`src/persona-connections.ts`), and each connection's events reach the event router (`src/persona-event-router.ts`) tagged with that persona's key; `server.ts` only wires the router to the routing instance. The steps below run in code order, once per receiving persona P.

1. Slack message arrives on P's own connection (`message` or `app_mention` event). The event router logs `[slack] RAW <event> event persona=<P's key>: <first 300 chars of the event JSON>` and calls `receive(event, ack, <P's key>)`: P is the only receiver. Two personas in one channel each receive the event on their own connection, and each runs its own pipeline.
2. **Intake.** `receive` acks the event first; an ack failure is logged and handling continues. Then, for the receiving persona P (the intake also accepts a key list, each run concurrently), the archive is written and P's pipeline runs. The archive write is unconditional and comes before dedupe and any decision; it is keyed by (channel, ts), so a message received by several personas, or received twice by one, is stored once (see `src/message-archive.ts`). Each persona's run is isolated: a throw is logged as `[slack] persona-routing: error handling event for persona <ref>` with a `describeSlackCallFailure` tail and never stops another persona's run.
3. **Dedupe** (b.av2 SR-4.1). P's own dedupe store (`src/inbound-dedupe.ts`) records the event's key: (channel, ts), or (channel, ts, edited.ts) for an event that carries a top-level `edited.ts`. A key P first saw less than 10 minutes ago (`INBOUND_DEDUPE_RETENTION_MS`) is a duplicate and stops here: no decision, dispatch, reaction, recovery, post or log line. This collapses the `message` / `app_mention` pair Slack sends for a channel @mention and any Slack redelivery (for example after a reconnect). An edit keeps the message's ts, so `edited.ts` tells an edited event apart from the original: an edit that adds P's mention arrives as an `app_mention` with the original ts and an `edited` object, gets its own key and reaches P once, with `via` `mention`, while a redelivery of that same edited event is a duplicate. A `message_changed` event is keyed like any other event but is then dropped by the decision (step 4.1, not a deliverable subtype), so an edit that adds `<!here>` / `<!channel>` wakes nobody. The window runs from the first sighting; a duplicate does not extend it. Expired keys are pruned lazily on each new record, with no timer. An event missing its channel or ts is not keyed and carries on as new. The routing instance keeps one store per persona key, created on first use, so it survives a reopen of P's connection; the stores are in memory only and are empty after a server restart.
4. **Decision** (`decideDelivery` in `src/delivery-decision.ts`, pure; see its Module Map entry). A key that is no applied persona first logs `[slack] persona-routing: no applied persona with key=<key> — event not delivered to it`. The decision runs against P in b.av2 SR-4.2 order:
   1. A subtype other than `file_share`, `bot_message`, `thread_broadcast` or `me_message`, or no channel, is dropped. An event with neither `user` nor `bot_id` is dropped as `no-author`.
   2. P's own messages (author `user` = P's bot user ID, or the event's `bot_id` = P's bot ID) are dropped. This self-exclusion is the only author filter: posts by people, bots, integrations, webhooks and other personas are delivered by the rules below, and nothing counts, throttles or arbitrates exchanges between personas.
   3. Conversation kind (b.av2 SR-4.3). A DM is an event with `channel_type` `im`; as a defensive fallback, an event without `channel_type` whose conversation ID starts with `D` is treated as a DM too (Slack does not send `app_mention` for 1:1 DMs, so a DM arrives as a `message` event with `channel_type` `im`). A DM that passed steps 1 and 2 depends only on P's `dm.enabled`: on, it is delivered with `via` `dm`, whatever the text mentions; off, it is dropped as `dm-disabled` and logs one `persona-dm-dropped` line naming P, the conversation, the ts and `dm.enabled`, with no Slack call. A DM is decided only against the persona whose connection received it, and nothing in this path is channel-specific, so a persona with zero channels and DMs on receives its DMs the same way. A group DM is recognised only by `channel_type` `mpim`. The app does not subscribe to `message.mpim` (the manifest has `message.im` but no `message.mpim`), so such events are rare; one that arrives is dropped as `group-dm` with the plain drop line, whatever `dm.enabled` says, and never logs `persona-dm-dropped`. Neither a DM nor an `mpim` event reaches the channel rules below, so neither logs `unclaimed-channel`. An `app_mention` in a group DM carries no `channel_type` and a `G…` or `C…` conversation ID, so it is decided by the channel rules below: it is not delivered unless a persona lists that ID, and it normally logs `unclaimed-channel`.
   4. A channel P is not configured into is not delivered. When no applied persona lists the channel, one `unclaimed-channel` line names the channel and P; when another applied persona lists it, nothing is logged.
   5. A `delivery: all` channel delivers.
   6. A `delivery: mentions` channel delivers when the text contains P's user mention (`<@P>` or `<@P|label>`) or `<!here>` / `<!channel>` (with or without a label); `<!everyone>` and user-group mentions do not count.

   A delivered message carries `via`, how it reached P; the first match wins: `dm`, `mention`, `broadcast`, `receive_all_shared` (a `delivery: all` channel that at least one other applied persona also receives with `delivery: all`), `receive_all`. Only a DM produces `dm`, and a DM never produces any other value.

   The two classed lines are built by `formatPersonaDiagnostic`, e.g. `[slack] unclaimed-channel: personas[<i>] "<name>" (key=<key>): message in channel <C…> not delivered: no applied persona lists this channel` and `[slack] persona-dm-dropped: personas[<i>] "<name>" (key=<key>): direct message in conversation <D…> ts=<ts> dropped: dm.enabled is off for this persona` (the `ts=` part is left out when the event has no ts). The other drop reasons log `[slack] persona "<name>" (key=<key>) dropped message from channel=<C…> user=<U…>: <reason>`, with `bot_id=<B…>` in place of `user=` for an author without `user`. No drop line carries message text.

   For when a confirmed change takes effect here, see Session Lifecycle, [In-place update](#in-place-update-bav2-sr-86).
5. **Author label and session lookup.** The author's name is resolved first, for the meta of a delivered message and for the notice of a lost one: through P's client, or for an author without `user` (a webhook or `bot_message`) from the event itself (`username`, else `bot_profile.name`, else its bot ID) with no Slack call. A failed user-name lookup falls back to the user ID and logs one line (`[slack] persona-routing: user-name lookup for persona <ref> failed, using the user ID: …`); the message is not lost. Then P's session is read with `getSessionByPersona(P's key)`, after that await, so a session replaced or dropped during the lookup is seen. With no registered, connected session the message is dropped (`[slack] No live session for persona <ref> chat_id=<C…> — dropping message`) and the b.kvq no-session branch runs (step 7).
6. **Stream check.** The dispatch line `[slack] Dispatching to persona <ref> chat_id=<C…> cwd="…" mcpSessionId=… hasGetStream=… connected=… text="<first 80 chars>"` is logged. If the session has lost its `_GET_stream` (`hasGetStreamKey` on the session's transport false), `notification()` would vanish silently, so it is not sent: `[slack] DROP: no _GET_stream for persona <ref> chat_id=<C…> …` is logged and the b.9cj streamless branch runs (step 7). Nothing is awaited from the session read to the send in step 8, so the probe and the send act on the same session (b.9cj).
7. **Lost message** (b.av2 SR-4.6, SR-7.3; b.jg5 SRJ-1011, SRJ-1501, SRJ-1509; b.kvq / b.9cj). Both branches are handled by `handleLostMessage` in `persona-routing.ts`. The message is not delivered, gets no ack reaction and no ack-tracker entry, and is never saved or replayed. `decideLostMessageState` (`lost-message.ts`) reports one of ten states, keyed by P, first match wins: P not up (the routing's injected `isPersonaUp` answers false: P is `retrying` or `broken`, or unknown to the controller) → `not-up`, and no restart is started, since P's own recovery launches it once it is up (a persona that is not up forwards no Slack event, so `not-up` is reached only when P stops being up between receiving the message and the session lookup, as with a Web API call refused for its bot token, or by a message the old half of a destructive modify receives after its bring-up state is cancelled and before its connection is stopped); P latched (the one conflict latch's `isLatched`, see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502); an unusable recorded name and a launch start not recorded are such latches, which the one row read below can set itself, b.jg5 SRJ-512, SRJ-513) → `held-for-human`; P held on `ErrInvalidFlags` → `cannot-launch`; P's kill-failure episode open (the ordinary version of the kill-failure alert was raised at P's destination and P's row has not since read `ended` or `missing`, or been found gone or deleted by the collision ladder; see [The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007)), or an old-life hold whose old key's kill failed → `kill-failed`; P's `tmux-unresponsive` condition holding, or its `tmux-unavailable` or `ad-config-malformed` outage flag raised, with P below the restart cap and P's retry timer armed (`isRetryArmed`) → `not-answering` (an open unclassified-error episode alone is not this state; b.jg5 SRJ-1011 as amended: state 5 applies only while P's retry timer is armed, and its notice says CSCB is retrying, so a P at the cap reports the next state that applies, usually `restart-limit-reached`, whatever condition or flag is raised, and so does a P below the cap with no timer armed, which can reach `starting-now`; with `tmux-unavailable` raised below the cap, P's missing retry timer is armed before the decision, below); a live-row sequence running for P (`isSequenceOrWaitRunning`, production the session manager's `isLiveRowSequenceRunning`, b.jg5 SRJ-706: from the start's answer until the sequence settles, its step-6 launch included, even while P's row reads `pending`) → `restarting`, asked here so it wins over the next state; a launch call for P in flight or P's dialog approver running (`isLaunchOrApproverRunning`, production `isLaunchInFlight(key) || isDialogApproverRunning(key)`; P's row reads `pending`), or the one row read below answering `pending` → `session-starting`, so a message lost while only the approver runs reports `session-starting` with no read and no human-triggered restart; a restart already pending or active → `restarting`; auto-restart disabled (`session_restart_delay: 0`) → `auto-restart-disabled`; P at the failure cap → `restart-limit-reached`; otherwise `starting-now`. The `kill-failed` input is bound to P's open kill-failure episode (`isKillFailed`: the kill-failure alerts' `isOpen`, read at call time through the holder `main()` sets), so state 4 is reachable: a message lost while the episode is open reports `kill-failed` and starts no restart. The alert's survivor version opens no episode, so a message lost after it never reports `kill-failed`, and neither does one lost after the episode ended. A CONFLICT latch that came with the alert (the kill's own CONFLICT after a survivor-naming failure) reports `held-for-human` first. The old-life-hold half of this input has no production binding yet: it answers false. The `cannot-launch` input is bound: `main()` passes `isHeldOnInvalidFlags`, read at call time from the server's `ErrInvalidFlags` hold (`isHeld`), so a message lost while P is held reports `cannot-launch` and fires no human-triggered restart ([The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold](#the-errinvalidflags-hold-bjg5-srj-207-srj-1008)). A message lost while a live-row sequence runs for P reports `restarting` with no row read (below) and fires no human-triggered restart. In the five states from `held-for-human` to `session-starting` no human-triggered restart fires (b.av2 SR-4.6 as amended by b.jg5 SRJ-1501; in `session-starting` it would be a launch over the `pending` row); only in `starting-now` (`firesHumanTriggeredRestart`) `scheduleRestart(key, cwd, undefined, { humanTrigger: true })` is called, with nothing awaited between the final decision and the call, so messages lost together schedule at most one restart (the restart it starts is Auto-Restart's, whose refused kill or launch counts nothing and posts no spawn-failure notice; for a retired key its reconnect starts the live-row sequence for an old life and its launch is a reuse spawn, never a `resume`, [Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)) (P's `working_directory` in the no-session branch, the session's `cwd` in the streamless branch). Before the decision (b.jg5 SRJ-311; `armStoppedRetryBeforeDecision`, asked before the read gate's check and again after the row read when one was awaited, since a retry may have stopped during it), when none of states 1 to 4 applies, state 5's condition holds, P's `tmux-unavailable` flag is raised and P is below the restart cap, the routing asks `armRetryTimerIfMissing(key)`, so the gated decision sees the timer and reports `not-answering`: production arms P's retry timer with the `environment` cause (`armEnvironmentRetryTimer`, the health tick's arm path) only when none is armed, P is not latched and nothing is in flight for it, logging `[slack] Lost message: persona=<key> has its tmux-unavailable outage raised with no retry timer — no restart scheduled; arming one (b.jg5 SRJ-311)`, and does nothing while the server is shutting down. A retry that stopped as not up, on a declined launch or on a failed run leaves the flag raised with no timer, so this lets a lost message start the retries again even with `health_check_interval` 0. The arm is the outage's own retry, never a restart; `ad-config-malformed` or the `tmux-unresponsive` condition alone arms nothing here, and at the cap nothing is armed (a timer armed there would stop at its first retry). When the check arms nothing (P latched, work in flight for P (a launch call, a running live-row sequence or a running dialog approver), no controller, shutting down), state 5 does not apply and the decision reports the next state: `held-for-human` in the first case, and `restarting` or `session-starting` in the second. Either branch then raises exactly one lost-message notice (`buildLostMessageNotice`) through the injected `notify`, the per-persona notifier's `notify`: it goes to P's destination, names the sender and the recovery state, and carries no message text. It takes the notifier's path like every persona notice (see the `persona-notifier.ts` entry and Permission Relay, [Destination hold](#destination-hold-bav2-sr-71-failures)). Nothing else is posted in the source conversation; when the destination is that conversation, the notice is the one post there. The notice is awaited; a failing `notify` logs one `persona-routing: lost-message notice … failed` line and is never thrown.

   **The one row read (b.jg5 SRJ-1011, SRJ-1501).** `handleLostMessage` reads P's row once (`readRowLiveness`, the liveness adapter of [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart) step 3, that is one `status` call) only when all of these hold, each asked at that time: the read is injected; none of states 1 to 5 applies (`decideEarlyLostMessageState`, the helper `decideLostMessageState` asks first); no launch call for P is in flight and no dialog approver for P runs (`isLaunchOrApproverRunning`); no live-row sequence runs for P (`isSequenceOrWaitRunning`); and nothing is in flight for P (`isWorkInFlight`, the server's "in flight for P" binding `isPersonaWorkInFlight`: a launch call, a running live-row sequence or a running dialog approver). Otherwise no read is made. There is never more than one read per lost message: it is not retried, and no timer is armed by the routing for it.

   - **Its answers.** A `pending` reading is the `session-starting` input. A configured persona's own row that reads `pending` with no launch start never gives that reading: the adapter's own-row `status` step latches P with `launch-start-not-recorded` and the read answers `unknown` (b.jg5 SRJ-513), so the decision made after it reports `held-for-human` and no restart fires (see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)). The same step clears a retired key's entry when the row reads live other than `pending` with the key's mark set, leaving the reading unchanged (b.jg5 SRJ-807; see [The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115)). Any other reading (`live`, `dead`, `unknown`, or a value that is not a reading) leaves `session-starting` out, and so does a rejected read, which is caught, logged once as `[slack] persona-routing: lost-message row read for persona <ref> failed — session-starting left out: <describeAgentDirectorFailure>` (redacted) and never thrown. So a failed read never reports `session-starting`. Before `main()` has built the adapter the read answers `unknown` with no `status` call.
   - **Outside any attempt.** The read is made from the Slack event path, outside any launch or recovery attempt, and is not the human-triggered restart. What its answer raises or arms is the adapter's, as at the health tick's read (see [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart) step 3): a success clears `ad-unreachable` and `ad-config-malformed`; `ErrSpawnNotFound` reads `dead`; `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` raises `ad-unreachable`, reads `dead` (not `pending`) and arms nothing; `ErrTmuxNotAvailable` (ENVIRONMENT) raises `tmux-unavailable`, arms the retry timer and reads `unknown`; `ErrConfigMalformed` (CONFIG) raises `ad-config-malformed`, arms the retry timer and reads `unknown`; an UNAVAILABLE, UNCLASSIFIED or any other error reads `unknown`, arms no retry timer and opens no unclassified-error episode. `status` is not tmux-touching, so no answer starts `tmux-unresponsive`.
   - **Decided again after the read.** `decideLostMessageState` runs once, after the read, asking every query afresh, so a latch or an outage that began during the read, one the read itself raised included (an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer), reports `held-for-human` or `not-answering` (the latter only while P's retry timer is armed and P is below the restart cap).
   - **A failed read and the restart.** When a failed read lets the state reach `starting-now`, the human-triggered restart still makes its own liveness read, and a `pending` row there is deferred, never launched over (see **`pending` rows** under [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart) step 3).

   **Invariant: lost-message reports go only to the persona's destination.** A server message in the conversation a message came from would give away, in a shared channel, a persona passing as a person. So no delivery failure is ever reported in the source conversation because the message came from there, for a channel or a DM source alike; when the source conversation is also the destination, the destination's one notice is the only post there. Future delivery or queueing work (b.4vj, guaranteed inbound delivery) is bound by the same rule and must report to the destination.
8. **Delivery.** P's session's MCP Server sends `notifications/claude/channel` (awaited) to its Claude Code client, with P's own mention token (`<@P>` or `<@P|label>`) stripped from the text; other mentions and broadcasts stay. Only P's session receives it. The meta, rendered by the harness as attributes of the `<channel>` tag, is `chat_id` (the source conversation), `message_id`, `user` (the author label from step 5), the author's `user_id` (or, for an author without `user`, its `bot_id`; never both), `ts`, `via` from step 4, `thread_ts` when present, and `attachment_count` / `attachments` when the message has files.
9. **Ack reaction** (b.av2 SR-4.5). Only after the send in step 8 has succeeded does P react, so only a dispatched message gets a reaction: a drop, a dedupe duplicate, a lost message (step 7) or a send that throws gets no reaction and no ack-tracker entry. If the server-wide `ack_reaction` is set (`deps.getReplySettings()`, the start-time value), `trackAck(P's key, channelId, messageTs)` records P's entry first, so P's first reply always finds it, and then the reaction is added through P's own client without being awaited (a failure is ignored; the entry stays and the message is still delivered). With `ack_reaction` absent, or no client for P (dry run, or P not serving), both are skipped. When one message is dispatched to several personas (each on its own connection), each runs this step for itself, so the message carries one reaction per dispatching persona, each under that persona's own identity, and each persona holds its own entry.

Injected messages (`/interject` and cron, which posts through `/interject`) reach the persona's instance but do not come through this pipeline: they are not Slack messages, so they get no ack reaction. Their meta is unchanged, `user` and `ts` only, with no `via`; see [POST /interject](#post-interject).

### Outbound (Claude Code → Slack)

1. Claude Code calls MCP tools (`reply`, `react`, `edit_message`, etc.)
2. The tool handler resolves the calling persona at call time from the session's registered persona key (`SessionToolDeps.getPersona`). A session not yet matched to a persona, or whose key is no applied persona, gets a tool error.
3. `checkPersonaTarget()` checks the tool's target (`chat_id`, or `channel` for `fetch_messages`) against the persona as applied now, before the dry-run branch (b.av2 SR-5.1). There are three target kinds:
