Sibling scope: the lost / never-created / inconclusive classification inside the resume path itself is **b.wrb / b.fwu**, not this module. Two layers:

    - **Layer 1 — non-persistent storage.** `checkJsonlPersistence` resolves the deduped set of the personas' effective `<claude_config_dir>/projects` roots (a persona with no configured dir uses `<home>/.claude`; with no personas at all, the home default root is checked) and classifies each root's mount fstype by longest-prefix match over `/proc/self/mountinfo` (string-prefix, not a stat — a not-yet-created dir classifies by its parent mount). A root on `tmpfs`/`ramfs` → `recordStartupError('jsonl-non-persistent', …)` plus one notice through the notifier to each affected persona's destination — those whose effective JSONL root is the flagged root, not every persona (resume is structurally impossible for those personas on this host). An undeterminable fstype (unreadable/unparseable/unresolvable) → `recordStartupError('jsonl-persistence-check-warning', …)`, no notice.
    - **Layer 2 — per-persona transcript loss.** For each applied persona it fetches the persona's AD row (through `withOutageDetection`, the sanctioned CSCB→AD entry point). A row the collision ladder will replace instead of resuming — its `cwd` differs from the persona's working directory by real path, or its `config_dir` label is missing or mismatched (`compareRowToPersona`, the same check as step 5's guards) — is not checked: one log line naming the persona, the mismatch (the row's `cwd` against the working directory, or the missing or changed `config_dir` label) and that the transcript was not checked because the collision ladder will replace the row, with no record and no notice. Otherwise, when the row carries a `claude_session_id`, it stats the AD-recorded `jsonl_path` **and** a config-dir-aware fallback path composed the same way agent-director composes it (`resolveJsonlPath`, under the persona's effective config dir). Outcomes: persisted exists → healthy, silent. Persisted stale/missing but fallback exists → `recordStartupError('jsonl-transcript-stale-path', …)` + a notice through the notifier to that persona's destination (history is on disk but AD 0.8.0's resume only stats the persisted path, so it would throw `ErrJsonlMissing` and wipe the persona's memory). Both missing → the `message_archive_db` archive (when configured) is consulted for evidence under the b.av2 SR-7.4 rule (`personaArchiveEvidenceScope`): only messages in the persona's `delivery: all` channels since `started_at` count, in one query over all of them. A persona with no `delivery: all` channel counts 0 without the archive being opened (even when none is configured), and since every persona has a channel or DMs on, that persona always takes (once `started_at` parses) the unattributable-zero path below. A count ≥1 → `recordStartupError('jsonl-transcript-lost', …)` + a notice to that persona's destination saying its conversation memory has been lost (conversation provably happened, transcript is gone). A zero count for a persona with any `delivery: mentions` channel or DMs on is not evidence of idleness, because the archive cannot attribute messages from `mentions` channels or DMs to a persona: one quiet log line saying the archive evidence is inconclusive (`UNATTRIBUTABLE_ZERO_REASON`), no record and no notice. The archive check is read-only: a missing archive DB file yields no evidence (it is never created here). Both missing with no archive evidence → a single quiet log line only: a persona idle since spawn has no transcript yet because Claude creates the `.jsonl` lazily on first message — normal, not an error, and must not alarm every boot. Log lines name the persona as `"<name>" (key=<key>)`. Per-persona AD/get errors (including `ErrSpawnNotFound`) are logged and skipped; the sweep never aborts. A persona whose `claude_config_dir` cannot be resolved to a real path (bug b.g57) is skipped before its row is fetched, with one quiet line: its launch waits for the directory with the row kept, so there is no lost history to report.
4a-ter. **b.osj / b.av2 SR-9.4 stop-hook bootstrap** — `stopHookBootstrap(personaConfig, STATE_DIR)` (from `src/stop-hook-bootstrap.ts`) is the start pass: over every applied persona (b.av2 SR-6.2) it installs or removes the CSCB-managed Slack Reply Guard Stop hook in `<claude_config_dir>/settings.json`. Call site: `main()` in `server.ts`, immediately after step 4a-quater (`runJsonlPersistenceSafeguard`) and before step 5 (`startupSessionManager`) — before any spawn fires. Runs in both real and dry-run modes (config-file patch, not a session operation). Never throws to the caller; per-dir failures are caught and recorded via `recordStartupError`. The same install rule runs again before every launch, as the launch pass (step 5, "Reply-guard steps before every spawn and resume"). Behavior:

    - **Install rule, per directory (b.av2 SR-9.4).** Each applied persona counts toward its effective `claude_config_dir` (its own, else the top-level one) and toward the directory its running instance launched with (the launched-with dir, kept in memory per persona key: set at each launch, cleared by `teardownPersonaReplyGuard`, empty at server start). Directories are grouped by real path (`resolveRealPath`, lexical fallback), so two spellings of one directory are one group and its `settings.json` is patched once, at the first contributing persona's configured path. A persona is enabled when its effective `stop_hook_bootstrap` is `true` or its record (`reply-guard/<key>`, see Configuration) reads `true`. The entry is ensured when any persona counting toward the directory is enabled and removed otherwise (emptied groups pruned). Whether one persona is reminded is its own record's business, read by the guard at hook time, so personas sharing a directory each follow their own value. Diagnostics name the contributing personas as `personas="<name>" (key=<key>), …`.
    - **Managed-entry shape.** Own group `{"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"<managed command>"}]}`, no `matcher` field (Stop is not tool-scoped). Recognition rule: any Stop-hook `command` string containing the substring `slack-reply-guard.sh` is CSCB-managed.
    - **Canonical command.** `managedHookCommand(stateDir)` is the guard's absolute path followed by the record directory `<state dir>/reply-guard`, each POSIX single-quoted (`shellSingleQuote`), because Claude Code runs a hook command through a shell; the guard reads the directory as its first argument. The script path resolves relative to the installed package (same idiom as `src/install-skill-pointer.ts`), correct under both published-package layout and repo checkout. Only the exact current command is canonical: a managed entry with a bare path, a stale install path or another record directory is rewritten to it (self-heal).
    - **Idempotent write decision.** `scanStopGroups` returns `hasSingleCanonicalGroup=true` only when there is exactly one Stop group whose sole hook entry has `type=='command'`, `command==canonicalCmd`, no `matcher`, and no extra keys. In that state the write is skipped entirely. Any drift — stale command, duplicates, extra keys, extra hooks in the managed group — triggers a strip-all-managed + append-canonical rewrite, written atomically (`atomicWriteFileSync`, `.tmp` + rename). Every read-modify-write is synchronous, so two personas launching at once cannot interleave on one `settings.json`.
    - **Create-missing.** ENOENT on the target `settings.json` for an enabled dir → the file is created with just the managed group.
    - **Malformed JSON soft-fail.** Non-ENOENT read errors, unparseable JSON, and non-object top levels all report a class label of `stop-hook-bootstrap-settings-read` / `stop-hook-bootstrap-settings-parse` / `stop-hook-bootstrap-settings-shape` and leave the file untouched — never a clobber.
    - **Personal-config-dir refusal (SR-3.11).** `isForbiddenHomeClaudeDir` resolves both the candidate dir and `homedir()/.claude` through `resolveRealPath` from `src/config.ts` (`realpathSync`, with a lexical `resolve()` fallback whenever realpath fails), so symlinked personal dirs cannot slip past a string compare. On a match the dir is skipped and never written, so a persona whose directory resolves there gets no reminder. The start pass records `stop-hook-bootstrap-refuse-home` once per server start (all spellings of `~/.claude` are one group); the launch pass logs the refusal to the server log only.
    - **Skip conditions.** A persona with no effective `claude_config_dir` gets a server-log line only (`[slack] stop-hook-bootstrap: "<name>" (key=<key>) has no claude_config_dir — skipping`), never a `startup-errors.log` record, and no reminder. Empty or whitespace-only dirs are treated as absent (guards against `resolve("")` landing in the process cwd). A dir that fails `statSync` (or is not a directory) is skipped; the ensure path reports `stop-hook-bootstrap-dir-missing` / `stop-hook-bootstrap-not-a-dir`, and a missing dir on the remove path is silent.
    - **jq presence check.** A one-time `command -v jq` probe per server start: if `jq` is absent the entry is **still installed** (the hook fails open at hook time when `jq` is missing) but a `stop-hook-bootstrap-jq-missing` startup error is recorded so operators see the warning. The launch pass does not probe.
    - **Duplicate collapse and removal (SR-3.7, SR-3.8).** When rewriting an enabled dir, every managed `{type, command}` object across every Stop group is stripped before the canonical group is appended, so pre-existing duplicates collapse to one. Removal for a dir with no enabled persona strips every managed object and prunes any group left with an empty `hooks` array.
    - **Never-throws contract.** A top-level `try/catch` around the whole entry point plus per-dir `try/catch` blocks record `stop-hook-bootstrap` / `stop-hook-bootstrap-dir` classes on unexpected failure. Other dirs continue processing. Timing note (SR-3.15): on-disk state is refreshed every boot and every launch, and Claude Code normally picks up hook edits in `settings.json` while running (its settings file watcher), so the managed hook's presence in a directory may change under a running instance, for example when a neighbour sharing the directory launches. A running instance still keeps the value it launched with, because the guard decides by that instance's own record (`reply-guard/<CSCB_PERSONA>`), which is written only at the instance's launch. A live session that survives a CSCB restart via reconnect is not relaunched, so its record, and its value, change only at its next spawn or resume.
5. **Per-persona bring-up and launch (b.av2 SR-6.1)** — `startupSessionManager(applied, { bringUp: personaBringUps })` over the applied set runs after the start-wide passes (step 4 sweep, 4a-bis trust patch, 4a-quater JSONL safeguard, 4a-ter Stop-hook bootstrap). It is the reload controller's `lifecycle.startBringUp`, and `main()` runs it through `reload.runStartBringUp()`, so it brings up exactly the persona set step 2a applied. `personaBringUps` is the bring-up controller (`createPersonaBringUpController` in `src/persona-bringup-controller.ts`), built in `main()` right after the connection manager. It brings each persona up once, so a persona listed in several channels is brought up and spawned exactly once. Steps 1–3 run for every persona at once (the controller's `bringUp`), so no persona's Slack connection waits behind another persona's launch. Only step 4 goes through the launch pool: at most `concurrency` launches (default 3) run at a time, taken first in, first out in the order the personas become ready. A persona that is not `up` takes no launch slot. Per persona, in order:
   - **`persona-start` line** — one line per applied persona as its bring-up starts, naming the persona, its entry and its key (see Logging, Persona bring-up lines).
   - **Steps 1 and 2: local credentials check** (`checkPersonaCredentials`) **and working-directory check** (`checkPersonaWorkingDirectory`), both evaluated before either stops the bring-up, so both causes are logged (`persona-credentials-*`, `persona-directory-*` lines). Dry run skips the credentials check and reads no credentials file.
   - **`claude_config_dir` check** — once steps 1 and 2 pass, the controller's `checkConfigDir` resolves the persona's effective `claude_config_dir`; an unresolvable one holds the persona (`persona-config-dir-unresolvable`, see Config-dir-unresolvable below) and step 3 does not run.
   - **Step 3: Slack validation and connection** — the connection manager's `bringUp(persona, tokens)`: `auth.test` on a short-lived validation client, then the long-lived Web API and Socket Mode clients (see the `persona-connections.ts` entry for the client options, the 10 s bounds on `auth.test` and `start()`, backoff and reopen). The manager logs every Slack outcome itself (`persona-slack-unreachable`, `persona-credentials-refused`). In dry run the persona is up at once with its placeholder identity.
   - **Step 4: launch** — only when the persona's outcome is `up`: `spawnForPersona` (SR-1.4 collision-then-act dispatcher), below. The connection is therefore up before the instance is launched.

   **Outcomes (b.av2 SR-6.1, SR-6.4).** Every bring-up ends with one outcome, which the controller keeps per persona:

   | Cause | Class | Outcome |
   |---|---|---|
   | None: steps 1–3 passed | — | `up` |
   | Credentials file missing, unreadable or invalid (step 1) | `persona-credentials-missing` / `-unreadable` / `-invalid` | `broken` |
   | Slack refused a token (step 3, at bring-up or on a reopen), or refused the bot token in a Web API call of the running persona (bug b.ujn) | `persona-credentials-refused` | `broken` |
   | Slack unreachable (step 3) | `persona-slack-unreachable` | `retrying` |
   | Working directory missing or unusable (step 2) | `persona-directory-missing` / `-unusable` | `retrying` |
   | `claude_config_dir` cannot be resolved to a real path, found right before step 3 or by a later launch (bug b.g57) | `persona-config-dir-unresolvable` | `retrying` |

   A persona with both a credentials cause and a directory cause is `broken`. Its directory is still re-checked, and its start and cleared lines are logged, but it goes no further while the credentials cause holds; it comes up only once both clear. A credentials-broken persona is not retried. While the server runs, it recovers only through a confirmed change to its credentials file (b.av2 SR-6.4): apply step 6 brings it up afresh (see [The apply pipeline](#the-apply-pipeline-sr-86) and [Bring-up at apply](#bring-up-at-apply-bav2-sr-61)). A start, from the record or not, also reads every credentials file as it stands (b.av2 SR-8.7), so a fixed file brings it up at the next start too.

   A persona that isn't `up` is not launched by the start, records no startup error, raises no notice and is not counted as a failed spawn. The lines above say why. Its agent-director row and any instance still running from before are kept (b.av2 SR-6.4): nothing kills them for the persona being down, but the server does not serve the instance. Its MCP registration is refused (Connection step 3), the permission poller skips its rows (Permission Relay, Per-tick flow) and `/interject` answers 503 (Endpoint Inventory). When the persona comes up, its launch reaches the row through the collision ladder below, so the history is kept. Personas are brought up independently, so one persona's failure stops neither the others nor the server.

   **Retries run on per-persona timers, outside `startupSessionManager`.** The start pass returns once every persona has an outcome and every `up` persona's launch has settled or is parked waiting for a `working` row (see the `working` branch below, b.f2b); it never waits on a retry, and a retrying persona never delays another. Nor does it wait for a live-row sequence: a launch for a persona whose sequence runs answers `sequence-waiting` at once (b.jg5 SRJ-706), counted neither as failed nor as succeeded. Two kinds of retry exist, both on the SR-3.2 backoff (5 s doubling to a 300 s ceiling, no cap, `persona-retry-schedule.ts`), and neither touches the restart failure counter or cap (`backoff.ts`):

   - **Slack-unreachable** — the connection manager retries on its own per-persona timer with the tokens it was handed.
   - **Directory-broken** — the controller opens no Slack connection and re-checks the directory (`checkPersonaWorkingDirectory`) on the persona's own timer. Once the directory is usable the bring-up continues with no restart and no confirmation: Slack validation and connection, then the launch. If Slack is then unreachable, the persona becomes Slack-unreachable `retrying`.
   - **Config-dir-unresolvable (bug b.g57)** — the controller checks the persona's effective `claude_config_dir` (`checkLaunchConfigDir`) right before step 3, at start, at an apply bring-up and when a directory retry reaches Slack; an unresolvable directory holds the persona there, so it never connects. Every launch (start, retry, restart, apply) also resolves it first. When it can't be resolved, the launch makes no agent-director call and hands the persona to the controller (`holdForConfigDir`), which closes its Slack connection. Either way the persona is `retrying` with no connection and receives nothing: its MCP session is dropped if it was up, its notices are held (per persona, at most 20, oldest dropped), and its row and instance are kept (no kill, delete or spawn). The controller re-checks the directory on the persona's own timer (5 s doubling to 300 s). Once it resolves, the controller logs the cleared line, connects the persona with its held credentials and launches it, which resumes its row through the ladder with no confirmation. The restart path's kill is skipped too (`holdLaunchIfConfigDirUnresolvable`), and the relaunch is `'skipped'`, counting toward no failure or cap. A confirmed credentials change while held is taken as a retrying persona's is (see [Credentials change](#credentials-change-bav2-sr-86-step-4)).

   A retry keeps using the credentials content it holds, read at the persona's bring-up, until a confirmed change replaces it; the controller holds those tokens and never re-reads the file. An edit to the file made meanwhile is ignored by the retry. The detection tick notices it: the file's digest no longer matches the one the controller holds for the persona (`credentialsDigest`), so a credentials change is pending (see [Reload Detection Tick](#reload-detection-tick-bav2-sr-82-sr-83)). Once confirmed, apply step 4 hands a retrying persona the new content, and its later attempts use it (see [Credentials change](#credentials-change-bav2-sr-86-step-4)).

   **Launch after a retry.** A persona that reaches `up` through a retry is launched from its own retry path, not by the health check: when a directory retry's Slack step leaves the persona's outcome `up` (the manager's status is `up`, `lost` or `retrying` in the `reopen` phase, since a blip right after the connection came up does not undo it), or when the manager reports `up` right after `retrying` its bring-up (the controller's `onConnectionStatus`). The launch runs once per persona through `spawnForPersona(persona, personaConfig, false)` with the persona's current applied declaration, so it shares the one-launch-in-flight guard that restarts use and a launch failure takes the runtime spawn-failure path. An `up` after `lost` or a reopen launches nothing, since the instance is already running.

   **Applied-set guard (b.av2 SR-8.6).** From a confirmed apply's step 1 on, no launch or restart path acts for a key outside the applied set, even before that persona's teardown. The checks read the set live (`personaConfig`) and live in three places: the bring-up controller (`appliedPersonas` getter and `isApplied(key)`, `persona-bringup-controller.ts`), where a directory re-check for such a key stops (`[slack] persona "<name>" (key=<key>): no longer applied — its working-directory retry stops`) and a launch after a retry is skipped (`… up after its bring-up retry (<via>) but no longer applied — not launching`), and a re-check tests the directory against the current set; the shared up check (`isPersonaUpGiven` in `persona-start.ts`, over `PersonaUpQuery.isApplied`), behind the relaunch gate (restart, `launchSession`, the health-check work list) and `isPersonaUp` (MCP session admission, the permission poller's skip, `/interject`'s 503); and `preLaunchReplyGuard` (`stop-hook-bootstrap.ts`), which does nothing for such a key. This is the one full statement of the guard; Auto-Restart and the Health-Check Poller refer here. What the guard does not do is stop anything: the removed persona's Slack connection and instance stay until its teardown in apply step 2 of the same apply (see [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65)). For what else a removal changes at step 1, see [The apply pipeline](#the-apply-pipeline-sr-86).

   **Never posted to Slack (b.av2 SR-7.2, part).** Bring-up failures are logged to the server log only, at start and on every later retry, and never to `startup-errors.log`. No notice is posted or held for a later flush under any identity.

   Spawn-path log lines name the persona JSON-quoted with the key beside it, e.g. `spawnForPersona: spawned "Ops Bot" (key=ops_bot_5e2526f3) …`; under dry run each persona logs `dry-run: skipping spawn for "<name>" (key=<key>) cwd=<dir>` and nothing is spawned.
   - **Trust patch before every launch (b.av2 SR-6.2).** Each ladder run first calls the installed pre-launch trust patcher (`trustPatchPersona`, see step 4a-bis) for the persona's working directory in its effective config dir — once, before the first spawn or resume the ladder can make, so it covers fresh spawns, resumes and the replace step's reuse spawns below. It never runs under dry run and never for a call that joins an in-flight launch. A throw is logged as `[slack] spawnForPersona: pre-launch trust patch failed for "<name>" (key=<key>) — launching anyway: <error>` and the ladder continues.
   - **Pre-trust is only logged (b.jg5 SRJ-413).** The server never passes `no_pre_trust` on a spawn (plain or reuse) or a `resume`, so agent-director pre-accepts the persona's folder trust at every launch and reports the outcome as the result's `pre_trust`: `ok` (the trust entry was written), `skipped` (pre-trust was off for this launch) or `failed` (it could not be written). Every launch that returns success writes exactly one line about it, first in the after-launch step (`afterLaunchSucceeded`, before the approver starts; see the pre-session dialog approval bullet below), from `preTrustLogLine`: `[slack] spawnForPersona: "<name>" (key=<key>) <spawn|resume|reuse spawn> pre_trust=<value> (logged only, b.jg5 SRJ-413)`, the value shown as it arrived; a result without the field (an agent-director older than Phase 1) logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: "<name>" (key=<key>) <spawn|resume|reuse spawn> result carries no pre_trust: it came from an agent-director older than Phase 1 (logged only, b.jg5 SRJ-413)`. No value changes what the server does: the launch's result, notices, startup-errors entries, outage state and retry counts are the same for all four cases, and a folder-trust prompt that follows `skipped` or `failed` is answered by the startup-dialog approver like any other. The server's own trust patch above is unchanged and still runs before every launch.
   - **Reply-guard steps before every spawn and resume (b.av2 SR-9.4, SR-6.2).** Immediately before each actual `client.spawn` or `client.resume` the ladder makes — the fresh spawn, a resume, a dead-session or `ErrSpawnNotFound` recovery, the replace step's reuse spawns and the restart relaunch through the same ladder — it calls the installed pre-launch reply guard (`preLaunchReplyGuard`, `src/stop-hook-bootstrap.ts`). In order it (1) writes the launching persona's effective `stop_hook_bootstrap` to its record `reply-guard/<key>` (see Configuration), (2) sets the persona's launched-with dir to its effective `claude_config_dir` (or forgets it, with the no-configured-dir log line, when none is set), and (3) runs the launch pass of the step 4a-ter install rule over the new effective dir and the previous launched-with dir only. It writes only the launching persona's record, so a neighbour's launch in the same directory never rewrites another persona's record. The launch pass does no `jq` probe and never writes `startup-errors.log`: its failures, the `~/.claude` refusal included, are server-log lines (`[slack] stop-hook-bootstrap: pre-launch pass [<class>] …`). A failed record write removes any stale record (the guard then fails open to no reminder), logs one line naming the persona and the record path, and the launch proceeds; nothing in these steps blocks a launch. A path that only reconnects to a live instance or does nothing (`waiting`/`working` reconnect, the `pending`/`check_permission`/`ask_user` no-op) runs no reply-guard step. The optimistic first spawn runs the steps before it and, on `ErrInstanceIdCollision`, undoes them, so a later spawn or resume in that ladder runs them afresh. The undo restores the record (the previous text, or deleted when there was none) only if the step wrote it successfully, changed it, and the record still holds what the step wrote; it restores the launched-with dir only if the entry is still the one the step set; then it re-reads the applied persona set and re-runs the launch pass over the new and previous dirs. A teardown or another launch in between is never overwritten. Side effect: when the collision leads only to a reconnect and the running persona's record disagrees with its current config, the step may remove or add the managed hook, and the undo re-runs the install rule with the restored record: a hook the step removed comes back, and one it added stays when the config now enables it (correct under the install rule). When the step removed the hook and the undo re-adds it, that directory's `settings.json` is written twice and the managed group moves to the end of the Stop hooks. `server.ts` installs the step once a persona config is loaded; with none it does nothing (no record, no patch). It passes a getter, not a snapshot, so the step and its undo each read the live applied persona set. The effect: a running instance keeps the value it launched with, and a changed value takes effect at the persona's next launch; a confirmed change reaches that launch through step 1's swap of the applied set, with no call at apply. Dry run returns before the ladder, so it writes no record.
   - Attempt `client.spawn(SR-1.1 params)`, built from `persona-identity.ts` (b.av2 SR-2.2). This first spawn is plain: `buildSpawnParams` never adds the reuse flag (b.jg5 SRJ-711), so a key whose row is already there collides (`ErrInstanceIdCollision`) and goes on to the collision `get` and the ladder below, whose `resume` keeps the conversation. Only the reuse launch adds the flag ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)). A key recorded as retired gets no plain first spawn: its first launch is one reuse spawn of the same id, and its collision `get` decides by the retired-key rule ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)).
     - `template: 'slack-channel-bot'`, `relay_mode: 'on'`, `cwd` = the persona's working directory.
     - `claude_instance_id: cscb_<key>`, `tmux_session_name: slack_bot_<key>`.
     - `label: ['service=cscb', 'persona=<key>', 'config_dir=<12 hex>']`, and no other label. The `config_dir` value hashes the real path of the persona's effective `claude_config_dir` (no configured dir means `~/.claude`), taken from the launch's pre-launch check (`checkLaunchConfigDir`, `resolveRealPathStrict`). There is no lexical fallback (bug b.g57). A directory not created yet under a resolvable parent gets the label of the real path it will have: its nearest existing ancestor's real path plus the rest, which is the lexical path when no symlink is involved. Claude Code creates it at first launch. A directory that can't be resolved (a symlink on its path that points to nothing, `ENOTDIR`, or any error other than `ENOENT`) gets no label and is not launched (see the Config-dir-unresolvable retry above). Known limit: a dropped mount that leaves an empty mount point looks like a directory not created yet. The start sweep (step 4) and the ladder read the `persona`, `config_dir` and `cwd` fields; the permission poller reads the `persona` label. The CLI's teardown reads no label: it addresses `cscb_<key>` directly.
     - `extra_env`: `CSCB_PERSONA=<key>`, `CLAUDE_MANAGED_CHANNEL=<key>`, `CSCB_CRONTABLE_PATH` on every spawn (the resolved tilde-expanded `cron_table_path`: the default `<config dir>/crontab` or the configured override), `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=false` on every spawn (see Environment Variables), and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` only when a `claude_config_dir` is configured (passed as configured, not real-pathed). Every plain spawn in the ladder sends these params unchanged (the first spawn, the retry spawn after the collision `get` found no row, and the spawn after `resume` found none); the reuse spawn (`reuseSpawnForPersona`) sends the same params with only `reuse_finished: true` added (b.jg5 SRJ-708; [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)); a resume passes only the instance ID, and agent-director restores the env it stored with the row at spawn.
     - No `no_pre_trust`, on a plain spawn or a reuse (`buildSpawnParams`'s doc comment says so; see the pre-trust bullet above).
   - **Never two live instances (b.av2 SR-6.3).** The instance ID is fixed at `cscb_<key>`, so agent-director refuses a second spawn for a persona that already has a row (`ErrInstanceIdCollision`), and the ladder below decides what happens to that row. Within the process, `spawnForPersona` allows one in-flight launch per persona key: a second call for a key whose launch is still running — from the start pass, a restart or a human-triggered restart — logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: launch already in flight for "<name>" (key=<key>) — joining it` and returns that launch's result instead of starting a second ladder. The entry is cleared when the launch settles, whatever its outcome; different keys never wait on each other. Dry run returns before the check.
   - **A launch attempt (b.jg5 SRJ-301).** The ladder a `spawnForPersona` call starts runs as a launch attempt for the persona (`runInAttempt`, `src/unavailable-retry.ts`) until its result, the `working`-row wait included (the dialog approver that starts after a launch call returned success is not: it runs outside every attempt, see Pre-session dialog approval below); a joining call, the claude_config_dir deferral and dry run are no attempt. An UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`), CONFIG (`ErrConfigMalformed`) or UNCLASSIFIED outcome from any verb in it, or an error from `status`, `get` or `list` other than `ErrSpawnNotFound` and UNUSABLE_NAME, arms the persona's UNAVAILABLE retry timer through the installed trigger sink (a trigger while armed keeps the due time). An UNCLASSIFIED outcome in it, a read's included, is also reported to the persona's unclassified-error episode ([The unclassified-error episode](#the-unclassified-error-episode-bjg5-srj-313-srj-1009)). An UNAVAILABLE outcome other than `ErrTmuxKillFailed` from a tmux-touching call in it also starts or continues the persona's `tmux-unresponsive` condition ([The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310)). At every spawn, resume and collision `get` below, the same outcome is a refusal ([Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), refusals at the launch and recovery sites). At the reconnect's `send-keys` it is the reconnect's `transient` answer (the `waiting` branch below), and at the `working`-row wait's `status` reads it is transient instead: the wait goes on, and at its timeout it ends `not-reconnected` (b.jg5 SRJ-605; the `working` branch below). A refusal logs one line, posts no spawn-failure notice, records no `spawn-failed` entry and ends the ladder with `failed`. Nothing is deleted, killed to recover or launched after it. Every other outcome takes the branch below as described, notices included. A `failed` result whose last agent-director error in the attempt armed the timer is marked `refused`, which the restart path does not count (Auto-Restart step 5). The timer then retries the persona on its own (Auto-Restart, UNAVAILABLE retry). Dry run makes no agent-director call, so it arms nothing.
   - On `ErrInstanceIdCollision`, call `client.get({claude_instance_id})` through the shared own-row read (`readPersonaOwnRow`) and keep the whole row. **The row-read rule decides first (b.jg5 SRJ-114, SRJ-513):** a read that latched the persona (its own row reading `pending` with no launch start, or a `provenance_conflict` note on its own row, the persona configured, or an UNUSABLE_NAME answer to the `get`, b.jg5 SRJ-512; see [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)) answers `latched` before the `cwd` and `config_dir` guards and the state branches, whatever the row's state: no wait, sweep, reconnect, sequence or launch, no notice, nothing counted. Any other note, or none, goes on below. **`cwd` guard (b.av2 SR-6.2 as amended, b.jg5 SRJ-1503)** first, before any state branch and so before any `findMissing` sweep or reconnect: a row whose `cwd` differs from the persona's working directory by real path (`compareRowToPersona`; a symlink to the directory matches, a row with no `cwd` never does) is never resumed, reconnected or waited on, whatever its state and `resume_enabled`. It is replaced on every ladder path with no row deleted: a live row goes through the live-row sequence, then a reuse spawn; a finished row gets a reuse spawn. It logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: "<name>" (key=<key>) row cwd=<row cwd> differs from working_directory=<dir> (state=<state>) — replacing the row by a reuse spawn of the same id; nothing is deleted`, then goes to the replace step (below) with the collision `get`'s state as the state last read. A row that also fails the `config_dir` check below is handled here. At start the sweep (step 4) has already removed rows in another directory, so this guard mostly catches runtime relaunches. **Unresolvable working directory (b.av2 SR-6.4):** when the row's `cwd` does not match, the persona's working directory has no real path at that moment, and the row's `cwd` has no real path either (`cwdCheckDeferred`), the row cannot be shown to be elsewhere, so it is kept: no replacement. The ladder logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: "<name>" (key=<key>) working_directory=<dir> cannot be resolved to a real path — keeping its row (cwd=<row cwd>, state=<state>); the launch fails and is retried by the restart path`, raises `cwd-unreachable` for the persona and returns `failed`. A row whose `cwd` equals the missing path lexically matches and goes on to the state branches. A row whose `cwd` resolves to an existing directory elsewhere isn't deferred: it is replaced through the replace step like any other `cwd` mismatch. The deferral covers only this `cwd` guard; the `resume_enabled=false` and `config_dir` paths below replace the row, and the `ErrNoSessionId` and `ErrJsonl*` paths make their reuse spawn, whatever the directory's state. Otherwise branch on state per the [SR-11 substitution table](#sr-11-substitution-table):
     - **The replace step (b.jg5 SRJ-707, SRJ-709; `replacePersonaRow`).** Every row the ladder cannot keep (the `cwd` guard above, `resume_enabled=false`, the `config_dir` guard and the `pending` step's `cwd` and `config_dir` comparison, below) goes through one step that never deletes, never kills and never launches over a live row. It decides on the row state the path last read: the collision `get`'s state for the `cwd` guard and the `ended`/`missing` and `pending` branches; on a dead-session path (`reconcileMissingFirst`) the collision `get`'s `waiting` or the working-row wait's last read, a live row unless the route's cause is a row read (`deadSessionLastRead`: no row for `row-absent`, the state read for `row-read-finished`); on the prompt-row recovery the re-read after its sweep, which read it finished.
       - **A finished row** (`ended`, `missing` or no row) gets one reuse spawn of the same id (`reuseSpawnForPersona`, [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708): `buildSpawnParams`'s params, the persona's `extra_env` included, with `reuse_finished: true`) through the finished-row branch (`reuseFinishedRow`), with no second trust patch. The step first logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: replacing the row of <ref> (<why>; last read <state>): a reuse spawn of the same id; nothing is deleted (b.jg5 SRJ-707)`, `<why>` being `resume_enabled is false`, `its cwd differs from the persona's working directory` or `its config_dir label is missing or differs`, and `<state>` the state read, `no-row` or `unreadable`. The reuse's outcomes are its own table's: a success answers `spawned` and keeps the old row as an earlier life; UNAVAILABLE and every other refusal answer the uncounted refused result and post no onset at once; a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME latches; `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` and a directory error are one counted launch failure; `ErrInvalidFlags` gets its version re-check and, unless that stops the server, holds the persona (`held`, launching nothing); an `ErrInternal` is never counted. A collision (`ErrInstanceIdCollision`: the row turned live) launched nothing. The first logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: the <what> of <ref> collided with a live row — nothing launched; re-running get-then-act once (b.jg5 SRJ-112)` and re-runs this step's get-then-act once (`ladderGetThenAct`, marked as the re-run): its collision `get` reads the row again and its branches decide again. A collision in that re-run makes no further call, arms the persona's retry timer with `reuse-collision` (`reportReuseCollisionAtSite`, `outage-state.ts`) and answers the uncounted refused result (`failed` marked `refused`): no spawn-failure notice, no entry, nothing counted, with `[slack] spawnForPersona: the <what> of <ref> collided with a live row again, in the re-run of get-then-act — nothing launched; answering the uncounted refused result, no spawn-failure notice, nothing counted; the retry timer is armed (cause=reuse-collision; b.jg5 SRJ-112)` (`could not be armed` outside an attempt with a trigger sink). `<what>` is `reuse spawn`, or `reuse spawn after its resume's no-transcript answer` for the no-transcript step, which goes through the same branch.
       - **A live row** (any other state, `pending` and an unreadable state included) is never launched over: the step starts the live-row sequence through the session manager's start entry (`startLiveRowSequence`; [The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)) with the state last read as its seed, entry at step 1, the conversation not kept, the retired-key flag set for a retired key (the reason `its key is retired and <mark words>`, [Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)), a launch at the end and the kill-failure alert context `recovery`. The sequence's checked kills and judged runs come first, and its step-6 launch is a reuse spawn of the same id. The step makes no other call and answers `sequence-waiting` (which `launchSession` maps to the uncounted `'refused'`) whatever the start entry answers, except `held`, which answers `held` (the persona is held on `ErrInvalidFlags`, `LIVE_ROW_START_HELD`), logging `[slack] spawnForPersona: replacing the row of <ref> (<why>; last read <state>): a live row goes through the live-row sequence first, which ends in a reuse spawn of the same id; start answered <answer> — answering <sequence-waiting|held>; no other call, nothing counted (b.jg5 SRJ-707, SRJ-705, SRJ-706)` (for a retired key the line reads `… goes through the live-row sequence first (its key is retired), which ends …` and its reference list ends `SRJ-706, SRJ-805)`), `<answer>` being `started`, `already-running`, `closed`, `not-installed` or `held`; the registry or the start entry logs its own line for each answer but `started`.
       - **A resume site's replacement with no dead evidence (b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611, SRJ-707; `replaceAtResumeSite`).** `resumeOrFreshSpawn`'s two replacements (`resume_enabled=false` and the `config_dir` guard) reach the step through `replaceAtResumeSite`. A row last read finished, or a path holding dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)), goes to the step as above. A row last read live on a path with no dead evidence (a dead-session route whose cause is `row-not-interactive`, or none carried) is not acted on from that earlier read, since the row may have finished since or be `pending` under another process's launch: the row is read again with one `get` through the shared own-row read (what `get before replacing`), and the fresh state decides. This never starts the live-row sequence itself. A read that latched the persona answers `latched`; a refused read answers the refusal result (`failed`; the `get` armed its read-error cause); `ended`, `missing` or no row goes to the step with the re-read state, so its reuse spawn of the same id; `pending` goes to the ladder's `pending` step (below: a covered row is left, a row that is not covered gets SRJ-411's sequence there); a known live state other than `pending`, or a state CSCB does not know (an unreadable one included, named `state=unreadable`), is the lost race of the not-resumable step (below): nothing killed, deleted or launched, `spawn-not-resumable-lost-race` armed, the uncounted refused result. One line (`replaceRereadLine`): `[slack] spawnForPersona: replacing the row of <ref> (<why>; last read <state>; <evidence>) — the path holds no dead evidence, so the row is read again first: re-read: <re-read> — <outcome> (b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611, SRJ-707)`, `<outcome>` being `the persona is latched: answering latched; nothing more is called for it`, `the read was refused: answering the refusal result; nothing more is called`, `the row is finished: the replace step's reuse spawn of the same id`, `a launch in progress: no live-row sequence of its own; the ladder's pending step decides`, or the lost race's outcome (`a lost race: nothing killed, deleted or launched; …`).
     - **`config_dir` guard before any resume (b.av2 SR-6.2 as amended, b.jg5 SRJ-1504).** `resumeOrFreshSpawn` compares the row's `config_dir` label (from the collision `get` above) with `personaConfigDirLabelValue` of the persona's current effective `claude_config_dir`, through `compareRowToPersona`. It runs after the `resume_enabled=false` branch and after the `reconcileMissingFirst` sweep (b.4dk), immediately before `client.resume(...)`, so it covers both the `ended`/`missing` resume and the dead-session resume. When the directory stopped resolving since the pre-launch check (`configDirResolved: false`), there is no verdict: the row is kept, nothing is launched and the persona is held as above (`deferred`). On a mismatch or a missing label it does not resume, because agent-director's `ResumeParams` carries only the instance ID and a resume keeps the old `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: a live row goes through the live-row sequence, then a reuse spawn of the same id (a new life); a finished row gets that reuse spawn directly; no row is deleted (the replace step above, through `replaceAtResumeSite`, so a row last read live on a path with no dead evidence is read again first). The old history stays in the old directory, archived to the earlier life; no transcript was lost, so neither `diagnoseJsonlMissing` nor an amnesia action runs. Log: `[slack] spawnForPersona: "<name>" (key=<key>) config_dir label missing (label absent, now=<hex> for claude_config_dir=<dir>) — not resuming; replacing its row by a reuse spawn of the same id`, or `config_dir label changed (was=<old hex>, now=<new hex> for claude_config_dir=<dir>)` with the same tail; `<dir>` is `<default>` when none is configured. The replace step's line follows.
     - `ended` / `missing` + `resume_enabled` → `config_dir` guard above, then `client.resume(...)`, logged `[slack] spawnForPersona: attempting resume for <ref>`. **`resume`'s outcomes (b.jg5 SRJ-113; `resumeAtSite`).** One handler decides them, by name or class, at both `resume` sites: here and at the live-row sequence's final launch (its `resume` leg, [The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717), whose lines start `[slack] live-row-sequence:`). Only the no-transcript and not-resumable rows differ between the two sites. Nothing assumes a failed `resume` restored the row (HO rev 28): a later read of the row decides.
       - success → `[slack] spawnForPersona: resumed <ref>`, the after-launch step (Pre-session dialog approval below), action `resumed`;
       - `ErrNoSessionId` / `ErrJsonlMissing` / `ErrJsonlNeverWritten` (by name, `isNoTranscriptResumeError`) → the no-transcript step (below);
       - `ErrSpawnNotResumable` (by name) → the not-resumable step (below; b.jg5 SRJ-710);
       - `ErrSpawnNotFound` (by name; the row vanished between the dead-session verdict and the resume: expired, or a race) → one plain spawn of the same id (`plainSpawnAfterResumeNotFound`): `buildSpawnParams`'s params with no reuse flag, inside which agent-director makes its pre-spawn scan (b.jg5 SRJ-111). It logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: ErrSpawnNotFound on resume for <ref> — fresh-spawn: one plain spawn of the same id, which makes agent-director's pre-spawn scan; no spawn-failure notice for the ErrSpawnNotFound (b.jg5 SRJ-113, SRJ-111)` (`resumeNotFoundSpawnLine`), and posts no spawn-failure notice for the `ErrSpawnNotFound` itself. A success logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: fresh-spawned (after ErrSpawnNotFound on resume) for <ref>`, runs the after-launch step and answers `spawned`; a failure takes the plain spawn's handling (`plainSpawnFailedAt`, `<what>` `fresh spawn after ErrSpawnNotFound on resume`): its CONFLICT latches with the refused operation `plain-spawn` and the state the path last read before the `resume`, and its `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` is one counted launch failure;
       - CONFLICT → the persona latches with the refused operation `resume`, whatever the case ("this row's own id", "left over from an earlier life", "no valid instance id", "a different instance id", "another agent-director store", or "conflicting labels", which a stray `@ad_owner` value or a duplicate label gives after "duplicate session" too), and the state the path last read; never a kill (the CONFLICT bullet below);
       - UNUSABLE_NAME → the persona latches with the refused operation `none` (the UNUSABLE_NAME bullet below);
       - UNAVAILABLE (a launch timeout included), ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`), CONFIG and UNCLASSIFIED → a refusal (the launch attempt above);
       - `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` → one counted launch failure that kills nothing, makes no spawn in its place and arms the retry timer at once in pending-only mode (the `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` bullet below);
       - DIRECTORY (`ErrCwdNotFound`, `ErrCwdNotADirectory`) → `failed`, counted; the wrapper raised `cwd-unreachable`;
       - `ErrInvalidFlags` → the `ErrInvalidFlags` step, then UNCLASSIFIED (below).

       **The no-transcript step (b.jg5 SRJ-707, SRJ-712; `noTranscriptReuse`).** The row `resume` refused for these reasons is finished, so the persona is brought up fresh by one reuse spawn of the same id (`reuseSpawnForPersona`, [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)) through the replace step's finished-row branch (`reuseFinishedRow`), and nothing is deleted, killed or plain-spawned. The ladder first logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: <failure> on resume for <ref> — a reuse spawn of the same id follows; nothing is deleted (b.jg5 SRJ-707)`. On `ErrJsonlMissing` specifically, `diagnoseJsonlMissing` runs **before** the reuse spawn, which resets the row it reads (see the b.wrb / b.fwu note below); a latched or refused diagnosis read ends the step with no reuse. The reuse is given the row state last read (the diagnosis `get`'s when it made one, else the caller's) and runs no second trust patch. A success after `ErrJsonlMissing` returns action `fresh-after-amnesia` (definite lost/never-created verdict) or `fresh-after-inconclusive-amnesia` (b.fwu — diagnosis inconclusive) rather than `spawned`, except for a recorded key: its reuse's `fresh-retired` (the key's new life has begun, its mark set; [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)) is answered as it is, with no amnesia result, and the diagnosis's persona notice is not posted; when the diagnosis held a notice, one line says so, `[slack] spawnForPersona: <ref>'s key is retired, so its reuse spawn answered fresh-retired — answering it, not an amnesia result; the lost-transcript diagnosis's persona notice is not posted (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-806)`. The amnesia results keep the startup summary from counting a memory-loss recovery as an ordinary clean spawn. `ErrNoSessionId` and `ErrJsonlNeverWritten` skip the diagnosis entirely and return plain `spawned` (b.jgf — see the note below). Every other reuse answer is the reuse spawn's own ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)), a CONFLICT latching with the refused operation `reuse-spawn`. A reuse collision (`ErrInstanceIdCollision`: the row is live again) takes the finished-row branch's one re-run of get-then-act, and a second collision arms `reuse-collision` and answers the uncounted refused result (the replace step above).

       **A `resume`'s `ErrInvalidFlags` (b.jg5 SRJ-104), at either `resume` site,** goes through the `ErrInvalidFlags` step (`classifyWithInvalidFlagsRecheck`, see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)): one immediate agent-director version re-check, then class UNCLASSIFIED. Nothing is deleted, killed or launched because of it, and no spawn-failure notice is raised. A re-check that stops ends the server as the runtime re-check defines (`ad-version-gate.ts`): one line built from the classification only, `[slack] spawnForPersona: resume failed for <ref>: class=UNCLASSIFIED name=ErrInvalidFlags[ message="…"] (after one immediate agent-director version re-check: stop)`, and the `failed` action is marked `stopping`, which `launchSession` answers as `'skipped'` (not counted). After any other re-check answer it is an UNCLASSIFIED refusal (b.jg5 SRJ-313): `reportUnclassifiedAtSite` arms the persona's retry timer with the `unclassified` cause and reports the outcome to its unclassified-error episode, and the one line is the refusal line, `[slack] spawnForPersona: resume refused for <ref>: class=UNCLASSIFIED name=ErrInvalidFlags[ message="…"] (after one immediate agent-director version re-check: <pass|could-not-run|not-running>) — no spawn-failure notice; nothing more is called (b.jg5 SRJ-105)`; the `failed` action is refused, never counted.
     - `ended` / `missing` + `resume_enabled=false` → not resumed (never reaches the `config_dir` guard): `[slack] spawnForPersona: resume_enabled=false for <ref> — not resuming; replacing its row by a reuse spawn of the same id`, then the replace step with the collision `get`'s finished state, so one reuse spawn of the same id. On a dead-session path the same branch decides on that path's last read and its evidence: a row last read live goes through the live-row sequence when the path holds dead evidence, and is read again first otherwise (`replaceAtResumeSite`, the replace step above).
     - **`ErrSpawnNotResumable` on a resume — the not-resumable step (b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-611; `spawnNotResumableAtLadder`).** It is never by itself a reason to kill and replace, and it is no reuse site. The step reads the row once more with one `get` through the shared own-row read (`notResumableStep`, what `get after ErrSpawnNotResumable`; [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)), so its note and launch-start latches apply, and decides on that re-read with the dead evidence the path holds ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611); `decideNotResumable`):
       - **The read latched the persona** (or found it latched) → `latched`, nothing more called.
       - **`pending`: a launch in progress, not a failure.** Nothing is counted or posted, and the `ErrSpawnNotResumable` starts no live-row sequence of its own, whatever evidence the path holds. The row goes to the ladder's `pending` step (`ladderPendingRowStep`, the `pending` branch below), whose answer is the ladder's: a covered row is left (`no-op`), with no kill and no launch, and a row that is not covered (its `cwd` or `config_dir` label differing) gets the replace step's live-row sequence (b.jg5 SRJ-411). Nothing is armed beyond what that step arms.
       - **A known live state other than `pending` (`AGENT_DIRECTOR_LIVE_STATES`), on a path holding dead evidence** (GONE-based: the reconnect's `tmux-gone`, the prompt row's `prompt-row-ladder-gone`, or a GONE-based verdict the restart path carried in) → one live-row sequence through `startLiveRowSequence`, seeded with the re-read state, entry at step 1, the conversation kept, the retired-key flag unset (a `resume` was made, so the key was not recorded; the start entry sets the flag if it is recorded by then), a launch at the end and alert context `recovery`; its step 6 is a `resume` when the row has a session id and the persona may resume it ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)). The ladder makes no other call, counts nothing and answers `sequence-waiting` whatever the start entry answers, except `held`, which answers `held`.
       - **Otherwise: a lost race** (a known live state with no dead evidence, a state CSCB does not know or an unreadable one whatever evidence the path holds, `ended`, `missing`, no row, or a read refused by the shared read's own error rows, whose read-error cause it armed). Nothing is killed, deleted or launched, nothing is posted or counted, the persona's retry timer is armed with `spawn-not-resumable-lost-race` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_LOST_RACE`, through `reportLostRaceAtSite`, `outage-state.ts`) and the ladder answers the uncounted refused result (`failed` marked `refused`), so the persona is decided again at its next tick or retry.

       One line (`spawnNotResumableLine`): `[slack] spawnForPersona: <failure> on resume for <ref> — re-read: <re-read>; <evidence> — <outcome> (b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-611)`, `<re-read>` being `state=<state>`, `state=no-row`, `the read failed` or `the read latched the persona`, `<evidence>` the dead evidence the path held (`describeDeadEvidence`), and `<outcome>` one of:
       - `the persona is latched: answering latched; nothing more is called for it` (`REREAD_LATCHED_OUTCOME`);
       - `a launch in progress, not a failure: nothing counted or posted, and no live-row sequence of its own; the ladder's pending step decides` (`NOT_RESUMABLE_PENDING_OUTCOME`), followed by the `pending` step's own line;
       - `the path holds dead evidence and the row is live: the live-row sequence, with the conversation kept (alert context recovery), ending in resume; start answered <answer> — answering <sequence-waiting|held>; no other call, nothing counted` (`notResumableSequenceOutcome`), `<answer>` being `started`, `already-running`, `closed`, `not-installed` or `held`, and the ladder answering `sequence-waiting` whatever the start entry answers, except `held`, which answers `held`;
       - `a lost race: nothing killed, deleted or launched; answering the uncounted refused result, no spawn-failure notice, nothing counted; the retry timer is armed (cause=spawn-not-resumable-lost-race)` (`lostRaceOutcome`; `could not be armed` outside an attempt with a trigger sink).

       At the live-row sequence's own `resume` the same re-read runs with the sequence barred: it never starts a second sequence ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717), step 6).
     - `waiting` → the reconnect, `reconnectMcpWithCause(key, lastRead, ref)` with the collision `get`'s `waiting` as its last read, makes exactly one `send-keys` of `/mcp reconnect slack-channel-router` through `withOutageDetection` (the tmux-touching `send-keys` verb; the library appends Enter). It never retries, starts no tmux server and makes no tmux call of its own (b.jg5 SRJ-118, SRJ-609). It logs `reconnectStartLine` (`[slack] reconnecting MCP server "slack-channel-router": <ref>`), then, on a failure, one line from its builder, and decides its answer by class and name through the classifier:
       - a persona already latched (`personaLatchedNow`) → no `send-keys`; `transient`, latched (`reconnectLatchedLine`);
       - success → `ok`; the ladder answers `reconnected`;
       - GONE (`ErrTmuxSendKeys`) → `dead-session` with cause `tmux-gone`, at once (`reconnectGoneLine`);
       - `ErrSpawnNotInteractive` → `dead-session` with cause `row-not-interactive` (b.dup; `reconnectNotInteractiveLine`). The row finished after the `get` read it (a findMissing sweep, such as the one another persona's launch wait starts with, marked it `missing`), or it reads `pending` and the session holding the persona's name may be another launch's. A finished row is not proof that the worker is gone, so this is only a route into the recovery's decision, and the line claims nothing about the worker's process (b.jg5 SRJ-609);
       - `ErrSpawnNotFound` → `dead-session` with cause `row-absent`: a row read, not a GONE (`reconnectRowAbsentLine`);
       - CONFLICT → the persona latches through the latch's CONFLICT entry with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery" and the last read (b.jg5 SRJ-501); `transient`, latched. Its one line (`reconnectConflictLine`) names the case and, for "not this launch's session", adds `RECONNECT_NOT_THIS_LAUNCH_NOTE` (a leftover of an earlier launch may hold the persona's session, b.jg5 SRJ-613). Nothing was typed, and the refused `send-keys` is never retried;
       - UNUSABLE_NAME → the persona latches through the unusable-name entry (refused operation `none`, the last read, b.jg5 SRJ-512); `transient`, latched (`reconnectUnusableNameLine`);
       - `ErrInvalidFlags` → the `ErrInvalidFlags` step (one immediate version re-check), then UNCLASSIFIED: `transient`, marked `stopping` when the re-check stopped the server (`reconnectInvalidFlagsLine`);
       - UNAVAILABLE (timeouts included), ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG and UNCLASSIFIED (`ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed` and `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` included), and any STATE, LAUNCH_FAILURE or DIRECTORY name not named above → `transient` (`reconnectTransientLine`, naming the class); the wrapper has raised the error's outage, armed the persona's retry timer and reported an UNCLASSIFIED answer to its unclassified-error episode.

       No answer posts a spawn-failure notice, records a `spawn-failed` entry or counts anything, and nothing is typed on any path but success. The ladder maps the answer. A `dead-session`, whatever its cause, takes the dead-session route (`deadSessionRoute`, b.jg5 SRJ-611): one line, `deadSessionRouteLine`, `[slack] spawnForPersona: dead session for <ref> (state=<state>) — <evidence>[; the restart path carried in <carried evidence>]; the path <holds dead evidence|holds no dead evidence>; recovering via resume/fresh-spawn (b.jg5 SRJ-611)`, naming the route's own cause (`cause=tmux-gone: dead evidence (GONE-based)`, or `cause=row-not-interactive: not dead evidence`, `cause=row-absent: not dead evidence`) and any verdict the restart path carried into the launch, then `resumeOrFreshSpawn(..., { reconcileMissingFirst: true })` (see the note below) with the evidence the path holds ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)), whose resume or spawn decides what holds the persona's name (agent-director classifies any leftover session, and a CONFLICT there latches the persona). A `transient` (`transientReconnectResult`, one `transientReconnectLine`) answers `failed` marked `stopping` after a re-check stop; `latched` when the reconnect latched or found the persona latched, or the latched query answers it latched; and otherwise the uncounted refused result (`failed` marked `refused`, which `launchSession` answers `'refused'`). Nothing more is called after a `transient` answer. The dialog approver's Enter `send-keys` is another site, with its own handling (**Pre-session dialog approval** below).
     - `working` → `waitForWaitingAndReconnect(...)` runs an up-front `findMissing({})` sweep via the shared `reconcileMissingSweep` helper (b.m4r — see note below), then polls `client.status(...)` until `waiting`, then sendKeys. While the row reads `working`, the wait also reads the persona's pane and, when it sits idle, the session's transcript, and a row that evidence shows stale is reconnected the same way (b.f2b, see note below). A `'dead-session'` verdict likewise takes the dead-session route, with the wait's cause (`waitForWaitingAndReconnectWithCause`, `WaitDeadSession`): the reconnect's own, `row-absent` for an absent row, or `row-read-finished` with the state read; only the reconnect's `tmux-gone` is dead evidence. Both `status` reads go through the shared own-row `status` read ([The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115)): an UNUSABLE_NAME answer there, or the persona's own row reading `pending` with no launch start (b.jg5 SRJ-513), latches the persona and ends the wait `latched` (a latched wait, below), never `'dead-session'`. `ErrSpawnNotFound` there gives `'dead-session'`, and any other `status` error is transient: the wait goes on, and never answers `'transient'` for it (b.jg5 SRJ-605; **b.ecw terminal verdicts**, below). The wait's reconnect is the same one-`send-keys` reconnect, with the row state the wait read just before as its last read (`waiting`, or `working` for a stale row), and its answer is the wait's, unchanged. The wait answers `'transient'` for that reconnect's `transient`, for a refused findMissing sweep and for a stop its evidence read's version re-check decided; the ladder maps it as the `waiting` branch maps the reconnect's (`stopping`, `latched` or the uncounted refused result), and a `'dead-session'` the same way too. No `working`-branch outcome records a `spawn-failed` entry. A `'not-reconnected'` verdict (the wait ended with the session alive and nothing typed) returns the action `not-reconnected`; `reconnected` means `/mcp reconnect` was typed. Right before the wait the ladder calls `hooks.onWorkingRowWait` (`LaunchHooks`, given only to the ladder a `spawnForPersona` call starts, never to a call that joins one), where the start pass parks the launch (b.f2b, see the parked-launch note below).
     - **b.4dk dead-session recovery — `reconcileMissingFirst`.** After a reboot/pod-resume a `waiting`/`working` row is frozen live-state but its tmux session is gone. AD's `resume` verb only accepts a terminal (`ended`/`missing`) row, so on such a row it throws `ErrSpawnNotResumable`, which takes the not-resumable step (above) and is never by itself a reason to kill. When `reconcileMissingFirst` is set (only the dead-session route of the `waiting` and `working` branches sets it, for every cause, dead evidence or not; b.jg5 SRJ-611 narrows only the evidence the route carries, never this run), `resumeOrFreshSpawn` runs a `findMissing({})` sweep via the shared `reconcileMissingSweep` helper before `resume`. AD's per-row, evidence-based sweep (requires agent-director ≥ 0.8.0, plan b.93m t1.93m.hp: degraded-mode guard removed) can move a row whose process is gone to `missing`, so the subsequent `resume` succeeds and restores the pre-reboot transcript (provided the row passes the `config_dir` guard, which runs after this sweep). Skipped when `resume_enabled=false`. A refused sweep (UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED, b.jg5 SRJ-105) answers the refused `failed` before the `config_dir` guard and the resume: a resume of the still-live row would answer `ErrSpawnNotResumable`. Any other `findMissing` error (UNUSABLE_NAME, for example) → fall through to `resume` anyway (an `ErrSpawnNotResumable` then takes the not-resumable step). A persona latched once the sweep is done (`FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`: the run's `get` of its own row in `unverified_ids` read the `provenance_conflict` note, or the latch answers it latched, b.jg5 SRJ-120, SRJ-502) answers `latched` with one line, `[slack] spawnForPersona: <ref> is latched after the findMissing sweep before resume — not resuming; nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`, and gets no further call: no resume, sequence or spawn. The `ended`/`missing` collision branch above does NOT set the flag (row already terminal).
     - **b.m4r `working`-row stall — up-front `findMissing` sweep.** A bot killed mid-turn (its tmux session ended under it) leaves its AD row at `working`. Its `SessionEnd` does fire, but agent-director only soft-refreshes the row (`working` → `working`): it marks a row `ended` only for the `SessionEnd` reasons `logout`, `prompt_input_exit` and `exit`. The row stays `working` until a `findMissing` sweep reconciles it. Without a reconcile, `waitForWaitingAndReconnect`'s poll loop spins on `status` for the full `WAIT_FOR_WAITING_TIMEOUT_MS` window (10 min) before the timeout verdict finally returns `'dead-session'` — the channel stays down that whole time. `waitForWaitingAndReconnect` therefore runs AD's per-row, evidence-based `findMissing({})` sweep before entering the poll loop (requires agent-director ≥ 0.8.0, same b.93m t1.93m.hp capability as the `reconcileMissingFirst` path). A genuinely-dead row reconciles to `missing`, so the **first** status poll hits the ended/missing branch and returns `'dead-session'` in seconds; a genuinely-alive long-turn row is untouched by the evidence-based sweep and keeps the existing polling behavior (long-turn guard preserved). A refused sweep (UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED, b.jg5 SRJ-105) ends the wait `'transient'`, before any `status` read. On any other `findMissing` error (UNUSABLE_NAME, for example), the sweep is logged and skipped and the poll loop proceeds unchanged. This prefers AD's `findMissing` verb over a CSCB-side tmux probe, mirroring `resumeOrFreshSpawn`'s `reconcileMissingFirst` branch (docs/engineering-guide.md, "Avoiding Duplicated Effort"). The sweep leaves a live session's row alone, so a `working` row that is stale while its session runs idle is handled by the b.f2b positive-idle rule below, not here.
     - **b.f2b stale `working` row — the positive-idle rule.** agent-director can leave a row `working` after the turn ended, with the session idle at its prompt, and nothing moves it back. The pane alone can't prove the session idle: Claude Code 2.1.280 can draw a live turn with no spinner (an API retry or stall shows static rows with no glyph and no timer). So while the row reads `working`, the wait reads its evidence every `WORKING_ROW_READ_INTERVAL_MS` (5 s; the first status poll reads at once, later polls in between read nothing, because every agent-director call goes through one queue shared by every persona) and folds it into the wait's run (`staleWorkingRowIsIdle`, `WorkingPaneWatch`):
       - **The pane.** `readPane` (last `FULL_PANE_READ_LINES` = 40 lines, `readWorkingPane`, through the shared read-pane `readPersonaOwnPane`; see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The shared read-pane**). A CONFLICT answer latches the persona with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery" (b.jg5 SRJ-501), and an UNUSABLE_NAME answer through the unusable-name entry (b.jg5 SRJ-512), each with the wait's last read (b.jg5 SRJ-117); a persona already latched is not read. Either way the wait ends `latched` at once, with no further call and nothing typed (b.jg5 SRJ-608; a latched wait, below). An UNCLASSIFIED answer carrying the reader's stop mark (its `ErrInvalidFlags` version re-check decided that the server stops, b.jg5 SRJ-205) logs one line and ends the wait `'transient'` with the stop noted, no further call and nothing typed; the ladder answers a `failed` result marked `stopping`, with no spawn-failure notice and no `spawn-failed` entry, and `launchSession` answers `'skipped'`. Every other failed read (GONE, an absent row, UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG, any other UNCLASSIFIED) is no evidence, and the wait goes on. `classifyWorkingPane` reads it as `prompt` when its bottom 12 lines show a dialog, anchored to Claude Code's layout (`paneShowsDialog`): a numbered option list (an option `1.` and, below it, an option `2.`) with the `❯` cursor on one of its options, plus a question line ending in `?` above it, a dialog option or footer (`DIALOG_NEEDLES`: a permission dialog's deny option, the select-menu footers, the pre-session dialogs' options) on or below it, or its options inside the dialog's box (`│`). Otherwise it is `busy` for Claude Code's spinner line anywhere (`BUSY_SPINNER_LINE_RE`, in the spinner's own shape: at column 0 a spinner glyph, a space, a short message with no ellipsis, which can be several words (a custom `spinnerVerbs` verb or a task's `activeForm`), then an ellipsis ending the line or followed by ` (` and the turn's status; a line that starts with `●`, which Linux also draws before every reply and tool call, counts only as a single word and an ellipsis ending the line, or with a status that starts with an elapsed time, a token arrow or `thinking`), for `to interrupt` or `esc to cancel` in the bottom lines (`BUSY_PANE_NEEDLES`), or for an API retry row there (`BUSY_API_RETRY_ROWS`: `No response from the API after … · retrying` with its `A proxy or gateway that buffers…` line, `Rate limit reached · Retrying in`, `Waiting for API response · will retry in`, `· attempt n/m`); `blank` with no text; else `idle`. A prompt outranks a busy sign. The patterns are verified against Claude Code 2.1.280.
       - **The transcript**, read only when the pane is `idle` (`readPersonaTranscript`): the row is fetched through the shared own-row read (`readPersonaOwnRow`, one `get` through `withOutageDetection`), its transcript located with the persona's effective `claude_config_dir` (`locateTranscript`: the row's `jsonl_path` when it names the row's `claude_session_id`, else `<claude_config_dir>/projects/<cwd slug>/<claude_session_id>.jsonl`), and its last 256 KiB read (`readTranscriptTurnState`, `src/session-transcript.ts`). It is `ended` when its last conversation entry is a completed turn (Claude's final reply, or the user's interrupt marker), else `open` (a Stop hook's context or blocking error after the reply keeps the turn open); an absent row (`ErrSpawnNotFound`, reason `its agent-director row is absent (ErrSpawnNotFound)`), a failed `get`, a row that names no transcript or a file that can't be read is `unreadable`. A `get` that latched the persona (its own row reading `pending` with no launch start, b.jg5 SRJ-513, a `provenance_conflict` note, b.jg5 SRJ-114, or an UNUSABLE_NAME answer, b.jg5 SRJ-512) gives no evidence and nothing more is read; the wait then ends (a latched wait, below). The state the `get` read (the row's state, no row, or `unreadable` for an UNUSABLE_NAME answer) becomes the wait's last read (b.jg5 SRJ-501).
       - **The run** (`foldWorkingPaneRun`, the positive-idle rule). An `idle` pane read with an `ended` transcript continues an idle run only while the screen and the transcript's snapshot (path, device, inode, size, mtime) are both unchanged, and otherwise starts one. A `prompt` pane continues or starts a prompt run. A `busy` or `blank` pane, a failed pane read, or an idle pane whose transcript is `open` or `unreadable` ends the run: no evidence.
       - An idle run spanning `STALE_WORKING_WINDOW_MS` (60 s) means the row is stale: the reconnect, as the `waiting` branch makes it (with `working` as its last read), whatever `session_restart_delay` is (the reconnect is part of the launch, not an auto-restart). A live turn, an API retry included, never ends its transcript with a completed turn, so it is never taken for idle and never typed into (the b.rmy invariant).
       - A prompt run spanning the window is logged and reported through the `blocked-on-prompt` not-connected notice (saying whether auto-restart is disabled), once per wait; nothing is typed and the wait goes on.
       - A failed pane read is no evidence: the wait's first failure is logged and the wait goes on. An idle pane whose transcript gives no evidence is logged, again only when the reason changes, and the wait goes on.
       - Each poll that reads the row `working` without reconnecting it is one more deferral in the persona's run on the row (`noteWorkingRowDeferral`, the run kept per persona in `workingRowDeferredSince` and shared with the restart path); any other state ends the run. Once the run has lasted `UNPROVEN_IDLE_NOTICE_AFTER_MS` (10 min) from its first deferral, the `unproven-idle` not-connected notice is raised (*Not connected*: its session reads working but CSCB can't prove it's idle, so it won't type into it), whatever `session_restart_delay` is, once per episode; the wait goes on.
     - **b.f2b a cancelled wait.** The persona's teardown cancels the wait (`cancelWorkingRowWait`, see [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65)). Each wait registers itself per persona (`workingRowWaits`); a cancel sets its flag and wakes it from its poll sleep (`sleepUnlessCancelled`). The wait checks the flag after each agent-director call, types nothing once it is set, logs that it was cancelled and returns `'cancelled'`, which the ladder reports as `not-reconnected`. A cancel that finds a launch in flight that hasn't started its wait yet records the key (`cancelledLaunchWaits`, forgotten when that launch settles), so a wait it starts is cancelled from its first check.
     - **b.jg5 SRJ-502 a latched wait.** At the same points as the cancel check, after each agent-director call the wait makes (its `find-missing` sweeps, `status` reads, pane reads and transcript `get`s), it asks whether its persona is latched (`personaLatchedNow`: the launch gate's reading of the installed latch, where a query that throws or a record that can't be read counts as latched; false with no latch installed). A latch its own transcript `get`, pane read or poll or timeout `status` read set (a `pending` row with no launch start, b.jg5 SRJ-513, a note, an UNUSABLE_NAME answer, b.jg5 SRJ-512, or the pane read's CONFLICT answer, b.jg5 SRJ-501), one the `get` after a `find-missing` run's `unverified_ids` set (b.jg5 SRJ-120; its sweep then answers `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`), or one set elsewhere ends the wait with `latched` (`WAIT_OUTCOME_LATCHED`) and one line, `[slack] waitForWaitingAndReconnect: <ref> is latched — the wait ends; nothing more is called and nothing is typed (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`: no further call, nothing typed and no not-connected notice. The ladder answers `latched`. A cancelled wait still answers `cancelled`.
     - **b.f2b a wait that ends without a reconnect.** Every path that ends the wait with the session alive and nothing typed returns `'not-reconnected'` (`'ok'` always means `/mcp reconnect` was typed): a transition to `pending`, `ask_user` or `check_permission`; the timeout, when the row is live but not `waiting`; and the timeout, when its `status` read fails with any error but `ErrSpawnNotFound` (b.jg5 SRJ-605). A row that reads `waiting` at the timeout is reconnected. Each of these give-up lines ends with what actually happens next for the restart delay in effect (`reportWaitEndedDisconnected`, its line built by the exported `waitEndedDisconnectedLine` from a `WaitEndedReport`: `waitEndedOnStateReport`, `waitTimedOutLiveReport` or `waitTimedOutUnreadReport`): with auto-restart on, the health check's recovery; with `session_restart_delay` 0, that nothing will reconnect the persona, and the not-connected notice is raised (once per episode; see Health-Check Poller): `blocked-on-prompt` when the row ended at `ask_user` or `check_permission`, `unproven-idle` when the timeout finds it `working`, otherwise `auto-restart-disabled` with a fixed, token-free cause (for a row read in a state, `waitEndedOnStateReport` and `waitTimedOutLiveReport` pick the prompt or the `auto-restart-disabled` notice through the module-private `waitEndedNotice`, which is not exported; for a failed timeout read, `waitTimedOutUnreadReport` gives the cause itself: that agent-director could not report the persona's state when CSCB stopped waiting for it). At any delay the timeout on a `working` row is one more deferral, so a run that has lasted `UNPROVEN_IDLE_NOTICE_AFTER_MS` raises the `unproven-idle` notice there too. The lines are listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.
     - **b.ecw terminal verdicts key on agent-director's row, never on the tmux session (b.jg5 SRJ-605).** Every terminal branch of `waitForWaitingAndReconnect` decides off agent-director's row for the claude process (AD ≥ 0.8.0: `findMissing` verdicts per-row and evidence-based); the wait makes no tmux probe. Where it answers `'dead-session'`, the recovery's resume or spawn (`resumeOrFreshSpawn`) decides what holds the persona's name: agent-director classifies any leftover session, and a CONFLICT there latches the persona (b.jg5 SRJ-501). Each `'dead-session'` end carries one cause (`WaitDeadSession`, b.jg5 SRJ-611): a row read (`row-read-finished`, `row-absent`) is not dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)).
       - **ended/missing branch (in-loop):** keys on the process. `ended` means the process exited with a `SessionEnd` reason agent-director marks ended (see the b.m4r note above); `missing`, after the up-front sweep, is agent-director's sweep verdict on the row. One line, `waitRowFinishedLine` (`[slack] waitForWaitingAndReconnect: <ref>'s row reads state=<state> — dead session (cause=row-read-finished: not dead evidence); the recovery's resume or spawn decides what holds its name (b.ecw, b.jg5 SRJ-605, SRJ-611)`), then `'dead-session'` directly with the cause `row-read-finished` and the state read — **no tmux probe**. A finished row is not proof that the worker is gone, so the verdict routes it to `resumeOrFreshSpawn`, whose resume or spawn decides; a `resume` there that answers `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` because the name is still taken is one counted launch failure, and nothing is killed because of it (the `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` bullet below).
       - **timeout branch:** keys on the process via a **fresh** `reconcileMissingSweep` (the 10s memo has long expired at the 10-minute deadline) + one `status` call. A refused sweep (b.jg5 SRJ-105) answers `'transient'`, and no `status` call follows. `ended`/`missing` → `'dead-session'`, cause `row-read-finished` (`waitRowFinishedLine`, its timeout form `[slack] waitForWaitingAndReconnect: timed out for <ref> after <ms>ms — its row reads state=<state> — dead session (cause=row-read-finished: not dead evidence); …`); `waiting` → reconnect (b.f2b: the turn ended at the deadline); any other live state (working/ask_user/check_permission/pending) → `'not-reconnected'` (b.f2b), the process left alive (a process mid-long-turn is not an error — the b.rmy/b.3ce long-turn guard, keyed on the process). `ErrSpawnNotFound` → `'dead-session'`, as at the poll (below). An UNUSABLE_NAME answer, or the row reading `pending` with no launch start, latches the persona and ends the wait `latched` (b.jg5 SRJ-512, SRJ-513).
