Any other `status` error (UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG, UNCLASSIFIED, `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` included) → `'not-reconnected'` through `reportWaitEndedDisconnected` (`waitTimedOutUnreadReport`: the line names the error's class and no tmux session), never `'dead-session'` or `'transient'`, so an agent-director outage can't manufacture a `'dead-session'` (the b.rmy invariant) or a counted failure.
       - **ErrSpawnNotFound branch (in-loop and at the timeout):** the row is absent. One line (`waitRowAbsentLine`, naming `cause=row-absent: not dead evidence`), then `'dead-session'` directly, cause `row-absent`, with no tmux probe: the recovery's spawn classifies any leftover session.
       - **Any other `status` error (in-loop):** transient (b.jg5 SRJ-605): UNAVAILABLE, a timeout, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG and UNCLASSIFIED, `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` included. The wait sleeps its poll interval and polls again, with no post, no result of its own, no `failed` and nothing counted toward `recordFailure`. It logs its first failed read (`waitPollStatusErrorLine`, naming the error's class) and again only when the class changes. The wrapper (`withOutageDetection`) has raised the error's outage (`ad-unreachable`, also for `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`; `tmux-unavailable`; `ad-config-malformed`), armed the persona's retry timer and reported an UNCLASSIFIED answer to its unclassified-error episode, as at any row read in a launch attempt (b.jg5 SRJ-105, SRJ-301), so the launch's result follows the wait's outcome, never `refused`. A refused sweep, up front or at the timeout, is still a refusal (above).
     - **b.m4r shared memoized sweep — `sharedFindMissingSweep` (b.jg5 SRJ-120).** Every `findMissing({})` call goes through one memoized, single-flight core, `sharedFindMissingSweep` in `src/session-manager.ts`, never `client.findMissing({})` inline. A persona's runs go through the module-private `reconcileMissingSweep`, one call through `withOutageDetection` for that persona; the start sweep's post-kill run (`runStartSweepPostKillFindMissing`, step 4.6, over every row the sweep gave a kill, whatever its outcome) calls the start sweep's client directly and acts for no persona. The callers are this `working`-row wait's up-front and timeout sweeps, `resumeOrFreshSpawn`'s `reconcileMissingFirst`, the tick/restart escalate-dead path (the exported `sweepDeadTmuxChannelWithCause`, which the reconnect adapter calls, and `sweepDeadTmuxChannel`, the same without its answer; both log their unconditional operator line first), the two b.jdc prompt-row callers through `reconcileAndReadRowState` (the sweep, then one `status` read of the row: the ladder's prompt row whose one-line `read-pane` answered GONE or found the row absent, and the restart path's deferrals on a prompt row once they have run for 10 min), and the start sweep's post-kill run. Every one of them makes an ordinary run.
       - **Ordinary runs** (`FIND_MISSING_RUN_ORDINARY`, module-private). An ordinary caller joins the run in flight, if there is one, a bypassing run included. Otherwise it reuses the memoized result when that run's call resolved less than `FIND_MISSING_MEMO_TTL_MS` (10 s) ago, measured on the session manager's clock (`_now`), with no call and no `get`. Otherwise it starts a run. This only sheds load: on a fleet restart (`startupSessionManager` at `concurrency=3`) every `working`-row collision and each `reconcileMissingFirst` would otherwise fire its own whole-store sweep, and after a reboot that wipes `/tmp` (b.nk5) every persona escalates dead-tmux at once; one shared run reconciles the whole store for all of them.
       - **Bypassing runs** (`FIND_MISSING_RUN_BYPASSING`, module-private). The exported entry `bypassingFindMissingSweep(key, logPrefix, nextStepGetKey?)` always starts a new run through `withOutageDetection` for `key`, whatever is memoized or in flight, for a caller that must see a run made after its own step (a memo can predate that step). The new run becomes the run in flight, so ordinary callers arriving meanwhile join it, and its result is memoized for later ordinary callers like any other run's. The live-row sequence is its one caller: each of its runs is a bypassing run with the persona's key as `nextStepGetKey`, since the sequence's next step is its own `get` of that row ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717), started from the collision ladder's replacement sites). Its run line reads `bypassing findMissing sweep` where an ordinary run's reads `findMissing sweep`, and so do its failure and refusal lines. It answers as an ordinary run does (the result, `FIND_MISSING_REFUSED`, `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED` or `undefined`, below); a persona already latched before the run gets `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED` too, whatever the run found, while a refusal still answers `FIND_MISSING_REFUSED`. It never throws.
       - **Which result the memo keeps.** Runs are numbered as they start. A run that succeeds is memoized only when no run that started after it has been memoized already, so an older run resolving later never overwrites a newer result, and it clears the in-flight slot only while it is still the run there. Each run logs its line once, with its starter's prefix and reference: `[slack] <prefix>: findMissing sweep for <ref> — count=<n> ids=[…] unverified=<n> unverified_ids=[…]`.
       - **Failures are never memoized.** A failed run, of either kind, clears only its own in-flight slot, leaves any earlier memoized result in place and makes no `get`; the next ordinary caller starts a new run. A refused run (UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED, b.jg5 SRJ-105) answers `FIND_MISSING_REFUSED` to its starter and to each joiner alike, a bypassing run's included, each logging its own refusal line, and each caller stops its attempt (see the `refusalAt` sites above). Any other failure logs `[slack] <prefix>: findMissing sweep failed for <ref>: <failure> — proceeding` (`bypassing findMissing sweep failed` for a bypassing run), and the caller goes on. Sharing a run never changes whose retry timer arms (b.jg5 SRJ-301): the persona that starts a run reports its failure through its own `withOutageDetection`, and a persona that joins a run someone else started (another persona's, or the start sweep's direct call) reports the failure under its own key (`reportAgentDirectorError(key, err, 'find-missing')`), which arms only when the joiner runs inside its own launch or recovery attempt; when the run failed with ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`), the joiner first raises its own `tmux-unavailable` (b.jg5 SRJ-311) through `raiseTmuxUnavailable(key, err)`, which picks the onset from the error, as the starter's wrapper does for the starter, and with CONFIG (`ErrConfigMalformed`) its own `ad-config-malformed` the same way (b.jg5 SRJ-316). The start sweep acts for no persona, so its own failure is reported for none and is never a refusal.
       - **The not-judged reading.** `readFindMissingRow(result, id, stateBefore)` (pure) reads one row of a result: in `ids`, marked `missing` (`marked-missing`); in `unverified_ids`, judged and left live (`judged-left-live`); in neither, `not-judged` when its state before the run was `pending` (the row is inside agent-director's grace period, or its launch's worker process is alive), else `judged-alive`. A not-judged row means retry later, whatever time has passed, and is never a reason to escalate, alert or kill. The start sweep's post-kill line reads its killed rows this way (step 4).
       - **One `get` after `unverified_ids`.** When a run the server makes resolves (never at a memo reuse), and before its starter or any joiner goes on, each configured persona's own row listed in `unverified_ids` (`cscb_<key>`, with `<key>` a persona of the applied configuration now, by the installed configured-persona query) is read with one `get` through the shared own-row read (`readPersonaOwnRow`, through `withOutageDetection` for that persona, whatever persona the run was made for): each persona once, all at once, and the run waits for every read to settle before any caller goes on. Two rows are skipped. One is the row of the starter's next-step key (`nextStepGetKey`, which only the bypassing entry passes; a joiner's is not considered): that path's next step is itself a `get` of the row. The other is the row of a persona already latched when the run resolves (`personaLatchedNow`; a latched query that throws counts as latched): it gets no `get` and no latch call, so the persona is not relatched and nothing is posted for it, and its own caller still gets `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`. A `provenance_conflict` note on a row read this way latches its persona, as at any shared read (see [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)); an absent `get` changes nothing. A `get` that fails with any other error never fails the run, is never memoized as a failure and never stops the other `get`s; the run carries it to its callers (`refusedReads`), and only the caller whose persona's own row it was acts on it: a refusal answers that caller `FIND_MISSING_REFUSED` with its `post-sweep get refused` line, while an UNUSABLE_NAME answer latches that persona, as the note does, and its caller gets `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`, except in the start sweep's run (below) (see **Errors** under [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)); for every other caller it only shows in the line below. A refusal answers `FIND_MISSING_REFUSED` whether or not the persona is latched. Any other row in `unverified_ids` (another caller's, a pre-persona row, the `cscb_<key>` row of a key outside the applied configuration) gets no `get`, and a note on it is not acted on: it is not CSCB's to act on or post about. With no query installed, no row is read. When at least one listed persona was read or skipped, one line lists every one of them, in `unverified_ids` order, with what its read answered or that it was skipped as already latched: `[slack] <prefix>: after the findMissing sweep for <ref> — one get of each configured persona's own row in unverified_ids: persona=<key> <read|latched|absent|refused (<failure>)|skipped (latched)>, … (b.jg5 SRJ-120)`. With no configured persona listed, no line is logged. **The start sweep's run** (`FindMissingSweepOptions.startSweepRun`, which only `runStartSweepPostKillFindMissing` passes; a run another caller started keeps that caller's reads) makes its post-run `get`s with `unusableNameRoutedIn` set (`'the start sweep'`), so an UNUSABLE_NAME answer there latches nothing (b.jg5 SRJ-512, SRJ-1002): `readPersonaOwnRow` logs `[slack] reconcileOrphans: post-sweep get for persona=<key>: <failure> — UNUSABLE NAME met in the start sweep: routed to the server log; nothing latches (b.jg5 SRJ-512, SRJ-1002)` (`<failure>` through `describeAgentDirectorFailure`) and answers `refused` carrying the error, so the persona shows as `refused (<failure>)` in the line above; carried to a caller, it is no refusal (`postRunGetRefusal` answers false) and that caller goes on as after any read. The note and launch-start decisions still latch in that run. The start sweep also passes `postRunGetsGo` (`FindMissingSweepOptions.postRunGetsGo`, the negation of its shutdown stop), asked once when the run it started returns: an answer other than true, or a throw, makes none of the post-run `get`s, and the run logs `[slack] <prefix>: after the <run> — no post-sweep get is made: its caller stopped (b.jg5 SRJ-120, SRJ-714)` instead; nothing is latched or refused. With the option absent, as for every other caller, the `get`s are made.
       - **A latched persona stops its path (b.jg5 SRJ-502).** A persona's caller gets `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED` instead of the result when its persona is latched once the sweep is done: the run's `get` latched it, or the latch answers it latched (`personaLatchedNow`), asked after a memo reuse, a run, a join or a failure that is no refusal. It then calls nothing more for the persona: `reconcileMissingFirst` answers `latched` with no resume (see the b.4dk note above), `reconcileAndReadRowState` reads no row and logs `[slack] <prefix>: <ref> is latched after the findMissing sweep — its row is not read; nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-502)` (its own row read after the sweep goes through the shared own-row `status` read, and one that latches the persona answers `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED` too, after its own latch line; so does a persona latched elsewhere while that read was awaited, whatever it gave, through `latchedAfterOwnRowRead`, which logs `[slack] <prefix>: <ref> is latched after its status read after the findMissing sweep — nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`), after which the ladder's prompt row answers `latched` and the restart path's prompt-row deferral answers `latched` (Auto-Restart step 3, **Prompt rows**), and the `working`-row wait ends with its latched line (a latched wait, above). The escalate-dead sweep reports a latched persona as an unrefused sweep, and the restart run's latch check after the reconnect stops it (Auto-Restart step 3).
       - **Against the health-check tick.** The 10 s window is far shorter than the ~120 s tick cadence, so the following tick's escalate-dead sweeps run again. A swept row is not sure to read dead afterwards, though: agent-director may leave it live (in `unverified_ids`, or, when `pending`, not judged), and it then stays live for further ticks, each of which tries again. The `reconcileMissingFirst` and `working`-row callers are clustered within one start rather than spaced by ticks, so they benefit from the memo directly.
     - `check_permission` / `ask_user` → never typed into (b.rmy). **b.jdc:** a session that dies under a prompt keeps its row in that state (agent-director only refreshes a row at SessionEnd and leaves reaping to its findMissing sweep), so the ladder (`launchOnPromptRow`, b.jg5 SRJ-607) first makes one `read-pane` of the persona's own row through the shared read-pane (`readPersonaOwnPane`, site `spawnForPersona: prompt row`, `PROBE_PANE_READ_LINES` = 1 line, the collision `get`'s state as the recorded state; see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The shared read-pane**), with no tmux call. Its outcome decides (b.jg5 SRJ-117's b.jdc ladder-action column):
       - **A pane** → no-op, as before (the poller relays the prompt; if the persona stays disconnected, the restart path reports it).
       - **UNAVAILABLE** (timeouts included), **CONFIG** (the wrapper has raised `ad-config-malformed`, b.jg5 SRJ-316) **or UNCLASSIFIED** (b.jg5 SRJ-105) → taken as alive: no-op, with one line naming the class (`promptRowLadderNoActionLine`).
       - **ENVIRONMENT** (the wrapper has raised `tmux-unavailable`, b.jg5 SRJ-311) → no-op, with one line naming the class (the same builder).
       - **UNCLASSIFIED carrying the stop mark** (`stopping`: the reader's `ErrInvalidFlags` version re-check decided that the server stops, b.jg5 SRJ-204, SRJ-205) → a `failed` result marked `stopping`, with its own line (`promptRowLadderStoppingLine`): no post, no `spawn-failed` entry, nothing counted.
       - **CONFLICT or UNUSABLE_NAME** (the reader has latched the persona with the collision `get`'s state: CONFLICT with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery", b.jg5 SRJ-501; UNUSABLE_NAME with `none`, b.jg5 SRJ-512), **or a persona already latched**, which the reader does not read → `latched` (`promptRowLadderLatchedLine`), nothing typed.
       - **GONE** (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`: agent-director found no pane of the row's launch) **or the row absent** (`ErrSpawnNotFound`, which takes the GONE column without being a GONE, b.jg5 SRJ-117) → one line (`promptRowLadderNoPaneLine`), then the latch is asked (`personaLatchedNow`, b.jg5 SRJ-502): a persona latched while the read was awaited answers `latched` with no sweep. Otherwise the memoized `reconcileMissingSweep` runs, then the row is read again: `ended` or `missing` is a dead session, recovered through `resumeOrFreshSpawn` (for a retired key a reuse spawn, never a `resume`, b.jg5 SRJ-805, SRJ-607; [Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)) after one `deadSessionRouteLine` naming its cause: `prompt-row-ladder-gone` after a GONE, dead evidence, and `row-absent` after an absent row, not dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)), handed on with any verdict the restart path carried in; any other state, or a failed read, is a no-op left to the restart path (`promptRowLadderAfterSweepLine`). A refused sweep (b.jg5 SRJ-105) reads nothing and answers the refused `failed`: no resume and no launch. A persona latched once the sweep is done (b.jg5 SRJ-120, SRJ-502) gets no row read and its latched line (`reconcileAndReadRowState`, see the b.m4r note above), and the ladder answers `latched`: no further call, no resume, sequence or launch.
     - `pending` → the ladder's `pending` step (`ladderPendingRowStep`; b.jg5 SRJ-409, SRJ-411, SRJ-1504), which the not-resumable step and a resume site's replacement also hand a row they re-read `pending` (above). It compares the row with the persona (`compareRowToPersona`). A row that is not the persona's current life is not covered: its `cwd` differs from the persona's working directory by real path (a check that cannot be made now is no mismatch, b.av2 SR-6.4), logged `[slack] spawnForPersona: <ref> pending row cwd=<row cwd> differs from working_directory=<dir> — not covered; replacing its row by a reuse spawn of the same id` (`<none>` for a row with no `cwd`), or its `config_dir` label is missing or differs, logged `[slack] spawnForPersona: "<name>" (key=<key>) config_dir label missing (label absent, now=<hex> for claude_config_dir=<dir>) on a pending row — not covered; replacing its row by a reuse spawn of the same id` (or `config_dir label changed (was=<old hex>, now=<new hex> for claude_config_dir=<dir>)` with the same tail). Either goes to the replace step, which starts the live-row sequence (a `pending` row is live; the sequence waits until G past its launch start). A directory that cannot be resolved gives no verdict: the row is kept and the launch answers `deferred` (bug b.g57). A covered row is left as it is (`no-op`, `[slack] spawnForPersona: no action — state=pending for <ref>`), with no kill and no launch; the step arms nothing. At the collision `get` the `cwd` guard above has already compared the `cwd`. A configured persona's own `pending` row with no launch start never reaches here: the read latched it.
     - **b.wrb `ErrJsonlMissing` diagnostic — legible amnesia (b.jg5 SRJ-712).** When resume throws `ErrJsonlMissing`, `diagnoseJsonlMissing` runs before the no-transcript reuse spawn, while the row it reads is still the old life's (`jsonl_path` / `claude_session_id` / `cwd` / `started_at`; the reuse resets them), to make the loss legible. It is a sibling of the b.zak safeguard (step 4a-quater), which runs *before* the resume path; this one runs *inside* it, on the row resume actually failed to open. Its row fetch is the shared own-row read (`readPersonaOwnRow`, b.jg5 SRJ-114). Never throws. Its texts are built from exported constants: the entry classes `JSONL_TRANSCRIPT_LOST_ENTRY_CLASS` (`jsonl-transcript-lost-on-resume`) and `JSONL_DIAGNOSIS_INCONCLUSIVE_ENTRY_CLASS` (`jsonl-diagnosis-inconclusive`), and the wording `JSONL_DIAGNOSIS_REUSE_WORDING`, "brought up fresh by a reuse spawn of the same instance, and its row is kept (its history archived to the earlier life)": the log lines and entry details say "the persona is " + that wording, the notices "I was " + it. The log line and, at start, the entry are written when the verdict is reached; a verdict's notice is held back and posted by the no-transcript step only when the reuse spawn answers `spawned`, and dropped otherwise (the entry stays; a later attempt makes its own diagnosis). Two things happen:
       - **Path + provenance logging.** AD's `ErrJsonlMissing` description enumerates every transcript candidate it stat'd as `<source> <path> (<stat error>)`, joined by `"; "` — a capability AD's bug `b.1ba` delivered, introduced in agent-director v0.10.0. When the description carries that enumeration, `parseJsonlMissingCandidates` parses it and logs the candidates verbatim, labelled *paths+sources reported by agent-director*. The parsed source tokens are `persisted` (AD's recorded `jsonl_path`), `fallback` (its `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`-aware recomputed path), and `history` (an archived `session_history` entry). When the description does **not** match that shape — a pre-0.10.0 AD, or any AD whose message wording differs — the parse yields nothing and CSCB reconstructs the candidates locally instead: the persisted `jsonl_path` column plus a `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`-aware fallback via `resolveJsonlPath` and the persona's effective `claude_config_dir` (its own, else the top-level one), labelled explicitly *locally computed* so a reader never mistakes a CSCB-side reconstruction for what AD actually stat'd. The parse keys off those literal source tokens, not any version string, so it degrades cleanly in both directions.
       - **lost / never-created / inconclusive classification (b.fwu).** Using b.zak's read-only `makeDefaultArchiveCount` / `rfc3339ToEpochSeconds` helpers over `message_archive_db`, bounded by `started_at`, and the b.av2 SR-7.4 scope from `personaArchiveEvidenceScope` (the same helper step 4a-quater's Layer 2 uses), `diagnoseJsonlMissing` counts archived messages only in the persona's `delivery: all` channels since `started_at` and returns one of `'lost' | 'never-created' | 'inconclusive'`:
         - **lost** — archive shows ≥1 message since spawn in the persona's `delivery: all` channels, real conversation history destroyed. Made operator-visible via `recordStartupError('jsonl-transcript-lost-on-resume', …)` (startup only), the log line `[slack] ErrJsonlMissing diagnostic: <ref> instance=cscb_<key>: resume threw ErrJsonlMissing and the persona is brought up fresh by a reuse spawn of the same instance, and its row is kept (its history archived to the earlier life), but the message archive holds <n> message(s) since spawn (started_at=<t>). Conversation history was LOST. Transcript candidates tried (<provenance>): <candidates>.`, **and**, once the reuse is up, a notice through the notifier to the persona's destination ("my conversation memory has been lost and I was brought up fresh by a reuse spawn of the same instance, and its row is kept (its history archived to the earlier life)").
         - **never-created** — strictly evidence-based: the archive was actually consulted and returned 0 messages since spawn, and that zero is attributable — the persona has no `delivery: mentions` channel and DMs off, so its `delivery: all` channels carry all of its traffic. The transcript was never written (Claude creates the `.jsonl` lazily on first message; expected and lossless). One quiet log line only, `[slack] ErrJsonlMissing diagnostic: <ref> instance=cscb_<key> — transcript never created (archive consulted: 0 archived messages since spawn). Nothing to lose; the persona is brought up fresh by a reuse spawn of the same instance, and its row is kept (its history archived to the earlier life). Transcript candidates tried (<provenance>): <candidates>.`
         - **inconclusive (b.fwu)** — "no evidence either way": the AD row fetch answered `ErrSpawnNotFound` (a CONFIG answer is a refusal at that `get`: no verdict, no notice, no entry), `started_at` was absent or unparseable, the count was 0 but the persona has a `delivery: mentions` channel or DMs on (b.av2 SR-7.4: the archive cannot attribute messages from `mentions` channels or DMs to a persona, so the zero proves nothing — `UNATTRIBUTABLE_ZERO_REASON`; a persona with no `delivery: all` channel counts 0 without the archive being consulted, so once `started_at` parses it always gets this reason, even when `message_archive_db` is not configured), `message_archive_db` is not configured, or the archive read failed. Each emits `recordStartupError('jsonl-diagnosis-inconclusive', …)` carrying the reason (`the agent-director row is absent (ErrSpawnNotFound)` / started_at absent or unparseable / zero count not attributable / archive unconfigured / archive read failed) with the log line `[slack] ErrJsonlMissing diagnostic: <ref> instance=cscb_<key>: resume threw ErrJsonlMissing and the persona is brought up fresh by a reuse spawn of the same instance, and its row is kept (its history archived to the earlier life), but diagnosis was INCONCLUSIVE — could not determine whether conversation history was lost because <reason>.` **and**, once the reuse is up, a notice through the notifier to the persona's destination, worded as *uncertainty* ("on restart I was brought up fresh by a reuse spawn of the same instance, and its row is kept (its history archived to the earlier life); I could not determine whether my prior conversation history was preserved") — deliberately distinct from the `lost` wording, since a false "your history was destroyed" is its own harm. When `message_archive_db` is unconfigured the operator message states diagnosis is impossible because no message archive is configured, with a hint to enable it.

         Any other error from the row fetch is a read error (b.jg5 SRJ-105), not an inconclusive diagnosis: `refusalAt` logs `spawnForPersona: ErrJsonlMissing diagnosis get refused for <ref>: …` and the diagnosis answers the refused `failed`. No inconclusive notice is posted, no `jsonl-diagnosis-inconclusive` entry is recorded, and the branch makes no reuse spawn (see the `refusalAt` sites above). An error `refusalAt` does not refuse (not reached: every `get` error but `ErrSpawnNotFound` and UNUSABLE_NAME is a refusal) logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: ErrJsonlMissing diagnosis get failed for <ref>: <failure> — nothing more is called` and answers an unmarked `failed` the same way: no diagnosis, no reuse spawn, no spawn-failure notice. Only `ErrSpawnNotFound` gives an inconclusive verdict.

         A row fetch that latched the persona (a `provenance_conflict` note on its own row, b.jg5 SRJ-114, SRJ-502, or an UNUSABLE_NAME answer, b.jg5 SRJ-512, which records the state `unreadable`) reports no diagnosis either, since its texts say the persona is brought up fresh: no `lost`, `never-created` or inconclusive verdict, no startup-errors entry, no notice and no amnesia count. The diagnosis answers `latched`, the branch makes no reuse spawn, and the ladder answers `latched` (see [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)). The same holds when the persona latched elsewhere while the fetch was awaited (the health tick's liveness read, b.jg5 SRJ-315), whatever the fetch gave: `latchedAfterOwnRowRead` (asked right after the fetch, unless it answered `latched`, and before any other answer is handled) logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: <ref> is latched after its ErrJsonlMissing diagnosis get — nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`. It asks the latch, not the fetch, so a row the fetch latched itself (its note or launch-start line comes first) logs this line too.

         All three verdicts go on to the same reuse spawn of the same id. On its success `lost` and `never-created` surface as the `fresh-after-amnesia` action; **inconclusive** surfaces as the `'fresh-after-inconclusive-amnesia'` action (see the honest-summary note below). For a recorded retired key the reuse's `fresh-retired` passes through instead: no amnesia result, and the diagnosis's persona notice is not posted (the no-transcript step above). This is distinct from b.zak's `jsonl-transcript-lost` class (which fires *pre-resume* to warn of an impending wipe); `jsonl-transcript-lost-on-resume` records a loss found on the row resume tried and failed.
     - **b.jgf `ErrJsonlNeverWritten` — the ceremony-free branch.** agent-director 0.10.0 split the old "resume cannot open a transcript" condition into two typed errors, and CSCB branches on both. `ErrJsonlMissing` means a transcript path was recorded but is not there now: history *may* have existed and been destroyed, and that ambiguity is exactly what the b.wrb / b.fwu diagnosis above exists to resolve. `ErrJsonlNeverWritten` asserts the opposite — the session produced no transcript at all — which proves there is nothing to lose, so bringing the persona up fresh is lossless by construction. It therefore shares the no-transcript reuse spawn but none of the ceremony: `diagnoseJsonlMissing` and the `fresh-after-*` actions are gated on the name `ErrJsonlMissing`, so this branch emits one informational log line, raises **no** persona notice, records no startup-error class, and returns plain `spawned` — the same shape as the `ErrSpawnNotFound` branch. Returning a successful action is the load-bearing part: `restart.ts` treats `failed` as retryable, so before b.jgf this error fell to the generic failure tail and the channel retried the one operation that could never succeed, on a doubling backoff, posting a spawn-failure message each pass. This branch is also the resume-path counterpart of the b.zak Layer 2 policy in step 4a-quater: a channel that has been idle since spawn has no transcript yet because Claude creates the `.jsonl` lazily on first message — normal, not an error, and it must not alarm.
   - `ErrSpawnNotFound` race after collision → single retry-spawn.
   - `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` (LAUNCH FAILURE, decided by name through the classifier, `isLaunchFailure`) from any launch the ladder makes (the first spawn, the retry spawn after the collision `get` found no row, the `resume`, the plain spawn after the `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotFound` (at either `resume` site), and every reuse spawn: the replace step's and the no-transcript step's) → one counted launch failure (b.jg5 SRJ-602, SRJ-111, SRJ-113): nothing is killed because of it, no spawn is made in its place, and the ladder answers `failed` marked `countedClass`. A plain spawn's failure goes through `plainSpawnFailedAt` and the `resume`'s through `resumeFailedAt` (the reuse spawn's through `reuseSpawnFailedAt`, below); each writes one line, `[slack] spawnForPersona: <what> failed for <ref>: <failure> — a counted launch failure; nothing is killed and no spawn is made in its place (b.jg5 SRJ-602)`, with `<what>` the call (`spawn`, `retry-spawn`, `resume` or `fresh spawn after ErrSpawnNotFound on resume`), raises the spawn-failure notice, and during the start pass records a `spawn-failed` entry `<what> failed for <ref>: <failure>`. Then `launchFailureResult` arms the persona's retry timer at once, with no `get` first, in pending-only mode (`armPendingOnlyAfterLaunchFailure`, `outage-state.ts`; SRJ-301, SRJ-409), and the result also carries `pendingOnlyArmed` when it armed (only inside a launch attempt with a trigger sink installed); the retry's read of the row decides what the failure left. A timer already armed keeps its mode and due time, and no `armed in pending-only mode` line is logged for it. The reuse spawn's `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` is handled the same way by `reuseSpawnFailedAt`, which also answers through `launchFailureResult` ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)). The failure counts toward the restart limit only at a restart's launch (`launchSession` answers `false`; Auto-Restart step 5) and at the live-row sequence's own launch (`countSequenceLaunch`; see Counting under the retry timer); a start pass only adds it to the `failed` count of its summary line, and a bring-up or apply launch counts nothing.
   - **Raw tmux calls address one session exactly (b.1ix).** No path in `src/` calls tmux directly: CSCB reaches tmux only through agent-director. The reconnect makes no tmux call and starts no tmux server: it types only through agent-director's `send-keys` (the `waiting` branch above). No liveness check probes a tmux session: the `working`-row verdict, the `waiting`-row check and both prompt-row paths (the restart path's prompt-row verdict `promptRowReconnectVerdict`, `server.ts`, and the collision ladder's prompt-row action `launchOnPromptRow`, above) read the pane through agent-director (Auto-Restart step 3; b.jg5 SRJ-606, SRJ-607). The launch's `working`-row wait (`waitForWaitingAndReconnect`) probes none either: its terminal branches key on agent-director's row (**b.ecw terminal verdicts**, above). The dialog approver calls no tmux: it reads and types only through agent-director (below). The raw tmux runner in `src/session-manager.ts` (`_runTmux`, with its test seams `_setTmuxCommandRunner` and `_resetTmuxCommandRunner`) is defined but has no caller in `src/`; unit tests install a recording runner through the seam to see that no argv reaches it. tmux resolves a bare `-t <name>` to the session of that exact name when there is one and otherwise to the one session whose name starts with it; persona keys can prefix one another (`dev`, `dev_2`), so a bare `slack_bot_dev` reaches `slack_bot_dev_2` once `slack_bot_dev` is gone. The one session target `src/` builds is the operator's `tmux attach -t =slack_bot_<key>` in the not-connected notices (`tmuxExactSessionTarget`, `=<name>`); no path in `src/` addresses a pane. The `/ci` scenario `tests/integration/test-11-exact-tmux-targets.sh` drives `tests/integration/fixtures/exact-tmux-driver.ts` against real tmux with `slack_bot_dev` and `slack_bot_dev_2`. Its probe and approver legs call a session-manager function (`hasPersonaTmuxSession`) and test seams (`_setDialogPollIntervalMs`, `_setDialogDeadGracePolls`) that `src/` does not have (the approver leg also expects an Enter in `slack_bot_dev`), and its later legs expect a launch to end `slack_bot_dev` after `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` and spawn again, which no `src/` path does. The probe leg runs first, so the scenario fails before its later legs. The approver and the prompt-row paths call no tmux, so no leg can cover them.
   - A CONFLICT (`ErrTmuxSessionConflict`, by name through the classifier) at any spawn or `resume` the ladder makes (the first spawn, its retry-spawn after the collision `get` found no row, the spawn after `resume` answered `ErrSpawnNotFound`, every reuse spawn (the replace step's and the no-transcript step's) and the resume) → the persona latches, with the refused operation `plain-spawn` for a plain spawn, `reuse-spawn` for the reuse spawn and `resume` for the resume and the row state the path last read before that call, and the ladder answers `latched` (b.jg5 SRJ-105, SRJ-501). It then takes no further step: no sequence, spawn, spawn-failure notice or `spawn-failed` entry, and nothing counted. See [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502).
   - An UNUSABLE_NAME answer (b.jg5 SRJ-105, SRJ-512) at any of those spawns or the resume → the persona latches (`unusableNameAt`) with the case `unusable-recorded-name`, the refused operation `none` and the row state the path last read (one latch-time `status` read when it read none), and the ladder answers `latched`. It then takes no further step: no sequence, spawn or reuse, so no tmux-touching call, no spawn-failure notice, no `spawn-failed` entry and nothing counted.
   - **The ladder makes no kill and no delete (b.jg5 SRJ-707, SRJ-110).** A live row's kills are the live-row sequence's, checked and retried there (steps 1 and 4 of [The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)), with the kill-failure alert's context `recovery`. No ladder path deletes a row before a spawn, so a row and its history stay as an earlier life of the instance and no still-running worker is orphaned.
   - A refusal (UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED, `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` included, or a read error at the collision `get`) at any of these calls → `failed`, with one line and no spawn-failure notice or `spawn-failed` entry (see the launch attempt above).
   - Other errors → `notifySpawnFailure(key, error)` raises a spawn-failure notice through the per-persona notifier to the persona's destination. A notice raised while the persona has no serving client is held in that persona's queue (step 6); in dry run it is only logged. A failed post of a startup spawn-failure notice records the `spawn-failure-post` startup error (outside startup, a `[slack] spawn-failure-post:` line) at the notice's first failed attempt only; after a destination failure the hold keeps the notice, so the record can be followed by a `cleared:` line and delivery.
   - **Scope of this ladder.** It handles only errors raised by the spawn/resume verbs (`spawn`, `get`, `resume`, `sendKeys`, `status`) — it is not a catalog of every AD error CSCB handles. The one place an agent-director error gets its class is the classifier (`src/ad-error-class.ts`, see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)); the resume path's `ErrInvalidFlags` branch goes through it, the reconnect's `send-keys` decides every answer through it, every refusal is decided through it by the arming predicate, and the other branches match the error directly as described above. The arming predicate of the launch attempt (above) classifies every error the ladder's calls report. It decides whether the retry timer is armed, and at the sites listed above, whether the error is a refusal. Decide-path errors are handled at their own call site: the only CSCB caller of AD's `decide` verb is `handlePermissionClick`, so `ErrAlreadyDecided`, `ErrInvalidFlags`, `ErrAmbiguousRequest`, and b.qi1's `ErrRelayFallenBack` are branched on there (see [Click handler (SR-4)](#click-handler-sr-4)) and never reach this ladder or its generic tail.
   - **Pre-session dialog approval (b.uhv / b.k54 / b.jg5 SRJ-402 — defense-in-depth).** The startup-dialog approver runs after every launch call that returns success, because a resumed bot faces the same dev-channels dialog as a fresh one. Each success site calls one after-launch step, `afterLaunchSucceeded(key, isStartup, ref, verb, launched)`: in `runPersonaLadder`, the first spawn and the retry spawn after the collision `get` answered `ErrSpawnNotFound`; in `resumeOrFreshSpawn`, the `resume` and the spawn after the resume's `ErrSpawnNotFound`; the live-row sequence's final launch (`launchForLiveRowSequence`), its `resume` and the plain spawn after that `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotFound`; and the reuse spawn (`reuseSpawnForPersona`, verb `reuse spawn`; the replace step's, and the no-transcript step's after a `resume` that answered `ErrNoSessionId`, `ErrJsonlMissing` or `ErrJsonlNeverWritten`, at the ladder and at the sequence's `resume` leg), whose approver works on the persona's own row as after any launch. No other branch starts one: not the `pending`, `waiting`, `working` or prompt-row branches, not a `latched`, `failed`, refused or deferred result, and not dry run. The step first writes the launch's `pre_trust` line (the pre-trust bullet above), then starts the approver (`startDialogApprover`) without awaiting it, so the launch's result is returned as soon as the launch call returns: `spawnForPersona` resolves before the approver's first call, and `isLaunchInFlight(key)` is false while only the approver runs. It is the only code that answers a startup dialog, and it does so only through agent-director: every call names only the persona's `claude_instance_id` (`cscb_<key>`), agent-director reads and types into the worker's recorded pane of a session carrying this launch's label (after a lost create reply, `send-keys` adopts the pane whose pane label carries the launch's token, never a pane found by index; HO rev 17), and the server starts no tmux process for it. One loop handles both known dialogs; `PRE_SESSION_DIALOG_NEEDLES` holds their option labels, `TRUST_DIALOG_NEEDLE` (`'Yes, I trust this folder'`) and `DEV_CHANNELS_DIALOG_NEEDLE` (`'I am using this for local development'`), both verified against Claude Code 2.1.120. Both are kept: a folder-trust prompt can still appear when the folder's trust was not pre-accepted for this launch. Each dialog pre-selects its accept option, so a single Enter accepts it. A launch, fresh or resumed, reads `pending` until its session reports in (HO C5), so every lap works on the `pending` row. Each lap (`approverLap`):
     - first asks the latch: a persona already latched stops the approver with one line and no call (`latched`, b.jg5 SRJ-502);
     - reads the row once through the shared own-row `status` read (`readPersonaOwnRowStatus` with the site `approvePreSessionDialogs`, what `readiness status read`; [The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115)), which carries the state and, on a `pending` row, its raw launch start. A read that latched the persona (an UNUSABLE_NAME answer, or a configured persona's own `pending` row with no launch start, b.jg5 SRJ-513) stops the approver with nothing read or typed; the step logged its line. `ErrSpawnNotFound` (an absent row) stops it with one line and no startup-errors entry. Any other refusal takes the class rules below. After the read the approver asks the latch again, so a persona latched while the read was awaited gets no further call (`latched`);
     - stops on a live state other than `pending` (`waiting`, `working`, `ask_user`, `check_permission`): the dialog is gone;
     - stops at once on `ended` or `missing`, with no pane read and one line: the launch is over and the restart path decides. During a start-pass launch it writes the `dev-channels-approve-spawn-died` startup-errors entry at that lap (`STARTUP_ERROR_APPROVE_SPAWN_DIED`);
     - on a `pending` row with no launch start, or one that does not parse (`parseLaunchStart`, `src/pending-row.ts`), that the read did not latch, stops with one line and reads and types nothing (`no-launch-start`). With a configured-persona query installed, the own-row step latches a configured persona's such row ("launch start not recorded"), and answers latched even when no latch store is installed, so the approver stops `latched` instead. `no-launch-start` is reached only when no configured-persona query is installed (unit tests, the integration driver) or the query answers that the key is not a configured persona's (for example, a persona removed while its launch's approver runs);
     - on a `pending` row with a launch start, first compares the launch start: the first lap whose `status` read the row `pending` with a launch start keeps it (a failed read keeps nothing) and re-arms B from it (below), and a later lap that reads a different one stops the approver (`superseded`) with one line and no `read-pane` or `send-keys`: the row belongs to a newer launch, whose own approver works on it (b.jg5 SRJ-401). Otherwise it makes one `read-pane` (`n_lines` 40, `allow_pending: true`) and, only when a needle is on screen, one `send-keys` with `text: ''` and `allow_pending: true`, which presses Enter. Before `read-pane` it checks B (or the cap); after `read-pane` it asks the latch again, so a persona latched meanwhile gets no `send-keys`. Enter is never sent without a visible needle, so no stray Enter reaches a live prompt. A refused `read-pane` or `send-keys` takes the class rules below;
     - on any other state value, reads and types nothing and logs one line; polling goes on within B.
     - **Stops by class (b.jg5 SRJ-117, SRJ-118, SRJ-404).** Each refused call is classified once (`approverAnswerTo`) by class and name through the classifier ([Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104); `classifyAdError`, `hasAdErrorName`, never `instanceof`), with one redacted line from an exported builder:
       - GONE (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`, `ErrTmuxSendKeys`) from any of its calls, or `ErrSpawnNotFound` from `read-pane` or `send-keys`: stops (`gone`; `approverGoneMessage`). `ErrSpawnNotFound` from `status` is the absent row above (`absent`);
       - `ErrSpawnNotInteractive` (`ERR_SPAWN_NOT_INTERACTIVE_NAME`, `src/agent-director-errors.ts`): stops with nothing typed and nothing killed (`not-interactive`; `approverNotInteractiveMessage`, which names both causes: the session holding the name is not this launch's by its label's token, or the row has no launch start);
       - CONFLICT: latches P through the latch's CONFLICT entry (`setFromConflict`) with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery" (`REFUSED_OPERATION_NEXT_CHECK_OR_RECOVERY`) and the recorded state `pending` (unreadable for a `status` answer, which read no state), then stops with nothing typed (`latched`; `approverConflictMessage`, which says what became of the latch);
       - UNUSABLE NAME from `read-pane` or `send-keys`: latches P through the unusable-name latch entry (`latchOnUnusableName`, case "unusable recorded name", refused operation none, recorded `pending`) and stops with nothing typed (`latched`; `approverUnusableNameMessage`). An UNUSABLE NAME answer to `status` is latched by the own-row `status` step (above) and never reaches this table;
       - ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`): stops (`tmux-unavailable`; `approverTmuxUnavailableMessage`); the outage wrapper raised P's `tmux-unavailable` outage, and nothing is counted;
       - UNAVAILABLE or CONFIG: polling goes on within B and the next lap waits the slow pace (backing off); for CONFIG the wrapper raised `ad-config-malformed` and arms P's retry timer, as from any verb (`approverStatusRefusedMessage` / `approverPaneCallFailedMessage`, "polling on within the bound");
       - anything else (UNCLASSIFIED, `ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed`, or a STATE name the approver gives no meaning): polling goes on within B at the pace in effect (same builders).
       Before it latches on its own CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answer, the approver marks itself stopping (`latched`), so the latch's set observer (below) finds it already stopping.
     - **Pace (b.jg5 SRJ-403).** The pace is measured from the previous pane read, not from a lap's start: the next lap waits until at least the pace has passed since the approver's previous `read-pane` call, on the approver's clock (the sleep is armed with `armNeverEarlyWait` from that read, so it never ends early). The read's time is the approver's clock just before its `readPane` call (`paneReadAtMs`); a lap that made no pane read (a refused or failed `status`, or a state neither pending, live nor finished) waits from its own start instead (`paceFromMs = lap.paneReadAtMs ?? lapStartMs`). `approverPaceMs(backOff, launchStartMs, nowMs, graceMs)` picks it after each lap: `DIALOG_SLOW_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` (5 s) when the lap backed off (an UNAVAILABLE or CONFIG answer), or when G in effect (`adGraceMsInEffect()`, read at that lap) has passed since the launch start that lap's own `status` read carried (a plain `elapsed >= G` comparison; the row's `started_at` is never used); otherwise `DIALOG_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` (1 s). A lap with no launch start, and a G of `AD_WAIT_NEVER_ENDS`, keep 1 s. So two `read-pane` calls are never closer than the pace in effect, even when a `status` call is slow: at least 1 s apart, and at least 5 s apart once G has passed since the launch start or after a lap that backed off.
     - **B, from the launch start (b.jg5 SRJ-210, SRJ-404).** B is CSCB's launch bound (`adLaunchBoundMsInEffect`; see `ad-settings.ts` in the [Module Map](#module-map) for its derivation). The approver arms it with `armNeverEarlyWait` and the accessor itself (so a value raised while armed never ends it early) from its own start, and re-arms it from the launch start once a lap keeps one (`keepApproverLaunchStart`; a launch start that is not a finite time is never armed). The approver's start is never earlier than the launch start, so the bound armed first never ends early; a resumed row's older `started_at` plays no part. Before each call it also checks B by a plain `elapsed >= B` comparison against the value in effect (a value that cannot be read is not reached). The timer cuts the sleep between laps short.
     - **The latch stop (b.jg5 SRJ-502).** `setConflictLatch` registers one set observer on the installed latch (`stopApproverOnLatch`); every set of P, by any site (a relatch and a same-case set included), calls `stopDialogApprover(P, 'latched')`. The approver is marked stopped inside the set call, so no approver call for P starts after the set returns; a call already in progress returns first, and no call follows it (see the stop below for what becomes of that call's answer). Installing another latch removes the observer from the one before.
     - **The registry: one approver per persona (b.jg5 SRJ-401, SRJ-404).** `startDialogApprover(key, isStartup, ref?)` runs the approver's loop on its own, unawaited, in a per-persona registry, and returns at once. The approver makes its first call only after the launch in flight that started it has settled. The registry holds at most one approver per persona: a start for P first stops P's running approver with the reason `superseded` (one line) and the new one makes its first call only once that stop has completed, so two approvers never work on P's row and no pane gets two Enters for one dialog. `stopDialogApprover(key, reason)` (`superseded`, `teardown`, `retired-key`, `shutdown` or `latched`) marks the approver and wakes its sleep at once; the mark is checked before each call and as each call returns, so no call follows a stop, and the returned promise resolves once the call in progress, if any, has returned. A call that returns after a stop was asked has its answer dropped with no line, except that a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answer to a `read-pane` or `send-keys` still latches P through the latch's entry for the class, with its one line (`approverStoppedDuringCall`, through `approverLatchOn`); either way the approver resolves with the stop's reason and types nothing. A stop while P's launch is in flight also cancels the approver that launch would start (the cancel ends when `spawnForPersona` settles); such a start logs one line and starts nothing. `stopAllDialogApprovers()` stops every approver, and no approver starts after it. A throw inside the loop is logged and stops the approver (`failed`); it never becomes an unhandled rejection. `isDialogApproverRunning(key)` answers from the approver's start until it has stopped, a stop asked but not yet completed included; `dialogApproverLaunchStart(key)` is the launch start the running approver kept.
     - **The retired-key stop (b.jg5 SRJ-808, SRJ-404).** Apply step 1 stops the approver of each key it records as retired (`stopApprover` of `ReloadControllerDeps`, production `stopDialogApprover(key, APPROVER_STOP_RETIRED_KEY)`, not awaited), right after a record that did not fail (written, or unchanged for a key already recorded with no mark), before the last-applied rewrite and so before the key's teardown and its kill ([The apply pipeline](#the-apply-pipeline-sr-86)). The approver logs `stopping the approver for <ref> (retired-key): its key was recorded as retired; it makes no further call (b.jg5 SRJ-401, SRJ-404)`, and its recorded calls end at that stop. Like every stop, it also cancels the approver a launch in flight would start. No pending-row rule run follows it. A failed step-1 write stops nothing, and a failed rewrite restarts no approver. The teardown's own stops (`teardown`, at submit and as its first step) still run after it.
     - **Outside the launch attempt (b.jg5 SRJ-401).** The registry runs the approver inside `runOutsideAttempts` (`src/unavailable-retry.ts`), so its calls are part of no launch or recovery attempt: an UNAVAILABLE answer arms no retry timer and starts no `tmux-unresponsive` condition, and an UNCLASSIFIED answer on `status`, `read-pane` or `send-keys` arms no retry timer and opens no unclassified-error episode. An ENVIRONMENT answer (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`) still raises `tmux-unavailable` and a CONFIG answer (`ErrConfigMalformed`) still raises `ad-config-malformed`, and each arms P's retry timer, as from any verb (b.jg5 SRJ-311, SRJ-316).
     - **Its answer, lines and clock.** The approver resolves with why it stopped (`ApproverStopReason`: `live`, `finished`, `absent`, `latched`, `no-launch-start`, `cap`, `bound`, `gone`, `not-interactive`, `tmux-unavailable`, `superseded`, `teardown`, `retired-key`, `shutdown`, `failed`; the `APPROVER_STOP_*` constants) and never rejects; the registry keeps it with the launch start it kept as an `ApproverOutcome`. `approvePreSessionDialogs(key, isStartup, ref)` runs one approver directly, outside the registry, where nothing but its own rules stops it, and outside every launch or recovery attempt (`runOutsideAttempts`), whatever attempt the caller runs in. Production starts an approver only through the registry (`startDialogApprover`); the direct entry is for tests. Its lines start `[slack] approvePreSessionDialogs: ` (`APPROVER_LOG_PREFIX`) and are built by the exported `approver…Message` builders. The B (or cap) timer and the sleeps between laps run on the approver's clock (`_setApproverClock` / `_resetApproverClock`, type `ApproverClock`, the real clock by default), so its tests run on `createFakeClock`.
     - **At B (b.jg5 SRJ-405).** The approver stops (`bound`), logs one line (`approverBoundMessage`: B in milliseconds, whether it was measured from the launch start or from the approver's start, and that nothing is posted) and, during a start-pass launch, records `dev-channels-approve-not-ready` (`STARTUP_ERROR_APPROVE_NOT_READY`) with the same text. Nothing is posted to Slack and no notifier is called.
     - **The test cap (b.jg5 SRJ-404, SRJ-1303).** `_setDialogReadyTimeoutMs(ms)` is unset by default (`_resetDialogReadyTimeoutMs` unsets it). While it is set (the stub-spawn harness, `installStubSpawnPath`, sets 200 ms), the approver arms the cap from its own start in place of B and re-arms nothing when a lap keeps a launch start; at the cap it stops (`cap`) with `approverCapMessage`'s line and the same start-pass entry, and posts nothing. No other wait reads it.
     - A fresh spawn that shows no dialog reaches a live state on its own and the approver returns quietly. The trust patch (step 4a-bis, repeated before every launch) is the primary fix for the trust dialog, so the expected path is that it ran for this launch and no trust dialog appears; this loop covers unprovisioned cwds, clobbered trust state and dialog changes in later Claude Code releases.
   - **b.f2b parked start launches.** One persona's `working` row must not hold up the others. `startupSessionManager` runs each launch through `launchOrPark`: when the ladder calls `onWorkingRowWait` (right before `waitForWaitingAndReconnect`, which can take up to `WAIT_FOR_WAITING_TIMEOUT_MS`), the pass stops waiting for that launch, frees its pool slot and records the persona as `waiting-in-background`. `followParkedLaunch` logs that the pass goes on without it, then, when the launch settles, `background launch for <ref> settled: <action>`; a rejection is logged and recorded as `spawn-failed`, as the pass records one, and never rethrown. The launch stays in `inFlightLaunches` until it settles, so the health check still reads the persona but makes no attempt for it (Health-Check Poller) and a restart joins it, as for any launch in flight; a teardown cancels its wait and then waits for it to settle (`whenLaunchSettled`). So neither the pass nor the health check and detection tick that start after it (steps 8 and 9) wait out one persona's wait. Only the start pass parks: an apply bring-up, a launch after a retry and a restart relaunch pass no hooks and wait for the launch to settle.
   - **b.wrb / b.fwu honest startup summary.** `startupSessionManager` tallies each persona's `SpawnPersonaResult['action']` into a per-outcome breakdown and prints `startupSessionManager: complete — N persona(s): N resumed, N fresh-spawned, N fresh-after-amnesia, N fresh-after-inconclusive-amnesia, N reconnected, N no-op, N failed, N not brought up, N not reconnected`. The last bucket (b.f2b) counts `not-reconnected` launches (the session runs but the `working`-row wait typed nothing, or its teardown cancelled the wait); they count in `succeeded` too. Since the pass parks every launch it starts once it waits on a `working` row, the bucket counts only such a launch the pass joined rather than started. Parked launches are counted in no bucket: when there are any, the summary is followed by `startupSessionManager: <n> persona(s) still waiting in the background for a working row to settle — not counted above; each logs its outcome when it settles (b.f2b)`. `fresh-after-amnesia` (a reuse spawn after a resume's `ErrJsonlMissing` where the archive gave a definite lost/never-created verdict) and `fresh-after-inconclusive-amnesia` (b.fwu — the same reuse but the diagnosis was inconclusive, so it is *unknown* whether history was preserved) are counted and reported separately; each has its own loud, grep-friendly follow-up line when its count is `> 0`, pointing at the per-persona `ErrJsonlMissing diagnostic` lines. The returned `StartupSessionManagerResult` carries the same breakdown (`resumed` / `freshSpawned` / `freshAfterAmnesia` / `freshAfterInconclusiveAmnesia` / `reconnected` / `notReconnected` / `noop`) alongside the retained `succeeded` (any non-failed action) and `failed` totals, `notBroughtUp` (personas whose outcome was `broken` or `retrying` when the pass reached them, including one launched later by its retry), `waitingInBackground` (b.f2b: launches parked when the pass returned), plus `perPersona` (each persona's key and action, `not-brought-up` with its `outcome` and failures, or `waiting-in-background`). A b.jgf `ErrJsonlNeverWritten` recovery counts as an ordinary `fresh-spawned`, not as either amnesia bucket: no history existed, so counting it as memory loss would overstate the damage. The replace step's reuse spawns (the b.av2 SR-6.2 `cwd` and `config_dir` guards and `resume_enabled=false`, on a finished row) also count as `fresh-spawned` (action `spawned`); they add no action or summary line of their own, and their per-persona log lines above say why the row was replaced. A live row there answers `sequence-waiting`, counted neither as failed nor as succeeded. A retired key's reuse that began its new life (`fresh-retired`, b.jg5 SRJ-806) counts as `fresh-spawned` too, with no count of its own in the summary line. A `latched` launch (b.jg5 SRJ-502) is counted neither as failed nor as succeeded and in no bucket of the summary line; `perPersona` carries its action `latched`. A launch that joined an in-flight one returns that launch's action.
6. **Held notices flush per persona (b.av2 SR-7.2)** — the connection manager's status listener (`createPersonaUpFlushListener`) calls the notifier's `flush(key)` each time a persona reports `up`: after its bring-up in step 5 and after every reopen. Only that persona's queue is posted, in raised order, through its own client; other personas' queues are untouched. A notice is held while its persona has no client (`clientFor` answers only for a serving persona), so notices raised before a persona comes up, such as start-pass notices from steps 4a-quater and 5, post once it is up. The hold is the same for a channel and a `dm` destination: every persona notice (spawn failure, restart cap, outage onset and all-clear, the history and transcript-loss warnings, non-persistent JSONL storage, lost message) reaches a `dm` destination as a DM to `dm.contact`, and for a held notice the DM is opened only when it is flushed, never before the persona's client is validated. A persona that is never brought up keeps its held notices, at most 20: past that the oldest is dropped with a log line and never posted (see the `persona-notifier.ts` entry). No bring-up failure is ever among them (step 5). A flushed notice whose post the destination refuses is then kept by the destination hold and retried with backoff (Permission Relay, [Destination hold](#destination-hold-bav2-sr-71-failures)). Dry run holds nothing: its notices are logged when raised.
7. **SR-2.1 poller start** — outside dry run, `main()` calls `resetAllToHealthy` with the applied persona keys (a clean outage slate before any persona is brought up) and then `startPermissionPoller({ getClient, clientFor, destinations: personaDestinations, destinationHold: personaDestinationHold, getPersona: getAppliedPersona, isPersonaUp, intervalMs: personaConfig.agent_director_poll_interval_ms })`. This runs right after the connection manager and the bring-up controller are built, before `Bun.serve` and step 4. The poller waits for no persona: it skips the rows of a persona that is not up (`isPersonaUp`, the shared up predicate) and reads them again on the first tick after it is up; `clientFor` and `destinationHold` are the same per-persona lookup and destination hold the notifier uses. Single-threaded interval loop; skipped-tick WARN at 5+ consecutive skips. Dry run logs `[slack] Running in dry-run mode — Slack disabled` instead and starts no poller.
8. **Health-check poller** — `startHealthCheck()` begins backstop liveness checks via `client.status(...)`, over the personas that are up (see Health-Check Poller). It starts once the step 5 pass returns, so it can be running while a retrying persona is still retrying, and while a start launch the pass parked on a `working` row is still waiting (b.f2b). A persona joins the tick only once it is up, which is when its own retry launches it, and the tick skips a persona while a launch for it is in flight, a parked one included. A restart scheduled meanwhile runs after the restart delay, and its kill and launch defer to a launch still in flight (Auto-Restart steps 4 and 5).
9. **Reload detection tick (b.av2 SR-8.2)** — `reload.startDetection()`, the last statement of `main()`, right after step 8. The controller arms the tick only once the step 5 pass has returned (`runStartBringUp` settled), so, like the health check, it never races the pass's bring-ups: every persona's bring-up has read its credentials by then, which is what the tick compares against. A launch the pass parked may still be in flight (b.f2b); that keeps SR-8.2's intent, and a teardown of that persona cancels its wait and then waits for its launch to settle (`whenLaunchSettled`). Its first pass runs 5 s later. See [Reload Detection Tick](#reload-detection-tick-bav2-sr-82-sr-83).

CSCB does NOT maintain its own `sessions.json` registry. agent-director owns Claude session-id state internally, surfaced via `client.resume(...)` and the SR-11 state machine.

### Disconnection

1. Transport closes → `onsessionclosed` fires
2. A pending session is simply removed. A registered session is removed with `unregisterByMcpSessionId()`, which returns its persona key; a stale close of a session already replaced by a newer one returns nothing and leaves the newer session registered
3. `restartDisconnectedPersona(key, via)`, the one handler `server.ts` builds at module scope with `_buildRestartDisconnectedPersona` (its dependencies read at call time), resolves the key to its applied persona; a key that is no applied persona is logged and not restarted. It logs `[slack] Session disconnected<via>: persona <ref> cwd="<path>"`. While the server is shutting down (the HTTP server's stop aborts every MCP stream, which lands here) it then logs `[slack] Skipping restart — server is shutting down (persona=<key>)` and does nothing more: no restart, no retry timer armed. Otherwise, with the persona's `tmux-unavailable` flag not raised (`getOutageFlags`), it calls `scheduleRestart(key, persona.working_directory)`. While the flag is raised it never schedules a restart (b.jg5 SRJ-311): the retry timer's retries are the persona's only attempts. It decides through `armMissingTmuxUnavailableRetry`, the check the lost-message routing's `armRetryTimerIfMissing` also uses (Inbound step 7), over the production deps `tmuxUnavailableRetryDeps` (the outage flag, the retry controller's `isArmed`, the server's one latch, the "in flight for P" binding `isPersonaWorkInFlight` (a launch call or a running dialog approver), `armEnvironmentRetryTimer` and the server log), each read at call time through the holders `main()` sets, and logs one line, `[slack] Session disconnected<via>: persona <ref> has its tmux-unavailable outage raised` followed by what it did, the first that applies: the retry timer is armed (`isArmed` answers `true`): nothing more (`— no restart scheduled; its retry timer recovers it (b.jg5 SRJ-311)`); the persona is latched: nothing armed (`and is latched — no restart scheduled, no retry timer armed (b.jg5 SRJ-311, SRJ-502)`); work is in flight for it: nothing armed (`with work in flight — no restart scheduled, no retry timer armed (b.jg5 SRJ-311, SRJ-315)`); `isArmed` answers anything but `false` (no retry controller yet): nothing armed (`and no retry controller — no restart scheduled, no retry timer armed (b.jg5 SRJ-311)`); otherwise it logs `with no retry timer — no restart scheduled; arming one (b.jg5 SRJ-311)` and arms the timer with the `environment` cause through `armEnvironmentRetryTimer`, the arm path the health tick's `armRetryTimer` uses too, so a retry comes even with `session_restart_delay` 0 and `health_check_interval` 0 (see [UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305), ENVIRONMENT). The armed read is made once, before the latch and in-flight checks. The SSE-abort path of a `GET /mcp` stream does the same

**Session drop when a persona stops being up (b.av2 SR-6.3, SR-6.4).** A session is registered only while its persona is up. When a running persona's outcome changes from `up` to `broken` or `retrying` (a refused reopen, or a Web API call refused for the persona's bot token, bug b.ujn; both log `persona-credentials-refused`), the bring-up controller calls its `onLeftUp` listener once, which the server sets to `createNotUpSessionDropper`. It stops the session's SSE keep-alive and calls `dropPersonaSession(key)`, which removes the persona's MCP session-ID mappings and registry entry before closing the transport, so the close finds no session and steps 2–3 schedule no restart. When a session was registered it logs `[slack] persona "<name>" (key=<key>): MCP session dropped — the persona is not up (<outcome>: <cause>); its instance and agent-director row are kept`. Nothing else happens: no restart, kill or delete, no agent-director call, nothing posted to Slack. A lost Slack connection being reopened (`lost`, or `retrying` in the `reopen` phase) keeps the persona `up` and drops nothing. While the persona is down, any new connection from the instance is refused (Connection, step 3). A credentials-broken persona recovers through a confirmed change to its credentials file (apply step 6's recovery bring-up) or at the next start, and the instance registers again through that bring-up's launch, which reaches the kept row through the collision ladder.

**Session drop at a persona teardown (b.av2 SR-6.5).** A persona teardown drops the persona's session through the same `dropPersonaSessionAndKeepAlive` (keep-alive stopped, registry entry removed before the transport closes), before its instance is killed, so neither the close nor the kill schedules a restart. It logs no drop line of its own.

### Auto-Restart

Restart guards, backoff, the cap latch and every restart dependency are keyed by persona key (b.av2 SR-6.3), and restart log lines name it as `persona=<key>`, e.g. `[slack] Scheduling restart for persona=<key> in <n>s (backoff)`.

Auto-restart only acts on a persona that is up. It is separate from bring-up retries (Server-Managed Startup step 5), which have their own per-persona timers on the SR-3.2 backoff with no cap and never touch this module's counter, backoff or cap. In particular, a directory that is missing at bring-up is a bring-up retry. A persona that is running and whose directory later disappears stays on this path: the health check raises `cwd-unreachable` for it (b.av2 SR-11), and its relaunches follow the backoff and cap below.

The UNAVAILABLE retry timer (`src/unavailable-retry.ts`, b.jg5 SRJ-302 to SRJ-305) is a third, separate per-persona mechanism with its own schedule: 30 s doubling to a 300 s ceiling from `doublingBackoffDelay`, with no attempt cap. The timer itself never reads or writes this module's failure counter, backoff or cap latch, so a refusal never counts toward `RESTART_FAILURE_CAP`; only a launch failure that a retry's own restart work counts does (see [UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305) below). It reads neither `session_restart_delay` nor `health_check_interval`, so a 0 in either does not turn it off. The restart work of a fired timer or of a retry (steps 1 to 5 below, from the shutdown check on) runs as one recovery attempt for the persona (`runInAttempt`, b.jg5 SRJ-301), with its adapters: an UNAVAILABLE or UNCLASSIFIED outcome from any agent-director call in it (the liveness read and re-probe, the reconnect with its reads, the sweep, the kill, the relaunch), or an error from `status`, `get` or `list` other than `ErrSpawnNotFound` and UNUSABLE_NAME, arms the persona's retry timer through the trigger sink `main()` installs (Server-Managed Startup), and a trigger while armed keeps the due time. An UNCLASSIFIED outcome there is also reported to the persona's unclassified-error episode ([The unclassified-error episode](#the-unclassified-error-episode-bjg5-srj-313-srj-1009)), except the liveness read's `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`. The one other arming site in this work is the arm hook (`RestartDeps.armRetryTimer`), called on every liveness reading of `unknown`, at the probe or the re-probe (step 3). The steps below otherwise do what they describe.

After `scheduleRestart(key, cwd)` is called:

1. **Latched check (b.jg5 SRJ-502)** — first, before any other gate, the latched query (`RestartDeps.isLatched`) is asked. A latched persona gets no timer: `[slack] Not scheduling restart for persona=<key> — the persona is latched; no timer armed (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`, logged once per call, and nothing else is asked. A query that throws counts as latched (fail safe), and the line then reads `[slack] Not scheduling restart for persona=<key> — the persona is latched (the latched query failed: <error> — taken as latched); no timer armed (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`. This covers every caller, a human-triggered restart included, and keeps a pending restart from hiding the latched persona from the health tick, which skips a persona whose restart is pending. A timer already pending for the persona is left as it is: when it fires, its work answers `latched` at its own latched gate (see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)).

   **Held check (b.jg5 SRJ-207)** — right after the latched query, `scheduleRestart` asks the held query (`RestartDeps.isHeld`). A persona held on `ErrInvalidFlags` gets no timer: `[slack] Not scheduling restart for persona=<key> — the persona is held on ErrInvalidFlags; no timer armed (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`, with ` (the held query failed: <error> — taken as held)` after `ErrInvalidFlags` when the query threw. `runRestartWork` asks it right after its first latched gate and again wherever it asks the latched gate again ([The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold](#the-errinvalidflags-hold-bjg5-srj-207-srj-1008)).

   **Live-row sequence gate (b.jg5 SRJ-706, SRJ-303)** — `scheduleRestart` itself does not ask it. When the work runs (a fired restart timer, a retry, a human-triggered restart's timer), `runRestartWork` asks `RestartDeps.isLiveRowSequenceRunning(key)` right after its first latched gate and its held gate, before the shutdown and up checks and the liveness read. While a live-row sequence runs for the persona the work answers `sequence-waiting` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_SEQUENCE_WAITING`) with `[slack] Skipping restart for persona=<key> — its live-row sequence runs; no agent-director call, nothing recorded (sequence-waiting; b.jg5 SRJ-706, SRJ-303)`: nothing is probed, reconnected, killed, launched or recorded, and nothing counts toward the cap. A query that throws counts as running, and the line then carries ` (the running query failed: <error> — taken as running)` after `runs`. A latched persona answers `latched` first. A launch outside the serializer can start the persona's sequence during the work's awaits (a collision ladder replacement site, b.jg5 SRJ-707), so the work asks the gate again wherever it asks the latched gate again (after the liveness probe, after an escalate-dead reconnect, after the re-probe, before the kill), once more right before the launch, and after a launch that answered `'refused'` (its own ladder started the sequence, or met it, and answered `sequence-waiting`). A sequence running then answers `sequence-waiting` too, nothing more called and nothing recorded, with `[slack] Restart for persona=<key> goes no further <where> — its live-row sequence runs; nothing more is called for it, nothing recorded (sequence-waiting; b.jg5 SRJ-706, SRJ-303)`, `<where>` being `after its liveness probe`, `after its escalate-dead reconnect`, `after its re-probe`, `before its kill`, `before its launch` or `after its launch`; a retry's re-armed line then names `live-row-sequence-waiting`.

   **Delay check** — next, if `session_restart_delay` is 0, restart is skipped immediately. The delay comes only from the loaded persona config (`getRestartDelay`). Nothing then reconnects an alive persona that is not connected, so the health check reports it through the not-connected notice instead (Health-Check Poller step 4, b.f2b). A launch's own reconnect of a `waiting` or stale `working` row still runs (Server-Managed Startup step 5). Delay 0 disables only the restart timer, not the UNAVAILABLE retry timer's runs: a retry skips this delay check and still runs the rest of the work (see [UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305)).

   **Shutdown check** — next, during graceful shutdown no timer is armed and the relaunch gate is not asked: `[slack] Skipping restart — server is shutting down (persona=<key>)`. Shutdown cancels every bring-up, so no persona is up, and stopping the HTTP server aborts every MCP stream, which lands here; asking the gate would log healthy personas as not relaunched. The timer callback repeats this check first when it fires.

   **Up check (b.av2 SR-6.4)** — next, `RestartDeps.canRestart(key)` (the relaunch gate, see step 5) is asked. A persona that is not up (its bring-up is broken or retrying, or its Slack connection is not serving) gets no timer: `[slack] Not scheduling restart for persona=<key> — the relaunch gate refused it (the persona is not up, or is no longer in the applied configuration)`. The timer callback asks again right after its shutdown check, before the liveness check, and once more right after the liveness check returns, before any reconnect or kill (the probe is an async agent-director call, and the persona may stop being up while it runs). After an escalate-dead reconnect answer it is asked again right after the second liveness probe, before the kill (step 3, b.d61). A persona that stopped being up by any of these checks (for example, Slack refused its token on a reopen) logs `[slack] Skipping restart for persona=<key> — the persona is no longer up; its instance is left as it is`. Nothing further is probed, reconnected, killed or launched, and no success or failure is recorded, so a not-up persona's instance and agent-director row are left alone. `launchSession` asks the gate once more (step 5).
2. **Backoff timer** — a `setTimeout` fires after `nextBackoffDelay(key, session_restart_delay)` seconds: `min(base * 2^preFailureCount, 900)`, so the delay doubles on each consecutive failure from the `session_restart_delay` base up to a 900 s (15 min) ceiling (`src/backoff.ts`, SR-25). `scheduleRestart` accepts `opts.humanTrigger`; when set, the computed delay is clamped **down** to `HUMAN_TRIGGER_DELAY_CEILING = 5` s (never raised) so a message lost to a down persona doesn't leave it down for a 900 s backoff. The clamp only shortens the wait — it does not reset the failure counter and does not bypass the re-entrancy guard, so each attempt still counts toward normal backoff/cap accounting. The `scheduleRestart` path itself does not consult the cap — it is cap-exempt (the cap only gates the health-check tick and the inbound message triggers, which check `isAtCap` themselves before firing, see below). Two triggers reach this path from inbound messages, both in `src/persona-routing.ts` and both keyed by the receiving persona: the b.9cj streamless branch, for a session that is *registered* for the persona yet lacks a `_GET_stream` (it calls `scheduleRestart(key, session.cwd, undefined, { humanTrigger: true })`; it does not call `notification()`, since the SDK's `send()` would evaporate silently with the stream gone), and the b.kvq no-session branch, for a persona with **no** registered, connected session (the "No live session for persona … — dropping message" line; it calls `scheduleRestart(key, persona.working_directory, undefined, { humanTrigger: true })`). Both go through `decideLostMessageState` (`src/lost-message.ts`), so the restart fires only in the `starting-now` state: none of the earlier states applies (not up, latched, not answering, a live-row sequence running, a launch in flight or the one lost-message row read answering `pending`, among the ten in [Inbound step 7](#inbound-slack--claude-code); b.jg5 SRJ-1501), no restart already pending or active, auto-restart enabled and the persona under the failure cap. Either way one lost-message notice naming the sender and the recovery state goes to the persona's destination through the notifier, and nothing else is posted in the source conversation (Data Flow, Inbound step 7). Guards and restart are keyed by the receiving persona's key, so there is no owner resolution and a recovery never spawns a second instance. At the cap the inbound path does **not** bypass the cap; only a server restart clears the in-process counter and revives a capped persona. In all cases the dropped message itself is lost — recovery starts a session but never delivers or replays that message.

   **Serialized work (b.av2 SR-6.6).** When the timer fires, it is removed from the pending map and the persona is marked active (`activeLaunches`) at once; the work below (the shutdown and up checks, the liveness probe, reconnect, kill and launch) is then submitted through the per-persona serializer, so it starts only after any teardown or bring-up retry already running or queued for the persona has settled, and its checks see the state at that moment. See [Per-persona serialization](#per-persona-serialization-bav2-sr-66).
3. **Liveness check (C12, b.jg5 SRJ-314)** — `isSessionAlive(key)` (`_buildIsSessionAliveAdapter`, `src/server.ts`) calls `client.status({claude_instance_id})` and answers one of four readings (`src/liveness-reading.ts`), never a boolean. Rule C12: a `status` error is never read as dead, and only `dead` leads to a kill and a launch. After its own call it applies the own-row `status` step (`applyOwnRowStatusStep`, [The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115)) to the result or to the thrown value; an answer that latched the persona reads `unknown`.

   | Answer | Reading | Outage flag |
   |---|---|---|
   | State `pending` | `pending`, carrying the row's launch start (`launch_started_at`, raw) when the result shows one (`livenessReadingForStatus`) | clears `ad-unreachable` and `ad-config-malformed` |
   | Another live state (`waiting`, `working`, `ask_user`, `check_permission`) | `live` | clears `ad-unreachable` and `ad-config-malformed` |
   | State `ended` or `missing` | `dead` | clears `ad-unreachable` and `ad-config-malformed` |
