   | Any other state string | `unknown` (logged) | clears `ad-unreachable` and `ad-config-malformed` |
   | `ErrSpawnNotFound` | `dead` | clears `ad-unreachable` and `ad-config-malformed` |
   | `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` | `dead`, marked as read from no row (`LIVENESS_READING_DEAD_INSTALL_GONE`: the slow-recovery count resets on it without ending its episode, b.jg5 SRJ-610); not reported to the unclassified-error episode | raises `ad-unreachable` with its binary path |
   | `ErrTmuxNotAvailable` (class ENVIRONMENT) | `unknown` | raises `tmux-unavailable` through `raiseTmuxUnavailable` with the error |
   | `ErrConfigMalformed` (class CONFIG) | `unknown` (logged at every read) | raises `ad-config-malformed` through `raiseAdConfigMalformed` with the error (one onset and one raise line per episode) |
   | UNUSABLE_NAME (an `ErrInternal` naming the recorded tmux session name) | `unknown`, after the own-row `status` step latched the persona (b.jg5 SRJ-512) | none |
   | Any other error: every UNAVAILABLE form (`ErrCallTimeout`, CSCB's `UnknownError` wrapper, an unknown name), an UNCLASSIFIED `ErrInternal` or store-open name (inside a restart run also reported to the unclassified-error episode), a value that is not an agent-director error | `unknown` (logged) | none |
   | A key not in the persona config (or no config) | `dead`, with no `status` call | none |

   Errors are decided by name through `src/ad-error-class.ts` (`hasAdErrorName` for `ErrSpawnNotFound` and `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, `classifyAdError` for ENVIRONMENT and CONFIG), with no `instanceof` ladder. Its ENVIRONMENT raise goes through the same entry as the wrappers', `raiseTmuxUnavailable(key, err)` (`statusErrorReading`), so a re-bound socket's answer posts the *tmux server changed* onset and any other `ErrTmuxNotAvailable` the *tmux unavailable* one (see the `outage-state.ts` entry of the Module Map). Its CONFIG raise goes through the wrappers' entry too, `raiseAdConfigMalformed(key, err)`, and the reading stays `unknown`, with the shared `status error … read as unknown, not dead` line at every read; a `status` success and `ErrSpawnNotFound` clear `ad-config-malformed` with `ad-unreachable` (b.jg5 SRJ-312: either answer means agent-director loaded its config and read its store), and every other error leaves it as it was. The adapter never clears `tmux-unavailable` (b.jg5 SRJ-312): a `status` is not tmux-touching, so neither its success nor its `ErrSpawnNotFound` shows that tmux answered. An unconfigured key reads `dead`, but the relaunch gate (step 5) refuses a key outside the applied set before any kill or launch. Its bare `status` is the one persona call made outside the outage wrappers, so its error branch reports the error itself (`reportAgentDirectorError`, verb `status`): inside this restart run any `status` error but `ErrSpawnNotFound` and UNUSABLE_NAME arms the persona's retry timer, and from the health tick, outside every attempt, only an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer arms it (b.jg5 SRJ-311, SRJ-316). The same instance is the persona routing's lost-message row read (b.jg5 SRJ-115, SRJ-1011, SRJ-1501; `readRowLiveness`, see [Inbound](#inbound-slack--claude-code) step 7), made from the Slack event path, also outside every attempt, so the health tick's rules hold there: an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer raises `tmux-unavailable` or `ad-config-malformed` and arms the retry timer; an UNAVAILABLE or UNCLASSIFIED answer (any other error) arms no retry timer and opens no unclassified-error episode; `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` raises `ad-unreachable`, reads `dead` and arms nothing. Every such answer but `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` reads `unknown`, and neither `unknown` nor `dead` is `pending`, so `session-starting` is left out. A read there that latches the persona (an UNUSABLE_NAME answer) reads `unknown` too, and the routing, deciding again after the read, reports `held-for-human`.

   `runRestartWork` acts on the reading (after the up check that follows the probe):
   - **`live`** → the connected check and the reconnect below.
   - **`pending`** → the row's session has not started. Whatever the session's connection shows, and before the connected check below, the run hands the reading, with its launch start, to the `pending` deferral (`RestartDeps.deferPendingRow`, see **`pending` rows** below) and returns `pending-deferred` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_PENDING_DEFERRED`): no reconnect, kill or launch, and no success or failure recorded. A connected `pending` row is never "already reconnected". A configured persona's own row that reads `pending` with no launch start never gives this reading: the probe's own read latched the persona and reads `unknown` (b.jg5 SRJ-513; see **`pending` rows** below).
   - **`unknown`** → agent-director could not report on the persona. A probe that throws, or answers something that is not a reading, reads `unknown` too. The run logs one line and returns `liveness-unknown` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_LIVENESS_UNKNOWN`): no reconnect, kill or launch, and no success or failure recorded. It calls the arm hook (`RestartDeps.armRetryTimer(key)`), which `main()` wires to the UNAVAILABLE retry controller's `arm` with the `read-error` cause, so the persona is retried on that timer even for a reading the adapter's own report arms nothing for (a state CSCB does not know, a probe that throws). For a `status` error the adapter's report arms first, so its cause is the one logged: `unavailable` for an UNAVAILABLE error (a timeout, an unreachable agent-director), `environment` for `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`, `config` for `ErrConfigMalformed`, `read-error` for the others it arms for (`unavailableRetryCauseFor`); the hook's later `read-error` arm then lands on an armed timer and logs nothing. An arm while the timer is armed or running keeps its due time; a hook that throws is logged and changes nothing else.
   - **`dead`** → the only reading that goes on to the kill (step 4) and the launch (step 5).

   A probe whose own read latched the persona (an UNUSABLE_NAME answer, b.jg5 SRJ-512) reads `unknown`, but never reaches these branches: the latch check right after the probe answers `latched`, with no deferral and no arm hook ([Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)).

   On `live`, `restart.ts` skips the reconnect as "already reconnected" only when the session is connected **AND** its standalone GET SSE stream is present (`RestartDeps.hasSessionStream`, b.9cj); a connected-but-streamless session (`connected === true` but the SDK dropped `_GET_stream`) cannot receive messages, so it is *not* waved through — it proceeds to recovery. If `live` and not skipped, `reconnectSession()` first probes AD state with its own `status` read. When the row is `working`, it defers the reconnect while a launch for the persona is in flight or the positive-idle rule has not shown the row stale, reconnects once it has, and escalates once agent-director's `read-pane` of the row finds no pane of its launch (GONE) or finds the row absent (see **`working` defer** below). When the row is `ask_user` or `check_permission`, it types nothing: it reads the row once with a one-line `read-pane`, escalates with nothing typed on GONE or an absent row, and otherwise defers (see **Prompt rows** below). When the row is `waiting`, it reads the pane once first, and escalates with nothing typed on GONE or an absent row (see **`waiting` rows** below). When the row is `pending` by this read (the probe read it `live`), its session has not started, so it defers and types nothing (see **`pending` rows** below). The adapter applies the own-row `status` step to its read's answer first (`applyOwnRowStatusStep`): an answer that latches the persona (an UNUSABLE_NAME answer, b.jg5 SRJ-512, or its own row reading `pending` with no launch start, b.jg5 SRJ-513) makes it forget the persona's idle evidence and answer `'transient'`, with nothing typed and no `deferPendingRow` hand-off. When the status call throws otherwise, nothing is known about the session, which may be mid-turn, so nothing is typed (b.f2b): the failure is logged, the persona's idle evidence is forgotten and the adapter returns `'transient'`; the next tick retries. Every `status` error is handled this way, `ErrSpawnNotFound` included: no error is decided by type here and none is escalated to dead; the next liveness read reads a missing row `dead`. Before typing, after those reads, the adapter asks the latch (its `isLatched` argument, b.jg5 SRJ-502): a latched persona, or a query that throws (taken as latched), gets nothing typed, logs `[slack] reconnectSession: persona=<key> is latched — not typing /mcp reconnect; nothing done (b.jg5 SRJ-502)` (with ` (the latched query failed: <error> — taken as latched)` after `latched` when the query threw) and the adapter returns `'transient'`. Otherwise the reconnect runs (`reconnectMcpWithCause(key, lastRead)`, its last read the state the adapter's `status` read gave): one `/mcp reconnect slack-channel-router` `send-keys`, never retried, with no tmux server start, answering `'ok'`, `'dead-session'` with its cause or `'transient'` by class (Server-Managed Startup step 5, the `waiting` branch). The adapter maps `'ok'` to `'success'`. A `'dead-session'` is swept once with the verdict its cause gives (`escalateDeadVerdictOfCause`; see the sweep below) and answered escalate-dead carrying that verdict (`ReconnectEscalateDead`, `{ outcome: 'escalate-dead', deadEvidence }`, built by `escalateDeadWith`, b.jg5 SRJ-611): `dead-session` for `tmux-gone` (GONE), dead evidence; `row-not-interactive` (`ErrSpawnNotInteractive`) and `row-absent-at-pane-read` for `row-absent` (`ErrSpawnNotFound`), not dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)). A `'transient'` (the reconnect latched the persona on a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE_NAME answer, found it latched, or met UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED, `ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed` included) is answered `'transient'` with no sweep: nothing typed, no spawn-failure notice, nothing counted, and nothing is killed or launched. Likewise a refused escalate-dead sweep, or a refused prompt-row deferral sweep, makes the adapter answer `'transient'` instead of an escalate-dead answer (see the sweep below). A `'success'` reconnect calls `recordSuccess` (resetting the failure count and cap latch); the non-success branches do **not** `recordFailure`. `restart.ts` never re-enters `scheduleRestart` on a reconnect verdict. On `'transient'` (including the `working`, prompt-row, `pending`, `waiting`-pane, status-error and latched defers) it returns, and the **next health-check tick** re-observes the persona and, if it is still not deliverable (alive-but-disconnected or connected-but-streamless) or has since gone dead, calls `scheduleRestart` again, so a deferred or `'transient'` reconnect is tried again on a bounded cadence, never counted.

   **`escalate-dead` recovery (b.sv7, b.d61).** For an escalate-dead answer (`ReconnectEscalateDead`, carrying its verdict; a bare `'escalate-dead'` carries none and is read as no dead evidence) CSCB recovers itself internally, in the same restart run:
   - **Sweep.** The `_buildReconnectSessionAdapter` mapping awaits `sweepDeadTmuxChannelWithCause(key, verdict)` (`src/session-manager.ts`; `sweepDeadTmuxChannel` is the same sweep without the answer) before returning the verdict. The verdict (`EscalateDeadVerdict`) says what the escalation came from:
     - from a GONE answer: `dead-session` when the reconnect's one `send-keys` answered `ErrTmuxSendKeys` (cause `tmux-gone`); `working-tmux-gone` when the `working` defer's `read-pane` answered GONE (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`); `waiting-row-pane-gone` (`ESCALATE_DEAD_WAITING_ROW_PANE_GONE`) when the `waiting`-row check's `read-pane` answered GONE; `prompt-row-tmux-gone` when the prompt-row verdict's one-line `read-pane` of an `ask_user` or `check_permission` row answered GONE (b.jdc, b.jg5 SRJ-606). These are dead evidence;
     - from a refusal: `row-not-interactive` when agent-director refused the reconnect's keystrokes as not interactive (`ErrSpawnNotInteractive`, cause `row-not-interactive`, b.dup): the row finished after it was read, or it reads `pending` and its session may be another launch's. It does not prove the worker gone and is not dead evidence, so it is only a route into the restart run's decision, and the run kills nothing because of it (step 4, b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611);
     - from a row read: `row-absent-at-pane-read` (`ESCALATE_DEAD_ROW_ABSENT_AT_PANE_READ`) when the row was absent (`ErrSpawnNotFound`) at the `read-pane` of the `working` defer, the `waiting`-row check or the prompt-row verdict, which takes the GONE handling without being a GONE (b.jg5 SRJ-117), or at the reconnect's `send-keys` (cause `row-absent`, never swept as a GONE, b.jg5 SRJ-118). Not dead evidence.

     The adapter's answer carries the verdict it swept with ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)). The prompt row's 10-minute deferral sweep, which runs no escalate-dead sweep of its own, carries the cause `row-read-finished` (see **Prompt rows** below), not dead evidence either.

     A GONE says that agent-director found no session or pane of the row's launch; it does not prove the worker's process gone (b.jg5 SRJ-613). The wrapper emits an operator-visible log line worded by the verdict, `[slack] escalate-dead: persona=<key> verdict=<verdict> — <evidence>, triggering internal findMissing reconciliation (the row may stay live for further ticks, each escalate-dead tick sweeping again; ~/startup/find-missing-loop.sh is belt-and-braces)`, built by the exported `escalateDeadSweepLine`, whose `<evidence>` is exactly one text per verdict, from the exported `ESCALATE_DEAD_EVIDENCE` (`src/session-manager.ts`). Every text says only what was observed and claims no tmux session or worker is gone; `row-not-interactive`'s says that the refusal does not prove the worker gone:

     | Verdict | `<evidence>` |
     |---|---|
     | `dead-session` | `agent-director's send-keys answered GONE (ErrTmuxSendKeys) at the /mcp reconnect: no session of the row's launch was found` |
     | `row-not-interactive` | `row not interactive (agent-director refused the /mcp reconnect keystrokes as not interactive: the row finished, or a pending row's session may be another launch's; this does not prove the worker gone)` |
     | `working-tmux-gone` | `agent-director's read-pane found no pane of the row's launch (GONE) on its working row` |
     | `waiting-row-pane-gone` | `agent-director's read-pane found no pane of the row's launch (GONE) on its waiting row` |
     | `row-absent-at-pane-read` | `its agent-director row was absent (ErrSpawnNotFound) at the pane read or the /mcp reconnect's send-keys: a row read, not a GONE` |
     | `prompt-row-tmux-gone` | `agent-director's read-pane found no pane of the row's launch (GONE) on its ask_user or check_permission row` |

     The sweep then runs the memoized `reconcileMissingSweep` (b.m4r), an ordinary run: it joins a run in flight or reuses a result memoized within 10 s, and otherwise starts a run. The run may reconcile the frozen row to `missing`; agent-director may also leave it live (in `unverified_ids`, or, when `pending`, not judged, b.jg5 SRJ-120). After a run the server makes (not a memo reuse), each configured persona's own row in `unverified_ids` is read with one `get` through the shared own-row read, and a `provenance_conflict` note there latches its persona (see the b.m4r note under Server-Managed Startup step 5). A refused sweep (UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED, b.jg5 SRJ-105) logs its refusal line and answers `{ refused: true }`; the adapter then answers `'transient'` instead of an escalate-dead answer, so the run re-probes, kills and relaunches nothing, and the persona is left to the retry timer the refusal arms. A persona latched once the sweep is done answers as an unrefused sweep, and the latch check below stops the run. The one escalation that runs no such sweep is a prompt row's deferral that has already swept and read the row dead (see **Prompt rows** below).
   - **Latch check (b.jg5 SRJ-502).** Right after the reconnect gives an escalate-dead answer, before the re-probe, `restart.ts` asks the latch (`RestartDeps.isLatched`) again, since the sweep's `get` may have latched the persona: a latched persona answers `latched` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_LATCHED`) with `[slack] Skipping restart for persona=<key> — the persona is latched; no agent-director call, nothing recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`, and gets no re-probe, kill or launch. It is asked once more right before the kill (step 4).
   - **Re-probe.** `restart.ts` then calls `isSessionAlive(key)` again (`reprobeDeadAfterEscalate`), and reads its answer as the first probe's is read: a thrown probe reads `unknown`. The shutdown check and the up check (step 1) are asked again after it, then the latch, since the re-probe's own read may have latched the persona (b.jg5 SRJ-512): a latched persona answers `latched`, with no arm hook, deferral, kill or launch. Only `dead` goes on to the relaunch:
     - **`dead`** → the run goes on to the relaunch (step 5) at once, with the same accounting as any dead-session relaunch, and the relaunch carries the verdict into the ladder (b.jg5 SRJ-611). Only after a verdict that is dead evidence (a GONE-based one, [Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)) does the checked kill (step 4) come first. After any other verdict (`row-not-interactive`, `row-absent-at-pane-read`, `row-read-finished`, or a bare `'escalate-dead'` that carries none) it makes no kill, even though the re-probe read the row dead (a `dead` reading of `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` reads no row at all): it asks the latch, logs `relaunchWithoutKillLine` (`[slack] No kill before the relaunch for persona=<key> — its escalate-dead verdict (<verdict>) is not dead evidence, which never by itself leads to a kill; the relaunch's own row read decides (b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611)`, `<verdict>` being `verdict=<source>` or `none carried`) and relaunches, the ladder's collision `get` reading the row itself (b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611). Waiting for the next tick instead would add a full `health_check_interval` plus another backoff delay.
     - **`live`** (the sweep failed, agent-director left the row live, or a memoized sweep result predates the kill) → it returns `reconnect-deferred`, as for `'transient'`, with no kill, launch or accounting. Nothing promises that a later tick reads the row dead: agent-director may take several ticks to mark it (b.jg5 SRJ-610). Each later tick whose reconnect escalates dead runs the ordinary sweep again and nothing more: no kill, no counted failure, no other destructive step, and no timer of its own. The re-probe also tells the slow-recovery count (see **Slow recovery** below).
     - **`pending`** → its session has not started (agent-director may not have judged the row); it returns `pending-deferred` with no relaunch, so the UNAVAILABLE retry timer records the row read `pending`. It resets the slow-recovery count and is not counted: a `pending` row is not the slow recovery this count is for.
     - **`unknown`** → it returns `liveness-unknown` with no relaunch and nothing counted, and calls the arm hook, as the first probe's `unknown` does. It neither adds to nor resets the slow-recovery count.

     Before the kill that follows `dead`, the run asks the latch again (step 4), so a persona that latched during the re-probe is never killed.

     The re-probe's lines are built by exported builders in `restart.ts`: one per reading (`reprobeDeadLine`, `reprobeLiveLine`, `reprobePendingLine`, `reprobeUnknownLine`), and `reprobeUnhandledLine` for the fallback on a reading kind none of the cases names (a kind the typecheck rules out), which relaunches nothing, tells the slow-recovery observer nothing and returns `reconnect-deferred`; the `live` one is `[slack] Session still reads live after escalate-dead — no relaunch in this restart run for persona=<key>; the row may stay live for further ticks, each escalate-dead tick sweeping again`.
   - **Slow recovery (b.jg5 SRJ-610, SRJ-1010, SRJ-1016).** The optional `RestartDeps.slowRecovery` observer (`RestartSlowRecoveryObserver`; production: the tracker `createSlowRecoveryTracker` builds in `src/slow-recovery.ts`, one per server, built in `main()` over the notice episodes and handed to `initRestart`) is told what each run read, only once the shutdown, up and latch gates after each probe have passed, and the health check resets the count on its own (below):
     - an escalate-dead answer (carrying its verdict or bare) whose re-probe reads `live` → `noteLive`: the persona's count goes up by one;
     - a row read of `ended` or `missing`, or no row (`ErrSpawnNotFound`), at the run's first probe or at the re-probe → `noteDead`: the count resets and the persona's slow-recovery episode ends silently;
     - the `dead` reading from `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, which reads no row (`LIVENESS_READING_DEAD_INSTALL_GONE`, `isInstallGoneDeadReading` in `src/liveness-reading.ts`) → `noteInstallGone`: the count resets and an open episode stays open (hatch A2);
     - a reconnect ending with any verdict other than an escalate-dead one (a success, `'transient'`, `'pending'`, no answer or a throw), and a run that finds the session already connected with its stream → `noteOther` with `RESTART_SLOW_RECOVERY_OTHER_VERDICT`; a `pending` first probe → `noteOther` with `RESTART_SLOW_RECOVERY_OTHER_PENDING_PROBE`; a `pending` re-probe → `noteOther` with `RESTART_SLOW_RECOVERY_OTHER_PENDING_REPROBE`: the count resets, an open episode stays open;
     - an `unknown` or thrown re-probe, and a run that stops before the reconnect for any other reason (an `unknown` first probe, a latch, a launch in flight, shutdown, not up) → nothing.

     The health check resets the count too ([Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 4, **Healthy: the slow-recovery count resets**): each tick that finds the persona `live` (never `pending`), connected and with its stream calls `HealthCheckDeps.resetSlowRecoveryCount(key)`, bound in `main()` to the tracker's `noteHealthy`, after the tick's other healthy-branch calls; the count resets and an open episode stays open, and a throw is the persona's error for the tick. So a persona that heals on its own starts a later count from 0, and the post needs three consecutive escalate-dead ticks whose re-probe reads `live` with no healthy tick between them. Each reset logs `[slack] slow-recovery: persona=<key> count reset from <n> — <reason>` only when the count was above 0.

     When `noteLive` brings the count to `SLOW_RECOVERY_POST_THRESHOLD` (3) and no episode is open, the tracker begins P's `slow-dead-session-recovery` episode (`PERSONA_EPISODE_KIND_SLOW_DEAD_SESSION_RECOVERY`) and posts `slowRecoveryText(key)` once through the episodes' sink, the persona notifier: `:hourglass_flowing_sand: *Slow recovery* — agent-director has not yet marked the worker row of this persona's session "slack_bot_<key>" ended or missing. CSCB keeps retrying; no action is needed unless this persists.` While the episode is open, further live re-probes count and post nothing. A count reset alone never ends an open episode; only a row read of `ended`, `missing` or no row, P's latch (the hold observer, see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)) or P's teardown ends it, so a second post needs a new episode and three more such ticks. Once the episodes are closed at shutdown, the third logs `notice not posted — the server is shutting down` and posts nothing. Between P's teardown submit and its window (b.jg5 SRJ-1003) the post is muted: nothing reaches Slack, it counts as posted in its episode, and the line reads `[slack] slow-recovery: persona=<key> notice not posted — muted, its persona teardown was submitted; it counts as posted in its episode; <n> consecutive escalate-dead verdicts whose re-probe still reads the row live` (`slowRecoveryNoticeMutedLine`). The count is the kind's count in the episodes instance (`addCount`, `resetCount`), kept apart from the episode, so a teardown's `forget` and shutdown's `close` clear it with the episode. The tracker makes no agent-director call, adds no timer and never throws; a note that throws inside logs `[slack] slow-recovery: persona=<key> failed: <error>`, and one that throws at the restart side logs `[slack] restart: the slow-recovery <note> failed for persona=<key>: <error>`; neither changes the run.

   Recovery of such a persona waits on agent-director marking its row `ended` or `missing`; until then the operator sees the persona silent and, after the third consecutive escalate-dead tick whose re-probe still reads the row live, one *Slow recovery* notice at its destination (README, Troubleshooting). The external `~/startup/find-missing-loop.sh` is belt-and-braces only — recovery does not depend on it, and removing it stays a separate operator decision. Not counting at the reconnect keeps the failure count tied to actual launch attempts (the single counting site, SR-25.1) rather than a non-launch reconnect site — the sweep and the re-probe record neither success nor failure. Each outcome logs one line; they are listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

   **`working` defer (b.9a7, b.rmy, b.d61, b.f2b, b.jg5 SRJ-603).** A `working` row means the persona may be mid-turn, and typing `/mcp reconnect` into its pane would corrupt the turn (b.9a7 hazard 2). The row alone is no proof of a live turn, though: when the persona's session is killed mid-turn, its `SessionEnd` only soft-refreshes the row (see the b.m4r note under Server-Managed Startup), so agent-director keeps it `working` until a `findMissing` sweep reconciles it to `missing`. Deferring on the row alone would repeat every tick, and the persona would never relaunch (b.d61). So `workingReconnectVerdict` (`src/server.ts`) checks, in order:
   - **Launch in flight** (`isLaunchInFlight(key)`) → `'transient'`, first and with no agent-director call. The launch owns the session's lifecycle.
   - Otherwise it makes one `read-pane` of the persona's own row through the shared read-pane (`readPersonaOwnPane`, site `reconnectSession`, `FULL_PANE_READ_LINES` = 40 lines, the row state `working`; see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The shared read-pane**), and probes no tmux session. Its outcome decides (b.jg5 SRJ-117's working-row column):
   - **A pane** → the positive-idle rule decides (b.f2b). A `working` row can be stale: agent-director may leave it `working` after the turn ended, and deferring on it forever would strand the persona. The pane may be a single leftover's (b.jg5 SRJ-613), so it is never proof on its own. `checkWorkingRowPane(key, pane, { persona, latchedNow })` works on that pane and makes no `read-pane` of its own; only when the pane shows an idle screen does it read the transcript (one `get` of the row), located with the persona's effective `claude_config_dir` (the adapter gets the persona from `getAppliedPersona`; without it only the row's persisted `jsonl_path` is read). It folds the evidence into a run kept per persona across attempts (`workingRowPaneRuns`), with the same `classifyWorkingPane` / `foldWorkingPaneRun` rules as the launch wait (Server-Managed Startup step 5):
     - the same idle screen and the same transcript, ended with a completed turn, unchanged at every read across reads spanning `STALE_WORKING_WINDOW_MS` → `'reconnect'`: the run is forgotten and the adapter goes on to the reconnect below, as for any other alive row;
     - a running turn (the b.9a7 deferral line), a blank pane, an idle pane whose transcript doesn't end with a completed turn or can't be located or read, or idle evidence not yet held for the window → `'transient'`, nothing typed; every case but the last ends the run, and a pending idle run makes the health check schedule the next attempt on its first undeliverable tick (Health-Check Poller step 4);
     - a prompt or dialog → `'transient'`, nothing typed; once shown across reads spanning the window, the `blocked-on-prompt` not-connected notice is raised (once per episode).

     The run is forgotten when an attempt reads the row in another state or its status call fails, when the read gives anything but a pane (`forgetWorkingRowEvidence`), when any launch for the persona starts (`spawnForPersona`), and with the persona's not-connected episode (`forgetNotConnectedEpisode`: its MCP session registered again, the health check found it deliverable, or it was torn down).

     **Bounded deferral (b.f2b).** Every `'defer'` of the check is also one more deferral in the persona's run on the row (`noteWorkingRowDeferral`, shared with the launch wait), and so is an UNAVAILABLE or CONFIG read below. Once the run has lasted `UNPROVEN_IDLE_NOTICE_AFTER_MS` (10 min) from its first deferral, the `unproven-idle` not-connected notice is raised, once per episode: its session reads working but CSCB can't prove it's idle, so it won't type into it; the notice says CSCB keeps checking. Without it, a row whose idleness can never be proven (an unreadable transcript, a compaction summary, a screen that keeps changing) would be held back from for good with nothing reported, since nothing else escalates it at a non-zero delay. The run ends (`endWorkingRowDeferral`) when an attempt reads another state (a failed status call leaves it as it is), when `'reconnect'` is returned, when a launch for the persona starts and with the episode. A read that meets ENVIRONMENT, UNCLASSIFIED or a latch neither extends nor ends it.

     The check asks the adapter's latched gate (`latchedNow`, b.jg5 SRJ-502) right before it notes a deferral, which can raise `unproven-idle`, and right before the `blocked-on-prompt` notice: a persona latched meanwhile gets `'transient'` with its run forgotten, no deferral noted and no notice. A persona latched by its transcript `get` is answered the same way (see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)).
   - **GONE** (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`: agent-director found no pane of the row's launch) → `escalateRowWithNoPane(key, 'working-tmux-gone', latchedNow)`: the evidence is forgotten, then `sweepDeadTmuxChannelWithCause(key, 'working-tmux-gone')` runs once and the answer is escalate-dead carrying `working-tmux-gone`, dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)) (`'transient'` when the sweep was refused, or when the persona is found latched before it, with no sweep). Nothing is typed. When the sweep reconciles the row to `missing`, the re-probe above relaunches the persona in the same run; a row agent-director leaves live waits for a later tick.
   - **The row absent** (`ErrSpawnNotFound`) → the same, with the verdict `row-absent-at-pane-read`: a row read that takes the GONE handling without being a GONE (b.jg5 SRJ-117), and not dead evidence, so a `dead` re-probe after it relaunches with no kill.
   - **UNAVAILABLE** (timeouts included) **or CONFIG** (the wrapper has raised `ad-config-malformed`, b.jg5 SRJ-316) → `'transient'`, with the evidence forgotten and one deferral noted on the row: a read that could not run is never proof the session is dead (b.rmy), nor evidence that it is idle.
   - **ENVIRONMENT** (the wrapper has raised `tmux-unavailable`, b.jg5 SRJ-311) **or UNCLASSIFIED** (the wrapper reported the persona's unclassified-error episode, or the reader did after an `ErrInvalidFlags` re-check; b.jg5 SRJ-105) → `'transient'`, with the evidence forgotten and no deferral noted. An UNCLASSIFIED carrying the stop mark (`stopping`: the reader's `ErrInvalidFlags` version re-check decided that the server stops, b.jg5 SRJ-204, SRJ-205) gets the same answer with its own line, and nothing more is called for the persona.
   - **CONFLICT or UNUSABLE_NAME** (the reader has latched the persona with the row state `working`: CONFLICT through the latch's CONFLICT entry with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery", b.jg5 SRJ-501; UNUSABLE_NAME through the unusable-name entry, b.jg5 SRJ-512), **or a persona already latched**, which the reader does not read → `'transient'`, with the evidence forgotten, no deferral noted, no notice and nothing typed (b.jg5 SRJ-502). So does a persona the latch holds by the time the read answers.

   The deferral lasts only while a launch is in flight, or agent-director reads the persona's pane, or cannot answer, and the positive-idle rule has not shown the row stale. Each branch logs one line; they are listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

   **Prompt rows (b.f2b, b.jdc).** `/mcp reconnect` and Enter typed into a session that waits on a question (`ask_user`) or a permission dialog (`check_permission`) could confirm the dialog's default, so the adapter never types into those states. The row alone is no proof anyone is waiting on the prompt, though: a session that dies under a prompt keeps its row in that state until a `findMissing` sweep reaps it, and deferring on the row alone kept such a persona "blocked on a prompt" for good, never relaunched, with a *Waiting on a prompt* notice about a session that no longer existed (b.jdc, `/ci-live` run 6). So `promptRowReconnectVerdict` (b.jg5 SRJ-606) checks, in order, reading before it notifies:
   - **Launch in flight** (`isLaunchInFlight(key)`) → `'transient'`, first and with no agent-director call and no notice: the launch owns the session.
   - Otherwise it makes one `read-pane` of the persona's own row through the shared read-pane (`readPersonaOwnPane`, site `reconnectSession: prompt row`, `PROBE_PANE_READ_LINES` = 1 line, the row state the adapter read; see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The shared read-pane**), and makes no tmux call. Its outcome decides (b.jg5 SRJ-117's b.jdc reconnect-verdict column):
   - **CONFLICT or UNUSABLE_NAME** (the reader has latched the persona with that row state: CONFLICT through the latch's CONFLICT entry with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery", b.jg5 SRJ-501; UNUSABLE_NAME through the unusable-name entry, refused operation `none`, b.jg5 SRJ-512), **or a persona already latched**, which the reader does not read → `'transient'`, with one line (`promptRowLatchedLine`), no deferral noted, no notice and nothing typed (b.jg5 SRJ-502).
   - **UNCLASSIFIED carrying the stop mark** (`stopping`: the reader's `ErrInvalidFlags` version re-check decided that the server stops, b.jg5 SRJ-204, SRJ-205) → `'transient'`, with its own line (`promptRowPaneReadStoppingLine`), and nothing more is called for the persona.
   - **Latched by the time the read answers** (the adapter's latched gate, `latchedNow`, b.jg5 SRJ-502) → `'transient'`, with the gate's line, no sweep, no deferral noted and no notice.
   - **A pane** → the deferral below.
   - **GONE** (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`: agent-director found no pane of the row's launch) → the run of deferrals on the row ends, one line (`promptRowPaneGoneLine`), then `escalateRowWithNoPane(key, 'prompt-row-tmux-gone', latchedNow)`: `sweepDeadTmuxChannelWithCause(key, 'prompt-row-tmux-gone')` runs once and the answer is escalate-dead carrying `prompt-row-tmux-gone`, dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)) (`'transient'` when the sweep was refused, or when the persona is found latched before it, with no sweep), with no notice. Once the row reads dead, the re-probe above relaunches the persona in the same run; a row the sweep leaves live may stay live for further ticks.
   - **The row absent** (`ErrSpawnNotFound`) → the same, with its own line (`promptRowAbsentAtPaneReadLine`) and the verdict `row-absent-at-pane-read`: a row read that takes the GONE handling without being a GONE (b.jg5 SRJ-117), and not dead evidence.
   - **UNAVAILABLE** (timeouts included), **CONFIG** (the wrapper has raised `ad-config-malformed`, b.jg5 SRJ-316) **or UNCLASSIFIED** (the wrapper reported the persona's unclassified-error episode, or the reader did after an `ErrInvalidFlags` re-check; b.jg5 SRJ-105) → taken as alive, with one line naming the class (`promptRowTakenAsAliveLine`), then the deferral below: a read that could not run is never proof the session is dead (b.rmy).
   - **ENVIRONMENT** (the wrapper has raised `tmux-unavailable`, b.jg5 SRJ-311) → `'transient'`, with one line (`promptRowPaneReadEnvironmentLine`), no deferral noted and no notice.

   **The deferral** (for a pane or a read taken as alive) is one more deferral in the persona's run on the row (`checkPromptRowDeferral`, the run kept per persona in `promptRowDeferredSince`). Once the run has lasted `PROMPT_ROW_SWEEP_AFTER_MS` (10 min) from its first deferral, each deferral first runs the memoized `reconcileMissingSweep` and reads the row again: on `ended` or `missing` the run ends, the check logs what it read (`promptRowSweepFinishedLine`: `[slack] reconnectSession: persona=<key> has read <state> for <N> min of deferrals, and after a findMissing sweep its row reads <ended|missing> — not deferring; escalating (escalate-dead), the restart path's re-probe decides (cause=row-read-finished: not dead evidence; b.jdc, b.jg5 SRJ-611)`) and the adapter answers escalate-dead carrying the cause `row-read-finished`. A finished row is a row read, not dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)): the re-probe decides, and a `dead` re-probe relaunches the persona with no kill. A refused sweep (b.jg5 SRJ-105) makes `checkPromptRowDeferral` answer `'refused'` without reading the row, and the adapter answers `'transient'` with no notice. A persona latched once the sweep is done (the run's `get` of its own row in `unverified_ids` read the `provenance_conflict` note, or the latch answers it latched, b.jg5 SRJ-120, SRJ-502) gets no row read and one line, `[slack] reconnectSession: prompt row: persona=<key> is latched after the findMissing sweep — its row is not read; nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`; `checkPromptRowDeferral` answers `'latched'`, and the adapter answers `'transient'` with no `blocked-on-prompt` notice and no escalation, since the persona is held (b.jg5 SRJ-502) and its latch's own notice already tells the human (SRJ-508). A row read after the sweep that latches the persona (an UNUSABLE_NAME answer, or its own row reading `pending` with no launch start, through the shared own-row `status` read) answers `'latched'` the same way, after its own line. Otherwise the adapter asks its latched gate once more (`latchedNow`): a persona latched meanwhile (for example by a launch outside the restart serializer while the `read-pane` was awaited) gets `'transient'` with no notice. Otherwise it defers (`deferPromptRow`, `'transient'`): it logs the deferral, raises the persona's `blocked-on-prompt` not-connected notice (once per episode) and types nothing. The run ends when an attempt reads another state, or its `read-pane` answers GONE or finds no row (a failed status call, a latched persona and an ENVIRONMENT read leave it as it is), when it escalates, when a launch for the persona starts and with the not-connected episode (`forgetNotConnectedEpisode`).

   Once the prompt is answered, a later tick reconnects the persona when it can tell the session is idle again: its row reads `waiting`, or the positive-idle rule shows a `working` row stale. The restart path runs only with auto-restart on, so the notice says exactly that, and to type `/mcp reconnect` if the persona stays disconnected (a row left `working` whose idleness can't be proven is never reconnected on its own).

   **`waiting` rows (b.f2b, b.jg5 SRJ-604).** Before typing into a `waiting` row, the adapter reads its pane once (`checkWaitingRowPane(key, latchedNow)`: one `read-pane` of the row through the shared read-pane, `readWorkingPane`, 40 lines, the row state `waiting`), and probes no tmux session. Its answer is `reconnect`, `defer`, `gone` (`WAITING_ROW_PANE_GONE`) or `absent` (`WAITING_ROW_PANE_ABSENT`), by b.jg5 SRJ-117's waiting-row column:
   - **A pane** → judged with the same `classifyWorkingPane`: a running turn defers (`'transient'`); a prompt or dialog defers too and raises the `blocked-on-prompt` notice (once per episode), unless the adapter's latched gate, asked right before the notice, finds the persona latched (no notice); anything else goes on to the reconnect. The pane may be a single leftover's (b.jg5 SRJ-613), so it is no proof the worker's own session is there.
   - **GONE** (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`) → `gone`: nothing is typed; the adapter calls `escalateRowWithNoPane(key, 'waiting-row-pane-gone', latchedNow)`, which runs the dead-tmux sweep once and answers escalate-dead carrying `waiting-row-pane-gone`, dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)) (`'transient'` when the sweep was refused, or when the persona is found latched before it, with no sweep), as the `working` row's GONE above.
   - **The row absent** (`ErrSpawnNotFound`) → `absent`: the same, with the verdict `row-absent-at-pane-read`, not dead evidence.
   - **CONFLICT or UNUSABLE_NAME** (the reader has latched the persona with the row state `waiting`, b.jg5 SRJ-501, SRJ-512), **or a persona already latched**, which the reader does not read → `defer`, with no notice and nothing typed (b.jg5 SRJ-502).
   - **ENVIRONMENT** (the wrapper has raised `tmux-unavailable`, b.jg5 SRJ-311) → `defer`, nothing typed.
   - **UNCLASSIFIED carrying the stop mark** (`stopping`: the reader's `ErrInvalidFlags` version re-check decided that the server stops, b.jg5 SRJ-204, SRJ-205) → `defer`, nothing typed, and nothing more is called for the persona.
   - **UNAVAILABLE** (timeouts included), **CONFIG** (the wrapper has raised `ad-config-malformed`, b.jg5 SRJ-316) **or any other UNCLASSIFIED** → `reconnect`, on the `waiting` row alone, agent-director's own idle signal, with one line naming the class.

   The check logs one line for each answer but a plain `reconnect`. A findMissing sweep can still mark the row `missing` before the keystrokes land (b.dup): agent-director refuses them as not interactive (`ErrSpawnNotInteractive`), and the reconnect answers `'dead-session'` with cause `row-not-interactive`. That refusal does not prove the worker gone (a finished row is not proof of death, and the row may read `pending` under another process's launch, b.jg5 SRJ-609), so it is not dead evidence and only a route into the restart run's decision: the adapter sweeps with the `row-not-interactive` verdict and answers escalate-dead carrying it, and a `dead` re-probe relaunches the persona in the same run with no kill, carrying the verdict into the ladder, with no spawn-failure notice (b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611).

   **`pending` rows (b.dup, b.jg5 SRJ-314).** A `pending` row's session has not started (SessionStart has not fired). agent-director refuses send-keys to it (`ErrSpawnNotInteractive`), which the reconnect would answer as `'dead-session'` with cause `row-not-interactive`, a route into the restart run's decision only and no proof the worker is gone (b.jg5 SRJ-609), and the session connects its MCP servers on its own once it starts. Two paths reach the one deferral, `deferPendingRow(key, launchStartedAt?)` in `src/server.ts`:
   - **The liveness probe reads `pending`.** `runRestartWork` calls `RestartDeps.deferPendingRow(key, reading)` (wired in `main()`) once, before it looks at the session's connection, so a `pending` row that is connected with its stream, connected but streamless, or disconnected is deferred alike. The reconnect adapter is not called.
   - **The probe read `live`, and the reconnect adapter's own `status` read finds `pending`.** The adapter answers `deferPendingRow`'s `'pending'`; `restart.ts` treats it as it treats `'transient'`, but answers `pending-deferred` instead of `reconnect-deferred`.

   Either way the deferral logs one line (naming the launch start when one was read), types nothing, kills and launches nothing, counts nothing and raises no notice. The run answers `pending-deferred`, so the UNAVAILABLE retry timer records the row read `pending`. The launch start is carried raw from the `status` result (the liveness reading's `launchStartedAt`, or `pendingLaunchStartOf` in the reconnect adapter) and only named in the line: the deferral neither parses nor ages it. Before b.dup the adapter typed into a `pending` row and the refusal raised a spawn-failure notice on every attempt.

   A configured persona's own `pending` row with no launch start reaches neither path (b.jg5 SRJ-513). The `status` read that found it, the liveness adapter's or the reconnect adapter's, applied the own-row `status` step first, which latched the persona with `launch-start-not-recorded` ([The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115)): the probe reads `unknown` and the run stops at its latch check, and the reconnect adapter answers `'transient'` with nothing typed and no `deferPendingRow` hand-off. No automated path sends keys to such a row or kills it. A `pending` row under a key no configured persona uses latches nothing and is deferred as above.

   **A retired key's old life (b.jg5 SRJ-805).** Right after its state read and latched gate, the reconnect adapter asks the session manager's `retiredKeyReadingOf(key)`. A key recorded as retired with no "new life has begun" mark (a mark held in memory after a failed write counts as set) whose row reads live other than `pending` (`waiting`, `working`, a prompt state, or a state CSCB does not know) is the old life (`isRetiredOldLife`): no pane is read and `/mcp reconnect` is never typed into it; the adapter ends the row's `working` evidence and deferral runs, starts the live-row sequence through `startLiveRowSequence` (seeded with the state read, entry at step 1, the conversation not kept, the retired-key flag, a launch at the end, alert context `recovery`), logs one line naming the start's answer, and answers `'transient'`, never counted (`replaceRetiredOldLife`). The pane reads of the `working` and `waiting` branches are awaited, so the adapter asks again right before typing `/mcp reconnect`, after its last latched gate: a key recorded meanwhile gets the same live-row sequence and `'transient'`, with nothing typed. With the mark set the live row is the new life and is reconnected as above; a `pending` row keeps the deferral; a key not recorded is unchanged ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)).
4. **Kill zombie** — right before it the work asks the latch once more (b.jg5 SRJ-502): a persona latched meanwhile (a launch outside the serializer can latch it during the work's awaits, the re-probe's included) answers `latched` with the `Skipping restart` line and is never killed (see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)). Only a GONE-based escalate-dead verdict, dead evidence, is followed by a kill ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)). After any other escalate-dead verdict (`row-not-interactive`, `row-absent-at-pane-read`, `row-read-finished`, or a bare `'escalate-dead'` carrying none) there is no kill: the work logs `relaunchWithoutKillLine`, then `[slack] Relaunching session for persona=<key> cwd="<path>" — kill: none (b.jg5 SRJ-611)`, and goes on to the relaunch carrying the verdict (step 3, **Re-probe**; b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611). A verdict derived from `ErrSpawnNotInteractive` never leads to a kill. A run whose first liveness read is `dead`, and a run after a dead-evidence verdict, make the checked kill: the work (`killBeforeRelaunch`) calls `RestartDeps.killSession(key, lastRead)`, with `lastRead` the run's last `dead` reading: it carries the row state the run read (`ended`, `missing` or no row, `rowRead`) or none (`ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`).

   **The guards stay.** The kill adapter (`_buildKillSessionAdapter` in `src/server.ts`) first asks `isLaunchInFlight(key)`: when a launch for the persona is already running, it logs `[slack] killSession (restart adapter): launch already in flight for persona=<key> — not killing` and answers `KILL_SESSION_NOT_KILLED_GUARD` with no call. Mid-ladder the row can read dead, so a kill here would take down the process the running launch is bringing up; the relaunch in step 5 joins that launch instead (b.av2 SR-6.6). A persona whose `claude_config_dir` cannot be resolved to a real path gets no call either (`holdLaunchIfConfigDirUnresolvable`, `[slack] killSession (restart adapter): persona=<key> claude_config_dir cannot be resolved to a real path — not killing; its row is kept`), and the relaunch gate then answers the launch `'skipped'`. After either guard the work logs `[slack] Relaunching session for persona=<key> cwd="<path>" — kill: not killed (a guard made no call)` and goes on as it always has.

   **The checked kill (b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-701, SRJ-702).** Otherwise the adapter's kill runs through the bounded retry (`retryPersonaKill`, inside the restart work's recovery attempt, on the clock the adapter was built with; [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The bounded kill retry**), each try one checked kill, `killPersonaInstance(key, { context: KILL_CONTEXT_ATTEMPT })`. The retry is seeded with the run's `dead` reading: only a live row's kill is retried, so this kill is one try, its outcome standing at once, with no `status` read and no wait. It logs its one try line (`[slack] killSession (restart adapter): kill try 1 of 1 for cscb_<key>: <outcome> — <what follows> (b.jg5 SRJ-702)`, and, for an `ErrTmuxKillFailed`, the end line naming the ordinary alert decision), then `[slack] killSession (restart adapter): kill for persona=<key>: <outcome>` (`describeKillOutcome`, `kill_sent` included), does the outcome's own handling (below), raises the retry's alert decision (`raisePersonaKillFailureAlert`, context `recovery`; [The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007)) and answers the outcome, so any alert comes before the launch: an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` that stands raises the ordinary version. This kill follows a `dead` reading, so it is not a kill of a row read live: it is not tmux-touching and starts no `tmux-unresponsive` condition. The work launches only after a success: a result with `kill_sent` true or false, a result with no `kill_sent` field, `ErrSpawnNotFound`, or GONE. It then logs `[slack] Relaunching session for persona=<key> cwd="<path>" — kill: <outcome>` (`relaunchAfterKillLine`) and goes on to step 5. Every other answer launches nothing, records no success or failure and leaves the counter, backoff and cap latch as they were (SRJ-302), and the kill is never repeated:
   - **CONFLICT:** the adapter latches P through the latch's CONFLICT entry (`latchOnRestartKillOutcome`; b.jg5 SRJ-501, SRJ-505) with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery" (`next-check-or-recovery`) and logs `[slack] killSession (restart adapter): kill refused for persona=<key>: <failure> — CONFLICT: <latch outcome>; no spawn-failure notice; nothing more is called (b.jg5 SRJ-105, SRJ-501)`. A "not this launch's session" answer is the kill backstop of [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104) (**No site acts on a pane alone**). The work logs `[slack] Session kill for persona=<key> did not succeed (<outcome>) — the persona is latched; no relaunch; not counted` and answers `latched` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_LATCHED`); the latched persona's kill is never sent again.
   - **UNUSABLE NAME:** the adapter latches P through the unusable-name entry (b.jg5 SRJ-512) and logs `[slack] killSession (restart adapter): kill refused for persona=<key>: <failure> — UNUSABLE NAME: <latch outcome>; no spawn-failure notice; nothing more is called (b.jg5 SRJ-105, SRJ-512)`; the work logs the same latched line and answers `latched`.
   - Either latch records the row state the run last read (`lastRead`) with no further `status` read. Only a reading that carries none (`ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`) leads to one latch-time `status` read, its lines prefixed `killSession (restart adapter)`.
   - **UNAVAILABLE** (`ErrTmuxKillFailed` included), **ENVIRONMENT** (the wrapper raises `tmux-unavailable`, b.jg5 SRJ-311), **CONFIG** (the wrapper raises `ad-config-malformed`, b.jg5 SRJ-316) and **UNCLASSIFIED** (`ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` included, whose wrapper still raises `ad-unreachable`; and a class the kill has no row for, which `killPersonaInstance` reports as UNCLASSIFIED): the persona's retry timer is armed inside the attempt (an UNAVAILABLE one once, by the outcome that stands, `reportDeferredUnavailable`), an UNCLASSIFIED outcome feeds its unclassified-error episode (b.jg5 SRJ-313), and the work logs `[slack] Session kill for persona=<key> did not succeed (<outcome>) — no relaunch; not counted` and answers `refused` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_REFUSED`).
   - **Latched meanwhile (b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-502):** after any non-success but a version re-check's stop, the work asks the latched query once more; a persona latched while the kill ran (a latch set elsewhere; a query that throws counts as latched) gets the latched line above and `latched`, with no relaunch and nothing counted.
   - **`ErrInvalidFlags`:** one immediate version re-check (b.jg5 SRJ-104, SRJ-204); after a re-check that does not stop, the outcome is UNCLASSIFIED, as above. When the re-check decides that the server stops, the adapter latches nothing, and the work logs `[slack] Session kill for persona=<key> did not succeed (<outcome>) — the version re-check decided that the server stops; no relaunch; not counted; nothing more is called` (`killStopsServerLine`) and answers `shutting-down` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_SHUTTING_DOWN`), recording nothing (b.jg5 SRJ-205).
   - A `killSession` that throws, or answers something that is not a kill outcome, shows no success: the work logs the same not-succeeded line with `killSession threw: <error>` or `killSession answered no kill outcome` in the parentheses and answers `refused`.
5. **Relaunch** — `launchSession(key, personaConfig, { canLaunch: canRelaunch, deadEvidence })` asks the relaunch gate (`createPersonaRelaunchGate` in `src/persona-start.ts`) first, then looks up the persona with that key (`false` when there is none; asking the gate first keeps a key a confirmed apply removed from counting as a failure), and otherwise collapses `spawnForPersona`'s richer outcome to `true`, `false`, `'skipped'` or `'refused'` — the single counting site (SR-25.1). The b.f2b action `not-reconnected` (a `working`-row wait that ended with the session alive and nothing typed, or that its teardown cancelled) maps to `true`: the session runs, so it is not a failure. Resume vs fresh is decided by the SR-1.4 collision-then-act dispatch (no separate `sessionId` arg from CSCB — agent-director owns resume state), the same persona-keyed ladder as startup, so the b.av2 SR-6.2 `cwd` and `config_dir` guards apply to runtime relaunches too. A relaunch runs only the launch: it never repeats the start bring-up's credentials, working-directory or Slack steps (Server-Managed Startup step 5): a row in another directory, and a row whose `config_dir` label is missing or differs, is replaced rather than resumed, with no row deleted: a finished row by a reuse spawn of the same id, a live row through the live-row sequence first (the relaunch then answers `'refused'` and the work `sequence-waiting`). For a key recorded as retired the relaunch is a reuse spawn, never a `resume`, and its success (`fresh-retired`) maps to `true` ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)). Like every launch, the relaunch is preceded by the trust patch for the persona's working directory in its effective config dir (the pre-launch patcher at the top of the ladder; see startup step 4a-bis), and a patch failure there is logged only. Its spawn or resume is likewise immediately preceded by the reply-guard steps (startup step 5), so the persona's record is rewritten with its current effective `stop_hook_bootstrap`; a relaunch that only reconnects writes nothing. The relaunch goes through `spawnForPersona`'s one-in-flight-launch-per-persona rule (b.av2 SR-6.3), so a relaunch that overlaps a still-running launch for the same persona (the start pass or another trigger) joins it and receives its outcome. `restart.ts` counts each `launchSession` result it receives, so overlapping restarts that join one failed launch count that failure once per caller. A joined launch's failure record and notice follow the mode (startup or runtime) of the launch that actually ran, not of the caller that joined it. On a `true` outcome, `recordSuccess` resets the counter and cap latch; on `false`, `recordFailure` increments it. The live-row sequence's final launch does not come back through `launchSession`: the sequence-launch entry counts its result once, by class (only a LAUNCH FAILURE or DIRECTORY failure, the result carrying `countedClass`), through `recordLaunchResultOutsideRestartWork` (`restart.ts`), and a call that joins that launch gets any failure neither refused nor stopping as the uncounted refused result ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)).

   **The carried verdict (b.jg5 SRJ-611).** A relaunch that follows an escalate-dead answer passes the verdict that answer carried (`RestartDeps.launchSession`'s fourth argument, `deadEvidence`), unchanged, through `main()`'s binding to `launchSession` and on to `spawnForPersona`, which decides it again from its cause or verdict (`carriedDeadEvidenceOf`) and keeps it for the ladder's run; every other launch passes none. A relaunch that joins a launch already in flight gets that launch's result, and its verdict is dropped with one line (`joinedLaunchDropsDeadEvidenceLine`). In the ladder the verdict goes with each path to `resumeOrFreshSpawn`: the `ended`/`missing` branch names it in one `deadSessionRouteLine`, and a dead-session route holds dead evidence when its own cause or the carried verdict is dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)). In the ladder the evidence reaches `resumeOrFreshSpawn`, where two steps decide on it: the not-resumable step starts the live-row sequence only when the path holds dead evidence, and a resume site's replacement of a row last read live re-reads the row first when it holds none (Server-Managed Startup step 5; b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-609). Their lines name it.

   **Refused and stopping launches are not counted (b.jg5 SRJ-301, SRJ-302).** A `failed` launch whose attempt's last agent-director error armed the persona's UNAVAILABLE retry timer comes back as `'refused'` (armed means the trigger sink answered that the persona has a timer after the call; when nothing is armed, after the controller is closed or when its first timer could not be set, the failure is an ordinary `false`): `restart.ts` records neither success nor failure, leaves the counter, backoff and cap latch as they were and logs `[slack] Session relaunch refused for persona=<key> — not counted; its UNAVAILABLE retry timer owns the persona`. A persona is never given up on for UNAVAILABLE or UNCLASSIFIED alone; only a counted launch failure (`false`) moves toward `RESTART_FAILURE_CAP`. The refusal itself posts no spawn-failure notice and records no `spawn-failed` entry: the ladder handles it at the site where it met it (Server-Managed Startup step 5). A resume whose `ErrInvalidFlags` re-check decided the stop comes back as `'skipped'` and is not counted either, and so does a launch whose reconnect's re-check decided it. A launch whose reconnect was `transient` for a persona that is not latched comes back `'refused'` (the ladder's uncounted refused result, b.jg5 SRJ-118). So does a `latched` launch (b.jg5 SRJ-502, SRJ-1015): the persona was already latched, or latched at a CONFLICT in this launch; the restart work then asks the latched query again and, finding it latched, logs `[slack] Session relaunch for persona=<key> ended latched — not counted; nothing more is done for it` and answers `latched`, recording nothing. A latched query that throws there is taken as latched too: the line then reads `ended latched (the latched query failed: <error> — taken as latched) — not counted; …`. A launch held for the persona's running live-row sequence (`sequence-waiting`, b.jg5 SRJ-706, SRJ-1015) comes back `'refused'` too: it made no call and records nothing.

   **Relaunch gate.** The gate (`createPersonaRelaunchGate`, over the connection manager and the bring-up controller) answers true only while the persona's Slack connection is serving, its bring-up outcome is `up` and its key is in the applied set (see the applied-set guard under Server-Managed Startup step 5). A key outside the applied set is refused first, whatever its status, with `[slack] persona=<key>: not relaunched — it is no longer in the applied configuration`, and restart.ts then logs its usual `Not scheduling restart` line. Besides step 1's up check, `launchSession` asks it, which covers a change during the kill. When that check answers false, `launchSession` returns `'skipped'` without spawning or running the trust patch or the reply-guard steps, and `restart.ts` records neither success nor failure, so the counter, backoff and cap latch stay as they were and no cap notice is raised. The gate's own log lines are in the `persona-start.ts` entry of the Module Map. Once the persona is up again it is eligible, and its next restart counts normally.
6. **Cap latch** — after the 5th consecutive failure (`RESTART_FAILURE_CAP = 5`, exported from `src/restart.ts`), `shouldNotifyCap(key, …)` fires once per episode and `onCapReached(key)` calls the session manager's `notifyRestartCapReached(key)`, which raises a synthetic `ErrSpawnCapReached` spawn-failure notice through the per-persona notifier to the persona's destination, with the remediation "restart the server to retry — automatic restarts are suspended for this persona"; **no** further timer is scheduled. `main()`'s `onCapReached` also ends the persona's unclassified-error episode silently (`UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_CAPPED`), each step isolated. A capped persona has no registered session; an inbound Slack message hits the no-session branch in `src/persona-routing.ts`, whose `decideLostMessageState` detects the cap (`isAtCap(key, RESTART_FAILURE_CAP)`) and does **not** fire a restart — firing one would only burn a spawn attempt against a persona that cannot come up. The persona's destination gets a lost-message notice in the `restart-limit-reached` state, saying automatic restarts are suspended and the server must be restarted. Only a **server restart** clears the in-process counter (lost on restart by design) and gives the persona a fresh attempt.

#### Dead evidence (b.jg5 SRJ-611)

Every `dead-session` and escalate-dead verdict carries what proved it, and one pure decision, `isDeadEvidence` (`src/session-manager.ts`), says whether that is dead evidence. It is decided by value alone, with an exhaustive switch over `DEAD_SESSION_CAUSES` and `ESCALATE_DEAD_VERDICTS`, so a new cause or verdict fails the typecheck until it is decided; an unknown value, `undefined` and `DEAD_EVIDENCE_NONE` are not dead evidence (fail safe).

| Cause or verdict | Where it comes from | Dead evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `tmux-gone` (cause) | the reconnect's `send-keys` answered GONE (`ErrTmuxSendKeys`) | yes |
| `dead-session` (verdict) | the restart adapter's verdict for `tmux-gone` | yes |
| `working-tmux-gone` (verdict) | the `working` defer's `read-pane` answered GONE (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`) | yes |
| `waiting-row-pane-gone` (verdict) | the `waiting`-row check's `read-pane` answered GONE | yes |
| `prompt-row-tmux-gone` (verdict) | the prompt-row verdict's `read-pane` answered GONE | yes |
| `prompt-row-ladder-gone` (cause) | the collision ladder's prompt-row `read-pane` answered GONE (`launchOnPromptRow`) | yes |
| `row-not-interactive` (cause and verdict) | the reconnect's keystrokes refused as not interactive (`ErrSpawnNotInteractive`) | no |
| `row-absent` (cause) | no row (`ErrSpawnNotFound`) at the reconnect, the launch wait's `status` read or the ladder's prompt-row `read-pane` | no |
| `row-absent-at-pane-read` (verdict) | no row at a restart-path `read-pane` or the reconnect | no |
| `row-read-finished` (cause) | the launch wait's `status` read, or the prompt row's 10-minute sweep, read the row `ended` or `missing` | no |

A refused `send-keys`, a finished row or an absent row proves nothing about the worker's process: the row may be `pending` under another process's launch (b.jg5 SRJ-613). A path carries its verdict as a `CarriedDeadEvidence` (`{ source, evidence }`, branded so that only `carriedDeadEvidenceOf` and `CARRIED_DEAD_EVIDENCE_NONE` make one and a value built by hand fails the typecheck; the restart module imports the type only and decides the kill only from its `evidence` flag); its lines render it with `describeDeadEvidence` as `cause=<source>: dead evidence (GONE-based)`, `cause=<source>: not dead evidence` or `no cause carried: not dead evidence`. Where it travels:

- **The launch wait** (`waitForWaitingAndReconnectWithCause`): each `dead-session` end carries one cause (`WaitDeadSession`): the reconnect's own, `row-absent` for an absent row, or `row-read-finished` with the state read.
- **The collision ladder:** each dead-session route of the `waiting` and `working` branches (`deadSessionRoute`) logs `deadSessionRouteLine` and hands `resumeOrFreshSpawn` the evidence the path holds: its own cause, or the verdict the restart path carried in, whichever is dead evidence (`heldDeadEvidence`). The `find-missing` run before the `resume` (`reconcileMissingFirst`) runs on every such route, for every cause; only the evidence differs. The prompt-row recovery hands on `prompt-row-ladder-gone` after a GONE and `row-absent` after an absent row.
- **The restart path:** every escalate-dead answer of the reconnect adapter carries the verdict it swept with (`ReconnectEscalateDead`); after a `dead` re-probe, only dead evidence leads to the checked kill before the relaunch (Auto-Restart step 4), and the relaunch carries the verdict into the ladder (step 5).

Two ladder steps decide on the evidence a path holds (Server-Managed Startup step 5):

- **The not-resumable step** (`decideNotResumable`, b.jg5 SRJ-710): a `resume` that answered `ErrSpawnNotResumable`, whose re-read finds the row in a known live state other than `pending` (`AGENT_DIRECTOR_LIVE_STATES`), starts the live-row sequence (conversation kept, ending in `resume`) only with dead evidence; without it the answer is the lost race. A `pending` re-read starts no sequence of its own, whatever the evidence, and a re-read in a state CSCB does not know (an unreadable one included) is the lost race whatever the evidence: an unknown state never leads to a kill.
- **A resume site's replacement** (`replaceAtResumeSite`, b.jg5 SRJ-609): a row last read live on a path with no dead evidence is read again before the replace step, so its earlier live read never starts the sequence.

A verdict derived from `ErrSpawnNotInteractive` never leads to a kill (b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611), nor does any other verdict that is not dead evidence, nor does `ErrSpawnNotResumable` by itself.

#### UNAVAILABLE retry (b.jg5 SRJ-303, SRJ-305)

A persona that agent-director refused is brought back by the restart path's own decision, run by its retry timer instead of a restart timer. `main()` builds one controller (`createUnavailableRetryController`) whose retry action is `createFullModeRetryAction` over the restart module's retry entry, `runRestartRetry(key, cwd, isInFlight)`, and the session manager's row read, `readPersonaRowState`. Each timer runs in one of two modes: in full mode a retry reruns the restart path's decision (below); in pending-only mode it only reads the persona's row (see [Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306)). A full-mode retry runs the steps above with two left out: step 1's delay check and step 2's backoff timer. `getRestartDelay` is never read, no restart timer is armed, cleared or needed, and it runs with `session_restart_delay` 0 too. Each full-mode retry:

1. **Pre-call checks** — before any call, the action stops the timer, in this order, when the server is shutting down, the persona is not in the applied configuration (`getAppliedPersona`), it is latched (`FullModeRetryDeps.isLatched`, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED`; see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)), it is held on `ErrInvalidFlags` (`FullModeRetryDeps.isHeld`, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_HELD`; see [The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold](#the-errinvalidflags-hold-bjg5-srj-207-srj-1008)), it is not up (the relaunch gate), or it is at the restart cap (`isAtCap(key, RESTART_FAILURE_CAP)`). These run outside the serializer.
2. **Through the serializer** — `runRestartRetry` marks the key active (`isRestartPendingOrActive`, so the health tick skips the persona meanwhile) and submits its work through the same `RestartDeps.serialize` as a fired restart timer. Before `initRestart` has run it does nothing and answers `not-initialised`.
3. **In-flight check first** — inside that serialized work, after the latched gate (`RestartDeps.isLatched`: a persona that latched while the retry waited answers `latched` with no agent-director call) and the held gate (`RestartDeps.isHeld`: a persona held while it waited answers `held` the same way), the first step is the "blocks a retry" binding (`isPersonaRetryBlocked` in `main()`, the controller's `isInFlight`: the session manager's `isLaunchInFlight` or `isLiveRowSequenceRunning`, b.jg5 SRJ-706; a check that throws counts as in flight). While a launch call is in flight or a live-row sequence runs for the persona, the retry makes no agent-director call and answers `in-flight`, with the line `[slack] Restart retry skipped for persona=<key> — a launch is in flight; no agent-director call` in both cases (again-reason `launch-in-flight`). A running dialog approver is not in this binding and never skips a retry (b.jg5 SRJ-303, SRJ-401): it runs after its launch call returned. The health tick, the session-disconnect handler and the lost-message routing's read gate (`isWorkInFlight`, Inbound step 7) take the broader "in flight for P" binding, `isPersonaWorkInFlight`, built from this one (`isPersonaRetryBlocked(key) || isDialogApproverRunning(key)`), so the tick never attempts over work that holds back a retry. The skip is a refusal: the timer re-arms at the doubled wait.
4. **Cap check second** — next, still inside the serialized work, the restart cap (`isAtCap(key, RESTART_FAILURE_CAP)`). A retry queued behind other restart work for the persona can find the cap reached while it waited: a counted failure in that work reached it after the pre-call check. It then logs `[slack] Restart retry skipped for persona=<key> — the persona is at the restart cap; nothing killed or launched` and answers `capped`, with no agent-director call, nothing counted and no notice (the cap notice went out with the failure that reached the cap). Failures are counted only inside restart work, which the serializer runs one at a time per persona, so the cap cannot be reached while the retry's own work runs. The restart timer's own work does not ask the cap.
5. **The restart path's decision** — otherwise it runs `runRestartWork`: its latched gate, held gate and live-row sequence gate (a sequence that started after the in-flight check answers `sequence-waiting` here), then, as one recovery attempt, step 1's shutdown and up checks, the liveness read (step 3), then a return with nothing done on `unknown`, the `pending` deferral on `pending` (whatever the session's connection shows), a reconnect of a `live` row (for a retired key's old life, the live-row sequence instead, [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart) step 3), or, on `dead` only, the checked kill (step 4) and the launch (step 5; for a retired key a reuse spawn, never a `resume`, [Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)), with the same success and failure accounting. It never launches over a live or `pending` row. A `live` persona already connected with its stream gets no launch. An `unknown` reading's arm hook lands while the timer is running its retry, so it keeps the due time; the answer below re-arms the timer.

`runRestartWork` answers what it did (`RESTART_OUTCOME_*`; the restart timer ignores it), and the action maps the outcome:

| Outcome | The retry timer |
|---|---|
| `already-connected` (the row reads live, connected with its stream), `reconnected` | Stops: nothing left to recover. `already-connected` also ends a holding `tmux-unresponsive` condition and clears `tmux-unavailable` through `FullModeRetryDeps.endTmuxUnresponsive` (reason `retry`, reading `live`); `reconnected` has no end hook of its own: its tmux-touching calls (the reconnect's `send-keys`) end the condition and clear the flag at the wrapper when they succeed |
| `capped` (a counted launch failure reached the cap, or the persona was already at it when the retry's serialized work started: the cap check) | Stops: at the restart cap |
| `not-up` | Stops: the persona is not up; its bring-up owns it |
| `launch-skipped` (the launch's own gate declined it) | Stops |
| `shutting-down` | Stops |
| `latched` (the work's latched gate found the persona latched, or its launch latched it) | Stops: the persona is latched (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED`) |
| `held` (the work's held gate found the persona held on `ErrInvalidFlags`, or its launch's reuse spawn held it) | Stops: the persona is held on `ErrInvalidFlags` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_HELD`) |
| `in-flight` (a launch call in flight, or a live-row sequence running, at the retry entry's in-flight check) | Re-arms at the next wait (a refusal; again-reason `launch-in-flight`) |
| `sequence-waiting` (the work's live-row sequence gate found a sequence running) | Re-arms at the next wait (again-reason `live-row-sequence-waiting`, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_AGAIN_SEQUENCE_WAITING`, a refusal); never stops the timer |
| `refused` (the launch was refused, and its UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED outcome armed the timer during the run; or the kill before it did not succeed and latched nothing, step 4) | Re-arms; the re-armed line names that cause |
| `counted-failure` (a launch failure counted below the cap) | Re-arms, until the cap stops it |
| `reconnect-deferred` (the reconnect did not succeed or was deferred, on a row other than `pending`) | Re-arms |
| `pending-deferred` (the run found the row `pending` and deferred it: the liveness probe read it `pending`, whatever the session's connection showed, or the reconnect adapter's read or b.d61's re-probe did) | Re-arms (a refusal, never "nothing left to recover", even for a session connected with its stream), recording `pending` as the last row read; stays in full mode |
| `launched` | Re-arms, recording `pending` (the launch's row) as the last row read, in pending-only mode: the timer keeps running after a successful launch. The switch is not taken, and the timer stays in full mode, when `arm` recorded another cause during that retry or a `kill-failed` cause is recorded |
| `not-initialised` | Re-arms |
| `liveness-unknown` (the liveness read or the re-probe read `unknown`, or threw) | Re-arms at the next wait (again-reason `liveness-unknown`, a refusal); never stops the timer. It read no row, so the last row read is kept as it is (`keepsLastRow`) |

Every re-arm takes the next wait of the one sequence (30, 60, 120, 240, 300, 300 … s), measured from the end of the retry, so, when retries take no time, they fall 30, 90, 210, 450 and 750 s after the arm, then every 300 s; nothing resets the wait count while the timer runs, a switch of mode included. A retry that throws, rejects or gives no answer re-arms too. A trigger while armed, waiting or running, keeps the due time and the wait count and records its cause kind. Two retries for one persona never overlap. Every retry, in either mode and a retry skipped for a launch in flight included, first calls the optional observer `UnavailableRetryDeps.onRetryFire(key, firedAt)` after its retry line and before its action; production binds the `tmux-unresponsive` condition's onset check at a retry, which posts the onset with the health check off ([Its three posts](#its-three-posts-bjg5-srj-308-srj-309-srj-1006)). The observer changes nothing here and a throw from it is swallowed.

**ENVIRONMENT (b.jg5 SRJ-311).** An `ErrTmuxNotAvailable` answer from any verb for the persona, `kill` included, raises `tmux-unavailable` and arms the persona's timer with the `environment` cause, in or out of an attempt (the `unavailable-retry.ts` entry of the Module Map); repeated answers raise one onset and keep the due time. Two kills are the exception (b.jg5 SRJ-110; hatch A3): a persona teardown's kill and a start-sweep kill arm nothing, and raise `tmux-unavailable` only for a persona in the applied configuration (for a teardown, the persona torn down; for the sweep, the persona the swept row's label names); otherwise the answer is only logged and recorded. The onset is *tmux server changed* when the first raising answer is the re-bound-socket form (`isDifferentTmuxServerError`), else *tmux unavailable* (b.jg5 SRJ-1021; the `outage-state.ts` entry); everything below holds for both forms. It is a refusal at every launch and recovery site: the collision ladder, the reconnect keystrokes, the `working`-row wait's sweeps and the restart path's kill. At the `working`-row wait's `status` reads it is transient instead: the wait goes on, and at its timeout it ends `not-reconnected` (b.jg5 SRJ-605). The startup-dialog approver, which runs outside every attempt, is a raising site too: the wrapper raises the outage and arms the timer as from any verb, and the approver stops (`tmux-unavailable`) with nothing typed and nothing counted (Server-Managed Startup step 5, Pre-session dialog approval). It never leads to a kill, delete or launch, never gives `dead-session`, posts no spawn-failure notice and records no `spawn-failed` entry. A launch it ends is `refused`, so it is never counted, and it never starts `tmux-unresponsive`. It is retried only on this timer's backoff, with `session_restart_delay` 0 and `health_check_interval` 0 alike: while `tmux-unavailable` is raised, the health tick reads the persona but makes no attempt for it ([Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 1), and the timer retries on its backoff; a tick that finds such a persona not healthy with no timer armed (a retry that stopped as not up, on a declined launch or on a failed run leaves the flag raised) arms one with the `environment` cause. A message lost while `tmux-unavailable` is raised schedules no restart; below the restart cap it arms a missing timer first (not while P is latched or a launch is in flight) and reports `not-answering`, and at the cap it arms nothing and reports the next state that applies, usually `restart-limit-reached` ([Inbound step 7](#inbound-slack--claude-code)). A session disconnect (`restartDisconnectedPersona` in `server.ts`, reached from `onsessionclosed` and the SSE abort) while the flag is raised never schedules a restart and logs one line ([Disconnection](#disconnection) step 3): with the timer armed (`isArmed`) it does nothing more, since the timer recovers it; with none armed it arms one with the `environment` cause (`armEnvironmentRetryTimer`, the tick's arm path), unless the persona is latched or work is in flight for it, which arm nothing.
