A timer so armed for a persona held on `ErrInvalidFlags` stops at its first retry on the pre-call held check, with no agent-director call. The outage ends, and the timer stops through the condition-end entry (Condition ends, below), only when tmux answers: a tmux-touching success or GONE error, or a health tick or retry that finds the row live other than `pending`, connected and with its stream. A successful read (`status`, `get`, `list`, `find-missing`) or `delete` ends neither.

**CONFIG (b.jg5 SRJ-316).** An `ErrConfigMalformed` answer (agent-director refuses its config file) from any verb for the persona, `kill` and the reads included, raises `ad-config-malformed` (the `outage-state.ts` entry of the Module Map) and arms the persona's timer with the `config` cause (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_CONFIG`), in or out of an attempt, so the persona is retried on this timer's backoff whatever `session_restart_delay` and `health_check_interval` are; repeated answers raise one onset and keep the due time. A persona teardown's kill and a start-sweep kill are the exception, as for ENVIRONMENT: they arm nothing and raise `ad-config-malformed` only for a configured persona (b.jg5 SRJ-110; hatch A3). An onset raised while the persona's teardown window is open (the teardown's kill, its read between tries, or the launch in flight it waits for), and that outage's all-clear whenever it comes, are written to the server log and a `persona-teardown-notice` entry, never posted (b.jg5 SRJ-1002, SRJ-1003; [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65)). The outage is a notice-episode kind of its own (b.jg5 SRJ-1016), so between the persona's teardown submit and its window its onset is muted as the episodes' posts are: the notifier logs `onset for <ref> of ad-config-malformed not posted — muted, its persona teardown was submitted; its all-clear is written, never posted: <first line>`, posts nothing and writes no entry, and that outage's all-clear is written the same way, never posted (`PERSONA_NOTICE_SUBMIT_MUTED_OUTAGE_CLASSES`). It is a refusal at every launch and recovery site: the collision ladder's spawns (plain and reuse) and resumes, the live-row sequence's kills, the collision `get` and the `ErrJsonlMissing` diagnosis `get`, the reconnect keystrokes, a persona's `find-missing` sweep, and the restart path's kill. At the `working`-row wait's poll and timeout `status` reads it is transient instead: the wait goes on, and at its timeout it ends `not-reconnected` (b.jg5 SRJ-605). The startup-dialog approver, which runs outside every attempt, is a raising site too: the wrapper raises the outage and arms the timer as from any verb, nothing is counted, and the approver keeps polling within its bound B, its next lap at the slow 5 s pace (Server-Managed Startup step 5, Pre-session dialog approval). The live-row sequence makes no kill of a row it last read `pending` while the outage is raised, at step 1 or step 4: it ends without its launch, arming the persona's timer with its other-end cause, and a kill's tries end at a CONFIG read between them on a row last read `pending` ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)). No step follows it: it never leads to a kill, delete or launch, the liveness reading stays `unknown` (never `dead`), it posts no spawn-failure notice, records no `spawn-failed` entry, is never counted toward the failure cap and never starts or continues `tmux-unresponsive`. A launch it ends is `refused`. The outage's clear (a successful wrapped call, or a liveness `status` success or `ErrSpawnNotFound`) posts the all-clear but stops no timer: SRJ-305 gives this outage no stop, and `main()` passes only `tmux-unavailable` clears to the condition-end entry, so the timer stops by the rules below. A message lost while the flag is raised reports `not-answering` only while P's retry timer is armed and P is below the restart cap; otherwise it reports the next state that applies, `restart-limit-reached` at the cap, and can reach `starting-now` below it ([Inbound step 7](#inbound-slack--claude-code)).

**UNCLASSIFIED (b.jg5 SRJ-313).** An UNCLASSIFIED answer (see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)) from any verb inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona arms its timer: with the `unclassified` cause (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_UNCLASSIFIED`) from a non-read verb, with the `read-error` cause from `status`, `get` or `list`. The resume path's `ErrInvalidFlags` and the reconnect's `send-keys` answering `ErrInvalidFlags` (not the reuse spawn's, which holds the persona and arms nothing) arm the `unclassified` cause through the outage state's site entry after the re-check. Outside an attempt it arms nothing and starts no episode. It is a refusal at every launch and recovery site, so it is never counted, never destructive, posts no spawn-failure notice and no condition, and never starts or continues `tmux-unresponsive`. At the `working`-row wait's poll and timeout `status` reads it is transient instead: the wait goes on, and at its timeout it ends `not-reconnected` (b.jg5 SRJ-605). The persona is retried on this timer's backoff, and a human hears of it once, through the unclassified-error alert ([The unclassified-error episode](#the-unclassified-error-episode-bjg5-srj-313-srj-1009)).

**Counting.** Refusals are never counted toward `RESTART_FAILURE_CAP`: a refused launch records nothing (Auto-Restart step 5), and an in-flight skip, a cap skip, a latched skip, a held skip or a `sequence-waiting` skip makes no call. A CONFLICT is never counted either: the launch it ends answers `latched`, which records nothing. Nor is a hold: a launch whose reuse spawn met `ErrInvalidFlags` answers `held`, which records nothing. A retry's own launch failure is counted at Auto-Restart step 5's single counting site like any other, so it moves the persona toward the cap, and at the cap the timer stops. A successful launch records a success, as in Auto-Restart step 5, and leaves the timer running, in pending-only mode unless the switch is blocked (the `launched` row above): the next retry reads the new row and stops the timer once it is out of `pending`. The live-row sequence's final launch is counted once by its own entry (`launchForLiveRowSequence`), by class: only a LAUNCH FAILURE (`ErrTmuxSessionCreate`) or DIRECTORY (`ErrCwdNotFound`, `ErrCwdNotADirectory`) failure from the `resume` or the reuse spawn counts, the result carrying `countedClass`; a `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotFound`, a reuse collision, and every refused, latched, held, stopping or deferred result count nothing, and a call joining that launch gets the uncounted refused answer ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)).

**The live-row sequence's causes (b.jg5 SRJ-301, SRJ-717).** A live-row sequence that ends without its launch arms the persona's timer through the trigger sink, with `sequence-not-judged` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_SEQUENCE_NOT_JUDGED`) after a run did not judge its `pending` row, and with `sequence-ended-without-launch` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_SEQUENCE_ENDED`) after any other end without the launch; a trigger while armed keeps the due time, as any trigger does. Neither cause is ever counted toward `RESTART_FAILURE_CAP`, and the sequence itself never calls the failure counter (its final launch's result is counted once by the session manager's sequence-launch entry). A reuse spawn's collision at the final launch arms `reuse-collision` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_REUSE_COLLISION`) instead, and a final `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotResumable` whose re-read found a lost race arms `spawn-not-resumable-lost-race` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_LOST_RACE`, b.jg5 SRJ-710; one whose re-read found the row `pending` arms `sequence-ended-without-launch`), neither counted. A final launch whose `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` armed the timer at once in pending-only mode gets no cause from the sequence. A stop for a latch, a teardown or shutdown, an abort that latched the persona, a final launch that answered `held` (b.jg5 SRJ-207) and the no-launch form arm nothing. See [The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717) for every end and its arm.

**Stop rules and where each is checked.**

| Stop | Checked at |
|---|---|
| Nothing left to recover | The `already-connected` or `reconnected` outcome |
| The restart cap, reached through counted launch failures | The pre-call `isAtCap` check; the retry entry's cap check inside its serialized work (the cap check above); the `capped` outcome |
| The persona is not up | The pre-call relaunch gate; the `not-up` and `launch-skipped` outcomes |
| The persona is not in the applied configuration | The pre-call `getAppliedPersona` lookup (the relaunch gate refuses it too) |
| The persona latches, whatever the case and whatever the timer's causes or last row read | The latch's hold, which calls `stop(key, UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED)` on every set, never `conditionEnded`, so neither exception below keeps the timer; the pre-call latched check, for a timer armed after the latch; the `latched` outcome |
| The persona is held on `ErrInvalidFlags`, whatever the timer's causes or last row read (b.jg5 SRJ-207) | The hold's set reaction, which calls `stop(key, UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_HELD)` at each new hold, never `conditionEnded`, so neither exception below keeps the timer; the pre-call held check, right after the latched one, for a timer armed while the persona is held; the `held` outcome. Not terminal: once the hold ends a later refusal can arm the timer again |
| The persona is torn down | [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65) step 1 (`stopRetryTimer`), again in step 3 once its launch in flight settled (a timer that launch armed), once more in step 8 after its kill (which arms none), and at submit for a destructive modify's old half |
| The server shuts down | The pre-call shutdown check; the `shutting-down` outcome; `shutdown()` closes the controller ([Graceful Shutdown](#graceful-shutdown-sr-11-event-11)), which also refuses every later arm |
| In pending-only mode, the row is out of `pending` (live, `ended`, `missing` or gone), unless a full-mode cause armed the timer during that retry | The pending-only row read ([Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306)) |
| A condition ends (`tmux-unresponsive`, `tmux-unavailable`), except while the last row read is `pending` or a `kill-failed` cause is recorded | `conditionEnded`: called by every end of the `tmux-unresponsive` condition ([The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310)) and every real clear of `tmux-unavailable` (the outage state's cleared-flag observer) |

The pre-call checks run in both modes, and no other stop is overridden: only the pending-only row read's stops yield to a full-mode cause. A stop forgets the persona, so a later trigger starts again at the first wait. A retry already running when its timer is stopped finishes, but its answer is dropped.

**The stop observer (b.jg5 SRJ-305, SRJ-308, SRJ-309).** Every real stop of a persona's timer calls the controller's optional `onStopped(key, reason)` once, after its stopped line and before the stop's hand-off: every stop in the table above, `stop`, `stopAll` and `close`, and a timer dropped because its re-arm failed (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_RUN_FAILED`, `its retry run failed`). A call that finds nothing armed, a first arm that failed (no timer ever ran) and a pending-only stop that yielded to a full-mode cause are not stops and call nothing. A throwing observer is swallowed and changes nothing about the stop. `main()` binds it to two consumers, each isolated so a throw in one does not skip the other: the `tmux-unresponsive` condition's `cancelAlert(key, reason)`, so any stop while the condition holds holds its onset back until a later refusal and cancels an alert check that has not posted ([Its three posts](#its-three-posts-bjg5-srj-308-srj-309-srj-1006)), then the unclassified-error episodes' `retryStopped(key, reason)`, which ends the persona's unclassified-error episode only for the stops `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_RECOVERED` (nothing left to recover), `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_ROW_LIVE` (a pending-only retry read the row live out of `pending`), `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_TMUX_UNAVAILABLE_CLEARED` and `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_TMUX_UNRESPONSIVE_ENDED` (the timer's tmux condition ended) and `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_ROW_GONE` (a pending-only retry read the row `ended` or `missing`, or found none) ([The unclassified-error episode](#the-unclassified-error-episode-bjg5-srj-313-srj-1009)). The terminal stop reasons, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_TERMINAL_STOPS` (torn down, not in the applied configuration, shutdown), are the ones after which a later refusal never arms that alert check again and never lets the onset post again in that episode; a terminal stop also withdraws a re-arm that an earlier non-terminal stop in the episode left pending. The timer's lines and the retry entry's are listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

#### Pending-only mode (b.jg5 SRJ-303, SRJ-305, SRJ-306)

A pending-only timer watches a row left `pending` without typing into it or launching over it.

**Entering and leaving.** A timer enters pending-only mode in two ways: the direct entry `armPendingOnly(key)`, for a covered `pending` row, and the switch after a full-mode retry whose launch succeeded (`launched`). The switch is taken only when no other cause armed the timer (`arm`) during that retry and no `kill-failed` cause is recorded; otherwise the timer stays in full mode. The wait count carries on through the switch. `armPendingOnly`'s one caller is the outage state's launch-failure arm (`armPendingOnlyAfterLaunchFailure`): a launch's `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` (a plain spawn's or a `resume`'s in the collision ladder, or the reuse spawn's or the `resume`'s at the live-row sequence's final launch) arms the persona's timer at once in pending-only mode, so the retry's read of the row decides what the failure left (b.jg5 SRJ-111, SRJ-112, SRJ-113, SRJ-409). Covered `pending` rows have no production entry, so in production a timer enters pending-only mode through an `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` at a collision-ladder launch or at the final launch of a live-row sequence a ladder replacement site started, or through a retry's successful launch. On a timer already armed, `armPendingOnly` keeps the due time, the wait count and the mode, and records its cause and `pending` as the last row read, so a full-mode timer stays in full mode. Any other cause that arms a pending-only timer (`arm`) promotes it to full mode and keeps its due time; nothing else leaves pending-only mode.

**The last row read.** After each retry it is the `row` of that retry's answer (`pending` for `pending-deferred`, `launched`, and a pending-only `row-pending` or `launch-in-flight`; the row read for a stop that yielded, below), else `pending` when `armPendingOnly` landed during that retry, else kept as it is when the answer read no row (`keepsLastRow`: the `liveness-unknown` outcome), else cleared. A retry that fails (throws or rejects) keeps it. `view` shows it as `lastRow`, with the `mode`.

**Each pending-only retry.** The same pre-call checks as full mode run first (shutdown, not applied, not up, at the cap), then the same "blocks a retry" check as in full mode (a running dialog approver does not skip it). Unless a launch call is in flight, it makes one `status` call (`readPersonaRowState`) inside a recovery attempt for the persona, and the state decides (the read also carries a `pending` row's raw launch start, which no retry uses yet):

| Row read | The retry timer |
|---|---|
| None: a launch call is in flight (the predicate answers true or throws) | Re-arms at the next wait (`launch-in-flight`, a refusal), with no agent-director call; the last row read stays `pending` |
| `pending` with no launch start (b.jg5 SRJ-513) | The read latches the persona with `launch-start-not-recorded` (the shared own-row `status` read): the latch's hold stops the timer, and the retry, asking the latched query right after its read, stops with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED` and hands nothing on. The row never reaches the `pending` row below |
| `pending` | Re-arms at the next wait (`row-pending`, a refusal), with no other call |
| Live, other than `pending` (`waiting`, `working`, `ask_user`, `check_permission` …) | Stops, with no call beyond the read (unless a full-mode cause armed during the retry, below). When the optional probes `isSessionConnected` and `hasSessionStream` both answer true, the retry first ends a holding `tmux-unresponsive` condition and clears `tmux-unavailable` through `endTmuxUnresponsive` (reason `retry`, the row's state as its reading); a probe that is absent, throws or answers false ends and clears nothing |
| `ended`, `missing`, or no row (`ErrSpawnNotFound`, logged as `absent`) | Stops, then hands the persona to one run of `runRestartRetry`, the restart path's decision. The stop comes first, so a refused launch in that run arms a fresh timer, in full mode, through the trigger sink (unless a full-mode cause armed during the retry, below) |
| A read error | A `status` error inside the attempt: its cause arms the timer and promotes it to full mode, and the retry re-arms. A CONFIG error arms its `config` cause and promotes it the same way. An UNUSABLE_NAME answer latches the persona (the shared own-row `status` read, b.jg5 SRJ-512): the latch's hold stops the timer, and the retry, asking the latched query right after its read, stops with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED` and hands nothing on |

**A full-mode cause overrides a row-based stop.** Both stops above rest on the row read alone. When a full-mode cause armed the timer during that retry (`arm`: another launch or recovery attempt for the persona met UNAVAILABLE while the read ran), the stop is not taken: the answer counts as `again`, the timer re-arms at the next wait in full mode, the row read becomes the last row read, and the re-armed line names that cause (`retry <n> (pending-only): <cause> — re-armed in full mode, next retry in <s> s`). The gone-row hand-off is held back, since the next full-mode retry runs the restart path's decision itself. The early stops (shutdown, not applied, not up, at the cap) come before the read and are never overridden.

The pending-row rule's own actions (its laps and runs) are E29's and are not built: a pending-only retry makes only its read, and the hand-off above.

**Condition ends (SRJ-306).** `conditionEnded(key, condition, reading?)` is the stop called when a condition ends. It has two callers, both bound in `main()`. One is the `tmux-unresponsive` condition's end, once per end of a holding condition, whichever rule ended it (a tmux-touching call, a health tick or a retry; see [The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310)). The other is the outage state's cleared-flag observer (`OutageStateDeps.onFlagCleared`), once per real clear of the persona's `tmux-unavailable` flag, with the condition `tmux-unavailable` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CONDITION_TMUX_UNAVAILABLE`): a tmux-touching success or GONE error at the wrappers, the health tick's healthy branch, or a retry that finds the persona healthy (b.jg5 SRJ-311, SRJ-312). The silent boot and teardown reset (`resetAllToHealthy`) reaches neither caller. A `reading` the end or clear brings (a tick's `live`, the live row state a retry read, or a successful launch call's `pending`) becomes the last row read before the rule below is applied, so a stale `pending` read does not keep the timer and a launch's `pending` row does; an end with no reading (any other tmux-touching success, or GONE) leaves the last row read as it is. It stops the timer with the condition's reason, except in two cases, where it keeps the timer with its due time and logs a `kept` line naming why:

- the last row read was `pending` (from `armPendingOnly`, a `pending-deferred` or `launched` outcome, or a pending-only retry: a `pending` read or a `launch-in-flight` skip), or
- a `kill-failed` cause is recorded (an `ErrTmuxKillFailed`, which starts no condition).

The exceptions hold against this entry only. Every other stop rule above still stops the timer in both cases. A successful launch leaves `pending` as the last row read: a launch call that ends a holding `tmux-unresponsive` condition brings the `pending` reading, so the timer is kept, and a retry whose own launch succeeds ends it that way and keeps running in pending-only mode.

While the persona's retry is running, `conditionEnded` records the condition and its reading, logs nothing and answers `deferred`. Once the retry has answered, the recorded reading replaces the last row read only when the answer carries no row of its own (a failed retry, the liveness-unknown `again`, an `again` without a row); otherwise the answer's row (such as a successful launch's `pending`, or a yielded pending-only stop's row) is the later read and stays. A deferred `pending` reading (only a successful launch call brings one) replaces the answer's row all the same, since the run cannot order its own read against that launch; keeping the timer costs one more retry, while dropping it would lose the pending-only watch on that row (`deferredReadingApplies`, `src/unavailable-retry.ts`). Once that retry's `again` answer (or a failed retry) has set the last row read and the mode, the rule is applied once, for the latest condition recorded: kept (one `kept` line, then the re-armed line) or stopped with the condition's reason, with no re-arm. A `stop` answer makes it moot: only the answer's stopped line is logged. A row-based stop that yielded to a full-mode cause (above) counts as `again` here: the rule is applied with the stop's row as the last row read. If it stops the timer, the held hand-off (a gone row's run of `runRestartRetry`) runs after that stop; if it keeps the timer, the timer re-arms in full mode. An `arm` or `armPendingOnly` (either mode) that lands later in the same run, a refusal that started the condition again, cancels the recorded end and its reading, so nothing is applied for it and the timer is not stopped while the condition holds (it re-arms at its doubled wait); an end that lands after that arm is recorded again and applied at the run's end as above.

`conditionEnded` answers `stopped`, `kept`, `deferred`, or `not-armed` (no timer, no line).

#### The tmux-unresponsive condition (b.jg5 SRJ-307, SRJ-310)

`tmux-unresponsive` is a per-persona condition: agent-director refused a call that touches the persona's tmux session. It is held in the notice episodes (`createTmuxUnresponsiveCondition`, `src/persona-episodes.ts`): it holds while the persona's `tmux-unresponsive` episode is open. Its only posts are its onset, alert and recovery notices ([Its three posts](#its-three-posts-bjg5-srj-308-srj-309-srj-1006) below); a refusal that clears before the next onset check posts nothing. A message lost while it holds reports `not-answering` only while P's retry timer is armed and P is below the restart cap; otherwise it reports the next state that applies, `restart-limit-reached` at the cap, and can reach `starting-now` below it ([Inbound step 7](#inbound-slack--claude-code)).

**Declared verbs.** Every call through `withOutageDetection` / `withSpawnDetection` declares its verb (`AdCall`, `src/ad-error-class.ts`). The tmux-touching calls (`isTmuxTouchingCall`) are `spawn` (plain or reuse), `resume`, `read-pane`, `send-keys`, `pause`, and a `kill` declared as a kill of a row the site read live. The live-row sequence's two kills declare it (`rowReadLive` true); the collision ladder makes no kill. The restart path's kill follows a `dead` reading and the persona teardown's kill reads no row, so both declare a kill of a row not read live, which is not tmux-touching. No wrapped call uses `pause` today.

**What starts it.** Only the reporting step, `reportAgentDirectorError` (`src/outage-state.ts`), and only when all of these hold:

- the call ran inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona (`isInsideAttempt`);
- the declared call is tmux-touching;
- the arming predicate (`unavailableRetryCauseFor`) answers the `unavailable` cause for the error, so it is an UNAVAILABLE outcome other than `ErrTmuxKillFailed`.

The reuse spawn's call is a `spawn` made inside its caller's attempt, so its UNAVAILABLE answer starts or continues the condition as a plain spawn's does, and its success ends it with the reading `pending` ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)).

The first such refusal starts the condition: its episode opens with the clock's time, the first refusal's time (`firstRefusalAt`), and one started line is logged. A later refusal while it holds continues it: the time is kept and nothing is logged. Whether the retry timer armed does not matter; the two sinks are told apart.

**What never starts it.** An error from `status`, `get`, `list` or `find-missing` (never tmux-touching), whatever its class. `ErrTmuxKillFailed`, which the arming predicate answers with the `kill-failed` cause. A kill of a row not read live (the restart path's kill, a teardown's kill). A try of a bounded kill retry (b.jg5 SRJ-702): its UNAVAILABLE answer is held back (`deferUnavailableReport`), and only the outcome that stands, after the tries, is reported (`reportDeferredUnavailable`), so a live row's kill that fails and then succeeds starts nothing, and one whose UNAVAILABLE stands starts the condition once, then. Any call outside every attempt for the persona: a persona teardown's or the CLI's bot teardown's kill, the start sweep, the health tick, the permission poller and click handler, the JSONL safeguard, and the startup-dialog approver's `read-pane` and `send-keys` (it runs outside every attempt, b.jg5 SRJ-401).

**What ends it.** One of two rules, in any context:

1. A tmux-touching call for the persona succeeds, or throws a GONE error (`ErrTmuxSendKeys`, `ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`): the wrapper ends it with reason `tmux-verb`. A successful launch call (`spawn` or `resume`, `AD_LAUNCH_VERBS` / `isLaunchCall` in `src/ad-error-class.ts`) brings the reading `pending`, since the row it launched is `pending`, so the retry timer is kept (SRJ-305, SRJ-306). Any other tmux-touching success, and a GONE error, brings no reading.
2. A health tick or a retry finds the persona's row live other than `pending`, with its session connected and its stream present: the tick's healthy branch (reason `tick`, reading `live`; [Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 4), a full-mode retry's `already-connected` outcome (reason `retry`, reading `live`) or a pending-only retry's read of a live row out of `pending` with both probes true (reason `retry`, the row's state as reading; [UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305) and [Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306)).

A successful `status`, `get`, `list` or `find-missing` alone never ends it, and neither does a live row whose session is not connected or has no stream. No launch-timeout end rule is built.

**A latch ends it silently (b.jg5 SRJ-310, SRJ-502).** When the persona latches, the latch's hold ends a holding condition with reason `latched` (`TMUX_UNRESPONSIVE_END_LATCHED`, ended line `the persona latched`), no reading and the silent option, after the hold has stopped the retry timer and before the CONFLICT notice is posted ([Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)).

**Each end reaches the retry timer.** An end of a holding condition ends its episode, logs one ended line naming the reason, and calls the retry controller's condition-end entry once, `conditionEnded(key, 'tmux-unresponsive', reading)`, so SRJ-306's exceptions apply ([Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306), Condition ends). An end on a persona that holds no condition does nothing. A persona teardown's forget and `shutdown()`'s close of the notice episodes drop a holding condition silently, with no post, no line and no call to the retry timer.

##### Its three posts (b.jg5 SRJ-308, SRJ-309, SRJ-1006)

The condition posts up to three notices, each at most once per episode (one mark each in the episode's latch), through the episodes' sink, the per-persona notifier, which adds the persona prefix. The texts are built by `tmuxUnresponsiveOnsetText(key)`, `tmuxUnresponsiveAlertText(key, thresholdMs)` and `tmuxUnresponsiveRecoveryText(key)` in `src/persona-episodes.ts`; each names the persona's session quoted, `"slack_bot_<key>"` (`personaTmuxSessionName`, SRJ-1001). No post is counted toward `RESTART_FAILURE_CAP`, none stops, re-arms or delays the retry timer, and none is an outage onset or all-clear. `main()` passes the condition two accessors: `healthCheckOn` (`health_check_interval` is not 0 in the configuration in effect, read at each onset check; absent, on) and `alertThresholdMs` (`adAlertThresholdMsInEffect`; absent, no alert check is armed).

- **Onset (SRJ-308).** Never at the first refusal. With the health check on, each health tick body checks it once, after all of the tick's per-persona work (`onsetAtTick(tickStartedAt)`; see [Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 5): for every condition still holding whose first refusal is strictly before the tick's start, including a persona the tick skipped (a restart pending or active, at the cap), read without an attempt (work in flight, `tmux-unavailable` raised) or left out, it posts the onset unless already posted. A condition that the same tick ended (the healthy branch) is no longer open, so a single refusal that clears by the next tick posts nothing. With the health check off, each fire of the persona's retry timer checks it (`onsetAtRetry(key, firedAt)`, the retry controller's `onRetryFire` observer, called after the retry line and before the action, so a retry skipped for a launch in flight counts too), and the onset is posted at the first fire at least `TMUX_UNRESPONSIVE_ONSET_FLOOR_MS` (120 s) after the first refusal while the condition holds. Once the episode's alert has posted, no onset posts in that episode, at a tick or at a retry: the alert already said more, and the first check that would have posted it logs `onset not posted — its alert already posted`, once per episode. So with the health check off and an alert threshold of 180 s, the alert posts just after 180 s, before the first retry at least 120 s after the first refusal (210 s when retries take no time), and the order is the alert, then the recovery, with no onset. Since the onset's text says CSCB keeps retrying, no onset posts either while the persona's retry timer is stopped (SRJ-305): every stop the retry controller's stop observer reports to `cancelAlert(key, reason)` while the condition holds (and the teardown's direct `cancelAlert` call), whatever its reason and whether or not an alert check is pending, marks the episode stopped, and the first check that would have posted the onset then logs `onset not posted — its retry timer stopped and no refusal has re-armed it`, once per episode. The alert-held line takes precedence once the alert has posted. A later refusal in the same episode (`start` answering `continued`, after its reporting point has armed the retry timer again) clears a non-terminal mark, so the onset may post again at a later check on the usual terms. A terminal stop's mark (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_TERMINAL_STOPS`: torn down, not in the applied configuration, shutdown) is never cleared in its episode, and a later non-terminal stop never weakens it, so no onset posts in that episode after such a stop. Only a refusal clears the mark: the health tick's own arm of a missing timer (`armMissingRetryTimer`, [Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller)) clears nothing, and the condition never reads whether the timer is armed. The mark is dropped when the episode closes, so a new episode starts with none. The check makes no agent-director call and never throws; its line is `onset posted — still not answering at <a health tick|a retry>, <s> s after its first refusal`.
- **Alert (SRJ-309).** One check per episode, armed when the condition starts, on the episodes' clock from the first refusal, with the never-early wait (`armNeverEarlyWait`) over the threshold in effect plus 1 ms, read at the arm and at every fire. So it posts only once the condition has lasted strictly longer than the threshold in effect then (360 s at agent-director's defaults, "over 6 minutes"; 180 s, "over 3 minutes", with `stopping_window_seconds` 30 and `starting_session_seconds` 120), and waits again when a raised threshold has not yet passed. It posts only while the episode it was armed for is still open (the `view().episode` number guards a later episode), needs no onset, never caps and never touches the retry timer: retries continue. The minutes come from `wholeMinutes` of the threshold in effect at the post. The episode's end, a new episode, `forget`, `forgetAll` and `close` cancel it (through the episodes' `whenClosed`). Since the alert's text says CSCB keeps retrying, any stop of the persona's retry timer while the condition holds cancels a check that has not posted: the retry controller's stop observer, `onStopped(key, reason)`, is bound to `cancelAlert(key, reason)` ([UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305), The stop observer), and the teardown's `stopRetryTimer` binding, at a destructive modify's submit too, also calls `cancelAlert(key, UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_TORN_DOWN)` itself after its stop, so a persona with no armed timer has its check cancelled too. `cancelAlert` first records the stop for the onset (above), then cancels only the check armed for the episode open now, keeps the condition and the episode (a teardown's forget ends it), and logs `alert check cancelled — its retry timer stopped: <reason>`; the direct call after a stop that already cancelled finds nothing and logs nothing. An alert already posted stays posted. When the stop's reason is not terminal (not in `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_TERMINAL_STOPS`: torn down, not in the applied configuration, shutdown), the episode is marked re-armable: the next refusal in the same episode (`start` answering `continued`, after its reporting point has armed the retry timer again) arms the check again against the episode's first refusal time, logging `alert check armed again — a new refusal armed its retry timer again`; so a condition already past its threshold posts the alert at the check's first fire, with no further wait. After a terminal stop, no later refusal brings the check back, even when an earlier non-terminal stop had already cancelled it and marked the episode re-armable: the terminal stop withdraws that pending re-arm, so no *Still not answering* posts after a teardown, a removal from the configuration or a shutdown. The marks are dropped when the episode closes. A failed arm leaves the condition holding with no alert check (`alert check not armed: <error>`). Its line is `alert posted — not answering for <s> s, over its alert threshold of <s> s`.
- **Recovery (SRJ-310).** At an end of a holding condition, by any end rule above, the recovery is posted before the episode ends, only when the episode's onset or its alert was posted (`hasPosted`, answered as `ended-after-notice`); an episode ended before either posts nothing, and it is never the generic all-clear. `end(key, reason, reading?, { silent: true })` posts no recovery even after a notice and logs `recovery not posted — a silent end (a CONFLICT answer ended it)`; its one caller is the latch's hold, whose CONFLICT notice follows. After the ended line, a posted recovery logs `recovery posted`. A teardown's forget and shutdown's close post nothing.

**During a persona teardown (b.jg5 SRJ-1003).** From the teardown's submit until its window opens (`teardownWindowState(key)` answers `submitted`), each of the three posts reaches no sink but still counts as posted in its episode, so an old half's onset, alert or recovery never reaches the new half's destination; the lines read `onset not posted — muted, its persona teardown was submitted; it counts as posted in its episode; still not answering at …`, `alert not posted — muted, its persona teardown was submitted; it counts as posted in its episode; not answering for …` and `recovery not posted — muted, its persona teardown was submitted`. While the window is open a post goes to the sink as usual, and the notifier's window writes it as a `persona-teardown-notice` entry, never posted.

A new episode after an end posts each notice again. Shutdown calls the episodes' `close()`: every episode ends silently, which cancels every alert check, and a later `start` (a launch still in flight that meets UNAVAILABLE) answers `closed`: no episode, no line, no alert check and no post. Each line is prefixed `[slack] persona-episodes: persona=<key> tmux-unresponsive`; every line, the failure-only ones included, is listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

**Held apart from the outages.** It is a condition, not an `OutageClass`, and `outage-state.ts` keeps it apart in four ways: starting or ending it raises or clears no outage flag (no `setOutageFlag` / `clearOutageFlag`); it posts no `ONSET_TEMPLATES` onset and no `ALL_CLEAR_TEMPLATE` all-clear; it records no bad-stretch history; and it never holds back or joins an outage's all-clear. The wrappers only tell the condition sink when it starts or ends, and a sink that throws changes nothing about the call's own outcome.

#### The unclassified-error episode (b.jg5 SRJ-313, SRJ-1009)

agent-director returned an error CSCB cannot classify (UNCLASSIFIED, by name: see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)) in a launch or recovery attempt for the persona. The persona is retried on its UNAVAILABLE retry timer, nothing is counted or destroyed, and a human hears of it once per episode, only when it outlasts the alert threshold. It is held in the notice episodes as the persona's `unclassified-error` episode (`createUnclassifiedErrorEpisodes`, `src/persona-episodes.ts`), which `main()` builds after the episodes instance and installs as the outage state's unclassified sink.

**What feeds it.** The outage state's reporting point (`reportAgentDirectorError`, `src/outage-state.ts`) reports each UNCLASSIFIED outcome met inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona, from any declared verb, a row read's included, once to `report(key, error)`. These sites reach it:

- every spawn and resume of the collision ladder, the collision `get`, the `ErrJsonlMissing` diagnosis `get` and a persona's `find-missing` sweep (all refusals through `refusalAt`);
- the reconnect's `send-keys` (`reconnectMcpWithCause`), whose UNCLASSIFIED answer, `ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed` included, is `transient` (b.jg5 SRJ-118);
- the `working`-row wait's `status` reads, where the answer is transient and the wait goes on (b.jg5 SRJ-605);
- the restart path's liveness read and re-probe, the reconnect adapter's reads, its sweeps, and the restart kill (`killPersonaInstance` in an attempt, Auto-Restart step 4);
- a retry's own row read (`readPersonaRowState`), so a store agent-director cannot open (`ErrSchemaMismatch`, `ErrSchemaMigrationRequired`, `ErrStoreOpen`) reaches it through every retry's read;
- the resume path's `ErrInvalidFlags` and the reconnect's `send-keys` answering `ErrInvalidFlags`, through the site entry `reportUnclassifiedAtSite`, with the classification its re-check step gave (nothing when the re-check stopped the server);
- the reuse spawn (`reuseSpawnForPersona`): an UNCLASSIFIED answer, a refusal through `refusalAt`; a name it gives no meaning (GONE, a STATE name other than `ErrInstanceIdCollision`), through `reportUnclassifiedAtSite` (its `ErrInvalidFlags` holds the persona instead and reports nothing here) ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708));
- a kill in an attempt (the live-row sequence's kills, the restart kill) whose outcome is of a class the kill has no row for (a STATE name other than `ErrSpawnNotFound`, `ErrInvalidFlags` after a re-check that did not stop included, LAUNCH FAILURE, DIRECTORY; b.jg5 SRJ-110), through the same site entry with `unclassifiedClassificationOf`'s classification. The persona teardown's kill and the start sweep's kills feed nothing.

The liveness adapter's `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` is not reported (it keeps its `dead` reading), and an `ErrInternal` carrying the unusable recorded name is UNUSABLE_NAME, not UNCLASSIFIED. Outside an attempt nothing is reported: the startup-dialog approver's `status`, `read-pane` and `send-keys` calls run outside every attempt (`runOutsideAttempts`, b.jg5 SRJ-401), so their UNCLASSIFIED answers open no episode and arm no retry timer.

**Start.** With no open episode, an outcome begins one on the episodes' clock, logging one started line. The episode's start time is its first outcome's time.

**The alert.** In an open episode whose alert has not been posted, an outcome met strictly more than the alert threshold in effect at that moment (`adAlertThresholdMsInEffect`, read at each check; b.jg5 SRJ-210) after the episode's first outcome posts the one alert, quoting that outcome. No timer is armed: unlike the `tmux-unresponsive` alert check ([Its three posts](#its-three-posts-bjg5-srj-308-srj-309-srj-1006)), only an outcome met past the threshold posts it, so with retries at 30, 90, 210, 450 s after the first outcome the alert comes at the 450 s retry at agent-director's defaults (360 s) and at the 210 s retry with a 180 s threshold. No second alert follows in the episode. The text is `unclassifiedErrorAlertText`: *Unclassified agent-director error*, naming the classifier's reported name when it is a safe identifier (left out otherwise, with no placeholder) and quoting its rendered message (redacted, one line, capped at `MAX_LOGGED_MESSAGE_LENGTH`), escaped for Slack after the cap; it says CSCB keeps retrying and takes no destructive action, and that a human should check the host's agent-director.

**Routing**, decided when the alert is posted:

- the persona's teardown window is open (b.jg5 SRJ-1003; the episodes' `teardownWindowState(key)`): the alert, unescaped, goes through the episodes' sink, whose window writes it as one server-log line and one `persona-teardown-notice` entry and posts nothing, whether the persona is configured or not (so no `persona-unclassified-error` entry); its line is `alert written to the server log and startup-errors.log (persona-teardown-notice) — raised during its persona teardown; <met>`. This is the launch in flight a teardown waits for meeting UNCLASSIFIED outcomes past the threshold;
- the persona is in the applied configuration (`getAppliedPersona`): the alert goes through the episodes' sink, the per-persona notifier, to the persona's destination; between the persona's teardown submit and its window the post is muted (it counts as posted, and its line reads `alert not posted to its destination — muted, its persona teardown was submitted; it counts as posted in its episode; <met>`);
- it is not (an attempt still in flight when the persona left the applied configuration), or the lookup throws: one `recordStartupError(PERSONA_UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_LABEL, 'persona=<key>: <text>')` call, with the text unescaped, which writes one server-log line and one `persona-unclassified-error` entry in `startup-errors.log`. Nothing reaches Slack.

Either way the alert counts as posted for the episode.

**End.** The episode ends silently, with one ended line naming the reason, when:

- a full-mode retry finds nothing left to recover (the retry timer's stop `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_RECOVERED`, through the stop observer: `UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_RECOVERED`);
- a pending-only retry reads the row live out of `pending` (the stop `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_ROW_LIVE`: `UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_ROW_LIVE`); a pending-only stop that yielded to a full-mode cause is no stop, so the episode stays open;
- the retry timer stops because the persona's tmux condition ended: its `tmux-unavailable` condition cleared or its `tmux-unresponsive` condition ended (the stops `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_TMUX_UNAVAILABLE_CLEARED` and `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_TMUX_UNRESPONSIVE_ENDED`: `UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_CONDITION_ENDED`);
- a pending-only retry reads the row `ended` or `missing`, or finds none, and hands the persona to the restart path's decision (the stop `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_ROW_GONE`: `UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_ROW_GONE`);
- the persona reaches the restart cap (`onCapReached`: `UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_CAPPED`);
- the persona latches, whatever the case (the latch's hold, after it stopped the retry timer and before the CONFLICT notice: `UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_LATCHED`; [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)); the timer's latch stop itself, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED`, is not one of the stops above;
- the persona is torn down (the episodes' `forget(key)`) or the server shuts down (`close()`), with no line.

These timer stops all mean the retries are over because the persona's state got better, and no retry follows any of them. Every other stop of the retry timer leaves it open: not up, not in the applied configuration, a declined launch, a failed run and the rest.

The ended line is `[slack] persona-episodes: persona=<key> unclassified-error ended — <reason>`, with `<reason>` one of `a retry found nothing left to recover`, `a retry read its row live out of pending`, `its retry timer stopped when its tmux condition ended`, `a retry read its row ended or gone`, `the persona reached the restart cap` and `the persona latched`. A later outcome after an end begins a new episode, whose alert is posted again.

**Held apart.** It touches no outage flag, retry timer or restart counter, posts no condition and is not a `tmux-unresponsive` episode. Each line is prefixed `[slack] persona-episodes: persona=<key> unclassified-error`; every line is listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

#### Session conflict latch (b.jg5 SRJ-501, SRJ-502)

A persona whose tmux session agent-director refuses to act on (`ErrTmuxSessionConflict`, class CONFLICT), or whose own row agent-director has noted conflicting labels on (`provenance_conflict`), or whose own row reads `pending` with no launch start, latches: from then on no automated path kills, reuses, launches or recovers it, and a human decides. The latch is the server's one instance (`createConflictLatch`, `src/conflict-latch.ts`), built in `main()` and held in memory only.

**What latches today.** A CONFLICT at a spawn or `resume` the collision ladder makes (Server-Managed Startup step 5): the first spawn, its retry-spawn after the collision `get` found no row, the spawn after `resume` answered `ErrSpawnNotFound`, and the resume. The live-row sequence's final `resume` and the plain spawn after its `ErrSpawnNotFound` latch the same way, through the same `resume` handler (`resumeAtSite`, b.jg5 SRJ-113). A `resume`'s CONFLICT latches with the refused operation `resume` whatever its case: "this row's own id", "left over from an earlier life", "no valid instance id", "a different instance id", "another agent-director store", or "conflicting labels", which a stray `@ad_owner` value or a duplicate label gives after "duplicate session" too ([Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 5, `resume`'s outcomes); never a kill. The reuse spawn latches the same way on a CONFLICT (`conflictAt`, refused operation "reuse spawn", its line prefixed `reuseSpawnForPersona` and naming the `reuse spawn`), at the live-row sequence's final launch, at the replace step's finished-row branch and at the no-transcript step after the ladder's `resume`, with the case its description gives ("another agent-director store" and "conflicting labels" included) and never a kill ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)). The only other agent-director error that latches is an UNUSABLE_NAME answer (**An unusable recorded name**, below). Two row reads latch too: a conflicting-labels note and a `pending` row with no launch start (both below), the start sweep's `list` rows included ([Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 4). The site's helper, `launchRefusalAt`, takes the CONFLICT row (`conflictAt`) before the refusal rows: the class comes from `classifyAdError`, by name. It latches the persona through `setFromConflict` (the set observers, holds before the notice, run inside the set), then logs one line, `[slack] spawnForPersona: <what> refused for <ref>: <failure> — CONFLICT: the persona latched; no spawn-failure notice; nothing more is called (b.jg5 SRJ-105, SRJ-501)`, and answers `latched`. The ladder then takes no further step: no sequence or spawn, no spawn-failure notice, no `spawn-failed` entry and nothing counted. A `setFromConflict` that throws changes only the middle of that one line, `— CONFLICT: latching the persona failed: <error>; …`, and the answer is the same. The dialog approver is the other CONFLICT site: a CONFLICT answer to its `status`, `read-pane` or `send-keys` latches the persona through `setFromConflict` with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery" (`REFUSED_OPERATION_NEXT_CHECK_OR_RECOVERY`) and the recorded state `pending` (unreadable for a `status` answer, which read no state); it logs one `CONFLICT` line (`approverConflictMessage`) and stops with nothing typed (`latched`; Server-Managed Startup step 5, Pre-session dialog approval). The shared read-pane (`readPersonaOwnPane`, the reader of the working-pane read, the `working`-row verdict and both b.jdc prompt-row paths) is the third: a CONFLICT answer latches the persona through the same entry and refused operation, recording the row state its caller last read, with one `CONFLICT` line, and its caller ends with nothing typed ([Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The shared read-pane**). The reconnect's `send-keys` (`reconnectMcpWithCause`, b.jg5 SRJ-118) is the fourth: a CONFLICT answer latches the persona through the same entry and refused operation, recording the row state the reconnect's caller last read (`waiting`, or `working` for a stale row), logs one `reconnectConflictLine` and answers `transient` with nothing typed; the refused `send-keys` is never retried, and every later path finds the persona latched (Server-Managed Startup step 5, the `waiting` branch). All three share one helper, `latchOnConflict`. The kills are the fifth (b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-501, SRJ-505): a CONFLICT at a live-row sequence's kill (through `latchOnKillOutcomeAt`) or the restart path's kill (`_buildKillSessionAdapter`, through `latchOnRestartKillOutcome`) latches the persona through `conflictAt` with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery" and the row state the path last read, logs one `CONFLICT` line prefixed `live-row-sequence` or `killSession (restart adapter)`, and nothing is deleted or launched after it; the refused kill is never sent again. On a live row such an answer, "not this launch's session", is the kill backstop of [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104). The start sweep's kills and the persona teardown's kill latch nothing.

**A conflicting-labels note (b.jg5 SRJ-114, SRJ-501).** A read of a configured persona's own row at the collision `get`, the `ErrJsonlMissing` diagnosis `get`, the transcript `get` or the `get` after a `find-missing` run lists the row in `unverified_ids` (b.jg5 SRJ-120), or the persona's own row as the start sweep's `list` gives it (b.jg5 SRJ-116; [Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 4, which then leaves every row of the persona unkilled), whose `liveness_note` is `provenance_conflict`, latches the persona too: the shared own-row read calls the latch's `set` with case `conflicting-labels`, refused operation `bring-up` (the persona's bring-up by the restart path's decision), the state that `get` read (or the row was listed in) as the recorded state (a `waiting` row counts as live), the session `slack_bot_<key>` and no description, since a note carries none. Its CONFLICT notice is the "conflicting labels" notice without the `agent-director said` description line. The site then calls nothing more for the persona. The `get` after a `find-missing` run is never made for a persona already latched, so that read never relatches one. Which reads count, and what each site does next, is in [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114).

**An unusable recorded name (b.jg5 SRJ-501, SRJ-512).** An UNUSABLE_NAME answer (an `ErrInternal` whose description carries "the recorded tmux session name", told by name through the classifier, `isUnusableNameError`) to a call on a persona's own row latches the persona with the case `unusable-recorded-name` and the refused operation `none`, through `unusableNameSetInput` (the latch's `setFromUnusableName` builds the same input): the classification's message as the description (redacted, on one line and capped by the classifier) and the session that message quotes, else `slack_bot_<key>`. The sites that set it, each logging one `UNUSABLE NAME` line (the engineering guide's Auto-Restart, Log Messages):

- the collision ladder's plain spawns and resume (`launchRefusalAt`, after the CONFLICT row), through `unusableNameAt`, with the row state the path last read, or one latch-time `status` read when it read none;
- the reuse spawn (`reuseSpawnForPersona`, through `unusableNameAt` after its CONFLICT row), with the row state its caller last read, no row included;
- the live-row sequence's kills (through `latchOnKillOutcomeAt` and `unusableNameAt`), with the state the sequence last read; the sequence then ends without its launch ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717));
- the restart path's kill (`_buildKillSessionAdapter`, through `latchOnRestartKillOutcome` and `unusableNameAt`, b.jg5 SRJ-110), with the row state the restart run last read (its `dead` reading: `ended`, `missing` or no row), or one latch-time `status` read when that reading carries none (`ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`); the restart work answers `latched` and launches nothing;
- the shared own-row `get` ([Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114); not the start sweep's post-run `get`s, which route the answer to the server log and latch nothing, b.jg5 SRJ-1002) and the shared own-row `status` read ([The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115): the launch wait's poll and timeout reads, the prompt rows' re-read after a sweep, the retry timer's row read, the latch-time read, the dialog approver's readiness read and a persona's kill retry's read between tries), each recording `unreadable` and making no further read;
- the liveness and reconnect adapters (`src/server.ts`), which apply the own-row `status` step after their own `status` call (the health tick's read, the restart path's probe and re-probe, the lost-message read, the reconnect's state read), recording `unreadable`;
- the persona's own pane reads (the launch wait's evidence read and `checkWaitingRowPane`, through `readWorkingPane`, the `working`-row verdict `workingReconnectVerdict`, and b.jdc's prompt-row verdict `promptRowReconnectVerdict` and the ladder's `launchOnPromptRow`), through the shared read-pane (`readPersonaOwnPane`) and `latchOnUnusableName`, with the row state its caller last read (`working` or `waiting` for the two restart-path checks, `ask_user` or `check_permission` for the prompt-row paths);
- the dialog approver's `read-pane` and `send-keys`, through `latchOnUnusableName`, recording `pending` (the state the lap's `status` read); the approver types nothing and stops (`latched`);
- the reconnect's `send-keys` (`reconnectMcpWithCause`, b.jg5 SRJ-118), through `latchOnUnusableName`, recording the row state its caller last read; nothing is typed, the `send-keys` is not retried, and the reconnect answers `transient` (`reconnectUnusableNameLine`).

No other site latches on it: the persona teardown's kill and the start sweep's kills keep their own handling, and a teardown latches nothing. An UNUSABLE NAME the teardown's kill meets, at a try or at the read between its tries, is raised as one notice that the teardown's window writes to the server log and a `persona-teardown-notice` entry (b.jg5 SRJ-1002, SRJ-1003; [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65) step 8). Every other `ErrInternal` stays UNCLASSIFIED.

**A launch start not recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-501, SRJ-513).** A configured persona's own row that reads `pending` with no launch start latches the persona with the case `launch-start-not-recorded`, the refused operation `none`, the recorded state `pending`, the session `slack_bot_<key>` and no description (`launchStartNotRecordedSetInput`; the latch's `setLaunchStartNotRecorded` builds the same input). Only an agent-director process older than the install, or a hand edit, writes such a row, and agent-director acts on no session for it. The trigger is the row-read rule's first decision ([Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)), so it latches wherever that rule is applied: every `get` through the shared own-row `get` read, every `status` through the own-row `status` step ([The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115)) and each own row of the start sweep's `list` through the same act step ([Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 4, which then leaves every row of the persona unkilled), whether or not the row is the persona's current life. A persona already latched with another case relatches with this one (one new notice, below); a persona already latched with it keeps its record. A row under a key no configured persona uses latches nothing. While it holds, no automated path sends keys to the row's session or kills it: `deferPendingRow` gets no hand-off (Auto-Restart step 3, **`pending` rows**) and the pending-only retry stops ([Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306)).

**What the record holds.** For a CONFLICT, the case and the quoted session come from agent-director's description (see the `conflict-latch.ts` entry of the Module Map). The refused operation is `plain-spawn` for a spawn, `reuse-spawn` for the reuse spawn and `resume` for the resume. The row state is the state the path last read before the refused call:

- no row, for the retry-spawn after the collision `get` answered `ErrSpawnNotFound`;
- for the resume and every spawn after a collision `get` that found a row (the replace step's reuse spawn, the spawn after `resume` answered `ErrSpawnNotFound` and the no-transcript reuse spawn after `ErrNoSessionId` or `ErrJsonlNeverWritten`, since `resume` reads nothing), the collision `get`'s state, or the later read that replaced it: the `working`-row wait's last `status` read, for a recovery after its `dead-session` verdict, or the prompt row's re-read after its sweep;
- for the live-row sequence's final `resume` and the plain spawn after its `ErrSpawnNotFound`, the state the sequence last read;
- for the reuse spawn after `ErrJsonlMissing`, its diagnosis `get` (`ErrSpawnNotFound` gives no row, any other error unreadable);
- for the reuse spawn, the state its caller passes as last read (`lastRead`): at the live-row sequence's final launch, the state the sequence last read; at the no-transcript step, as for the ladder's spawns above; no row for a reuse of an id with no row (agent-director's pre-spawn scan refused it and wrote no row); never a latch-time read;
- for a kill (refused operation "P's next check or recovery" for a CONFLICT): the live-row sequence's kills record the state the sequence last read, and the restart path's kill the restart run's last `dead` reading (`ended`, `missing`, or no row for `ErrSpawnNotFound`) with no further `status` read.

When the path read nothing before the call (the first spawn, and the restart path's kill after an `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` reading, which read no row), the CONFLICT row (and the UNUSABLE NAME row) makes exactly one `status` read then (`latchTimeRowState`), through the shared own-row `status` read inside the launch attempt: `ErrSpawnNotFound` gives no row, and any other error gives unreadable, which counts as live. A latch-time read that itself answers UNUSABLE_NAME latches the persona there (unusable recorded name, `unreadable`) and no further read is made; the call's own latch is then not set, so that latch stands alone, with one notice. So does a latch-time read that finds the persona's own row reading `pending` with no launch start (launch start not recorded, `pending`, b.jg5 SRJ-513): a CONFLICT or an UNUSABLE_NAME answer that made the read sets no latch of its own, and the persona gets that latch's one notice. A persona latched elsewhere while the latch-time read was awaited (`personaLatchedNow`; the health tick reads even while a launch is in flight, b.jg5 SRJ-315, SRJ-502) is handled the same way, whatever the read gave: that latch stands, no case is set on top of it, and the call's one line gives the outcome `the persona was latched elsewhere during the latch-time status read, so that latch stands` (where a read that latched itself gives `the latch-time status read latched the persona, so that latch stands`). No state is read again after a write the path made since (a kill, a delete, a sweep).

**The order at a set.** The latch-time read (when made), the set and its latched line, the holds, then the notice of the record's latch kind. The read's error may arm the persona's retry timer or open its unclassified-error episode; the holds, bound in `main()` before the notice (`bindConflictLatchHolds`), then stop the retry timer through the controller's `stop` with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED`, end the `tmux-unresponsive` condition silently, end the unclassified-error episode, and reset the slow-recovery count and end the slow-recovery episode silently (b.jg5 SRJ-610, SRJ-1016). After a set, no retry timer, `tmux-unresponsive` condition, unclassified-error episode, slow-recovery episode or slow-recovery count is left for the persona. The holds run on every set, a same-case set included.

**What a latch holds back.** Every path asks the latch where it acts, through `isLatched`:

- **Every launch path.** `spawnForPersona` answers `latched` for a latched persona right after the in-flight join, with one line, `[slack] spawnForPersona: not launching <ref> — it is latched (case=<case>); no agent-director call (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`, and nothing else runs: no claude_config_dir check, trust patch, reply-guard step or agent-director call. The gate fails safe: a latch it cannot read is taken as latched, with `case=unknown`. An `isLatched` that throws gives `not launching <ref> — the latched query failed: <error> — taken as latched (case=unknown); no agent-director call (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`, a `record` that throws for a latched persona gives `— its latch record could not be read: <error> — taken as latched (case=unknown); …`, and a latched persona whose record comes back empty gives `— it is latched (case=unknown); …`. It is the one launch entry point, so this covers the start pass, the bring-up's launch (at start, after a bring-up retry and at an apply), a restart's relaunch and a retry's. `latched` is no failure and no attempt: `launchSession` answers `'skipped'`, and the start pass counts it neither as failed nor as succeeded.
- **The restart path.** `scheduleRestart` asks the latched query before any other gate and arms no timer for a latched persona, a scheduled and a human-triggered restart alike, logging `[slack] Not scheduling restart for persona=<key> — the persona is latched; no timer armed (b.jg5 SRJ-502)` once (a query that throws counts as latched, with ` (the latched query failed: <error> — taken as latched)` after `latched`); a timer already pending is left as it is. `runRestartWork`'s first step, before the shutdown and up checks and the liveness read, is the latched gate (`RestartDeps.isLatched`): a restart timer that was pending when the persona latched and then fires, and the retry entry (before its in-flight and cap checks), answer `latched` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_LATCHED`) with `[slack] Skipping restart for persona=<key> — the persona is latched; no agent-director call, nothing recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`, and nothing is probed, reconnected, killed, launched or recorded. The work asks the latch again at three later points, because a launch outside the serializer (the start pass's, for example) can latch the persona while the work awaits, and so can the `get` after the escalate-dead sweep (b.jg5 SRJ-120): after the liveness read, right after the second up check and before any reconnect or kill; right after an escalate-dead reconnect answer, before its re-probe; and immediately before the kill (or, after an escalate-dead verdict that is not dead evidence, the relaunch) (after that re-probe, or on a `dead` reading). Any check that finds the persona latched answers `latched` with the same line, recording nothing, so a persona that latched during the restart's own awaits gets no reconnect and no kill. The reconnect adapter (`_buildReconnectSessionAdapter(getAppliedPersona, isLatched)`, bound in `main()` with the latch's `isLatched`) asks the latch once more after each of its own awaited steps that a further call follows (its `status` read; the `working` row's `read-pane`, before the fold, the sweep or a deferral; a prompt row's `read-pane`, before the sweep or the deferral; the `waiting` row's `read-pane`, before the sweep on a GONE or absent answer), right before each not-connected notice the `working`-row, `waiting`-row and prompt-row checks raise (the `unproven-idle` notice a noted deferral can raise, and the `blocked-on-prompt` notice), and right before it types `/mcp reconnect`, since a launch outside the serializer can latch the persona during those too. A latched persona, or a latched query that throws (taken as latched), gets nothing typed and one line, `[slack] reconnectSession: persona=<key> is latched — not typing /mcp reconnect; nothing done (b.jg5 SRJ-502)` (with ` (the latched query failed: <error> — taken as latched)` after `latched` when the query threw); the adapter answers `'transient'`, which the work maps to `reconnect-deferred` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_RECONNECT_DEFERRED`): no kill, nothing recorded. A query that throws is taken as latched (fail safe), at these gates and at the check after a `'skipped'` launch: the line then reads `[slack] Skipping restart for persona=<key> — the persona is latched (the latched query failed: <error> — taken as latched); no agent-director call, nothing recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-502)` and the outcome is the same.
- **The retry timer.** Stopped by the hold at the set, whatever its mode, causes or last row read (the condition-end entry and its exceptions are not used). A timer armed after the latch stops at its first retry, on the pre-call latched check, with no agent-director call; a full-mode retry whose work answers `latched` stops too. Its stopped line is `[slack] unavailable-retry: persona=<key> stopped[ (pending-only)] — the persona is latched`. A latched query that throws is taken as latched: the retry logs `[slack] unavailable-retry: persona=<key> the latched query failed: <error> — taken as latched; no agent-director call` and stops the same way.
- **A lost message.** It reports `held-for-human` and schedules no restart ([Inbound step 7](#inbound-slack--claude-code)).
- **The dialog approver (b.jg5 SRJ-502).** A persona latched before a lap stops its approver with no call; the approver asks the latch again after its `status` read and after its `read-pane`. A set of P by any site stops P's running approver at once with the reason `latched`, through the set observer `setConflictLatch` registers on the installed latch (`stopApproverOnLatch`): no approver call for P starts after the set returns.
- **A running live-row sequence (b.jg5 SRJ-502, SRJ-706).** A set of P by any site, the sequence's own latching kill included, stops P's running sequence with the reason `latched`, through a second set observer (`stopSequenceOnLatch`) the session manager registers once both the latch and the live-row sequence registry are installed: its stop signal is set inside the set call, so it makes no call after the one in progress returns. A latch stop drops no answer: the call's answer is handled as for a latched P, so a sequence's own CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME kill still ends as its latched abort ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)).
- **The health tick.** `latched` is its first no-attempt reason ([Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 1), asked again right after the tick's own liveness read, which may latch the persona: the persona is still read, and a healthy reading takes the healthy branch, but the tick never calls `scheduleRestart`, posts no not-connected notice and arms no retry timer for it.
- **A read that latched the persona stops its path (b.jg5 SRJ-502, SRJ-512, SRJ-513).** The launch wait ends `latched`; the dialog approver stops with nothing read or typed; the prompt rows' re-read answers `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`; the retry action asks the latched query right after its row read and stops; `runRestartWork` asks the latch right after the probe and after the re-probe; the reconnect adapter answers `'transient'`; the restart path's `working`-row verdict and prompt-row verdict answer `'transient'` and its `waiting`-row check `defer`; the ladder's prompt-row action answers `latched`. After an unusable-recorded-name latch nothing deletes, kills, launches, reuses or types for the persona, so no tmux-touching call is made for it; its own row is still read (`status` and `get` are not tmux-touching). After a launch-start-not-recorded latch the same paths stop, and nothing hands the row to `deferPendingRow` or to the pending-only retry.

The latch is per persona: other personas are unaffected.

**The notices (b.jg5 SRJ-508, SRJ-1004, SRJ-1016, SRJ-1019, SRJ-1020).** One notice reaction posts every latch kind's notice: `createConflictNoticeObserver`, bound once in `main()` by `bindConflictNotice`. On a `latched` or `relatched` set it first ends the persona's open notice episodes of the other latch kinds silently (`LATCH_NOTICE_EPISODE_KINDS`: `conflict`, `unusable-recorded-name`, `launch-start-not-recorded`), so a later relatch back to one of them posts again; then it begins or keeps the episode of the record's kind (`latchNoticeEpisodeKindOf`) and posts that kind's text in it at most once. A CONFLICT case or unrecognised text posts the CONFLICT notice; each hold case posts its own notice (`HOLD_NOTICES`), never the CONFLICT notice. A same-case set posts nothing. No not-connected notice holds a post back. The unusable-recorded-name notice (`unusableNameNoticeText`) is one line: *Held: unusable tmux session name*, that agent-director will not act on the persona's row `cscb_<key>` because its recorded tmux session name cannot be used, `agent-director said: "<description>".`, the pointer to the "Operator actions" section of agent-director's README for this row, that CSCB takes no action for the persona and that messages sent to it meanwhile are lost, and the human-only line. It names no command. The launch-start-not-recorded notice (`launchStartNotRecordedNoticeText`, from the `LAUNCH_START_NOTICE_*` parts) is one line too: *Held: launch start not recorded*, that the persona's agent-director row reads pending but records no launch start, so an agent-director process older than the install wrote it and agent-director will not act on its session, the quoted session `"slack_bot_<key>"` (rendered as the CONFLICT notice renders a session), the pointer to the "Operator actions" section of agent-director's README, what CSCB does meanwhile (`LAUNCH_START_NOTICE_HOLD`), and the human-only line. It names no command and quotes no description.

**Its lifetime (b.jg5 SRJ-504).** A latch lasts until one of two things ends it; nothing else re-checks or clears it:

- **The persona's teardown.** A removal and a destructive modify's old half both run the [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65), which forgets the persona's latch silently (no post, no set observer call, no line) in its first steps, again once the launch in flight has settled, and once more after its kill (steps 1, 3 and 9), each of the first two times followed by its notice episodes, the CONFLICT episode included. A latch that launch set during the teardown goes too. Its CONFLICT notice is not held back: the CONFLICT observer runs synchronously inside the set (during step 2), before the teardown forgets anything, but the teardown's notice window is open by then, so the notifier writes it as one server-log line and one `persona-teardown-notice` entry, never posted to the old or the new half's destination and never dropped, for a removal and a destructive modify's old half alike (b.jg5 SRJ-1003). A CONFLICT the teardown's own kill meets latches nothing and is raised as one notice through the same window (step 8). Other personas' latches stay. A destructive modify's new half therefore starts unlatched (see [Destructive modify](#destructive-modify-bav2-sr-86)).
- **A server restart.** The latch is held in memory only, with no persistence and no timer, so a process that ends drops every latch; Graceful Shutdown forgets none of them first. After a restart a persona that was latched starts unlatched, and its next attempt that meets the same condition latches it again, with one new CONFLICT notice, through the collision ladder as above. Today that is the persona's launch at start: a leftover that a plain spawn's pre-spawn scan refused left no row, so the plain first spawn meets the scan again (case `leftover`); and a session with no valid label, met at "duplicate session" by a plain spawn that ended its row, is met again when the collision `get` reads that row `ended`, `resume` answers `ErrNoSessionId`, and the bring-up's reuse spawn of the same id meets "duplicate session" again: it relatches with one post, recording the refused operation `reuse-spawn` and the collision `get`'s `ended`, and nothing is deleted. A `provenance_conflict` note still on the persona's own row latches it again at the next read at one of the shared read's sites, such as the collision `get` of its launch at start. A persona's own row still reading `pending` with no launch start latches it again at the next `status` or `get` of that row that applies the row-read rule, such as the collision `get` of its launch at start. Each relatch records the row's state as the path reads it then, not the state the dropped latch recorded.

#### The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold (b.jg5 SRJ-207, SRJ-1008)

A reuse spawn that agent-director answers `ErrInvalidFlags` shows that the installed binary rejects the flags of this release's launch, so every further launch would be rejected the same way or do something unintended. The persona is held: nothing is launched for it until the binary changes, the server restarts or it is torn down, and a human is told once. The hold is the server's one instance (`createInvalidFlagsHold`, `src/invalid-flags-hold.ts`), built in `main()` before the start pass and installed in the session manager (`setInvalidFlagsHold`). It holds at most one record per persona key, the version the hold began under (absent when unknown), in memory only: no persistence and no timer.

**What holds.** Only a reuse spawn holds (`reuseSpawnForPersona`, its `ErrInvalidFlags` row `invalidFlagsAtReuse`; [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)), wherever it runs: the replace step's finished-row branch, the no-transcript step, the live-row sequence's final launch, and a retired key's reuse at its first launch and in place of a `resume` ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)). The `ErrInvalidFlags` gets exactly one immediate version re-check through the `ErrInvalidFlags` step ([Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)), and the pure `decideInvalidFlagsHold(answer, lastAdVersionSeen())` decides on its answer:

- `pass`: the persona is held under the version the re-check found;
- `could-not-run`, `not-running` (no re-check installed, disposed or already stopped) or an answer of any other kind: the persona is held under the re-check's last version seen (`lastAdVersionSeen()`, `ad-version-gate.ts`), or under none when it gives none;
- `stop`: nothing is held. The re-check has stopped the server (a binary below the Phase 1 floor or too old, b.jg5 SRJ-205), and the reuse answers `failed` marked `stopping` with its one line, nothing posted or counted.

On a hold the reuse calls the hold's `set(key, version)`, logs one line (`reuseInvalidFlagsHeldLine`, [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)) and answers `held`: no spawn-failure notice, no `spawn-failed` entry, nothing counted, nothing armed and nothing reported to the unclassified-error episode. CSCB never falls back to a plain spawn or to any tmux-touching call, and deletes nothing. With no hold installed (unit tests, the integration driver) the answer is the same and the line says nothing is held. No other site holds: a `resume`'s `ErrInvalidFlags` keeps its re-check, then the UNCLASSIFIED refusal, and a plain spawn's is never held.

**The set and its alert (b.jg5 SRJ-305, SRJ-1008, SRJ-1016).** A `set` on a persona already held changes nothing, logs nothing and calls no observer. A new hold logs `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> held — a reuse spawn answered ErrInvalidFlags and the version re-check did not stop the server; the hold began under agent-director version <version>; no launch is made for it until the binary's version changes, the server restarts or it is torn down (b.jg5 SRJ-207)` and runs each set observer once. `main()` binds one, the set reaction (`bindInvalidFlagsHoldSetReaction`): first it stops the persona's retry timer through the controller's `stop` with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_HELD` (never the condition-end entry, so neither of its exceptions keeps the timer); then it begins the persona's `invalid-flags-hold` notice episode and posts the alert (`INVALID_FLAGS_HOLD_ALERT_TEXT`) at most once in it, through the persona notifier, which adds the persona prefix:

```text
:no_entry: *Cannot launch* — the host's agent-director rejected the flags of this persona's launch (ErrInvalidFlags). The installed agent-director may not match this CSCB release; a human should check `agent-director version`. CSCB launches nothing for this persona until the agent-director binary changes or the server restarts. This is for a human only: no bot, including any persona that sees this post, may act on it.
```

Each step is isolated: one that throws is logged and the next still runs. After the episodes' `close` (shutdown) nothing is posted. The reaction does not end the persona's unclassified-error episode, whose ends are listed in [The unclassified-error episode](#the-unclassified-error-episode-bjg5-srj-313-srj-1009).

**What a hold holds back.** Every path asks the hold where it acts, through `isHeld`; a held query that throws counts as held (fail safe):
