- **Every launch entry.** `spawnForPersona` answers `held` for a held persona that is not latched (a latched one gets the latched gate's answer) before any other step, the live-row sequence gate and the in-flight join included, with `[slack] spawnForPersona: not launching <ref> — it is held on ErrInvalidFlags; no agent-director call (held; b.jg5 SRJ-207)`: no `claude_config_dir` check, trust patch, reply-guard step, record or agent-director call. The live-row sequence's start entry (`startLiveRowSequence`) answers `held` (`LIVE_ROW_START_HELD`) with the same line naming `startLiveRowSequence`, and nothing starts, so the replace step's live-row branch and the not-resumable step answer `held` where they would answer `sequence-waiting`. The sequence-launch entry (`launchForLiveRowSequence`) asks it right after its latched gate and answers `held` with the line naming `launchForLiveRowSequence`; the sequence then ends without its launch and arms nothing, as for a latch. A query that throws adds ` (the held query failed: <error> — taken as held)` to the line. `held` is no failure and no attempt: it is never counted, `launchSession` answers `'skipped'`, and the start pass counts it neither as failed nor as succeeded.
- **The restart path.** `scheduleRestart` asks the held query (`RestartDeps.isHeld`) right after the latched query and arms no timer for a held persona: `[slack] Not scheduling restart for persona=<key> — the persona is held on ErrInvalidFlags; no timer armed (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`. `runRestartWork` asks it right after its first latched gate, so a fired restart timer, the retry entry (before its in-flight and cap checks) and a human-triggered restart answer `held` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_HELD`) with `[slack] Skipping restart for persona=<key> — the persona is held on ErrInvalidFlags; no agent-director call, nothing recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`. It asks again wherever it asks the latched gate again (`after its liveness probe`, `after its escalate-dead reconnect`, `after its re-probe`, `before its kill`), each with `[slack] Restart for persona=<key> goes no further <where> — the persona is held on ErrInvalidFlags; nothing more is called for it, nothing recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`, and after a launch that answered `'skipped'`, with `[slack] Session relaunch for persona=<key> ended held on ErrInvalidFlags — not counted; nothing more is done for it (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`. A query that throws adds ` (the held query failed: <error> — taken as held)` after `ErrInvalidFlags`. Nothing is probed, reconnected, killed, launched or recorded, and nothing counts toward the cap.
- **The retry timer.** Stopped by the set reaction, whatever its mode, causes or last row read. A timer armed while the persona is held (a session disconnect while `tmux-unavailable` is raised arms one) stops at its first retry, in either mode, on the pre-call held check right after the latched one, with no agent-director call; a full-mode retry whose work answers `held` stops too. Its stopped line is `[slack] unavailable-retry: persona=<key> stopped[ (pending-only)] — the persona is held on ErrInvalidFlags`. A query that throws gives `[slack] unavailable-retry: persona=<key> the held query failed: <error> — taken as held; no agent-director call` and the same stop. The stop is not terminal: once the hold ends a later refusal can arm the timer again ([UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305)).
- **The health tick.** `held` is its no-attempt reason right after `latched` ([Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 1): the persona is still read, and a healthy reading takes the healthy branch, but the tick never calls `scheduleRestart`, posts no not-connected notice and arms no retry timer for it.
- **A lost message.** It reports `cannot-launch` and fires no restart ([Inbound step 7](#inbound-slack--claude-code)).

The hold is per persona: other personas are unaffected.

**How it ends (b.jg5 SRJ-204, SRJ-207).** Nothing else re-checks or clears a hold:

- **The binary's version changes.** `main()` registers one listener on the runtime re-check's version-changed signal (`onAdVersionChanged`, `ad-version-gate.ts`). When a re-check, timed (every 120 s) or triggered, passes with a version different from the last version seen, `endInvalidFlagsHoldsOnVersionChange` ends every hold whose version differs from the new one, or that began under none (the hold's `versionChanged`), with one line each, `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> hold ended — agent-director version <began> changed to <new> (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`. A hold under the new version stays, and a pass on the same version or a re-check that could not run ends nothing. For each persona whose hold ended, its hold episode ends silently, and then, when it is still in the applied configuration, it is retried at once: `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> retried at once after its hold ended (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`, then one run of the restart path's retry entry (`runRestartRetry`, without the delay gate), whose answer is logged as `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> retry after its hold ended answered <outcome> (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`. A persona no longer applied gets `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> not retried after its hold ended — it is not in the applied configuration (b.jg5 SRJ-207)` and no retry.
- **The persona's teardown.** A removal and a destructive modify's old half forget its hold ([Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65) steps 1 and 3, `forgetInvalidFlagsHold`), in its first steps and again once the launch in flight settled, each time right before its notice episodes, the hold episode included: `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> hold forgotten — it began under agent-director version <version>; nothing is posted or retried (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`. A hold the launch in flight sets during the teardown posts its *Cannot launch* alert at the set, inside the teardown's notice window, so the notifier writes it as one server-log line and one `persona-teardown-notice` entry, posted to neither half's destination (b.jg5 SRJ-1003). A key added again starts unheld.
- **A server restart.** `shutdown()` forgets every hold the same way (`forgetAll`), and nothing persists one, so a fresh server holds nothing.

A new `ErrInvalidFlags` at a reuse after an end begins a new hold, and so a new episode with one new alert. A version in these lines is rendered by `describeHoldVersion`: the version agent-director reported when it is a short version string, `unknown` for none, `unreadable` otherwise. A set or end observer that throws or rejects is logged as `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> set observer failed: <error>` (or `end observer failed`); a failing reaction step as `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> <step> failed: <error>`, `<step>` being `retry timer stop`, `alert`, `ending its hold episode` or `its retry`; and a failing end of the holds as `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: ending the holds on a version change failed: <error>`.

#### The kill-failure alert (b.jg5 SRJ-704, SRJ-1007)

A kill that could not end a worker, or that ended it while another process of its session outlived the kill, needs a human: only a human may end such a process, and nothing in CSCB checks it again. The bounded kill retry decides which of the alert's two versions its tries call for (**The bounded kill retry** under [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)). The texts and the route selection are in the pure `src/kill-failure-alert.ts`. A persona's episode is its `kill-failure` episode in the notice episodes, raised, posted and ended by the kill-failure alerts (`createKillFailureAlerts`, `src/persona-episodes.ts`), which `main()` builds after the unclassified-error episodes and installs in the session manager (`setKillFailureAlerts`).

**The two versions.**

- *Kill failed*, the ordinary version: the retry's `ordinary` decision, when an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` stands after the tries, or the tries end in any failure after a survivor-naming `ErrTmuxKillFailed` earlier in them (a stop by a read or by the keep-going check included). It quotes the last kill failure's description; after a survivor-naming failure it quotes the latest survivor-naming description when the last outcome is another failure, and both, the last kill failure's first, when the last outcome is an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` naming no survivor. The row is kept and nothing is launched over it. The text names a human's read-only check and next step, gives both `read-pane` caveats (the read-pane passage under [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)), points to the "Operator actions" section of agent-director's README for those cases and anything beyond, and says its commands are for a human only: no bot, including a persona that sees the post, may run them.
- *Process outlived kill*, the survivor version: the retry's `survivor` decision, when a survivor-naming `ErrTmuxKillFailed` is followed by any end of the tries as a success (a read of `ended`, `missing` or `ErrSpawnNotFound`, or a later try's success). It quotes the latest survivor-naming description and lists the pids it names (`survivorPids`), names no command, points to "Operator actions" and says it is for a human only. It neither holds the persona nor says the kill failed: the caller's next step runs after it.

Each quoted description is redacted, on one line and capped at 300 characters (b.jg5 SRJ-1001); the Slack text is escaped once after that, and a log line or an entry is not. Neither version starts, continues or ends the `tmux-unresponsive` condition: `ErrTmuxKillFailed` reports only the `kill-failed` cause to the retry timer ([The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310)), and a condition already holding keeps its first refusal time.

**Closing sentences.** Each body is followed by the closing sentence for where it goes:

| Where it goes | Ordinary version | Survivor version |
|---|---|---|
| A configured persona's destination, not latched | `CSCB keeps retrying on its own and posts no second alert about this.` | `CSCB takes no further action on this process and posts no second alert about it.` |
| A configured persona's destination, latched (by the retry's last outcome, a `status` read between its tries, or meanwhile) | `This persona is held for a human (see its hold post); CSCB posts no second alert about this.` | The destination sentence above (no latched row) |
| A CLI teardown | `The CLI does not retry this kill: once the worker is ended, run the command again.` | `This persona's teardown has finished; nothing in CSCB checks this process again.` |
| A start-sweep kill, a persona teardown, or a persona no longer in the applied configuration | `CSCB retries this kill only while a persona waits on this worker (its own persona's next launch, or a persona in its working directory); until one does, nothing retries it.` | `CSCB does not retry this kill or check this process again.` |

**Routes** (`selectKillFailureAlertRoute`), first match wins, for either version:

1. a start-sweep kill: the server log and an `orphan-cleanup` entry (the survivor version: a `persona-kill-survivor` entry);
2. a CLI teardown: printed, the server log and a `persona-kill-failed` entry (survivor: `persona-kill-survivor`);
3. a persona teardown: the server log and a `persona-teardown-notice` entry (survivor: `persona-kill-survivor`);
4. a persona no longer in the applied configuration (an old-life wait's kill always): the server log and a `persona-kill-failed` entry (survivor: `persona-kill-survivor`);
5. any other persona in the applied configuration: its destination, the ordinary version once per kill-failure episode, the survivor version once per bounded retry.

**Before the selection** (`KillFailureAlerts.raise`, b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-1003), two checks come first, in this order. An ordinary decision raised `stopped` is no notice, inside a teardown window or not (**Latched and stopped tries**, below). Then, while the key's persona teardown window is open (the episodes' `teardownWindowState(key)` answers `open`), an alert of any context but a start-sweep or CLI teardown kill takes the persona-teardown route: its text is built with route 3's closing sentence, prefixed `(<context>) ` for any context other than `persona teardown` (such as a `recovery` kill of the launch in flight whose tries ended in the window), so its entry names that context, and handed to the episodes' `postWithoutEpisode` (the survivor version with `teardownEntryClass: 'persona-kill-survivor'` in its options), whose sink, the notifier, writes it as one server-log line and one entry (`persona-teardown-notice`, or `persona-kill-survivor`), with no episode and no Slack post; it answers `logged` and logs `… <version> alert written to the server log and startup-errors.log (<class>) — persona-teardown, raised during its teardown (<context>)`. So a kill failure a launch in flight meets while the teardown waits for it (`recovery`) is written there too, whatever the persona's configuration. Between a teardown's submit and its window (`submitted`), a destination route's post is muted by the episodes ([Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65), at submit): it still answers `posted` and counts in its episode, and its line says `… alert not posted to its destination — muted, its persona teardown was submitted …`.

The selection covers every context SRJ-1007 lists, but only the start sweep, the `recovery` context and the persona teardown raise an alert today: no site raises the CLI teardown's, the old-life wait's or the stuck-launch abort's route yet. The live-row sequence raises its alerts with the context its request carries: `recovery`, from the collision ladder's replacement sites that start it. A log-only route writes one `recordStartupError(<class>, <entry>)` call (`main()`'s `logOnly` binding), which writes the server-log line and the entry; the entry is `<ref> (<context>): <text>`, the text unescaped. Nothing on a log-only route reaches Slack or opens an episode.

**Who raises it.**

- The restart path's kill (`_buildKillSessionAdapter`, one try after a `dead` reading; Auto-Restart step 4), through `raisePersonaKillFailureAlert` (`src/session-manager.ts`) with the context `recovery`. Each raises after the standing outcome's own handling: a CONFLICT's latch and its notice first, an UNAVAILABLE outcome's one report to the retry timer (the `kill-failed` cause for `ErrTmuxKillFailed`). The survivor version comes before the caller's next step, the restart work's launch. For a persona still in the applied configuration the alert goes to its destination; for one no longer in it (removed while the kill ran) it is one `persona-kill-failed` or `persona-kill-survivor` entry, `persona=<key> (recovery): <text>`, with the log-only closing sentence.
- The live-row sequence ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)), through the given kill-failure alerts with its request's context, `recovery` for a sequence the collision ladder starts (up to 3 tries 2 s apart per kill, on a row read live). The collision ladder makes no kill and raises no alert itself. Its two kills raise their bounded retry's decision as the sites above do (`raisePersonaKillFailureAlert`), the survivor version before the sequence's next step. Step 5 is a trigger of its own: when the row still reads live after step 4 and at least one of the sequence's `find-missing` runs judged it, the sequence raises the ordinary version with no description (`raiseSequenceEscalationAlert`, the decision `ordinary` with no description, so the text has no "agent-director said" sentence), and ends without its launch. A run that did not judge its row never leads to it: a `pending` row a run left in neither list stops the sequence at once with no alert, and a sequence none of whose runs judged the row ends with no alert. The episode holds it once: a later sequence in the same episode posts no second alert, even when a kill in it succeeds while the row stays live (a kill's success ends no episode).
- The persona teardown's kill ([Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65) step 8; b.jg5 SRJ-715, SRJ-704): `runTeardown` raises its bounded retry's `ordinary` or `survivor` decision right after the kill step, through the injected `raiseKillFailureAlert`, which `main()` binds to the one kill-failure alerts instance's `raise`, unlatched, with the context 'persona teardown'. It is raised inside the teardown's notice window, so it takes the persona-teardown route through the window whether the persona is still applied (a destructive modify's old half) or not (b.jg5 SRJ-1003): the notifier writes one `persona-teardown-notice` entry for the ordinary version, one `persona-kill-survivor` entry for the survivor version, each `persona "<name>" (key=<key>), raised during its teardown: <text>` (`personaTeardownNoticeEntryText`) with the log-only closing sentence, and no post or episode. Raised with no window open, route 3 writes it through the log-only sink with the same builder, its reference `persona=<key>`. A raise that throws fails its step and is logged.
- The start sweep's kills (`reconcileOrphans`; Server-Managed Startup step 4): the ordinary text rides in the kill's `orphan-cleanup` entry, and the survivor version is one `persona-kill-survivor` entry, each naming the row by `instanceId=<id>` with the context `start sweep`, at every sweep kill, swept or pre-persona. The sweep acts for no persona, so no row of it gets a post, an episode, a retry timer or a latch. A sweep kill whose tries a shutdown stopped, or whose version re-check stops the server, raises neither version: its `orphan-cleanup` entry carries no alert text, and its one stopped line (`startSweepStoppedKillLine`, with either cause) quotes the latest survivor-naming description (b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-714; Server-Managed Startup step 4, **The stops**).

**Latched and stopped tries.** The ordinary version at a destination ends with the latched closing sentence when the persona is latched as it is raised: by the retry's last outcome (a CONFLICT or an UNUSABLE NAME answer), by a `status` read between its tries, or by another path meanwhile. The latch's hold has stopped its retry timer, so none runs for it. An ordinary decision whose tries the keep-going check stopped while the persona is not latched (it is torn down or not up, or the server is shutting down), or whose last outcome's version re-check decided that the server stops, is raised `stopped`, with the last outcome's class (`lastOutcomeClass`: its failure class, or its outcome kind) and the stop's cause (`stopCause`), both given by `raisePersonaKillFailureAlert`. The cause is `the last outcome's version re-check stops the server` for a re-check's stop; for tries the live-row sequence's own stop ended, the sequence passes it (`liveRowStopCauseText`: `its live-row sequence was stopped: the persona's teardown began`, `… the server is shutting down`, `… the persona is not up` or `… the persona latched`); otherwise it is what the server's keep-going query tells right after the tries, `its keep-going check answered false: the server is shutting down` or `its keep-going check answered false: the persona is torn down or not up`, with the generic `PERSONA_KILL_STOP_CAUSE_GENERIC` (`its keep-going check answered false: the persona is torn down or not up, or the server is shutting down`) when no query is installed, it throws, or it tells neither (the caller's own keep-going check stopped the tries). A stopped decision is no notice (b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-1003, SRJ-1013) and is decided before every route, the teardown window's included: neither version is raised, nothing is posted and no episode is read or changed. One line names the persona, the stop's cause, the last outcome's class, the redacted descriptions (the latest survivor-naming one included) and the context: `… ordinary alert not raised — its tries were stopped (<cause>)[; its last outcome's class: <class>], so nothing retries this kill; <descriptions> (<context>)`. For a persona with no destination route (one no longer in the applied configuration, so a persona removed during the tries) that line's content is also written through the log-only sink as one `persona-kill-failed` entry, `persona=<key> (<context>): the kill-failure ordinary alert not raised — …`, with no alert text, logged `… stopped retry's log line (no alert text) written to the server log and startup-errors.log (persona-kill-failed) — stopped`; never a `persona-teardown-notice` entry. A configured persona's stop writes the line only. It answers `stopped`.

**The episode (b.jg5 SRJ-1016).** The ordinary version at a destination begins the persona's `kill-failure` episode and posts once in it; a later ordinary alert in the same episode posts nothing. It ends silently, with one ended line, when a read of the persona's own row reads `ended` or `missing`, or answers `ErrSpawnNotFound` (`endKillFailureEpisodeOnRead`): the shared own-row `get` (`readPersonaOwnRow`) and the own-row `status` step (`applyOwnRowStatusStep`), so the shared `status` read, the kill retry's read between tries and the liveness and reconnect adapters' step all end it. On the replacing path these are the collision ladder's `get` and the live-row sequence's `get`s and between-try `status` reads, so a row seen gone or finished there closes the episode, and a recovered persona no longer reports `kill failed`. A teardown's `forget` and shutdown's `close` drop it with no line. Nothing else ends it: not a kill that succeeds while the row stays live, and not `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, which reads no row. The survivor version opens no episode, ends none and is not held back by an open one.

**After the alert.** After the ordinary version the persona is retried on its retry timer, which a condition end does not stop while the `kill-failed` cause is recorded (**Condition ends** under [Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306)), unless it latched. A kill failure is never counted toward the restart cap. While the episode is open, a message lost for the persona reports `kill-failed` ([Inbound step 7](#inbound-slack--claude-code)). After the survivor version the caller's next step runs, and a later ordinary failure still posts its alert.

**Its lines.** Each is prefixed `[slack] persona-episodes: persona=<key> kill-failure`; with no alerts installed (unit tests) `raisePersonaKillFailureAlert` logs one line carrying the decision instead. Every line is listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

#### The live-row sequence (b.jg5 SRJ-705, SRJ-717)

A persona's live row `cscb_<key>` (`pending` included) is never launched over and never deleted: it is replaced only by the live-row sequence, `runLiveRowSequence` in `src/live-row-sequence.ts`, run in the background through the dependencies the session manager's `buildLiveRowSequenceDeps` binds. Its production starters are the collision ladder's replacement sites (b.jg5 SRJ-707; Server-Managed Startup step 5, the replace step `replacePersonaRow`): a row the ladder cannot keep (`resume_enabled` false, a `cwd` that differs by real path, a `config_dir` label missing or different, at a resume or at a `pending` row, or a retired key's old life: a live row of a key recorded as retired with no "new life has begun" mark, b.jg5 SRJ-805, [Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)) that it last read live, `pending` and an unreadable state included. Each such request enters at step 1, seeded with the state the ladder last read, with the conversation not kept, the retired-key flag set for a retired key, a launch at the end and the alert context `recovery`, so its step 6 is a reuse spawn of the same id. The restart path's reconnect adapter starts the same request, with the retired-key flag, in place of its `/mcp reconnect` for a retired key with no mark whose row reads live other than `pending` (`replaceRetiredOldLife`, `server.ts`; [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart)). A dead-session path's earlier live read starts one there only when that path holds dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611); `replaceAtResumeSite`). The other starter is the ladder's not-resumable step (b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-611; `spawnNotResumableAtLadder`): a `resume` that answered `ErrSpawnNotResumable` on a path holding dead evidence, whose re-read finds the row in a known live state other than `pending` (`AGENT_DIRECTOR_LIVE_STATES`), starts the same request seeded with the re-read state and with the conversation kept, so its step 6 is a `resume` when the row has a session id and the persona may resume it. `ErrSpawnNotResumable` by itself starts none: a `pending` re-read, a re-read in a state CSCB does not know (an unreadable one included), a path with no dead evidence and a finished or absent row start no sequence. Either way the ladder answers `sequence-waiting` whatever the start entry answers, except `held`, which answers `held`. A starter passes a request: the instance id, the state it last read, the entry step, whether the persona keeps its conversation, whether its key is retired, whether the sequence ends in a launch, and the kill-failure alert's context.

**The steps, in order.**

1. **One kill**, checked, through the bounded retry (`retryPersonaKill`, site `live-row-sequence`), seeded with the state the starter last read. A success (any `kill_sent`, `ErrSpawnNotFound`, GONE, or a read between tries that found the row finished) goes on, after raising the retry's survivor decision if it has one. A non-success aborts the sequence by its class: a CONFLICT latches the persona through the latch's CONFLICT entry with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery" and the state last read, and is never sent again (SRJ-613's kill backstop: the step-1 kill of a `pending` row answering "not this launch's session" latches it); an UNUSABLE NAME latches it through the unusable-name entry; any other class ends the sequence. The retry's ordinary decision (`ErrTmuxKillFailed`, or any non-success after a survivor-naming failure in its tries) is raised after that handling. Tries the keep-going check stopped, and an `ErrInvalidFlags` whose version re-check stops the server, stop the sequence.
2. **One `get`.** A `pending` row is waited on until G past its launch start (below). A `pending` row with no launch start has no wait; a configured persona's own such row has latched the persona through the shared read (the launch-start decision, [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)), which stops the sequence before any wait. A row read `ended`, `missing` or absent here still goes on to step 3.
3. **Up to `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_STEP3_RUNS` (3) bypassing `find-missing` runs**, the first at once and each later one `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_RUN_SPACING_MS` (5 s) after the previous run's `get`, each followed by one `get`. A `get` reading `ended`, `missing` or no row (`ErrSpawnNotFound`) goes to step 6.
4. **One more kill** as in step 1, seeded with the state step 3's last `get` read, then a `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_STEP4_PAUSE_MS` (5 s) pause, one more run and one more `get`, read as in step 3.
5. **The row still live after step 4.** When at least one run judged it, the kill-failure alert's ordinary version with no description ([The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007)), and the sequence ends without its launch; when no run judged it, no alert, and it ends the same way.
6. **The launch**, for a request that ends in one (below). The no-launch form makes no launch and ends as "row finished".

A starter that made the first kill itself enters at step 2 (`LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_ENTRY_GET`); every other starter enters at step 1 (`LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_ENTRY_KILL`). One sequence makes at most `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_MAX_RUNS` (4) runs and `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_MAX_KILLS` (2) kills, each kill with its tries. Only step 3's and step 4's `get`s send the sequence to step 6.

**The wait (b.jg5 SRJ-406, SRJ-210).** The step-2 wait takes the launch start from `parseLaunchStart` (`src/pending-row.ts`) and arms with `armNeverEarlyWait` on the sequence's injected clock, passing the G accessor itself (`adGraceMsInEffect`), so G is read from the settings in effect at the arm and at every timer fire and a value raised while the wait is armed never ends it early; a G beyond the timer maximum is held by a chain of timers ([Module Map](#module-map), `ad-settings.ts`). A launch start that does not parse to a finite time is never armed. A launch start already older than G arms a wait that fires at once. The wait is measured from the launch start, not from the row's `started_at`.

**The runs and what "judged" means (b.jg5 SRJ-120, SRJ-717).** Each run is a bypassing run (`bypassingFindMissingSweep`, a new call whatever is memoized or in flight) with the persona's key as its next-step `get`, read for the instance id against the state the sequence last read (`readFindMissingRow`). A run judged the row when it put it in `ids` (marked `missing`) or in `unverified_ids` (judged and left live), or, for a row last read live other than `pending`, in neither list (judged alive). A run that puts a row last read `pending` in neither list did not judge it (the row is inside agent-director's grace period, or its launch's worker is alive): the sequence stops that episode at once, with no alert, no counted failure and no further kill, and arms the persona's retry timer with the not-judged cause. A refused run (`FIND_MISSING_REFUSED`: UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED) ends the sequence at once without its launch, with the persona's retry timer armed and no further run, kill or launch; a run after which the persona is latched (`FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`) stops it; any other failed run judges nothing, and the step goes on (its `get` is still made).

**The reads (b.jg5 SRJ-114, SRJ-513).** Each `get` goes through the shared own-row read (`readPersonaOwnRow`), and each read between a kill's tries through the shared own-row `status` read. A `provenance_conflict` note on a `get` latches the persona and stops the sequence, as does an UNUSABLE NAME answer and a configured persona's own `pending` row with no launch start ([Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)). A `get` that fails otherwise, at step 2, 3 or 4, ends the sequence without its launch, with the persona's retry timer armed.

**What a step may do (b.jg5 SRJ-706, SRJ-316).** Before every agent-director call the sequence asks its stop signal (`createLiveRowSequenceStop`, set for the persona's latch, its teardown or shutdown; a kill's tries the server's keep-going query stopped because the persona is not up end the sequence stopped `not-up` without it) and the latched query, and makes no call when either holds; a wait or pause ends early once the signal is set. A result that arrives after a teardown or shutdown stop is dropped, with one line and no further call; a latch stop drops nothing: the answer is handled as for a latched persona (the sequence's own latching call included), and the sequence makes no call after it. For a dropping stop, in full:

- a `get`, run or launch that answers after the stop is logged after the step's own line (a `get` or run line, or step 6's launch-kind line) with `the step <n> get` / `step <n> run` / `step 6 launch` `answered after the sequence was stopped — its answer is dropped; no further call`, and the sequence ends stopped;
- a kill that answers after the stop (any answer but tries the keep-going check stopped) logs its kill line, then the same line for `step <n> kill`, and the sequence ends stopped: no latch, no kill-failure alert, no retry arm. Tries the keep-going check stopped go on to the retry's log-only alert decision for a stop, which posts nothing;
- a stop set while a kill's CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME latch call runs logs the same line for `step <n> kill's latch`, and the sequence ends stopped without the ordinary kill-failure alert (the latch's own post has gone out);
- a dependency that throws after the stop logs `a step failed: <redacted failure> — the sequence ends without its launch`, then the same line for `failed step`, and the sequence ends stopped;
- a sequence whose stop signal is set arms no retry timer, whatever its last step answered.

A teardown that stops the sequence waits for the call in flight to return (the registry's `stop` resolves once the sequence settled), so the teardown's later stops of the persona's retry timer clear an arm that call made from inside its own handling (an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer to a kill already in flight).

The kill retry itself asks the sequence's keep-going check once more after its tries and makes no deferred report when it answers false (**Only the outcome that stands is reported** under [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)). No kill is made, at step 1 or step 4, of a row the sequence last read `pending` while the persona's `ad-config-malformed` outage is raised: the sequence ends there without its launch. Every kill's tries are seeded with the state last read and go on only while the sequence is neither stopped nor the persona latched. In the no-launch form a kill's CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME latches nothing.

**The launch (step 6).** `decideLiveRowLaunchKind` answers `resume` only when the request keeps the persona's conversation, the key is not retired, a row was read and carries a non-empty session id, the persona is in the applied configuration with `resume_enabled` true, and the row's `cwd` and `config_dir` label match the persona (`compareRowToPersona`; a `cwd` check that cannot be made now counts as a match, and a `config_dir` that cannot be resolved gives no mismatch). Otherwise it answers a reuse spawn of the same id, with the first reason that holds, in this order: the key is retired, the persona does not keep its conversation, there is no row, the row has no session id, the persona is not in the applied configuration, `resume_enabled` is false, the row's `cwd` differs, the row's `config_dir` label is missing or differs. A persona no longer in the applied configuration is not launched at all (`not-applied`), with no call. Otherwise the launch goes through the session manager's sequence-launch entry, `launchForLiveRowSequence`, a launch call registered in the in-flight launch map:

- it waits for a launch already in flight for the persona to settle, or for the sequence's stop signal, whichever comes first; once the signal is set it makes no call and is not launched (`stopped`), with one line. It is the sequence's own launch, exempt from the `sequence-waiting` gate below;

- the `resume` leg logs `[slack] live-row-sequence: resuming <ref> (b.jg5 SRJ-705)` after the trust patch, and its outcomes are SRJ-113's through the one `resume` handler the collision ladder uses too (`resumeAtSite`; Server-Managed Startup step 5, `resume`'s outcomes), with the head `[slack] live-row-sequence:`; a success logs `[slack] live-row-sequence: resumed <ref>`. A `resume` whose answer is `ErrNoSessionId`, `ErrJsonlMissing` or `ErrJsonlNeverWritten` (by name) goes on to the no-transcript step (`noTranscriptReuse`, shared with the collision ladder), logging `[slack] live-row-sequence: <failure> on resume for <ref> — going on to a reuse spawn of the same id; nothing is deleted (b.jg5 SRJ-705, SRJ-707)`: after `ErrJsonlMissing` the lost-transcript diagnosis runs first (its `get` before the reuse; a latched or refused read ends the launch with no reuse, `latched` or the refused `failed`), then the reuse once, and a launched outcome after `ErrJsonlMissing` carries the amnesia action (`fresh-after-amnesia` or `fresh-after-inconclusive-amnesia`), `spawned` after the other two. The sequence's launch is no start-pass launch, whichever path started the sequence (it runs detached, after its starter's `sequence-waiting` was counted, so every call passes the start flag false, the `resume` a recovery holding dead evidence ends in included), so the diagnosis writes no startup-errors entry; its line and, on success, its notice are as at the ladder. A `resume` answering `ErrSpawnNotFound` makes one plain spawn of the same id (`buildSpawnParams`, no reuse flag; agent-director's pre-spawn scan runs inside it, b.jg5 SRJ-111), logging `[slack] live-row-sequence: ErrSpawnNotFound on resume for <ref> — fresh-spawn: one plain spawn of the same id, which makes agent-director's pre-spawn scan; no spawn-failure notice for the ErrSpawnNotFound (b.jg5 SRJ-113, SRJ-111)`, with no spawn-failure notice for the `ErrSpawnNotFound` itself; that spawn's failure takes the plain spawn's handling (`plainSpawnFailedAt`). A `resume` answering `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` is a counted launch failure that also arms the persona's retry timer at once in pending-only mode (`armPendingOnlyAfterLaunchFailure`), and a DIRECTORY failure of the `resume` or of that plain spawn is a counted launch failure. Any other non-success ends by class (`resumeFailedAt`: a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME latches the persona with the state last read; `ErrInvalidFlags` gets its version re-check, then UNCLASSIFIED) with no further call;
- **`ErrSpawnNotResumable` at step 6 (b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-706; `sequenceNotResumable`)** never starts a second sequence. The step reads the row once more through the shared own-row read (`notResumableStep` with the sequence barred, what `get after ErrSpawnNotResumable`), logs one line, `[slack] live-row-sequence: <failure> on resume for <ref> — re-read: <re-read> — <outcome> (b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-706)` (no evidence part: the sequence carries none), and the launch is not made, nothing counted:
  - the read latched the persona: `not-resumable-latched`, outcome `the persona is latched: no second sequence; the sequence stops with nothing armed`; the sequence ends stopped for the latch;
  - `pending`: `not-resumable-pending`, outcome `a launch in progress: no second sequence and no further call; the sequence ends without its launch, nothing counted or posted`; the end arms `sequence-ended-without-launch`;
  - any other state (a known live one, a state CSCB does not know or an unreadable one), no row, or a refused read (the shared read's own error rows applying): `not-resumable`, a lost race, outcome `a lost race: no second sequence and no further call; the sequence ends without its launch (cause=spawn-not-resumable-lost-race unless the persona is latched), nothing counted`; the end arms `spawn-not-resumable-lost-race`.

  The `resume` leg never deletes and never kills;
- the reuse is the session manager's reuse spawn (`reuseSpawnForPersona`, [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)), given the state the sequence last read; after a `resume` that went on to it, the trust patch is not run again. A reuse that collides with a live row (`ErrInstanceIdCollision`), of either kind or after the `resume` leg, makes no further launch, counts nothing and is not launched (`reuse-collision`), with one line; the sequence ends without its launch;
- a success runs the after-launch step (the `pre_trust` line and the dialog approver). Any other result (`failed`, `deferred`, `latched`), or a launch that throws, ends the sequence without its launch, with no further call;
- the entry counts its launch's result once (`recordLaunchResultOutsideRestartWork`, `restart.ts`), by class: a success resets the persona's failure count; a `failed` result neither refused nor stopping whose class is LAUNCH FAILURE (`ErrTmuxSessionCreate`) or DIRECTORY (`ErrCwdNotFound`, `ErrCwdNotADirectory`), from the `resume` or the reuse, is one counted launch failure, with the cap notice at the cap. Those results carry `countedClass` (`SpawnPersonaResult`), set where the class is handled, and the entry counts a failure only when it is set (`sequenceLaunchCounted`). Any other `failed` result and a refused, stopping, latched, deferred or not-launched answer record nothing. A launch that joins the entry's launch gets every failure neither refused nor stopping, and every not-launched answer, as the uncounted refused result (`failed`, `refused`), so the failure is counted at most once, by the entry.

**What each end arms (b.jg5 SRJ-301).** A successful launch, a row finished in the no-launch form, every stop (latch, teardown, shutdown, not up), an abort that latched the persona, a launch that latched it or whose result says the server is stopping, and any end while the persona is latched arm nothing. The not-judged stop arms `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_SEQUENCE_NOT_JUDGED`. Every other end without the launch arms `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_SEQUENCE_ENDED`: step 5 with or without its alert, a refused `get` or run, the `ad-config-malformed` no-kill end, an abort that latched nothing, a launch not made other than a reuse collision or a lost race (`not-resumable`), and a launch that failed (`deferred` and a counted directory error included) or threw, whether or not the launch's own refusal handling armed the timer first. A reuse collision arms `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_REUSE_COLLISION` (`reuse-collision`), and a step-6 `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotResumable` whose re-read found a lost race (`not-resumable`) arms `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_LOST_RACE` (`spawn-not-resumable-lost-race`), each unless the persona is latched; one whose re-read found the row `pending` (`not-resumable-pending`) arms `sequence-ended-without-launch`, and one whose re-read latched the persona arms nothing. A final launch whose `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` armed the timer at once in pending-only mode (`pendingOnlyArmed`) arms nothing more: the timer's read of the row decides, and the end line says `the retry timer armed by the launch (pending-only)`. An end that arms nothing says `no retry timer armed`. The sequence itself counts no failure toward `RESTART_FAILURE_CAP`; its final launch is counted by the sequence-launch entry (above).

**Scheduling (b.jg5 SRJ-706, SRJ-811).** Sequences run in the server's one registry (`createLiveRowSequenceRegistry`), which `main()` builds over `buildLiveRowSequenceDeps` and installs in the session manager (`setLiveRowSequenceRegistry`) before the start pass. A starter reaches it only through the session manager's start entry, `startLiveRowSequence(request)`, which the collision ladder's replace step and its not-resumable step call, and the restart path's reconnect adapter for a retired key's old life. While the installed retired-key store has the request's key recorded, marked or not (`retiredKeyReadingOf`), the start entry forwards the request with its retired-key flag set whatever the starter passed (`retiredKeyRequest`, with one line when the starter had not set it), so no sequence for such a key ends in a `resume` (b.jg5 SRJ-805).

- **In the background.** The start entry starts a sequence without awaiting it and answers at once: `started` (the sequence's first agent-director call comes after the answer), `already-running` or `closed`, and `not-installed` when no registry is installed. A refused start logs one line and starts nothing. The start pass, an apply and another persona never wait for a sequence.
- **One per persona.** Entries are keyed by instance id and record the persona key; a start is refused (`already-running`) while a sequence runs on that instance id or for that persona. An entry is removed when its sequence settles, whatever its outcome, so a later start begins a new sequence. A sequence is one episode's replacement of the row: it ends when it launches, aborts by class, stops on a run that did not judge its row, or escalates (step 5); a later retry or tick may begin a new one.
- **Its own attempt.** Each sequence runs as a recovery attempt for the persona of its own (`runDetachedRecoveryAttempt`), detached from its starter's attempt: an error it meets arms by the attempt rule there and never marks the starter's launch refused.
- **Every other launch for P waits.** While a sequence runs for P (`isLiveRowSequenceRunning`: from the start's answer until it settles, its step-6 launch included), every other launch path for P makes no agent-director call and reports `sequence-waiting`. `spawnForPersona` asks right after its held gate, before the in-flight join (so it joins no launch, the sequence's step-6 launch included), and a latched P goes on to the latched answer instead; `launchSession` maps the answer to the uncounted `'refused'`, and the start pass counts it neither as failed nor as succeeded. The restart work asks right after its first latched gate (`RESTART_OUTCOME_SEQUENCE_WAITING`), for a fired restart timer, a retry and a human-triggered restart; at a retry it is a refusal that re-arms the timer. The running sequence also blocks a retry and is in flight for P ([Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller)), and a message lost meanwhile reports `restarting` ([Inbound](#inbound-slack--claude-code) step 7).
- **Its three stops.** `stop(key, reason)` sets the sequence's stop signal at once, logs `stop asked — <reason>; no further call`, and resolves once the sequence has settled, its call in flight returned and its end line logged. P's latch stops it (`stopSequenceOnLatch`, reason `latched`; [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)), P's teardown right after the approver stop (reason `teardown`; [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65)), and shutdown through the registry's `close()` (reason `shutdown`, after which every start answers `closed`; [Graceful Shutdown](#graceful-shutdown-sr-11-event-11)). After any of them the sequence makes no further call and leaves no timer pending.

**Its lines.** Every line starts `[slack] live-row-sequence:`: one start line, one line per kill, `get`, run and wait (a failed `get` reads `failed: class=<class> name=<reportedName> message="…"`, as a kill line reports a failure, when the classification carries a reported name or a message, else agent-director's error name and message), step 6's launch-kind line, and one end line naming the outcome, the counts and the cause armed; the registry adds a not-started line for a refused start and a stop-asked line per stop. Its calls' own lines carry the site `live-row-sequence`. Every line is listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

#### Reuse spawn (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-708)

The reuse spawn brings a persona up fresh on its own instance id `cscb_<key>` and keeps its row, when it has one, as an earlier life: agent-director's `spawn` of the same id with the reuse flag. It is one launch, `reuseSpawnForPersona(persona, config, { isStartup, lastRead, trustPatchRan?, firstLaunch? })` in `src/session-manager.ts`, which every reuse site calls. Its callers are the live-row sequence's final launch ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717), step 6), the collision ladder's replace step for a finished row (`replacePersonaRow` through `reuseFinishedRow`; Server-Managed Startup step 5), a retired key's first launch (`retiredKeyFirstLaunch`, with `firstLaunch` and nothing read) and its reuse in place of a `resume` (`retiredKeyAtResumeSite`, through `reuseFinishedRow`; [Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)), and the no-transcript step (`noTranscriptReuse`) after a `resume` that answered `ErrNoSessionId`, `ErrJsonlMissing` or `ErrJsonlNeverWritten`, at the collision ladder (Server-Managed Startup step 5) and at the sequence-launch entry's `resume` leg. It runs inside its caller's launch or recovery attempt and opens none of its own; its caller registers the launch in flight and counts its result.

**Its parameters (b.jg5 SRJ-708).** `buildSpawnParams`'s params with only `reuse_finished: true` added (`Phase1SpawnParams`, `src/ad-phase1-types.ts`): the same template, `cwd`, labels and `extra_env` as any launch of the persona, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=false` included (Server-Managed Startup step 5, the spawn params). No `no_pre_trust` is set. The 0.10.0 client neither declares nor emits the flag.

**Before and after the call.** First the launch path's `claude_config_dir` check: a directory that does not resolve goes to the deferral hook, and the answer is `deferred`, with no agent-director call. Then the pre-launch trust patch, once per launch attempt (not again when the caller ran it in this attempt, `trustPatchRan`: a `resume` that went on to the reuse), and the call made as `launchWithReplyGuard` makes it: the reply-guard steps immediately before it, then spawn detection, which reports an error by class (Server-Managed Startup step 5, the trust-patch and reply-guard bullets). The reuse runs the reply-guard steps itself, so that with `firstLaunch` (a retired key's first launch, b.jg5 SRJ-805) an `ErrInstanceIdCollision` undoes them, as the plain first spawn's collision does. A success logs one line, by the state the caller last read: with no row (`lastRead` `LATCH_ROW_STATE_NO_ROW`) the reuse is an ordinary fresh spawn and keeps no earlier life, `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: reuse-spawned <ref> instanceId=cscb_<key> — a new life on its own id; the id had no row when last read (an ordinary fresh spawn), so no earlier life is kept (b.jg5 SRJ-112)`; with nothing read (a retired key's first launch) `… — a new life on its own id; nothing of its row was read before it (a retired key's first launch), so any finished row is kept as an earlier life (b.jg5 SRJ-112)`; otherwise `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: reuse-spawned <ref> instanceId=cscb_<key> — a new life on its own id; its row is kept as an earlier life (b.jg5 SRJ-112)`. It takes the installed retired-key store's reading of the key when its launch attempt started, recorded or not, and, for a recorded key, its record generation (`recordGeneration`), from its caller (`retiredAtStart`: the collision ladder's, or the live-row sequence's request's), or reads it just before the call when the caller gave none. For a key recorded both then and at success, with its record generation unchanged, it then sets the key's "new life has begun" mark through the store's `mark` unless the mark is already set, with one line; a key recorded while the launch attempt was in flight gets no mark and answers `spawned`, with one line (`reuseSuccessAction`, b.jg5 SRJ-806; [Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)). Then it runs the after-launch step (`afterLaunchSucceeded` with `LAUNCH_VERB_REUSE_SPAWN`): the `pre_trust` line naming `reuse spawn`, then the dialog approver on the persona's row (Server-Managed Startup step 5, the pre-trust and pre-session dialog approval bullets). It answers `fresh-retired` (`SPAWN_ACTION_FRESH_RETIRED`) when it set the mark or found it set, and `spawned` for any other key.

**Its outcomes (b.jg5 SRJ-112).** `reuseSpawnFailedAt` decides each failure by name through `src/ad-error-class.ts`, with the refused operation "reuse spawn" and the caller's `lastRead` as a latch's recorded row state. A refusal logs `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: reuse spawn refused for <ref>: <failure> — no spawn-failure notice; nothing more is called (b.jg5 SRJ-105)` and answers `failed`, which the attempt marks refused because its error armed the retry timer; a latch logs the CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME line with the same prefix ([Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)). The reuse counts nothing itself: it marks a LAUNCH FAILURE or DIRECTORY failure `countedClass`, and its caller counts a `failed` result that is neither refused nor stopping and carries that mark as one launch failure, and nothing else.

| Outcome | What follows |
|---|---|
| Success | A new life on the id; for a key recorded before the call and at success with its record generation unchanged, the mark set; the `pre_trust` line and the approver on the persona's row; `fresh-retired` for that key, `spawned` for any other (a key recorded while the call was in flight included), which its caller records as a success |
| `ErrInstanceIdCollision` (the row is live, a launch in progress included) | `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: <failure> on the reuse spawn of <ref> — its row is live, so nothing was launched; no spawn-failure notice, nothing counted (b.jg5 SRJ-112)`, and the collided answer (`REUSE_SPAWN_COLLIDED`, `reuse-collided`), which is no launch result: no notice, no entry, nothing counted, nothing armed by the reuse. At the live-row sequence's final launch it is not launched (`reuse-collision`): no further launch, and the sequence ends without its launch, arming the persona's retry timer with `reuse-collision` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_REUSE_COLLISION`). At a collision ladder reuse site (the replace step's or the no-transcript step's) the first collision re-runs the ladder's get-then-act once; a retired key's first-launch reuse is the attempt's first reuse collision too, so the get-then-act it goes on to is that one re-run (`run.reuseCollisionRerun`); a second ends the attempt with the uncounted refused result (`failed` marked `refused`), nothing posted or counted, and arms the same cause (`reportReuseCollisionAtSite`) |
| UNAVAILABLE, every form (`ErrCallTimeout` included) | A refusal, never counted, no notice. The reporting point has armed the retry timer with `unavailable` and started or continued the `tmux-unresponsive` condition, whose onset posts only at a later check, never at the refusal ([Its three posts](#its-three-posts-bjg5-srj-308-srj-309-srj-1006)). Nothing is assumed of the row |
| CONFLICT (`ErrTmuxSessionConflict`) | The persona latches (`conflictAt`) with the refused operation `reuse-spawn`, the case its description gives ("another agent-director store" and "conflicting labels" included) and the caller's `lastRead`; `latched`. Never a kill and never another launch |
| UNUSABLE NAME | The persona latches (`unusableNameAt`) with the case `unusable-recorded-name` and the refused operation `none`; `latched`, nothing counted |
| ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`) | A refusal: the wrapper raised `tmux-unavailable` and armed the timer with `environment`; never counted |
| CONFIG (`ErrConfigMalformed`) | A refusal: the wrapper raised `ad-config-malformed` and armed the timer with `config`; never counted |
| UNCLASSIFIED (an `ErrInternal` other than an unusable recorded name included) | A refusal: the timer armed with `unclassified` and the outcome reported to the persona's unclassified-error episode; never counted |
| `ErrInvalidFlags` | One immediate version re-check (the `ErrInvalidFlags` step, [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)). A re-check that stops the server answers `failed` marked `stopping`, with `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: reuse spawn failed for <ref>: <classification> (after one immediate agent-director version re-check: stop); no other launch`, nothing posted or counted. After any other answer (`pass`, `could-not-run`, `not-running`) the persona is held on `ErrInvalidFlags` ([The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold](#the-errinvalidflags-hold-bjg5-srj-207-srj-1008)): `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: reuse spawn of <ref> answered <failure> (after one immediate agent-director version re-check: <answer>) — the persona is held under agent-director version <version>; answering held: no other launch, no delete, no spawn-failure notice, nothing counted (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-207)` (`reuseInvalidFlagsHeldLine`), and `held`: nothing reported to the unclassified-error episode and nothing armed. Never another launch, a delete or a tmux-touching call |
| LAUNCH FAILURE (`ErrTmuxSessionCreate`) | A counted launch failure: `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: reuse spawn failed for <ref>: <failure> — a counted launch failure; nothing is killed and no spawn is made in its place (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-602)`, the spawn-failure notice, a `spawn-failed` entry (`reuse spawn failed for <ref>: <failure>`) only during the start pass, and `failed`. Whatever row the reuse was made over, the persona's retry timer is also armed at once in pending-only mode (`armPendingOnlyAfterLaunchFailure`; the result's `pendingOnlyArmed`), so the retry's read of the row decides what the failure left. Never a kill |
| DIRECTORY (`ErrCwdNotFound`, `ErrCwdNotADirectory`) | `failed`, counted; the wrapper raised `cwd-unreachable` |
| Any other name (GONE, a STATE name other than `ErrInstanceIdCollision`) | The UNCLASSIFIED row through `reportUnclassifiedAtSite`, with the refusal line |

**A reuse of an id with no row.** It is an ordinary fresh spawn: agent-director makes its pre-spawn scan, and its outcomes are the table's. A scan refusal (a CONFLICT) latches the persona with the refused operation "reuse spawn" and the recorded state "no row", and agent-director writes no row. Its `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` is counted, never followed by a kill, and arms the retry timer at once in pending-only mode, as above.

Nothing in the reuse spawn deletes or kills, makes a second launch, or reads the row after its answer. Its lines are listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

#### Launching a retired key (b.jg5 SRJ-805, SRJ-806)

A key the retired-key record holds ([retired-keys.json](#retired-keysjson-state_dirretired-keysjson)) is never resumed: its next launch starts a new life on the same instance id, and the old conversation stays in the row as an earlier life. The session manager reads the record through the one installed store (`setRetiredKeyStore`; production: `main()`'s store, installed before the start sweep) with `retiredKeyReadingOf(key)`, which answers `{ recorded, marked }`. With no store installed no key is recorded, and every launch path launches as before (b.jg5 SRJ-711). A recorded query that throws reads not recorded; a mark query that throws reads not marked, so a live row is taken as the old life; each logs one line.

**Every launch path.** The apply bring-up, the start pass, the restart path's relaunch, the lost-message trigger (through the restart path), the bring-up retries and the UNAVAILABLE retry timer's full-mode rerun all launch through the collision ladder (`spawnForPersona`, Server-Managed Startup step 5), so each applies the same rule. While the key is recorded, marked or not, the ladder makes no plain spawn and no `resume` for it:

- **First launch.** One reuse spawn of `cscb_<key>` in place of the plain first spawn (`retiredKeyFirstLaunch`, [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)). With no row it is an ordinary fresh spawn, which makes agent-director's pre-spawn scan; on a finished row it resets the row to a new life. A collision (the row is live, `pending` included) undoes the reply-guard steps, as the plain first spawn's collision does, logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: the retired key's reuse spawn of <ref> collided — fetching current state; this is the one get-then-act a reuse collision gives (b.jg5 SRJ-805, SRJ-112)` and goes on to the collision `get`. That collision is the attempt's one reuse collision (b.jg5 SRJ-112), so the get-then-act is its one re-run: a reuse spawn there that collides too re-runs nothing, arms the persona's retry timer with `reuse-collision` and answers the uncounted refused result (`reuseFinishedRow`).
- **The collision `get` decides** (`retiredKeyAtCollision`, after the `cwd` guard), with no further read: a finished row or no row gets the replace step's reuse (`replacePersonaRow`); a live row (`pending` and a state CSCB does not know included) with no mark is the old life, and the replace step starts the live-row sequence with the retired-key flag, the conversation not kept and alert context `recovery`, answering `sequence-waiting` (`held` for a persona held on `ErrInvalidFlags`) ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)); a live row with the mark set is the new life and takes the ladder's live branches as any live row, never replaced by this rule.
- **No `resume` anywhere.** `resumeOrFreshSpawn`, reached from the ladder's finished branch, the dead-session routes from `waiting` and `working`, and the prompt-row recovery's finished re-read (`launchOnPromptRow`, b.jg5 SRJ-607), makes one reuse spawn of the same id first, whatever row the path last read, after the find-missing run and the unresolvable-directory deferral (`retiredKeyAtResumeSite`). The record is read again after that run's await, so a key recorded during it is never resumed; the reading taken before the run decides only the `resume_enabled` false step. A finished row or no row gets its new life, and a live row makes it collide, and the re-run of get-then-act decides as above. Nothing is deleted or killed there.
- **The live-row sequence.** Its start entry (`startLiveRowSequence`) sets the retired-key flag whatever the starter passed, so the sequence's step-6 launch is a reuse spawn, never a `resume`. Step 6 takes the flag from the request or from a fresh read of the store (P's facts, `retired`), so a key recorded while the sequence ran ends in a reuse spawn too. When the starter gave no `retiredAtStart`, the start entry forwards the store's reading of the key with its record generation (`retiredKeyAttemptStartOf`) as the attempt's start, which step 6 hands its reuse unchanged.
- **The reconnect adapter.** A recorded key with no mark whose row reads live other than `pending` is not reconnected: the adapter starts the live-row sequence with the flag and answers `'transient'` ([Auto-Restart](#auto-restart) step 3, **A retired key's old life**). A `pending` reading keeps the `pending` deferral. The `working` and `waiting` branches read the pane, which is awaited, so the adapter asks the store again right before typing `/mcp reconnect`: a key recorded meanwhile gets the same live-row sequence, with nothing typed.

**The new-life mark.** A reuse spawn compares against the store's reading of the key when its launch attempt started (`RetiredKeyAttemptStart`: recorded, marked and record generation, `retiredKeyAttemptStartOf`): the collision ladder's, taken once at its launch decision and kept for the run (`LadderRun.retiredAtStart`), which every reuse the ladder makes and every live-row sequence it starts carries; a live-row sequence's, taken when it was requested and carried to step 6 (the request's `retiredAtStart`); or, for a reuse with no attempt context, one taken just before its call. A reuse spawn that succeeds for a key recorded both when its launch attempt started and at its success, with the key's record generation (`RetiredKeyStore.recordGeneration`) the same at both reads, sets the key's "new life has begun" mark through the store's `mark`, the mark's only writer, unless it is already set, logs one line and answers `fresh-retired` (`SPAWN_ACTION_FRESH_RETIRED`, `reuseSuccessAction`); a key that is not recorded answers `spawned` with nothing written. A key recorded while the launch attempt was in flight (not recorded when the attempt started, recorded again during it, or with a record generation that could not be read, so a recording during the attempt cannot be ruled out) answers `spawned` with no mark set and one line, `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: <ref>'s key was recorded as retired while this reuse spawn's launch attempt was in flight (<how>) — the launch was decided before that recording, so its life is the old life: no mark is set; answering spawned (b.jg5 SRJ-806, SRJ-805)`: the launch was decided before that recording, so the life it began is the one being retired, and the key's next launch decides on the record as it then stands (for a destructive modify applied during the attempt, the modify's bring-up then begins the new life, sets the mark and answers `fresh-retired`). The generation shows a re-record that writes nothing (an unmarked key recorded again), which the record itself cannot; a generation query that throws logs `[slack] retired-keys: the record-generation query for <ref> failed: <err>; a recording during the launch attempt cannot be ruled out, so no mark is set (b.jg5 SRJ-806)`. Every reuse site gets the mark this way: the first launch, the replace step, the reuse in place of a `resume`, the no-transcript step and the live-row sequence's final launch. `fresh-retired` is a success wherever `spawned` is: `launchSession` maps it to `true`, the live-row sequence's launch counts it a success (`LIVE_ROW_LAUNCH_SUCCESS_ACTIONS`), the after-launch step starts the dialog approver, and the start pass counts it with the fresh spawns. The mark is durable and survives a restart, so a server that starts over a marked entry reads the key's live row as its new life; its first launch is still a reuse, never a plain spawn or a `resume`, until the entry clears.

**A failed mark write.** The store holds a mark whose write failed in memory and reads it as set (its own one line), so this server treats the live row as the new life. Each later launch decision for a recorded, marked key calls `mark` again (`retiredLaunchReadingOf`), which writes a held mark and writes nothing for a mark already in the file; a `mark` that throws there logs one line, and the key still reads marked. A restart loses a held mark.

**The clear.** Once the mark is set, the first read of the key's own row in `waiting`, `working`, `ask_user` or `check_permission` clears its entry (**The retired-key entry clear** under [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)), and from then on the key launches as any other.

#### Reads of a persona's own row (b.jg5 SRJ-114)

These sites read a persona's own agent-director row (`cscb_<key>`), and all go through one shared read, `readPersonaOwnRow` in `src/session-manager.ts` (the live-row sequence's `get`s too, [The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)):

| Site | `<site>: <what>` in its lines | After a latch (a `pending` row with no launch start, a note, or an UNUSABLE_NAME answer) |
|---|---|---|
| The collision `get` of the ladder (Server-Managed Startup step 5) | `spawnForPersona: collision get` | The ladder answers `latched` before its `cwd` and `config_dir` guards and its state branches |
| The `ErrJsonlMissing` diagnosis `get` (`diagnoseJsonlMissing`) | `spawnForPersona: ErrJsonlMissing diagnosis get` | No diagnosis is reported; the branch launches nothing (no reuse spawn); the ladder answers `latched` |
| The re-read after a `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotResumable` (the not-resumable step, `notResumableStep`, b.jg5 SRJ-710) | `spawnForPersona: get after ErrSpawnNotResumable` at the ladder, `live-row-sequence: get after ErrSpawnNotResumable` at the sequence's step-6 `resume` | At the ladder the not-resumable line names `the read latched the persona` and the ladder answers `latched`; at step 6 the launch is not made (`not-resumable-latched`) and the sequence stops for the latch, nothing armed |
| The re-read before a resume site's replacement of a row last read live on a path with no dead evidence (`replaceAtResumeSite`, b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611) | `spawnForPersona: get before replacing` | The ladder answers `latched`; no replacement, sequence or launch |
| The transcript `get` of the stale-`working`-row evidence (`readPersonaTranscript`) | `readPersonaTranscript: transcript get` | No evidence. The launch's `working`-row wait ends `latched` ([a latched wait](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1)); the restart path's working-row check answers `defer` |
| The `get` after a `find-missing` run lists the row in `unverified_ids` (b.jg5 SRJ-120; one per configured persona listed, after a run the server makes, never at a memo reuse, except the row the calling path's next step reads with a `get` and the row of a persona already latched, which gets no `get` and so is never relatched there) | `<prefix>: post-sweep get`, where `<prefix>` is the run's (`escalate-dead`, `spawnForPersona: before resume`, `waitForWaitingAndReconnect`, `waitForWaitingAndReconnect: timeout`, `spawnForPersona: prompt row`, `reconnectSession: prompt row` or `reconcileOrphans`), with `<ref>` `persona=<key>` | The caller of that persona's sweep gets `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED` and calls nothing more for it (see the b.m4r note under Server-Managed Startup step 5); the restart run stops at its latch check after the escalate-dead reconnect (Auto-Restart step 3). A note on another caller's row in the result is never read or acted on |

The read makes one `get` through `withOutageDetection`, then applies the rule, and never throws.

**The start sweep's `list` rows (b.jg5 SRJ-116).** The read's act step, the unexported `actOnOwnRowRead(key, row, at, clearRetiredEntry)`, takes a row already read: `readPersonaOwnRow` applies it to its `get` row, and the start sweep (`reconcileOrphans`) to each row of its one `list` whose id is a key's own, at `START_SWEEP_LIST_SITE` (`reconcileOrphans: start sweep list`, with the persona's ref added for a configured persona). One code path for both: the same rule, latch record, notice per episode, clear and lines, with no agent-director call of its own. `readPersonaOwnRow` passes `clearRetiredEntry` true; the sweep passes false for a key the same sweep records as retired, which leaves the clear out of the read (that recording clears the mark). A latch there leaves every row of the persona unkilled for the whole pass ([Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 4).

**Latched while the read was awaited (b.jg5 SRJ-502).** A read is awaited, and the health tick's liveness read may latch the persona meanwhile (b.jg5 SRJ-315). So the collision `get`, the diagnosis `get` and the two re-reads (after `ErrSpawnNotResumable` and before a resume site's replacement), unless the read answered `latched`, ask `latchedAfterOwnRowRead(key, site, what, ref)` (`personaLatchedNow`) right after it, before any other answer is handled; the prompt rows' `status` re-read (`reconcileAndReadRowState`) does the same. A persona latched then gets one line, `[slack] <site>: <ref> is latched after its <what> — nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`, and the site answers as after a latch (the table above; `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED` for the re-read). It asks the latch, not the read, so a row the read latched itself logs it too, after its own latch line. Nothing is logged when the persona is not latched. The rule is the pure `decideOwnRowRead` in `src/row-read-rules.ts`, which holds no state, logs nothing and calls nothing; the shared read does the logging and the latching.

**The rule.** It is one rule with two latch decisions and, beside them, one entry-clear decision with its own conditions (**The retired-key entry clear**, below). Neither latch decision applies unless both of these hold:

- the row is the persona's own: its `claude_instance_id` is exactly `cscb_<key>`;
- the key is a persona of the applied configuration now, as the installed configured-persona query answers. `main()` installs it (`setConfiguredPersonaQuery`) right after the latch and before the start sweep; it reads `getAppliedPersona` at each call, so an apply's added persona counts at once and a removed one stops counting at once. With no query installed, or a query that throws, no key counts and no read latches.

Then the first decision that holds decides:

1. **Launch start not recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-513).** The row reads `pending` with no launch start (`isPendingWithNoLaunchStart`, `src/pending-row.ts`): its `launch_started_at` is absent, `null`, not a string, empty, or does not parse to a finite instant (`parseLaunchStart`, a lenient RFC 3339 read: `Z` or a numeric offset, a fraction of any length). It latches with `launch-start-not-recorded`, the refused operation `none` and the recorded state `pending`, whatever the row's `cwd`, `config_dir` or note, and whatever case the persona is already latched with. A row that also carries `provenance_conflict` answers this decision only. Nothing ages the launch start: a `pending` row with a valid one goes on to the next decision.
2. **Conflicting labels (b.jg5 SRJ-114).** The row's `liveness_note` is exactly `provenance_conflict` (`LATCHING_LIVENESS_NOTE`), with no prefix, substring or case-folded match.

A note that is present counts, whatever state the row reads. Every other note (`tmux_server_changed`, `process_not_seen_*`, `probe_eacces`, `tmux_session_name_*` and any note CSCB does not know) latches no one, and the site goes on. `provenance_conflict` on a row that is not a configured persona's own (another caller's id, or the `cscb_<key>` row of a key outside the applied configuration) is ignored: it is not CSCB's to act on or post about, and the site goes on. The shared read asks `decideOwnRowRead` on every row it reads. A row that latches on either decision logs one line on every read; otherwise a row with no note logs nothing; any other note logs its line once per persona per note, and again only when the note changes, after a read with no note or the latching note, or once the persona's not-connected episode is forgotten (`forgetNotConnectedEpisode`: its removal's teardown, a health-check tick that finds it deliverable, or its MCP registration) (the engineering guide's Auto-Restart, Log Messages).

**The note latch.** The read latches through the installed latch's `set` (case `conflicting-labels`, refused operation `bring-up`, the state the `get` read, session `slack_bot_<key>`, no description); the record, holds and notice are those of [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502). The read answers the row with `latched` true and the site calls nothing more for the persona (b.jg5 SRJ-502). With no latch installed, or a `set` that throws, nothing is latched and the answer is still `latched` true, as at the CONFLICT row.

**The launch-start latch (b.jg5 SRJ-513).** The read latches through the same `set` with `launchStartNotRecordedSetInput`'s input (case `launch-start-not-recorded`, refused operation `none`, state `pending`, session `slack_bot_<key>`, no description), answers the row with `latched` true, and the site does what the table gives for a latch: at the collision `get` that is before the `cwd` and `config_dir` guards, so a row of another life latches too. Its line names the reason, `its row reads pending with no launch start`, where the note latch's names the note (the engineering guide's Auto-Restart, Log Messages). The record, holds and notice are those of [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502).

**The retired-key entry clear (b.jg5 SRJ-807).** The third decision of the rule (`decideRetiredEntryClear`, folded into `decideOwnRowRead`'s `clearRetiredEntry`) removes a key's entry from the retired-key record ([retired-keys.json](#retired-keysjson-state_dirretired-keysjson)) when all of these hold:

- the row is the key's own (`cscb_<key>`), for any key: configured or not, so a key outside the applied configuration clears too;
- the row reads `waiting`, `working`, `ask_user` or `check_permission` (`RETIRED_ENTRY_CLEARING_STATES`, the live states less `pending`);
- the installed retired-key store (`setRetiredKeyStore`; production: `main()`'s one store, installed right after the configured-persona query and before the start sweep) has the key recorded with its "new life has begun" mark set (`isMarked`).

It never fires on `pending`, with or without a launch start, nor on `ended`, `missing` or a state CSCB does not know, on an unmarked or unrecorded key, or on another key's row. It sits beside the launch-start decision and never changes it: a configured persona's own `pending` row with no launch start latches whatever the key's mark, and clears nothing. It is independent of the note latch: one read can latch on `provenance_conflict` and clear. The shared reads call the store's `clear` before any latch handling, and what the read answers its site is the same whatever the clear did. The removal is durable (one whole-record write); an entry leaves the record for no other reason than this clear and a failed apply's restore.

Every site above applies it through `readPersonaOwnRow`, every `status` site through the own-row `status` step ([The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115)), and the start sweep's `list` rows through the same act step, with `retiredMarked` read from the installed store, except for a key the same sweep records as `absent-at-start`, whose recording clears its mark instead (Server-Managed Startup step 4). Two reads are the exception: the start sweep's bare `status` read between kill tries (`sweepKillRead`), for a row whose id is a key's own (`cscb_<key>`, configured or not), and the persona teardown kill's `status` read between its tries (`readTeardownKillRow`); each applies no step but makes this decision itself and acts on it, latching nothing (the start sweep's names the site `START_SWEEP_KILL_STATUS_SITE`, `reconcileOrphans: status read between kill tries`, and clears nothing once the server has begun shutting down; its post-run `get` reads through `readPersonaOwnRow`). The CLI never clears: it installs no store and never writes the record. The reads under **Other `get`s apply no rule** clear nothing either. A clear logs one line (success or a failed write, [Retired-key record lines](#retired-key-record-lines-bjg5-srj-1013-srj-1014)); a failed write leaves the entry in memory and on disk, the site acts on its read as usual, and the next qualifying read tries again. With no store installed, or an `isMarked` that throws, nothing is cleared.

The mark is set by a reuse spawn that succeeds for a recorded key ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)), so the clear fires once the persona's new life is read live, the new life of a key that had no row included.

**Errors.** `ErrSpawnNotFound`, recognised by name, reads as absent: the collision `get` keeps its single plain-spawn retry; a re-read reads it as no row (finished: a lost race at the not-resumable step, the replace step's reuse spawn before a replacement); the diagnosis `get` reports `inconclusive` with the reason `the agent-director row is absent (ErrSpawnNotFound)`; the transcript `get` gives an `unreadable` transcript with the reason `its agent-director row is absent (ErrSpawnNotFound)`; the post-sweep `get` changes nothing. An UNUSABLE_NAME answer latches the persona with the state `unreadable` and no further read (b.jg5 SRJ-512), and the read answers `latched` (`OWN_ROW_READ_LATCHED`): each site does what the table gives for a latch; at the post-sweep `get` the persona counts among the latched ones, and its caller gets `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`, except in the start sweep's run, where the answer is routed to the server log and latches nothing (b.jg5 SRJ-1002; see the b.m4r note under Server-Managed Startup step 5). Any other error goes back to the site unchanged, and each site handles it in its own way:

- **The collision `get` and the diagnosis `get`** take the read-error row of [Refusals at the launch and recovery sites](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104) (`refusalAt` with verb `get`): every such error is a refusal, with its one refusal line, and the attempt calls nothing more. At the diagnosis `get` a refused read reports no diagnosis and launches nothing (no reuse spawn) too. An error `refusalAt` did not refuse (not reached) logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: collision get failed for <ref>: <failure> — nothing more is called` or `[slack] spawnForPersona: ErrJsonlMissing diagnosis get failed for <ref>: <failure> — nothing more is called` and the ladder answers an unmarked `failed`: no spawn-failure notice, no `spawn-failed` entry, no diagnosis, delete or launch.
- **The re-reads** take the same read-error row (`refusalAt` with verb `get`: one refusal line, the read-error cause armed inside the attempt).
