The old half of a destructive modify cancels more at submit (see [Destructive modify](#destructive-modify-bav2-sr-86)).

**The notice window (b.jg5 SRJ-1003, SRJ-1002, SRJ-1013).** At the start of its serializer turn (`runTeardown`), after its `starting` line and with nothing awaited before or between them, the teardown forgets its outage flags silently (`resetOutageState([key])`, `resetAllToHealthy`, step label `forgetting its outage state`), so a flag raised before the teardown posts no all-clear, and opens its notice window (`openTeardownWindow(persona)`, step label `opening its notice window`). The steps below run inside it. When they complete, whatever a step throws, it closes the window (`closeTeardownWindow(key)`, step label `closing its notice window`) and ends its submit; a step's returned promise that rejects is counted before the `complete` line, which is always last. While the window is open, every notice raised for the key goes through the notifier's window: one server-log line and one `startup-errors.log` entry naming the persona and "raised during its teardown" (`personaTeardownNoticeEntryText`: `persona "<name>" (key=<key>), raised during its teardown: <text>`), of class `persona-teardown-notice`, or `persona-kill-survivor` for the kill-failure alert's survivor version. The entry and the line carry the notice's text with Slack's control-character escapes undone (`unescapeSlackControlCharacters`), so a notice built for Slack reads as an unescaped one does. That covers an outage onset from its calls or from the launch in flight it waits for, a latch's notice or an `ErrInvalidFlags` hold's *Cannot launch* alert raised by that launch, an unclassified-error alert, every kill-failure alert (one of a context other than `persona teardown`, such as the launch in flight's `recovery` kill, prefixed `(<context>) `), a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME its kill meets, its kill's non-success that no other notice records (step 8), a stuck-prompt warning and a lost-message notice. None reaches a Slack destination, the old half's or the new half's, and none is queued, held or dropped: the window comes before the notifier's drop for a key no longer applied, its dry-run branch, its pre-validation hold and the destination hold, so dry run routes the same way. An outage flag raised in the window is kept past the teardown, and its all-clear, whenever it comes, is written the same way, never posted (after the window has closed its entry says `the all-clear of an outage raised during its teardown`). An all-clear that lists such a class and another class is split (`allClearOf`): the window-marked classes' all-clear is written, and the rest's, listing only the other classes, is posted to the destination. A bounded retry of a launch or recovery attempt's kill that the teardown's start stops is no notice: it writes the stop's line, naming its cause (`its live-row sequence was stopped: the persona's teardown began`, or what the keep-going check answered), and for a removed persona a `persona-kill-failed` entry with no alert text, never a `persona-teardown-notice` entry ([The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007), **Latched and stopped tries**).

The steps run in this order. A step that fails is logged and the rest still run:

1. **First, before the wait for its launch in flight (b.jg5 SRJ-715).** Its dialog approver is stopped (`stopApprover`, awaited; b.jg5 SRJ-404): a running approver makes no call after the one in progress returns, and the approver the launch in flight would start does not start. An approver still running logs `stopping the approver for <ref> (teardown): its teardown began; …` when this is the first stop asked of it (apply step 1's `retired-key` stop usually came first and logged its own), or, for one the launch had not started, `not starting the approver for <ref> (teardown): …` when that launch returns. Right after it, its live-row sequence is stopped (`stopLiveRowSequence`, awaited, step label `stopping its live-row sequence`; b.jg5 SRJ-706): the sequence logs `stop asked — the persona's teardown began; no further call` and makes no further call, and the step waits for its call in flight to return (a step-6 launch it had started included), so the retry-timer stop that follows clears any arm that call made. Then its UNAVAILABLE retry timer is stopped (`stopRetryTimer`, the controller's `stop` with the reason `the persona was torn down`, b.jg5 SRJ-305). The persona's pending `tmux-unresponsive` alert check is cancelled with it (b.jg5 SRJ-309), since its text says CSCB keeps retrying: the stop's observer calls `cancelAlert(key, reason)`, and the same binding then calls `cancelAlert(key, UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_TORN_DOWN)` itself, which cancels the check when no timer was armed; either logs `alert check cancelled — its retry timer stopped: the persona was torn down` once, and a terminal reason never lets a later refusal arm the check again. Other personas' timers stay armed. Then, silently, its latch is forgotten (`forgetConflictLatch`, the latch instance's `forget`, b.jg5 SRJ-504: no post, no set observer call, no line; see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)), its `ErrInvalidFlags` hold (`forgetInvalidFlagsHold`, the hold's `forget`, b.jg5 SRJ-207: nothing posted and nothing retried, one `hold forgotten` line when it was held; see [The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold](#the-errinvalidflags-hold-bjg5-srj-207-srj-1008)), and every notice episode it has open with every count kept beside them, the slow-recovery count included (`forgetNoticeEpisodes`, the episodes instance's `forget`, b.jg5 SRJ-1016, SRJ-610). A forget that throws logs its step line (`forgetting its latch failed`, `forgetting its ErrInvalidFlags hold failed`, `forgetting its notice episodes failed`), counts as a failed step, and the rest still run.
2. Its bring-up retries are cancelled and its bring-up state forgotten (the controller's `cancel`), and its pending restart timer is cancelled (`cancelRestartTimer`). A retry already running or queued ahead of the teardown finishes first, since the teardown waits for its serializer turn, and its answer is dropped. Its launch's wait for a `working` row is cancelled (`cancelLaunchWait`, production `cancelWorkingRowWait`, b.f2b), as it already was when the teardown was submitted (see above); this call catches a wait that started since. Then a launch still in flight for it is awaited (`whenLaunchSettled`), so the kill never races a launch that is bringing the row up. This covers a start-pass launch, which runs outside the serializer. A cancelled wait types nothing and its launch settles promptly, so the teardown doesn't wait up to 10 minutes for it.
3. **Again, once that launch has settled (b.jg5 SRJ-715).** Its live-row sequence is stopped again, awaited (step label `stopping its live-row sequence again, after its launch in flight settled`), its UNAVAILABLE retry timer stopped again, its latch forgotten silently again, and its `ErrInvalidFlags` hold and its notice episodes forgotten again (each step label ending `again, after its launch in flight settled`): that launch can have started a sequence at a collision ladder replacement site (b.jg5 SRJ-707), armed the timer, set a latch or a hold, or opened an episode after step 1. So a launch in flight that meets UNAVAILABLE during the teardown leaves no retry timer armed, and a latch or a hold it set goes, with the CONFLICT or hold episode it began. The teardown itself latches nothing (b.jg5 SRJ-1002).
4. Its Slack connection is stopped (the connection manager's `stop`), then its inbound dedupe store is dropped (the routing's `forget`) and its ack-tracker entries are dropped (`forgetPersonaAcks`, injected as `forgetAcks`; other personas' entries stay), so a key added again starts clean. The connection goes first, because an event for the key would create a new store.
5. Its cached DM conversation is forgotten (`personaDestinations.forget`), its destination hold is cancelled (held notices dropped, retry timer cleared) and its pre-validation held notices are dropped (the notifier's `forget`, step label `dropping its held notices`, with its one line). Nothing held is posted. Only notices queued before the window opened are dropped: one raised in the window is written, never queued (b.jg5 SRJ-1003).
6. Its tracked permission prompts, their not-posted records and its wedge state are dropped (`forgetPersonaPrompts`). Their Slack messages stay as posted.
7. Its MCP session is dropped with `dropPersonaSessionAndKeepAlive`, the session drop of Disconnection, so the close schedules no restart.
8. **The kill (b.jg5 SRJ-715, SRJ-110, SRJ-702).** Its outage flags were reset right before the window opened, so a success posts no all-clear for a flag raised before the teardown, and a flag raised in the window is not reset again. Outside dry run, `cscb_<key>` is killed through `killInstance`, production `killPersonaInstanceForTeardown(key, { clock: KILL_RETRY_SYSTEM_CLOCK })` (`src/session-manager.ts`): the bounded kill retry (**The bounded kill retry** under [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)) over one checked kill per try (`killPersonaInstance` with `KILL_CONTEXT_TEARDOWN`, through `withOutageDetection` arming nothing; hatch A3), seeded as a live row the teardown has not read (`KILL_RETRY_SEED_LIVE_UNREAD`). An UNAVAILABLE outcome gets up to 3 tries 2 s apart, with one `status` read of the row before each further try; a read of `ended`, `missing` or `ErrSpawnNotFound` ends the tries as a success. A CONFLICT is never tried again. The read goes through `withOutageDetection` arming nothing too, with no own-row step, so it latches nothing (`readTeardownKillRow`). Of the row-read rule only the retired-key entry clear applies (b.jg5 SRJ-807, SRJ-115): a row read `waiting`, `working`, `ask_user` or `check_permission` of a key recorded with its mark set clears the key's entry, the store's clear line naming the site `persona teardown kill: status read between tries`, and what the read answers is the same whatever the clear did. A `pending` row with no launch start is a live read, and an UNUSABLE NAME answer a failed read after which the next try goes ahead. No keep-going check stops the tries: the persona teardown's own kill is never stopped early by one (SRJ-702). Neither SRJ-316's rule against starting a kill of a row last read `pending` nor a latch holds the kill's start back, so a `pending` row with no launch start (b.jg5 SRJ-513) and a latched persona's row are killed too; between tries, a CONFIG answer at a read following a read of `pending` still ends the tries, the last try's outcome standing (SRJ-702), and a CONFIG answer after any other last state read lets the next try go ahead. Each CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answer met, at a try or at a read, is answered in the result's `refusals` and latches nothing. The kill is no launch or recovery attempt: no try or read arms a retry timer, starts a `tmux-unresponsive` condition or feeds the unclassified-error episode, nothing is reported after the tries, and an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer raises `tmux-unavailable` or `ad-config-malformed` only while the persona is in the applied configuration (a destructive modify's old half; a removed persona's raises no outage, and is recorded by the kill-outcome notice below); `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` still raises `ad-unreachable`. An `ErrInvalidFlags` from a try gets its immediate version re-check (b.jg5 SRJ-104, SRJ-204) and is a non-success all the same. The outcome that stands is logged with `kill_sent` (`describeKillOutcome`) and the number of tries. A success (`killLetsNextStepRun`: any `kill_sent`, `ErrSpawnNotFound`, GONE, or a read between tries that found the row finished) passes the step; a successful `kill_sent: false` raises nothing (b.jg5 SRJ-703). Any other outcome, an answer that is not a kill outcome, or a throw fails the kill step, and the other steps still run. After any outcome the row is kept: no delete call exists (b.jg5 SRJ-715). Each CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answer in the result's `refusals` (`teardownKillRefusalsOf` keeps only well-formed ones) is then raised as one notice through the notifier's `notify` (step label `raising the notice for the <CONFLICT|UNUSABLE_NAME> its kill met`; b.jg5 SRJ-1003, SRJ-1002), which the open window writes to the server log and a `persona-teardown-notice` entry: its text is `teardownKillRefusalNoticeText(instanceId, refusal)`, `agent-director kill of cscb_<key> refused at a try: <outcome>` or `… refused at a status read between its tries: <outcome>`, `<outcome>` being `describeKillOutcome`'s one-line rendering (its class and agent-director's redacted description). Nothing latched on it, so it carries no hold sentence and is never the CONFLICT notice's or the unusable-name notice's text. With no `notify` in the injected notifier the step logs `no notifier route is installed for the notice: <notice text>`. Every failed kill is recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-110): when the standing outcome is a non-success and none of the following records it, a raised kill-failure alert decision, a refusal notice for a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answer at a try (an answer at a read between tries does not count), or the onset of its outage written in the window (read once after the kill through the injected `outageFlags`, production `getOutageFlags`: an ENVIRONMENT outcome's `tmux-unavailable`, a CONFIG outcome's `ad-config-malformed`, `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`'s `ad-unreachable`; with no reader, an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG outcome counts as recorded while the key is applied and `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` always), the next step (step label `raising the notice for its kill's outcome`) raises one notice through `notify`, which the window writes as one `persona-teardown-notice` entry: `teardownKillNotSucceededNoticeText(instanceId, outcome, tries)`, `agent-director kill of cscb_<key> did not succeed after <n> kill(s); the row is kept: <outcome>` (both builders live in `src/checked-kill.ts`, beside `describeKillOutcome`). So an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer for a removed persona, an UNAVAILABLE outcome other than `ErrTmuxKillFailed`, an UNCLASSIFIED value, and a standing outcome after a read-time refusal each get an entry. Nothing latches and nothing is armed on it. When the retry's alert decision is `ordinary` or `survivor`, the next step raises it (`raiseKillFailureAlert`, step label `raising the kill-failure alert`; b.jg5 SRJ-704) through the server's one kill-failure alerts instance, unlatched, with the context 'persona teardown': inside the window the ordinary version goes to the server log and a `persona-teardown-notice` entry, the survivor version to the server log and a `persona-kill-survivor` entry, never to Slack ([The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007)). In dry run no agent-director call is made, so no refusal notice, kill-outcome notice or alert is raised, and one dry-run line says the kill is skipped and the row kept. In both modes its UNAVAILABLE retry timer is then stopped once more (`stopRetryTimer`, step label `stopping its UNAVAILABLE retry timer once more, after the kill`, `TEARDOWN_RETRY_TIMER_STOP_AFTER_KILL_STEP`), so no timer stays armed after the teardown. An outage flag the kill raised (`ad-unreachable`, or for a destructive modify's old half `tmux-unavailable` or `ad-config-malformed`) is kept: its onset was written in the window, and its all-clear is written the same way when it comes (b.jg5 SRJ-1002). No second `forget` of held notices follows: none was queued in the window.
9. Its restart failure count and cap latch (`forgetFailures`), its health-check streak (`forgetDisconnectedStreak`) and its not-connected episode (`forgetNotConnectedEpisode`, b.f2b: the notice latch and the restart path's idle evidence for its `working` row) are forgotten, then its latch once more, silently (`forgetConflictLatch`, step label `forgetting its latch once more, after the kill`; b.jg5 SRJ-715, SRJ-504).
10. Its reply-guard record is deleted and its launched-with directory forgotten (`teardownPersonaReplyGuard`). The Stop-hook launch pass (`stopHookLaunchPass`) then re-evaluates the persona's configured and launched-with config directories against the personas still applied, so the managed hook stays only where a remaining persona needs it.

Step 1's approver and sequence stops and step 2's launch-wait cancel also run at submit; the old half of a destructive modify also runs step 2's cancels and step 1's retry-timer stop then. Step 1's and step 3's forgets do not run at submit: they run only at the teardown's serializer turn.

**Afterwards.** The row is kept, as the kill left it. The key was recorded as retired at apply step 1, so the row is the key's old life and is never resumed or reconnected: the next launch of a persona with that key, a persona added again with the same key or a destructive modify's new half, is a reuse spawn of `cscb_<key>` that resets a finished row to a new life and answers `fresh-retired` ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)). A row still live after a kill that did not succeed is replaced only through the live-row sequence with the retired-key flag, which kills it again first. A removed persona's kept row is swept at the next start like any row of an absent persona (`absent persona`, Server-Managed Startup step 4, where it is deleted only after its own kill succeeds). The teardown posts nothing to Slack. Every notice raised for the key while its window was open (the kill-failure alert, a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME its kill met, its kill's non-success that nothing else recorded, an outage onset, the notices of the launch in flight, the CONFLICT notice of a latch it set during step 2 included) is a server-log line and a `startup-errors.log` entry, and none was dropped (b.jg5 SRJ-1003). After the window has closed, a notice for the key routes as any other: a removed persona's is dropped by the notifier because the persona is no longer applied, and a destructive modify's goes to the new half once it is applied. The one exception is the all-clear of an outage whose onset the window wrote (or whose `ad-config-malformed` onset the submit muted), which is written the same way whenever it comes (b.jg5 SRJ-1002); an all-clear that also lists another class is split, and only the other classes' all-clear is posted. The lines are under Logging, [Persona lifecycle lines](#persona-lifecycle-lines-bav2-sr-65-sr-61).

**Not the CLI's bot teardown, and not Graceful Shutdown.** The CLI's `teardownBots` (`stop --stop-bots`, `clean_restart`) is graceful: it pauses each persona's bot and polls its status, killing it only on escalation or timeout, and never deletes a row, so the next start can resume it. Graceful Shutdown leaves every instance and row in place. Persona teardown acts on one removed or destructively modified persona while the server keeps running: it kills its bot without waiting and keeps its row, which is never resumed because its key is retired. No persona teardown deletes a row.

### Destructive modify (b.av2 SR-8.6)

A persona whose `name` (same key), `credentials_file` path or `working_directory` changed is destructively modified: previewed `DESTRUCTIVE:`, then torn down in step 2 and brought up fresh in step 6. There is no separate path. Step 2 runs the [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65) on the persona as the previous configuration declares it (`destructiveOld`), and step 6 runs the [Bring-up at apply](#bring-up-at-apply-bav2-sr-61) on it as the confirmed configuration declares it (`destructiveNew`). Both run through the per-persona serializer, and steps 3–5 run between them.

**Fresh.** The teardown kills `cscb_<key>` and keeps its agent-director row (b.jg5 SRJ-715), and step 1 recorded the key as retired, so the launch in step 6 is a reuse spawn of `cscb_<key>` ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)): over the kept row, once it reads finished, it resets the row to a new life (with no row, an ordinary fresh spawn), and the conversation is not resumed. When the old row still reads live (its kill did not succeed, for example), the reuse collides with it, and the collision `get` sends it through the live-row sequence with the retired-key flag, which kills it and launches only after that kill succeeds: the new half never launches over a still-live old row. The bring-up reads the credentials file the new declaration names, as it stands, with a new bring-up entry. The persona then holds that file's content and digest, so nothing is pending for it until the file changes again. Whatever changed, the old life is never resumed or reconnected, at the step-6 launch or any later one, a restart included. The next start's sweep doesn't remove such a row, since its key is applied.

**Unlatched (b.jg5 SRJ-504).** The teardown forgets the persona's latch and its notice episodes (steps 1, 3 and 9), the CONFLICT episode included, so the latch does not carry over: the new half starts unlatched, and its launch reaches agent-director. It latches only if that launch meets a CONFLICT itself, and then posts one CONFLICT notice to its own destination, since its CONFLICT episode begins afresh.

**The key stays applied.** Unlike a removed persona, the old half's key is still in the applied set after step 1, so the applied-set guard does not stop work for it. The teardown therefore also does these things:

- **At submit.** Besides the approver stop, the sequence stop and the launch-wait cancel every teardown makes, it cancels the persona's bring-up retries and its restart timer, and stops its UNAVAILABLE retry timer, as soon as it is submitted, before its serializer turn. Work already queued ahead of it for the key (a restart timer's work, a retry's work, a bring-up retry and its launch) then finds the persona not up or cancelled and launches nothing. Otherwise that work would launch the new declaration, only for the teardown to kill it. From then until step 6, the relaunch gate and the up predicate answer not up for it.
- **After the agent-director kill.** The kill arms no retry timer, and the stop once the launch in flight settled (step 3) and the stop after the kill (step 8) leave none a launch in flight or an earlier call armed, so none retries against the new half.
- **Its notices (b.jg5 SRJ-1003).** Between the submit and the turn, the submit mutes every notice-episode kind posted through the episodes (each counts as posted in its episode) and the `ad-config-malformed` onset, whose all-clear is then written, never posted ([Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65), at submit). Only notices outside the episodes route as any configured persona's: another outage's onset (`tmux-unavailable`, `ad-unreachable`), the stuck-prompt warning, a spawn-failure notice and the lost-message notice. From the turn until the teardown completes, every notice for its key is written by the window (the server log and a `persona-teardown-notice` entry), never posted to the old half's destination or the new half's, and never held, so none waits for the new half's client and nothing is flushed to it once it is up. This covers the CONFLICT notice of a latch the old half's launch in flight sets during the teardown, and the *Cannot launch* alert of an `ErrInvalidFlags` hold it sets. An outage onset written in the window keeps its flag, and its all-clear, even one raised after the new half is up, is written the same way, never posted to the new half's destination; the new half's own notices post to its destination.

A destructively modified persona is listed in no other class of the change plan. Its other changed settings, in-place or next-launch, come with the fresh bring-up, and a credentials change needs the same path, so it never applies.

### In-place update (b.av2 SR-8.6)

Apply step 3 updates each persona modified in place (a change to `channels`, `delivery`, `permission_prompts`, `dm.enabled` or `dm.contact`) through `PersonaLifecycle.updateInPlace` (`src/persona-lifecycle.ts`), all of them at once, each through the per-persona serializer. It makes no lifecycle call: no kill, delete, launch, reconnect or MCP session drop, and no Slack or agent-director call. The persona's instance, agent-director row, Slack connection and Web API client, MCP session and conversation are kept, as are its restart, backoff, health, outage and retry state, its reply-guard record, its tracked prompts and its held notices.

**The new values already apply at step 1.** Step 1's swap replaced the persona's entry in `personaConfig`, and every consumer reads that entry at each use, so step 3 has no values left to push. The consumers, and when each sees the change:

- **Inbound delivery and DM intake** (Data Flow, Inbound step 4): from the next event, including the cross-persona `receive_all_shared` and unclaimed-channel results.
- **MCP tool posting scope** (`checkPersonaTarget`, Outbound step 3): from the next tool call.
- **Destination** (`persona-destination.ts`): from the next permission prompt, stuck-prompt warning or notice. The permission poller resolves the persona each tick, the notifier and its flush on each notice, and the destination hold on each attempt.
- **Archive evidence** (b.av2 SR-7.4, the `delivery: all` scope of the JSONL checks): at the persona's next launch. A launch already in flight during the apply finishes with the entry it started with.

**What step 3 does.** When the key is no longer applied (a later apply removed it first; its teardown owns it), it does nothing and logs nothing. Otherwise, when `permission_prompts`, `dm.enabled` or `dm.contact` changed, it forgets the persona's cached DM conversation (`personaDestinations.forget`), so the next post to a `dm` destination opens the DM with the current contact through `conversations.open`. The cache also re-checks the contact on each use, so this is a cheap second guard. It then logs one line naming the changed settings (Logging, [Persona lifecycle lines](#persona-lifecycle-lines-bav2-sr-65-sr-61)). It never rejects, and dry run behaves the same.

**A persona that is not up.** A `retrying` or `broken` persona gets the same update: its cache entry is forgotten when one of those three settings changed, and the line is logged. Its bring-up state and retries are not touched; when it comes up, it serves with the new values.

**Posted and held items.** Prompts already posted stay where they were posted and stay answerable, including a DM prompt after DMs are turned off (b.av2 SR-5.1 exception; see Permission Relay, [In-memory state](#in-memory-state-sr-1)). Nothing held is dropped or moved: a prompt the destination hold is holding is derived again on a later tick and goes to the new destination, and each held notice's retry re-reads the destination, so it goes to the new one too (Permission Relay, [Destination hold](#destination-hold-bav2-sr-71-failures)).

### Credentials change (b.av2 SR-8.6 step 4)

Apply step 4 applies each confirmed change to a persona's credentials content, at the same path, through `PersonaLifecycle.reconnectCredentials` (`src/persona-lifecycle.ts`), all of them at once, each through the per-persona serializer (b.av2 SR-6.6). The operation calls the bring-up controller's `changeCredentials` (`src/persona-bringup-controller.ts`) over the connection manager's `reconnectCredentials` and `replaceRetryTokens` (`src/persona-connections.ts`). It touches no other persona and makes no agent-director call. When the server is shutting down it logs `credentials change not applied — the server is shutting down` and does nothing.

**State is decided when it runs.** The controller reads the persona's bring-up state again. A persona credentials-broken by now resolves `{ kind: 'credentials-broken' }` and is left to step 6's recovery bring-up. A persona that is neither up nor retrying, or is unknown, cancelled or no longer applied, is skipped.

**The new file is checked first.** It is read once through the same local check a bring-up runs (`checkPersonaLocalSteps`), against the applied set as it stands after step 1. When it is missing, unreadable or invalid, or its real path is another applied persona's credentials file (b.av2 SR-1.4, apply part), nothing changes: the persona keeps its connection or its retry content, one `persona-credentials-change-failed` line is logged, and the change stays pending (b.av2 SR-8.3).

**An up persona is reconnected.** The new connection opens first and the old one closes only once the new one is up (see the `persona-connections.ts` entry of the Module Map). The persona stays `up` throughout, so its MCP session is not dropped, its instance is not touched and nothing is launched.

**A persona held for its `claude_config_dir` is retrying.** It has no connection (bug b.g57; see Config-dir-unresolvable under [Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 5), so it takes the new tokens and digest as a retrying persona does, opens no connection, and connects with them once the directory resolves. Its cached DM conversation is forgotten when it takes the new content. A hold that starts while an up persona's reconnect is in flight or retrying closes that reconnect with the connection; the persona keeps the new content and connects with it on its return.

**Held and live content.** The controller keeps two things per persona: the held content (tokens and `credentialsDigest`, what the reload detection tick compares against, so it decides whether the change is pending) and the live content (`live`, what the persona's own connection uses). Both are set at bring-up. Right before a swap, at the first attempt or later, both become the new file's. While the new connection retries, the held content is the new file's and `live` stays the old. A refusal, at once or later, holds `live` again, so the change is pending again. The first attempt decides what the persona holds:

| First attempt | Connection | Held content (`credentialsDigest`) | Still pending | Line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| New connection up | The new one is in use; the old one is closed | The new file's | No | `reconnected with its changed credentials; its instance and MCP session are kept` |
| Slack refused a new token | The old one stays in use; the new clients are discarded | The live content (what its own connection uses) | Yes | `persona-credentials-change-failed`, cause `bot_token refused by auth.test: Slack error <code>` or `app_token refused by the Socket Mode open: Slack error <code>` |
| Slack unreachable (a `start()` abandoned at 10 s included) | The old one stays in use; the new one retries on its own SR-3.2 schedule | The new file's | No: it is retrying with it | `its changed credentials cannot reach Slack yet; the new connection retries and the current one stays in use` |

Each line is worded from the persona's state after the attempt. When the persona's own connection was refused while the attempt ran (it is credentials-broken now, for example after a Web API call refused its bot token), it is not said to keep that connection:

- A refused change's `persona-credentials-change-failed` line ends `it stays broken by its credentials, and the change stays pending`.
- An unreachable one logs `its changed credentials cannot reach Slack yet; the new connection retries, and it stays broken by its credentials until that connection is in use`.
- A swap logs `reconnected with its changed credentials and up again; its instance is kept`, and the persona is launched as below.

A reconnect left retrying ends later in one of four ways:

- **It swaps.** The new connection comes into use and the reconnected line is logged (`…; its instance and MCP session are kept`, or `… and up again; its instance is kept` for a persona credentials-broken meanwhile), beside the connection manager's cleared line.
- **It is refused while the persona is still up on the old connection.** The controller holds `live` again, so the change is pending again (and so is an earlier change whose retrying reconnect this one replaced), and logs `persona-credentials-change-failed` ending `the current connection stays in use, and the change stays pending`. `live` is what the connection uses when the refusal lands, which a later swap may have changed since the change was confirmed.
- **It is refused after the old connection was itself refused meanwhile** (the persona is credentials-broken). The persona stays credentials-broken, holding the confirmed content, so nothing is pending, and the refusal is logged as `persona-credentials-refused`.
- **It is cancelled** by a later confirmed credentials change or by the persona's connection being stopped (a teardown, a recovery bring-up, shutdown). Its open `persona-slack-unreachable` episode ends with a cleared line saying why (Logging, [Persona bring-up lines](#persona-bring-up-lines-bav2-sr-103)).

A persona that was credentials-broken meanwhile and whose pending reconnect then swaps is `up` again. It is launched through its launch path's collision ladder, logging `up after its confirmed credentials change — launching`.

**A retrying persona retries with the new content.** A persona that is Slack-unreachable, directory-broken or still on its first attempt takes the new tokens and digest at once, as both held and live content, so nothing stays pending. A Slack-unreachable one gets them through `replaceRetryTokens`; a directory-broken one holds them for when its directory retry reaches Slack. It logs `it retries its bring-up with its changed credentials`. With a locally bad new file, it keeps retrying with its current content, and the `persona-credentials-change-failed` line ends `it keeps retrying with its current credentials, and the change stays pending`.

**The DM destination is forgotten before the swap.** The persona's cached DM conversation is forgotten (`personaDestinations.forget`) in the controller's `beforeSwap` hook, which the manager runs right before every swap, at the first attempt or later, while the persona still reports its old connection. So when the persona is reported up on the new connection and the notifier flushes its held notices, none goes to the old app's DM; the new credentials may belong to another app, with another DM. A throw is logged as `forgetting its cached DM conversation failed: <thrown value>`, and the swap goes ahead.

### Recovery of a credentials-broken persona (b.av2 SR-6.4)

While the server runs, a credentials-broken persona recovers only through a confirmed change to its credentials file. Credentials-broken is `isCredentialsBroken`: outcome `broken` with a local credentials cause (missing, unreadable, invalid or a real-path collision), or with Slack's refusal (`persona-credentials-refused`). Apply step 6 brings up each credentials-changed persona that step 4 did not reconnect because it was credentials-broken, whether or not an instance of it runs, through `PersonaLifecycle.bringUp(persona, applied, { recovery: true })`.

The operation checks the state again when it runs. A persona no longer credentials-broken (step 4 left it here because it was, and a pending reconnect of an earlier change has brought it up since) logs `not brought up again — it is not broken by its credentials now, so its changed credentials are applied as a credentials change` and gets the confirmed change as step 4 would have applied it: the credentials change body runs directly in the same serializer turn (not through the serializer again), with its usual lines, and the operation resolves the persona's outcome after it. Only when that change finds the persona credentials-broken again does the recovery go ahead. Otherwise it logs `broken by its credentials and its credentials file changed — bringing it up again` and clears what the broken bring-up left:

1. Its bring-up state and timers are cancelled (the controller's `cancel`).
2. Its connection is stopped (the manager's `stop`). The bring-up then builds a fresh connection entry with a fresh episode tracker, so a new refusal is logged rather than swallowed by the old episode.
3. Its cached DM conversation is forgotten.

A step that fails logs `<step> before bringing it up again failed: <thrown value>`, and the rest still run. The server's `shuttingDown` flag is checked again once these steps are done, so a shutdown that began meanwhile connects and launches nothing (`not brought up — the server is shutting down`). Then comes the same procedure as [Bring-up at apply](#bring-up-at-apply-bav2-sr-61): storage check, bring-up (a new `persona-start` line, the file read as it stands and checked against the confirmed set) and, when up, the launch. The instance and agent-director row were kept while it was down (b.av2 SR-6.4), so the launch reaches them through the collision ladder and the history is kept. A file that is still bad leaves the persona broken with the new cause logged. It then holds the new file's digest, so nothing is pending until the file changes again.

### Template refresh (b.av2 SR-8.6 step 5)

Apply step 5 refreshes the agent-director template once, through `PersonaLifecycle.refreshTemplate(applied)` and `refreshSlackChannelBotTemplate` (`src/agent-director-template.ts`). `applyStepsFor` selects it only when the change plan's `configDirsChanged` is true: the set of effective config directories (`effectiveClaudeConfigDirs`, compared lexically) differs between the applied and the confirmed personas. That also holds for a plan with no effective change. It runs after step 4, which settles once every reconnect's first attempt has settled, and before step 6. So a persona that step 6 brings up with a new directory launches from the refreshed template.

**Memory-read rules only.** The refresh overwrites the template with the params the boot install wrote (`installSlackChannelBotTemplate`'s `params`), with only the `allow` list derived afresh from the confirmed personas (`deriveMemoryReadAllowRules`, the boot derivation). The rules therefore keep the `projects/*/memory/**` scope and never cover a config-dir root. Every other field is kept, including `claude_args` with the start-time MCP config and system-prompt flags (the append file is not probed again), and `name`, `label`, `deny` and `relay_mode`. A changed server-wide setting behind those arguments takes effect at the next start. The refresh belongs to no persona, so it does not go through the serializer.

**Not fatal.** A rejection, either a typed agent-director error or any throw, is logged in one line and nothing else happens. No startup error is recorded, nothing is posted, no persona is touched, and the rest of the apply and later ticks run. Nothing retries it. The rules stay as last installed until a later confirmed change alters the config-dir set again, or until the next start's boot install. Meanwhile, a persona using a directory new to the set gets a permission prompt for each memory-note read. The boot install is different: a rejection there is fatal (Server-Managed Startup step 3). In dry run the refresh makes the same call the boot install makes. The lines are under Logging, [Persona lifecycle lines](#persona-lifecycle-lines-bav2-sr-65-sr-61).

### Next-launch and server-wide settings (b.av2 SR-8.6)

**`claude_config_dir` and `stop_hook_bootstrap`, own or inherited.** These get no lifecycle call at apply. Step 1's swap is all they need, and the running instance and its conversation are kept. The persona's next launch (a spawn, resume, restart or retry launch) reads the new value from the applied set. For `claude_config_dir`, that covers `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, the pre-launch directory check, the `config_dir` label, the trust patch, the reply-guard steps and the transcript diagnosis. A changed directory has a different `config_dir` label, so the ladder's `config_dir` guard replaces the row by a reuse spawn of the same id, which starts a new conversation (a live row through the live-row sequence first; SR-6.2 as amended, b.jg5 SRJ-1504), with no row deleted; the old history stays in the old directory, archived to the earlier life. A new path to the same real directory keeps the label, and the persona resumes.

For `stop_hook_bootstrap`, the reply-guard record is written at the persona's next launch (`preLaunchReplyGuard`). The apply rewrites no record, and a neighbour's launch writes only its own. The apply does not run the per-directory install rule either: the next launch's launch pass does, over the new and previous directories.

**Inherited defaults.** The top-level `claude_config_dir` and `stop_hook_bootstrap` act only through the personas that inherit them. The loader has already resolved them into each persona, so a changed default takes effect at each inheriting persona's next launch, exactly as an own change does.

**Server-wide settings.** Step 1 writes them to `config.json.last-applied`. The server then runs `configInEffect(startTime, applied)` (`src/reload.ts`): the confirmed personas over every server-wide setting it started with. Running consumers keep their start-time values until the next start, which runs the record. These include the listener's `port` and `bind`, the intervals, timeouts and restart delay, `resume_enabled`, the cron paths, the template's server-wide arguments, and `ack_reaction`, `reply_chunk_limit` and `reply_chunk_mode` (read through `getReplySettings()`). The exceptions are `stop_timeout` and `exit_timeout`. Only the CLI uses them, and it reads them from the record (`readAppliedPersonaConfig`), so once applied they apply to its next `stop` or `clean_restart`. `agent_director_call_timeout_ms` is used by both: the running server keeps its start-time value (`configInEffect`) until its next start, and the CLI reads the recorded value as soon as an apply rewrites the record. The preview says so for each.

**Several changes at once.** A destructive change overrides everything else (see [Destructive modify](#destructive-modify-bav2-sr-86)). Otherwise the kinds combine. A persona can be modified in place (step 3), have its credentials content changed (step 4, after step 3) and have next-launch changes (its next launch).

### Per-persona serialization (b.av2 SR-6.6)

Lifecycle operations on one persona run strictly in sequence. Operations on different personas are independent, except that an apply finishes each step for every persona before the next step starts. The mechanism is a per-key promise chain, `createPersonaSerializer` in `src/persona-serializer.ts`. `server.ts` builds one instance at module scope (`personaLifecycle`) and hands its `run` to every user. `run(key, operation)` starts an operation only once every operation already submitted for that key has settled; a rejected operation doesn't stop the next one.

| Runs through the serializer | Doesn't |
|---|---|
| A fired restart timer's work: its shutdown and up checks, the liveness probe, reconnect, kill and launch (`RestartDeps.serialize`); a retry timer's work (`runRestartRetry`): its in-flight check first, then the same work | Scheduling a restart, the backoff, the cap, the `activeLaunches` guard and the human-trigger clamp; the UNAVAILABLE retry timer's scheduling and backoff, and its retry action's checks before the call |
| Each bring-up retry attempt with the launch it triggers: a directory re-check with its Slack step and launch, and the launch after a Slack retry reached `up` | The start bring-up pass and its launches: the detection tick, the only source of applies, is armed only after that pass returns. A launch the pass parked on a `working` row (b.f2b) may outlive it; a teardown cancels its wait and waits for it to settle (`whenLaunchSettled`) |
| The apply's teardown (step 2), in-place update (step 3), credentials change (step 4) and bring-up with its launch (step 6, recoveries included; a recovery that finds the persona no longer credentials-broken runs the credentials change body directly in the same turn, never through the serializer again); the launch after a pending credentials reconnect swapped in for a refused connection; the network close of the socket detached when a Web API call refused the persona's bot token (submitted, never awaited, bug b.ujn) | The connection manager's own Slack retries and reopens, including the later attempts of a credentials reconnect left retrying; marking a persona credentials-broken on a Web API bot-token refusal, which happens at once so an operation holding the persona's turn cannot delay it |

`spawnForPersona`'s one-launch-in-flight rule stays inside the operations that launch. The live-row sequence runs outside the serializer, in the background in its own detached recovery attempt ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)): while it runs every other launch for the persona answers `sequence-waiting`, and the persona's latch, its teardown and shutdown stop it.

**Checks run when an operation starts, not when it is submitted.** For a persona being torn down, this means:

- **Restart timer.** A timer still pending is cancelled by the teardown and never fires. Restart work already running or queued ahead of the teardown finishes first: its checks find the persona out of the applied set, so it launches nothing, and then the teardown runs.
- **UNAVAILABLE retry timer.** The teardown stops it (step 1). A start-pass launch still in flight at step 2 that then meets UNAVAILABLE arms a fresh timer for the key; the teardown stops it again once that launch settled (step 3) and once more after its kill (step 8), so no retry timer stays armed for the key when the teardown completes (b.jg5 SRJ-715), and none can rerun the restart path's decision on a destructive modify's new half. A retry already running or queued ahead of the teardown finishes first: its checks find the persona not up (a removed persona is out of the applied set, and a destructive modify's old half has had its bring-up state cancelled), so it launches nothing, and its answer is dropped.
- **Notice episodes.** A launch or recovery attempt that runs before the teardown's turn (restart or retry work ahead of it in the serializer, or a start-pass launch that step 2 waits for) can start the persona's `tmux-unresponsive` condition, which opens its notice episode ([The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310)). That work has settled before step 3, so step 1's or step 3's forget drops the episode silently: no post, no ended line, and no call to the retry timer's condition-end entry. A condition the launch in flight started after step 1 arms its own alert check, which runs until step 3's forget cancels it. A persona added again with the same key holds no condition.
- **Bring-up retry.** Retry work queued behind the teardown finds its entry cancelled and does nothing. Work running ahead of the teardown finishes first, and its launch is refused because the persona is no longer applied.
- **Start-pass launch.** It runs outside the serializer, so the teardown itself waits for it (`whenLaunchSettled`) before anything is killed. That includes a launch the pass parked in the background (b.f2b), which can still be waiting for a `working` row when the apply runs; the teardown cancels that wait first, so the launch settles promptly.

**Re-entrancy rule.** An operation running for a key must never await `run` or `whenIdle` for the same key: both wait for the running operation, which would then wait for itself forever. Code that already runs inside a key's operation calls the next body directly, as the directory re-check calls its launch and the apply bring-up calls its launch. It may submit work for the same key without awaiting it, and may await operations for other keys.

### start command

`start` (CLI subcommand) has one prerequisite: the configuration file (`resolveServerConfigPath()`) or its last-applied record `config.json.last-applied` beside it must exist, else it prints `missing prerequisite: config.json not found at <config path>, and no config.json.last-applied at <record path>` and exits 1. With a record, `config.json` may be absent, since the server starts from the record (Server-Managed Startup step 2a). No environment variable stands in for either file. It reads no Slack token (b.av2 SR-10.2): each persona's tokens are in its credentials file, which only the server reads. Neither file's contents are checked here; the server validates them at start and `start` reports that failure (below). It then **self-daemonizes**: the parent process spawns a detached background child, waits for its startup outcome and exits, leaving the child running as the server. Detection of parent vs. child is via the `_CLI_DAEMON_CHILD` env marker.

The parent spawn (`CliDeps.spawnDaemon`) uses `detached: true` (child becomes its own session leader via `setsid`), `stdio: ['ignore', logFd, logFd]` (stdin from `/dev/null`, stdout/stderr to `STATE_DIR/server.log` — no inherited pipes), and `child.unref()`. This isolates the server from the launcher's session and process group, so killing the launching shell's group does not kill the server. The child re-execs `start` with the marker set, redirects logging to `server.log`, and calls `startServer()`.

**Early-failure report (b.av2 SR-1.7, SR-8.7).** Before the spawn the parent records `server.log`'s size. It then polls every `DAEMON_STARTUP_POLL_MS` (100 ms) for up to `DAEMON_STARTUP_WAIT_MS` (30 s), long enough for the startup gate, the start resolution and the template refresh that precede the PID file:

- The daemon exits, or cannot be launched: `[slack] Server failed to start (exit code N | killed by <signal> | could not be launched: …). From <log>:` followed by the last `DAEMON_FAILURE_LOG_LINES` (20) non-empty lines this run appended to `server.log` (read from the start if the log shrank, i.e. rotated), or `…; it wrote nothing to <log>`; exit 1. These lines carry the server's own fatal reason, such as the `[slack] Fatal: configuration error — …` line with the conversion error for a pre-persona file, the `[slack] Fatal: last-applied record error — …` line with its deletion hint, the `reload-record-write-failed` line, or the PID-conflict error when a server is already running. Server log lines never carry a token.
- `STATE_DIR/server.pid` names the child's PID (the server writes it once it is listening, after the start resolution): `[slack] Server starting in background (PID n)`, exit 0.
- The wait expires: `[slack] Server is still starting in the background (PID n) after 30s — its log is <path>`, exit 0. The daemon is never signalled.

The clock, sleep and log reads (`now`, `sleep`, `fileSize`, `readFileFrom`) are `CliDeps` seams, as are the log-file operations: `openLogAppend` / `closeFd` open and close the parent's `server.log` descriptor, and `initLogging` performs the child's redirect (and `clean_restart`'s).

**Marker-leak guard (b.acn)**: the `_CLI_DAEMON_CHILD` marker alone is untrusted, because it can leak from an operator wrapper script (e.g. `start-all.sh` / `cscb-up`) into the launching environment. If leaked, the parent daemonize branch would be skipped and the server would run in-place inside the launcher's session — dying when that process group is killed. A genuine daemon child is always a session leader, so `start` requires the marker **and** session-leadership to trust it. `isSessionLeader()` reads the session id (field 4 after `comm`) from `/proc/self/stat` on Linux and compares it to the pid; it fails open (treats the process as a leader) where `/proc` is unavailable, preserving prior behavior on non-Linux platforms. A set-but-not-leader marker is treated as a leak: it is deleted and `start` falls through to the parent path to re-detach properly.

### stop command

`stop` (CLI subcommand) sends SIGTERM to the running server via the PID file at `STATE_DIR/server.pid`. If the process does not exit within `stop_timeout` seconds (default 30 s), a SIGKILL is sent. `stop_timeout` comes from the configuration the server runs (`readAppliedPersonaConfig`): the last-applied record when it exists, else `config.json`; when that configuration cannot be loaded (a pre-persona file or an unreadable or invalid record included), `stop` logs one line saying so, with the cause, and uses 30 s. A brief 2 s confirmation poll (`STOP_KILL_WAIT_MS`) follows the SIGKILL. Both waits check every `STOP_POLL_MS` (100 ms) through the `CliDeps` clock and sleep seams (`now`, `sleep`), so tests drive them with a fake clock. Stale PID files (process no longer running) are silently removed. A non-zero exit from this phase causes `stop` to exit 1.

Plain `stop` leaves the managed bots running (they are meant to survive server restarts — see [Graceful Shutdown](#graceful-shutdown-sr-11-event-11)). The **`--stop-bots`** flag (b.4dk) additionally exits the bots gracefully, mirroring `clean_restart`'s order: the server daemon is stopped **first**, then the shared `teardownBots` closure runs over the persona set of the configuration the server runs, with its `exit_timeout`: the last-applied record's when it exists, else `config.json`'s (the same per-persona pause/poll/kill sequence on `cscb_<key>` as `clean_restart`, minus the restart phase). An edit to `config.json` that was never applied therefore does not change which personas are torn down. A config with no personas tears down nothing.

Stopping the server first prevents its `onsessionclosed`/`scheduleRestart` handler (`initPendingSession` in `src/server.ts`) from respawning a just-exited bot mid-teardown — the respawn would delete the bot's `ended` row and history before SIGTERM lands. `directorPause` is an agent-director client subprocess that needs no live CSCB daemon (SessionEnd hooks are wired by agent-director into the spawned claude process and call the AD binary), so teardown works fine after the server is down.

Before teardown runs, `stop --stop-bots` loads the configuration (best-effort, as below) and then initializes the agent-director Client singleton via the non-exiting startup gate (`initClient` in `CliDeps`, b.qwo), with that configuration's `agent_director_call_timeout_ms` as the client's call timeout, or the default when it could not be loaded (b.jg5 SRJ-213) — the same init the `clean_restart` algorithm covers in step 3 below (see there for the b.qps / `incident-2026-09-18-clean_restart.md` root cause). The production `initClient` is `initProductionClient(callTimeoutMs)`, which runs the full gate with that call timeout, CSCB's Phase 1 floor included, and on failure throws `StartupGateFailedError`, which keeps the outcome's class label and message and its `refusalKind` (`client-too-old`, `below-phase1-floor`, `other`), so a caller branches on which check refused rather than on text. The gate's `skipPhase1Floor` option, which leaves only the floor check out, is reserved for this initialization. An AD-unreachable initialization or teardown failure is a **loud** `exit(1)`, not a swallowed skip; a config-load failure, a pre-persona file or an unreadable or invalid record included, is best-effort (logged, teardown skipped, but the server stop still succeeds, since the server is already down). A pause-timeout kill escalation does NOT guarantee an `ended` row — that residual case is recovered later by the dead-session `findMissing`→`resume` path.

### clean_restart (SR-11 Event 12)

`clean_restart` (CLI subcommand) stops the server daemon first, then concurrently pauses every managed Claude Code spawn via agent-director, then starts a fresh server. The stop-first ordering prevents the health-check poller and auto-restart logic from interfering with the teardown. It logs to `STATE_DIR/clean_restart.log` via `initLogging()`; its four fatal lines (`failed to load config:` in step 1, `agent-director initialization failed:` in step 3, `bot teardown failed — aborting restart:` in step 6, `start failed with exit code N` in step 8) are also written to the terminal's stderr, through the `console.error` captured before the redirect, so an operator sees why it exited without opening the log. If the redirect fails, every line stays on the terminal and a fatal line appears once. `CliDeps` exposes injectable `directorStatus`, `directorPause`, and `directorKill` adapters (production builds them with the exported `createDirectorOps(getClient)`, which calls `getClient().status/pause/kill` on each operation and maps only `ErrSpawnNotFound` to "no row") plus an optional `initClient` (b.qwo) that installs the AD Client singleton before any per-persona work — tests that pre-install a stub via `setClientForTests` omit it. Each adapter takes the persona's instance ID, `cscb_<key>` (`personaInstanceId`); no label lookup is involved. The per-persona teardown (steps 4–5 below, `teardownPersona`) runs for every persona at once inside a shared `teardownBots(personas, exit_timeout)` closure reused by `stop --stop-bots` (b.4dk). Teardown log lines name the persona as its JSON-quoted name with its key, e.g. `[slack] teardownBots: no spawn row for persona "Ops Bot" (key=ops_bot_5e2526f3) — skipping`.

Algorithm:

1. **Init logging + load config** — `initLogging()` redirects output to `clean_restart.log`. `loadConfig(resolveConfigPath())` (production: `readAppliedPersonaConfig` on the server's config path) provides the persona set and `exit_timeout` from the configuration the server runs: the last-applied record when it exists, else `config.json`. Config load failure is fatal, a pre-persona file included (the loader's conversion error), and so is a record that exists but cannot be read or validated (its deletion hint in the message); the CLI never falls back to `config.json` then, and never writes any reload file.
2. **Stop server daemon** — shells out to `claude-slack-channel-bots stop`, which sends SIGTERM and escalates to SIGKILL after `stop_timeout`.
3. **Init agent-director client** (b.qwo) — this short-lived CLI process does not run the server startup gate, so `getClient()` would otherwise throw. `initClient` (`CliDeps`, production `initProductionClient`) installs the Client singleton via the non-exiting `runStartupGate` variant, built with the step 1 configuration's `agent_director_call_timeout_ms` as its call timeout (b.jg5 SRJ-213; step 1 is fatal before any client is built when the configuration can't be loaded). The gate runs both version checks (the client's minimum and CSCB's Phase 1 floor), as the server's start does; `clean_restart` never leaves the floor out. A gate failure throws `StartupGateFailedError` carrying the outcome's `refusalKind` and is a distinct loud `exit(1)` — the restart never proceeds to teardown or `start` on top of bots it could not reach. Skipping this init was the b.qps / `incident-2026-09-18-clean_restart.md` root cause: the throw was swallowed and every bot reported a bogus "no spawn row — skipping".
4. **Per-persona precheck** — `directorStatus(cscb_<key>)` returns `null` only when the row is genuinely absent (`ErrSpawnNotFound` from `client.status`); "no spawn row — skipping" is printed only in that case. Terminal states (`ended`, `missing`) → skip; otherwise proceed. Any error reaching agent-director (connection refused, uninitialized client, binary unreachable) **propagates** — it is no longer collapsed into a `null`/"no row". Such rejections surface after the parallel loop as a loud aggregate error (see step 6).
5. **Pause + poll** — `directorPause(cscb_<key>)` is called; if it rejects, escalate immediately to `directorKill(cscb_<key>)`. After a successful pause, `directorStatus(cscb_<key>)` is polled with exponential backoff (100 ms start, capped at 2 s, total budget `exit_timeout`). The first poll observing `null` / `ended` / `missing` is treated as clean exit. If the budget is exhausted, `directorKill(cscb_<key>)` force-terminates the spawn. On both the escalation and timeout kill paths the kill's outcome decides the persona's fate (b.dnt): a kill failure other than the benign already-gone race (`ErrSpawnNotFound`) is itself a teardown failure surfaced as a rejection in step 6. Teardown is **kill-but-never-delete**: rows are paused/killed but never deleted, preserving each row's `claude_session_id` so the next start can resume with context.
6. **Loud AD-unreachable failure** (b.qwo, b.dnt) — after the parallel loop, any settled rejection (an agent-director connectivity error raised by a precheck in step 4, a poll-loop `directorStatus` in step 5, or (b.dnt) an escalation- or timeout-path `directorKill` that failed with anything other than the benign already-gone race, never a normal terminal-row skip and never an `ErrSpawnNotFound` already-gone kill, both of which resolve quietly) is logged and re-thrown as an aggregate error (`teardown incomplete for N persona(s); other personas may already have been paused or killed; rows are never deleted, safe to retry`). `clean_restart` catches it and `exit(1)`, aborting the restart **before** starting a new server. A silent no-op teardown is thus impossible.
7. **Start new server daemon** — shells out to `claude-slack-channel-bots start`. Reached only if teardown completed without an AD-unreachable failure.
8. **Exit** — a non-zero exit code from `start` is propagated and the process exits with that code, logged as `[slack] clean_restart: start failed with exit code N`. Because `start` now waits for the daemon's startup outcome, a server that fails early (for example on a config error) makes this exit 1; the reason is in `server.log`, not `clean_restart.log`.

Per-persona polling cadence (100 ms → 2 s cap, `exit_timeout` total) is unrelated to the SR-2.1 permission poller's `agent_director_poll_interval_ms`.

### credentials command (b.av2 SR-12)

`credentials <persona>` (CLI subcommand) writes one persona's credentials file from the operator's terminal; it is the setup wizard's credentials command. It loads the configuration file as it stands (`loadConfigFile`, production `loadPersonaConfig`), never the last-applied record: a persona the wizard has just declared is found before any confirmation, and on a running server the reload tick previews it as added but unable to come up (`credentials file does not exist`) until the file is written, then previews it afresh (the fingerprint covers every referenced credentials file). It resolves the argument by name or key (`resolvePersonaTarget`), prints `Credentials file of persona "<name>" (key=<key>): <path>`, and runs `runCredentialsScript(credentials_file)` (production: `bash <CREDENTIALS_SCRIPT_PATH> <path>` with stdio inherited, SIGINT and SIGQUIT ignored in the CLI process while it runs), exiting with its status. Exit 2 with `CREDENTIALS_USAGE` unless given exactly one non-empty argument; exit 1 with the loader's error when the configuration file can't be loaded, or with the declared personas listed when none has that name or key (the argument is never printed, in case a token was typed there). No agent-director, server or record access. The tokens are read by the script at its own no-echo prompts and never pass through the CLI process or any argv.

### Graceful Shutdown (SR-11 Event 11)

`shutdown(reason, exitCode = 0)` in `server.ts` has two triggers:

- **`SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`**: reason `received SIGTERM` / `received SIGINT`, exit code 0. No deadline is armed: after a CLI `stop`, the CLI sends SIGKILL once `stop_timeout` runs out, which bounds a hung shutdown.
- **The runtime version re-check's stop (b.jg5 SRJ-205)**: a re-check that refuses the binary (see `ad-version-gate.ts` in the Module Map) first writes its one `startup-errors.log` entry, then calls `shutdown('the runtime version re-check refused the agent-director binary (see startup-errors.log)', 1)`, exit code `AD_VERSION_RECHECK_STOP_EXIT_CODE` (1). Nothing is posted to Slack. No outside party bounds this stop, so the `stop` callback arms the shutdown deadline (`armShutdownDeadline`, `src/shutdown-deadline.ts`) right before calling `shutdown`: after `SHUTDOWN_DEADLINE_MS` (30 s, the CLI's default `stop_timeout`) it logs `[slack] Shutdown did not complete within 30 s — exiting with code 1` and exits with code 1, so a shutdown that hangs (an MCP transport close or a Slack disconnect that never settles) still ends the process non-zero. Its timer is unref'd, so it never keeps the process alive, and a shutdown that completes exits first, which makes it moot. The callback also sets `process.exitCode` to 1 right after arming the deadline, before calling `shutdown`: a shutdown that hangs on a promise with no open handle behind it lets Bun run out of work and exit on its own, which the unref'd deadline cannot prevent, and that exit still carries code 1. A signal's shutdown disposes the re-check before its first await, so a re-check stop never starts once a signal's shutdown runs; a signal that arrives during a re-check stop's shutdown is a no-op, so that shutdown keeps exit code 1 and its deadline.

The sequence:
1. Flips the `shuttingDown` flag (idempotent guard: a second call while one runs is a no-op, so a signal during a re-check stop's shutdown keeps exit code 1).
2. Calls `stopPermissionPoller()` to stop the SR-2.1 tick.
3. Calls `stopHealthCheck()`, `disposeAdVersionRecheck()` (the runtime version re-check's timers are cleared, a call in flight is never acted on, a trigger waiting on the check in flight answers `not-running` at once and no later install arms anything), stops the reload detection tick (`reloadController.stopDetection()`, so no further pending-file check runs), stops the cron scheduler, then closes the live-row sequence registry (`liveRowSequences.close()`, b.jg5 SRJ-706; not awaited: every running sequence's stop signal is set at once with the reason `shutdown`, each logging `stop asked — the server is shutting down; no further call`, so none makes a call after the one in progress returns and none holds a timer, and a later start answers `closed` with one line; a rejection is logged as `[slack] stopping the live-row sequences on shutdown failed: <error>`), then `cancelAllRestartTimers()`, the UNAVAILABLE retry controller's `close('the server is shutting down')` (b.jg5 SRJ-305: every armed persona's timer stops with one `stopped` line, and a later arm, from a launch still in flight that meets UNAVAILABLE, logs one `not armed` line and arms nothing, so no retry is pending or fires; a retry already running finishes and its answer is dropped), the notice episodes' `close()` (b.jg5 SRJ-1016: every persona's episodes end silently, nothing posted, every `tmux-unresponsive` alert check cancelled and every unclassified-error episode ended, and a later condition start or unclassified report, from a launch still in flight that meets UNAVAILABLE or UNCLASSIFIED, answers `closed`, so nothing opens, arms or posts after it), the `ErrInvalidFlags` hold's `forgetAll()` (b.jg5 SRJ-207: every hold ends with one `hold forgotten` line, nothing posted and nothing retried), the bring-up controller's `cancelAll()` (every pending directory re-check; a re-check already running does nothing more, and no launch after a retry starts), the destination hold's `cancelAll()` (every persona's retry timer is cleared and its held notices are dropped, not posted, with one `shutting down` line per persona that had notices held, see Logging, [Persona destination lines](#persona-destination-lines-bav2-sr-103); an attempt already in flight still completes but no longer changes the hold's state; held prompts need nothing, since they live in agent-director and are derived again after the next start), `stopAllKeepAliveTimers()` and then `stopAllDialogApprovers()` (b.jg5 SRJ-404; not awaited: every running approver is marked and woken at once, so none makes a call after the one in progress returns, each logs `stopping the approver for <ref> (shutdown): …`, and no approver starts after it, a launch still in flight that returns success logging `not starting the approver for <ref> (shutdown): …`; a rejection is logged as `[slack] stopping the dialog approvers on shutdown failed: <error>`). The manager's Slack retries stop with `stopAll()` in step 5. Then logs `[slack] Shutting down: <reason>`.
4. Stops the HTTP server, drains pending + active MCP transports. Each aborted stream reaches `scheduleRestart`, which arms no timer during shutdown (Auto-Restart step 1, shutdown check).
5. Closes every persona's Slack connection through the connection manager (`stopAll()`), logging `[slack] Disconnecting persona Slack connections`.
6. Calls `closeClient()` inside a try/catch to release the agent-director Client handle. The library's `close()` is idempotent and never throws; the catch is belt-and-suspenders.
7. Removes the PID file, logs `[slack] Shutdown complete` and exits with `exitCode`.

The sequence makes no agent-director call: `closeClient()` only releases the handle. It forgets no latch: every latch is dropped with the process and persists nowhere, so the next start begins with none (b.jg5 SRJ-504; see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)). No `ErrInvalidFlags` hold persists either: step 3 forgets them all, so the next start holds no persona (b.jg5 SRJ-207; [The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold](#the-errinvalidflags-hold-bjg5-srj-207-srj-1008)). The bots are NOT killed, paused or deleted, and their agent-director rows are left as they are, whichever trigger ran it (SR-11 Event 11; b.jg5 SRJ-205). After a re-check stop the bots keep running, unserved, until the server is started again.

A confirmed apply already under way is not awaited, on either trigger: stopping detection doesn't wait for the pass. Its queued or running bring-ups at apply bring nothing up and launch nothing ([Bring-up at apply](#bring-up-at-apply-bav2-sr-61), shutdown skip). Its step 1 already stopped the approver of each key it recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-808), and its teardowns still run to completion, each stopping its approver, sequence and retry timer first; one whose agent-director kill runs after `closeClient()` logs it as a `… failed` teardown line and keeps the row, as every teardown does, accepted noise before the exit.

A start sweep under way (a shutdown begun while `main()` is still starting, such as a runtime version re-check's stop) is not awaited either, and kills nothing more: it reads `shuttingDown` through its shutdown query, so once the flag is set it makes no further `kill`, `status` read, `find-missing` or `get` and no further latch, record write, clear or outage raise (an answer that arrives after it is not acted on), logs its stop line and its summary, and keeps every row (Server-Managed Startup step 4, **The stops**; b.jg5 SRJ-205, SRJ-714). A call already in flight when the flag is set still returns, and its outcome stands. `main()` then starts no bootstrap pass and no bring-up.

## SR-11 Substitution Table

State transitions and event triggers follow `t1.qfc.bg` SR-11 in full. Where the predecessor SRD references a CLI verb, this implementation calls the equivalent typed library method:

| `t1.fp3.63` CLI verb | This implementation's library equivalent |
|---|---|
| `claude-director spawn` | `client.spawn(SpawnParams)` |
| `claude-director resume` | `client.resume({ claude_instance_id })` |
| `claude-director kill` | `client.kill({ claude_instance_id })` |
| `claude-director pause` | `client.pause({ claude_instance_id })` |
| `claude-director delete` | `client.delete({ claude_instance_id: [...] })` |
| `claude-director list --label/--state` | `client.list({ label, state })` |
| `claude-director get` | `client.get({ claude_instance_id })` |
| `claude-director status` | `client.status({ claude_instance_id })` |
| `claude-director read-pane` | `client.readPane({ claude_instance_id, n_lines })` — the liveness checks (the launch wait's evidence read, the `working`-row verdict `workingReconnectVerdict`, `checkWaitingRowPane`, with `n_lines` 40, and b.jdc's two prompt-row paths, the prompt-row verdict `promptRowReconnectVerdict` and the ladder's `launchOnPromptRow`, with the one-line `n_lines` 1, b.jg5 SRJ-606, SRJ-607) read a persona's own row only through the shared read-pane `readPersonaOwnPane` (b.jg5 SRJ-117, see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)); the dialog approver makes its own call, with `allow_pending` |
| `claude-director send-keys` | `client.sendKeys({ claude_instance_id, text })` |
| `claude-director decide` | `client.decide({ claude_instance_id, decision })` |
| `claude-director version` | `client.version({})` |
| `claude-director find-missing` | `client.findMissing({})` — every call goes through the shared memoized, single-flight core `sharedFindMissingSweep` (b.m4r, b.jg5 SRJ-120): an ordinary run joins a run in flight or reuses a result memoized within 10 s, and a bypassing run (`bypassingFindMissingSweep`, whose one caller is the live-row sequence) always makes a new call, whose result later ordinary runs reuse. After a run the server makes, each configured persona's own row in `unverified_ids` is read with one `get` (`claude-director get`), unless the calling path's next step is that `get` or the persona is already latched (then no `get` is made for it). Every other production path's runs are ordinary, driven through `reconcileMissingSweep` from the dead-session pre-resume path (b.4dk, `reconcileMissingFirst`) and, via `sweepDeadTmuxChannelWithCause`, from the tick/restart escalate-dead path (self-recovery: a `working` or `waiting` row whose `read-pane` answered GONE or found the row absent, b.d61, b.f2b, b.jg5 SRJ-603, SRJ-604; a reconnect's keystrokes refused or answered GONE; and an `ask_user` or `check_permission` row whose one-line `read-pane` answered GONE or found the row absent, b.jdc, b.jg5 SRJ-606). A prompt row also drives it directly: the collision ladder when its one-line `read-pane` answered GONE or found the row absent (b.jg5 SRJ-607), and the restart path's deferrals on it once they have run for 10 min (b.jdc). The `working`-row wait's up-front and timeout sweeps go through `reconcileMissingSweep` too, and the start sweep's post-kill run (`runStartSweepPostKillFindMissing`) calls the core on its own client. Also runnable by operators as a periodic sweep (SR-5.4). |

## Configuration

### config.json (`SLACK_STATE_DIR`/config.json, default ~/.claude/channels/slack/config.json)

The server's configuration is the persona config described in the next section: a `personas` array plus the server-wide settings below. The operator edits `config.json` in the state directory (`resolveServerConfigPath()`), but what a start runs is the last-applied record beside it (see Reload files below) whenever one exists; `config.json` is read at start only when there is no record, and is then validated, recorded and applied (b.av2 SR-1.7, SR-8.7; Server-Managed Startup step 2a). No environment variable supplies the bind address, port or anything else. With no record, a `config.json` that cannot be used stops the start with one line, `[slack] Fatal: configuration error — <message>`, and exit code 1, before any port is bound, the PID file is written, a Slack connection opens or anything is spawned:

- a missing file: `The configuration file "<absolute path>" does not exist. The server requires the configuration file to start.` (`cannot be read`, with the errno code in parentheses when there is one, in place of `does not exist` for any other read failure: `EISDIR` for a directory, `not a regular file` for a FIFO, socket or device, which is never opened for a blocking read);
- a pre-persona file (top-level `routes`, `default_route` or `default_dm_session`): the loader's conversion message, unchanged (see Pre-persona rejection below);
- malformed JSON: `loadPersonaConfig: malformed JSON in "<path>" at line <L>, column <C>.`, giving the 1-based position of the first invalid character and none of the file's text;
- unknown keys (b.av2 SR-10.3): an unknown key's name is shown only when it is a plain setting name, matching `ECHOABLE_KEY_NAME_RE` (`/^[A-Za-z_]{1,48}$/`: ASCII letters and underscores, up to 48 characters); any other name, including one with a digit such as `channels2`, is counted, not shown, since it could be a pasted token (`describeUnknownKeys`). The running server's detection tick writes loader errors into `config.json.pending` and `server.log` every 5 s, so an echoed key name would leak there. The forms are `…unknown top-level field(s) in config.json: "chanels".`, `…: 1 field whose name is not shown (it is not a plain setting name, so it could be a pasted secret).` and `…: "chanels", plus 2 fields whose names are not shown (they are not plain setting names, so they could be pasted secrets).`; persona entries, `dm` and `channels[j]` use the same wording (`unknown field(s) in the persona entry: …`, `… in dm: …`, `… in channels[<j>]: …`);
- any other validation failure: the loader's error, unchanged.

The CLI (`stop`, `stop --stop-bots`, `clean_restart`) takes its settings and persona set from the same configuration the server runs, through `readAppliedPersonaConfig`: the record when it exists, else `config.json`. `start` only checks that one of the two files exists. See the command sections under Session Lifecycle.

Server-wide settings (the persona entry keys are in the next section):
- `bind` — HTTP server bind address (default: 127.0.0.1)
- `port` — HTTP server port (default: 3100)
- `session_restart_delay` — seconds before auto-restarting dead sessions (default: 60, 0 = disabled)
- `health_check_interval` — seconds between health-check polls (default: 120, 0 = disabled)
- `exit_timeout` — seconds `clean_restart` and `stop --stop-bots` wait for a Claude session to exit cleanly before force-killing it (default: 120)
- `stop_timeout` — seconds the `stop` command waits after SIGTERM before escalating to SIGKILL (default: 30)
- `mcp_config_path` — path to MCP config file for Claude launch (default: ~/.claude/slack-mcp.json)
- `append_system_prompt_file` — optional path to a file appended to every managed session's system prompt via `--append-system-prompt-file`; missing file silently skipped
- `system_prompt_mode` — controls whether `append_system_prompt_file` is applied (default: `"append"`; valid: `append`, `none`). `"append"` passes `--append-system-prompt-file` to Claude when launching sessions; `"none"` skips the flag entirely so only `CLAUDE.md` is used
- `cozempic_prescription` — cozempic cleaning intensity used before `--resume` launches (default: `"standard"`; valid: `gentle`, `standard`, `aggressive`); has no effect if cozempic is not installed
- `message_archive_db` — optional path to the SQLite message archive (`src/message-archive.ts`); absent means no archive
- `agent_director_poll_interval_ms` — permission-poller interval in milliseconds (default: 1000; 200 to 3 600 000). The old `claude_director_poll_interval_ms` name is rejected with a rename message
- `agent_director_call_timeout_ms` — timeout in milliseconds of each agent-director call CSCB makes for a persona (default: 60000; 1000 to 3 600 000). Server-wide only: a persona entry that sets it is rejected as an unknown field. Every persona-call client carries it as `callTimeoutMs`: the server's persona client from its start's configuration (Server-Managed Startup step 2c; the startup gate's client, built before the configuration is read, uses the client's default), and the CLI's client in `stop --stop-bots` and `clean_restart` from the configuration the server runs (the default when `stop --stop-bots` can't load it). A confirmed change is taken by the CLI at once and by the server at its next start. A call that passes it ends in `ErrCallTimeout`, classified UNAVAILABLE.
