The server warns once per start when it is at or below the need agent-director's timing settings give, or `[pause] timeout_seconds` is not used (`ad-settings.ts`)
- `claude_config_dir` — optional path to a Claude on-disk config directory used for managed sessions; when set, launches carry `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` so the persona authenticates against a specific account. `~` is expanded and the path is resolved to absolute. A persona's own `claude_config_dir` overrides this top-level value. When neither is set, Claude's own default applies.
- `resume_enabled` — boolean (default: `true`). When `false`, the session manager skips `--resume` entirely and always performs a fresh launch, even when a stored session ID exists. Use this to work around versions of Claude Code that crash on `--resume` (e.g. the v2.1.120 "sandbox required but unavailable" regression). Affects both startup (Server-Managed Startup step 5) and auto-restart (Auto-Restart step 5).
- `stop_hook_bootstrap` — boolean (default: `true`). Whether a persona gets the Slack Reply Guard reminder. The top-level value defaults to `true` when absent; a non-boolean is rejected at either scope. A persona's own `stop_hook_bootstrap` overrides the top-level value. The effective value applies per persona, at its next launch: it is written to the persona's record `reply-guard/<key>` before each spawn or resume, and the guard reminds only when that record reads `true`. It also feeds the install rule of step 4a-ter, which keeps the CSCB-managed Stop hook in `<effective_claude_config_dir>/settings.json` while any persona counting toward that directory is enabled.
- `cron_table_path` — optional path to the cscb_cron crontable file (default: `<config dir>/crontab`, where `<config dir>` is the directory of the loaded config file). Anything that is not a non-empty string is rejected; `~` is expanded and the path is resolved to absolute, yielding a required string on the resolved config. Boot-fixed: only the crontable's contents hot-reload at runtime; its location never does.
- `cron_log_path` — optional path to the cscb_cron log file (default: `<config dir>/cron.log`). Same non-empty-string validation, tilde expansion, required-resolved-string, and boot-fixed notes as `cron_table_path`.
- `cron_log_max_bytes` — optional positive integer (>= 1); no default. Any value that is not a positive integer is rejected when set. When absent, log pruning is disabled — this bullet states the contract only; the prune mechanics ship in a later Epic.

The path keys are pointers only: schedules never live in `config.json` — the crontable file is the single source of truth.

### Reload files (config.json.last-applied, config.json.pending, config.json.apply)

Three files sit beside the configuration file, in the same directory, named by appending a suffix to its name (`reloadFilePaths` in `src/reload.ts`, b.av2 SR-8.1). The CLI never writes any of them.

| File | Contents | Written by | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config.json.last-applied` (the record) | A byte copy of the last applied configuration | The server's reload controller | At a start with no record, after `config.json` validates and before anything is applied; and rewritten with the confirmed bytes at step 1 of a confirmed apply (including a no-op). The server never deletes it |
| `config.json.pending` | A fixed header line, the pending state's fingerprint (`fingerprint: sha256:<hex>`), a blank line and the SR-8.4 preview: a header with the counts, then one line per affected persona and changed server-wide setting stating its effect, removals and destructive modifies starting `DESTRUCTIVE:`; or `no effective change`; or one `INVALID:` line with the validation error (see [The preview](#the-preview-sr-84)) | The server's reload detection tick | Present only while a change is pending: written when missing or stale, deleted when nothing is pending (see [Reload Detection Tick](#reload-detection-tick-bav2-sr-82-sr-83)) |
| `config.json.apply` | The operator's confirmation: `config.json.pending` renamed, so it carries that preview's fingerprint line | The operator (the server never writes it) | Consumed by the next detection pass: read, deleted, then applied when its fingerprint matches the current files, else `reload-stale-confirmation`. One made while the server was down is processed by the first pass after the start (see [Confirmation](#confirmation-sr-85)) |

- **The record is what runs.** Every start runs the record when it exists and reads `config.json` only when it doesn't (Server-Managed Startup step 2a). The record is validated in record mode, where two personas sharing a real path are a bring-up failure rather than a validation error. The CLI reads the record the same way for its settings and persona set.
- **Pending is not applied.** The pending file only reports; nothing in it is applied, and editing or deleting it changes nothing (the next pass rewrites it while the change is still pending). Only its fingerprint line matters once it is renamed to `config.json.apply`; the apply uses the files as the matching pass read them, never the preview text. It holds no token, credentials content or digest.
- **Durable writes.** Every server write of a reload file is atomic and durable (`durableWriteFileSync` in `src/atomic-write.ts`): a uniquely named temporary file beside the target, fsync, rename over the target, then fsync of the directory. A reader sees the old bytes or the new, never a partial file, and the new bytes survive a crash once the write returns. A record write that fails stops the start (`reload-record-write-failed`), including one whose rename succeeded but whose directory sync failed (`DurableWriteUnsyncedError`): that record is in place and the next start runs it, but it is not known to be durable, so the start is refused. At a confirmed apply the same failures apply nothing, and after a failed directory sync the previous record is written back (see [The apply pipeline](#the-apply-pipeline-sr-86)). The pending file and the confirmation are deleted with the matching durable delete (`durableUnlinkSync`: unlink, then fsync of the directory); a delete whose directory sync failed (`DurableUnlinkUnsyncedError`) counts as removed. A pending file that reappears after a crash is removed by the next start's first pass; a confirmation that reappears is processed by it.
- **Size cap.** This is the one full statement of the cap; other sections refer here. None of these files, nor `config.json` or a credentials file, is read past 64 KiB (`MAX_RELOAD_FILE_BYTES`), with two uncapped reads, below. The cap lives only in the shared readers `readPersonaConfigBytes` (`config.ts`) and `readCredentialsFile` (`persona-credentials.ts`), so the start, the bring-up, the CLI and the detection tick judge one file the same way (the same digest or unreadable marker). A larger file is refused on its `fstat` size before any read, and the read itself is bounded (`readFdAtMost`, at most one byte over the limit), so a file that grows after the stat is refused too and never read in full. A larger file counts as unreadable: a record refuses the start, a `config.json` is an `INVALID` candidate (or refuses a start without a record), a confirmation is stale, and a credentials file is `persona-credentials-unreadable` with the unreadable digest marker. The read fails with code `EFBIG` (`FILE_TOO_LARGE_CODE`), worded `is larger than the 64 KiB limit` (`configReadFailurePredicate`). The server's own `config.json.pending` can exceed the cap for a very large single change (hundreds of personas renamed or credentials files changed at once) even while `config.json` is under it: each pass then finds it unreadable and writes it again, and its rename to `config.json.apply` is refused as stale (`is larger than the 64 KiB limit`); the fix is to split the change into smaller edits and confirm each.
  - **The first exception: the file guard's read.** `credentialsFilesToProtect` (the SR-5.2 file-send guard, reached through `protectedCredentialsFiles()`) reads `config.json` with `readPersonaConfigBytes(path, fs, { uncapped: true })`, which skips both size checks and reads the whole file. It must, so a credentials path named only in an oversized, unapplied `config.json` stays protected. The read is still opened and stat'ed first, so a directory, FIFO, socket or device is refused, never read. Its bytes feed only `referencedCredentialsPaths` and are never recorded, applied or logged. 
  - **The second exception: the retired-key record's start read.** `loadRetiredKeyStore` (`retired-keys.ts`) reads `retired-keys.json` with `readPersonaConfigBytes(path, deps.readFs, { uncapped: true })`. Only the server writes the record and entries leave it only by a clear or a restore, so it can legitimately grow past 64 KiB; a record the server wrote must never stop the start for its size. It is read once, at start, and its bytes are parsed into the store, never digested or compared. The open-then-fstat rule still refuses a directory, FIFO, socket or device unread. No other caller passes `uncapped`.
- **Recovery.** A record that cannot be read or validated stops the start, and the logged line says that deleting the record makes the next start apply `config.json` as it stands.

### retired-keys.json (STATE_DIR/retired-keys.json)

The retired-key record (b.jg5 SRJ-801, SRJ-802), owned by `src/retired-keys.ts`: the persona keys the server holds as retired. It sits in the server's state directory (`retiredKeysPath`, over `resolveServerStateDir()`: `~/.claude/channels/slack/` unless `SLACK_STATE_DIR` is set), beside `config.json.last-applied`. Only the server writes it, through the one store `main()` loads at start (Server-Managed Startup step 2); the CLI never builds a store and never writes, creates or removes the file. It survives a server restart: a new store over the same directory reads what an earlier one wrote.

A UTF-8 JSON object, written by `serializeRetiredKeys` (two-space indented, a final newline, keys sorted) and read by `parseRetiredKeys`:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | The integer `1` (`RETIRED_KEYS_FORMAT_VERSION`) | The format version |
| `keys` | An object: one entry per retired key, the key any non-empty string | The retired keys |
| `keys.<key>.retired_at` | An RFC 3339 UTC timestamp ending in `Z` (fraction optional; the date and time must exist) | When the key was last recorded |
| `keys.<key>.cause` | One of `removed`, `destructive-modify`, `absent-at-start` (`RETIRED_KEY_CAUSES`) | What recorded it last |
| `keys.<key>.new_life_begun_at` | Such a timestamp, or `null` | The "new life has begun" mark; `null` when it is not set |

- **Strict.** Every field is required with its type; only `new_life_begun_at` may be `null`; a field the format does not name is refused at either level; the bytes must be valid UTF-8 with no byte order mark. A key is not checked against the persona-key pattern.
- **Missing means empty.** A missing file means no key is retired; loading it writes nothing.
- **Unreadable stops the start.** A file that exists but cannot be read (a directory, FIFO or other non-regular file included, refused by `readPersonaConfigBytes`'s open-then-fstat rule; there is no size cap, see [Size cap](#reload-files-configjsonlast-applied-configjsonpending-configjsonapply)), parsed or validated stops the start with one `retired-keys-unreadable` startup-errors entry (`retiredKeysUnreadableMessage`): it names the file and what is wrong, and says that moving the file aside lets the server start, at the cost that the keys it held are no longer retired. The start never guesses, and no partial record is used. The entry carries no file content and no parser text.
- **Durable writes.** Every write is atomic and durable, as for the reload files (see the Durable writes bullet under [Reload files](#reload-files-configjsonlast-applied-configjsonpending-configjsonapply)), and writes the whole record held in memory; a restore of an empty record deletes the file with `durableUnlinkSync`.
- **Causes.** The module accepts and writes all three causes. A confirmed apply records `removed` and `destructive-modify` keys; the start sweep records `absent-at-start` keys.
- **Written at apply step 1; restored after a failed rewrite.** A confirmed apply's step 1 records, in one write before it rewrites `config.json.last-applied`, the key of each removed persona (a renamed persona's old key included), of each destructive modify, and of each added persona whose key the store holds only in memory; when the rewrite (or that write itself) fails, the record is restored to what it held before the apply (b.jg5 SRJ-803, SRJ-804; see [The apply pipeline](#the-apply-pipeline-sr-86)). The start resolution records no key.
- **Written by the start sweep (b.jg5 SRJ-116, SRJ-714, SRJ-803).** The start sweep (`reconcileOrphans`, [Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 4) records, in one `record` batch after its latch pass and before its first kill, the `persona` label value of every listed row, in any state, that names no persona of the applied configuration, with the cause `absent-at-start`. A failed write leaves the file as it was, and the store holds those keys as retired in memory for the server's life (`isHeldInMemory`), flagged unwritten until a later write that succeeds carries them: an apply that brings such a key's persona up writes the record first (step 1 above). The next start records them again.
- **Marked when its new life begins.** The `new_life_begun_at` mark is set, in one durable write through the store's `mark` (its only writer), when a reuse spawn for the recorded key succeeds (b.jg5 SRJ-806; [Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)). It survives a restart, so a server that starts over a marked entry reads the key's live row as its new life. A `mark` whose write fails is held in memory by the store (read as marked) and written again at the key's next launch decision; a restart loses it.
- **Cleared when its row reads live with the mark set.** A key's entry is removed, in one durable write, when the server reads the key's own row (`cscb_<key>`) through the session manager's shared `get` read or own-row `status` step, reads it with the `status` read between a persona teardown kill's tries or a start-sweep kill's tries, or lists it in the start sweep's `list` (except for a key that sweep records, whose recording clears the mark instead), in `waiting`, `working`, `ask_user` or `check_permission` while its `new_life_begun_at` mark is set; never on `pending` (b.jg5 SRJ-807; see **The retired-key entry clear** under [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)). A failed clear leaves the entry in memory and in the file for the next qualifying read. An entry leaves the record for no other reason than this clear and a failed apply's restore.

### Persona config

The persona loader in `src/config.ts` (`resolvePersonaConfig`, `parsePersonaConfigBytes` and `loadPersonaConfig`) accepts the persona shape of b.av2 SR-1. It is the only configuration shape; the server and the CLI both load it, from the last-applied record or `config.json` (see Reload files). The operator reference, with a complete example that `tests/shipped-docs.test.ts` loads through this loader, is README.md's [Personas (config.json)](../README.md#personas-configjson); this section describes the loader's rules, not the operator's steps.

**Entry points and purity (b.av2 SR-13.1).** `resolvePersonaConfig(raw, configDir, home)` parses, defaults and validates an already-parsed value. It never opens, reads, creates or writes a file and never requires a path to exist; the only file-system access is resolving the real paths of persona working directories and credentials files for the cross-persona rules below. `parsePersonaConfigBytes(bytes, source, configDir, options)` is the one JSON-parse path: it parses the exact bytes that were read and delegates to `resolvePersonaConfig`, naming `source` in errors; the reload controller validates the record and `config.json` through it. `loadPersonaConfig(path, home?)` reads the file once and delegates to it; it never writes, renames or converts the file. Nothing runs at import.

**Record mode (b.av2 SR-1.5, record-start part).** With `record: true` (the last-applied record at a start, and the CLI's read of it) every rule below runs except the shared-real-path rejection. At a start from the record such a collision is a bring-up failure of each persona involved instead (Server-Managed Startup step 2a).

**Top level.** A required `personas` array, which may be empty, plus the server-wide settings. The server-wide settings are the ones listed in the `config.json` section above, with the meaning, default and validation given there, including path resolution for the top-level path keys. Unknown top-level keys are rejected, named only when they are plain setting names (see the unknown-keys message above), and the renamed poll-interval key `claude_director_poll_interval_ms` gets a rename message naming `agent_director_poll_interval_ms`. Three more server-wide keys, the reply settings, are listed here; they drive the inbound ack step and `reply` chunking (see Data Flow) through `getReplySettings()` in `server.ts`, at their start-time values.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ack_reaction` | non-empty string | absent | Emoji name of the acknowledgement reaction. Absent means no acknowledgement. |
| `reply_chunk_limit` | positive integer | `4000` | Largest reply chunk, in characters. |
| `reply_chunk_mode` | `length` or `newline` | `newline` | How a long reply is split. |

**Persona entry.** Each element of `personas` is an object with these keys:

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | non-empty string, required | — | Persona identity; the persona key is derived from it by `src/persona-identity.ts`. No format rule (b.av2 SR-1.2): any non-empty string loads (see Names below). |
| `credentials_file` | path, required | — | The persona's credentials file. |
| `working_directory` | path, required | — | The instance's working directory. |
| `channels` | array of channel entries | none | Channels the persona is in. The same channel ID may not appear twice in one persona. |
| `dm.enabled` | boolean | `false` | The DMs switch. Inbound: on, a DM to the persona's app is delivered to its session with `via` `dm`; off, it is dropped with a `persona-dm-dropped` line (see Data Flow, Inbound). Outbound: on, the persona's tools may also target a `D…` DM conversation, and `reply` may target a user ID, which it opens with `conversations.open` on the persona's client before posting; off, every DM and user-ID target is refused with no Slack call, so the persona never opens or posts in a DM (see Data Flow, Outbound). It is read at each tool call. Exception: a permission prompt already posted in the persona's DM is still updated after DMs are turned off (see Permission Relay, [In-memory state](#in-memory-state-sr-1)). A group DM (`channel_type` `mpim`) is never delivered either way; an @mention in a group DM is decided by the channel rules instead. |
| `dm.contact` | Slack user ID | absent | The user who receives prompts and notices when `permission_prompts` is `dm`, in the persona's DM with that user (opened with `conversations.open` on the persona's client when none exists). |
| `permission_prompts` | `dm` or a channel ID, required | — | Where permission prompts and notices go: that channel, or, for `dm`, the persona's DM with `dm.contact` (see Permission Relay, Per-tick flow). |
| `claude_config_dir` | path | top-level `claude_config_dir` | Claude config dir for the persona. Absent at both levels means Claude's own default. |
| `stop_hook_bootstrap` | boolean | top-level `stop_hook_bootstrap` | Whether this persona gets the reply reminder; written to its `reply-guard/<key>` record at each launch and applied from its next launch. |

**Channel entry.** Both keys are required: `id`, a Slack channel ID matching `^[CG][A-Z0-9]+$`, and `delivery`, either `all` (every message) or `mentions` (only messages that mention the persona or hold `<!here>` / `<!channel>`, with or without a label; `<!everyone>` and user-group mentions do not count). `dm.contact` must match `^[UW][A-Z0-9]+$`, and a channel ID in `permission_prompts` uses the channel ID format.

**Path rule.** Persona paths (`credentials_file`, `working_directory`, per-persona `claude_config_dir`) must be absolute, exactly `~`, or start with `~/`. The tilde is expanded under the home directory passed in (the OS home when not given) and the result is made absolute. Relative paths are rejected.

**Names (b.av2 SR-1.2, SR-2.2).** A persona's name has no format rule beyond being a non-empty string. It and the key derived from it are shown exactly as written wherever a persona is named: log lines, previews, loader errors (`personaEntryStyle` renders the persona reference for any non-empty name; cross-persona errors echo each name involved), Slack notices, MCP tool results, agent-director labels, the instance ID and the tmux session name. Nothing masks or rejects a name that happens to look like a token.

**Unknown keys.** An unknown key in a persona entry, its `dm` object or a channel entry is rejected, naming the persona and the key when the key is a plain setting name (other names are counted, not shown; see the unknown-keys message under config.json). A token-like key such as `bot_token` is rejected the same way: credentials live only in the credentials file.

**Per-entry rejections.** On top of the type and format rules above, a persona entry is rejected when:

- `permission_prompts` is missing
- it has zero channels and DMs off (`dm.enabled` not `true`), so it can receive no messages
- `permission_prompts` names a channel the persona isn't in
- `permission_prompts` is `dm` but `dm.contact` is missing or DMs are off (both are named when both are wrong)

**Cross-persona rejections (b.av2 SR-1.5).** Once every entry has parsed, the loader rejects:

- a duplicate name or key. Each persona's name and key are compared, by exact string, with every other persona's name and key, so a name equal to another persona's derived key is a duplicate too. The error names the duplicated name or key.
- a key that starts with another persona's key (b.1ix follow-up; `checkPrefixRelatedKeys`), such as `dev` and `dev_2`, or `dev` and `"Dev Bot"` (key `dev_bot_<hash>`). agent-director 0.10.0's verbs (read-pane, send-keys, kill, and the tmux session check inside resume) pass `slack_bot_<key>` to tmux bare, and tmux takes a session whose name starts with a bare target when none has that exact name, so once `slack_bot_dev` is gone they could act on `slack_bot_dev_2`. Every name derived from a key is fixed text around the whole key (`cscb_<key>`, `slack_bot_<key>`), so two derived names start one another only when their keys do, and this one rule covers them all. Checked after the duplicate rule, so equal keys keep its message, and in record mode too: the relation depends on the names alone. The error says which key starts with which, names both tmux sessions and, when `suggestNonPrefixingName` finds one, suggests a new name for the persona with the shorter key: the key plus `_main`, else `_main_2` to `_main_99`, the first whose key starts no other key, is the start of none and equals no other name or key. It finds none when another key is the start of every candidate (`d` beside `dev`, or `dev_main` itself), and the error then gives only the rule.
- a shared `working_directory`, then a shared `credentials_file`. Each is compared by `resolveRealPath` (real path, with a lexical `path.resolve` fallback when realpath fails for any reason), so a symlink to another persona's path, or `~/x` against its absolute form, is a duplicate. Only the same setting is compared: one persona's working directory against another's credentials file is not a collision. The error names the setting and the expanded path; when the two expanded paths differ (only a symlink can cause this), it shows both and the real path they share.

Each error names both personas, each as its array position plus the `src/persona-identity.ts` rendering. Personas are scanned in array order and the first colliding persona is reported against the earliest persona it collides with.

One persona listed in several channels loads: the rule is one working directory per persona, not one per channel.

**Pre-persona rejection (b.av2 SR-1.7).** If the top level has `routes` (in any shape), `default_route` or `default_dm_session`, the loader stops with the conversion message before any other check. The message names the key and says the configuration must be rewritten by hand as personas. The file is never written and nothing is auto-converted. The CLI uses the same loader. When it is the file a start or the CLI reads (there is no record), such a file stops the server's start, makes `clean_restart` exit 1 before stopping anything, and makes `stop` fall back to its default `stop_timeout` (with `--stop-bots`, bot teardown is skipped). A record with a pre-persona key is an invalid record: it stops the start with the deletion hint.

**Check order and errors.** The loader checks, in order: the value is an object, the pre-persona keys, unknown top-level keys, `personas` is present and an array, the server-wide settings, each persona entry in array order, the name/key rule, the prefix-related key rule, then the shared-path rule (`working_directory` before `credentials_file`). It reports the first violation only, so a per-entry error anywhere wins over any cross-persona one. Entry errors name the entry's position and, when `name` is a non-empty string, the persona as its JSON-quoted name with its key (the `src/persona-identity.ts` renderer), plus the setting. Errors don't echo rejected values: they may repeat only the persona name and IDs that already passed their format rule (e.g. a `permission_prompts` channel ID that isn't in the persona's channels, or a duplicated channel ID). The shared-path errors are the deliberate exception: they show the expanded, absolute paths, which have already passed the path rule. A malformed-JSON error gives only the line and column of the first invalid character (`src/json-position.ts`) and omits the parser's detail, which could quote file content. An unknown key's name is shown only when it matches `ECHOABLE_KEY_NAME_RE`; other unknown keys are counted, so a token pasted as a key name never reaches the start log, the pending file or `server.log`.

**Not checked at load time.** The loader doesn't read the credentials file and doesn't check that any directory or file exists. Those are bring-up checks: the credentials-file check is in `src/persona-credentials.ts` and the working-directory check is in `src/persona-bringup.ts` (see the Module Map). The server runs them at start, for each persona, as steps 1 and 2 of its bring-up (`checkPersonaLocalSteps` in `src/persona-start.ts`, run by the bring-up controller; see Server-Managed Startup step 5). A credentials failure leaves that persona `broken`; a working-directory failure leaves it `retrying`, and its directory is re-checked until usable. The `claude_config_dir` check (`checkPersonaConfigDir`, `src/persona-bringup.ts`) is a bring-up check too, run before the persona's Slack connection opens: an unresolvable directory holds the persona with no connection (`persona-config-dir-unresolvable`) until it resolves.

### Credentials files (`credentials_file`)

Each persona's Slack tokens live only in its own credentials file: a JSON object with exactly `bot_token` and `app_token` (shape and checks in the `persona-credentials.ts` entry of the Module Map; operator reference in README.md's [Credentials files](../README.md#credentials-files)). `config.json` holds only the path. The server reads the file at the persona's bring-up and, outside dry run, in each reload detection pass (a digest only; see [Reload Detection Tick](#reload-detection-tick-bav2-sr-82-sr-83)). It never writes, copies or chmods it and never checks its mode. The operator writes it, by hand or with the setup wizard's credentials command, `claude-slack-channel-bots credentials <persona>` (`## Credentials command` in `skills/setup-slack-channel-bots/SKILL.md`), which runs the packaged `scripts/write-credentials.sh` and creates it with mode 0600; see Security Model. A changed file on a running server is a pending credentials change, applied only once confirmed ([Credentials change](#credentials-change-bav2-sr-86-step-4)).

### agent-director state.db (~/.agent-director/state.db)

Persistent CSCB-spawn registry — owned by agent-director, not CSCB. CSCB reads this transitively via `client.list/status/get/resume(...)`. Same-user invariant verified at SR-5.1 startup gate.

### agent-director config.toml (~/.agent-director/config.toml)

agent-director's own settings file — owned by agent-director; CSCB only reads it, never writes it (b.jg5 SRJ-209). CSCB reads it under the server process's HOME, at start (Server-Managed Startup step 2b) and at each 120 s tick of the runtime version re-check, because agent-director offers no interface that reports its effective timing values. It uses only the nine `[tmux]` keys and `[pause] timeout_seconds`, with agent-director's rule (`src/ad-settings.ts` in the Module Map has the keys, defaults, minimums, the 2^63 − 1 bound and the refused forms). Other tables and keys are ignored. CSCB's read refuses only what the server checks: an unreadable, oversized (64 KiB, CSCB's own cap), non-UTF-8 or unparseable file, a `tmux` that is not a table, or a `[tmux]` value agent-director refuses. A file that agent-director refuses for another reason (a wrong-typed `[pause] timeout_seconds`, or a wrong-typed or out-of-range key in another table) reaches CSCB as agent-director's own answers to its calls; CSCB's read never overrides them. A file agent-director refuses as a whole answers every call that reads its store with a CONFIG answer (`ErrConfigMalformed`), which raises the persona's `ad-config-malformed` outage (`outage-state.ts` in the Module Map); CSCB's own read never raises it. The values in effect at start also size the need of `agent_director_call_timeout_ms` (b.jg5 SRJ-213): the startup check (Server-Managed Startup step 2c) warns once when the setting is at or below it or `[pause] timeout_seconds` is not used; see `ad-settings.ts` in the Module Map.

### startup-errors.log (~/.claude/channels/slack/startup-errors.log)

Append-only log of startup errors, fatal and non-fatal, written by `recordStartupError` (`src/startup-errors.ts`). A start whose retired-key record cannot be read, parsed or validated writes one fatal `retired-keys-unreadable` entry (see [retired-keys.json](#retired-keysjson-state_dirretired-keysjson)). It also receives the runtime version re-check's one entry when it stops the server (`ad-below-phase1-floor` or `ad-system-install-too-old`, runtime form, carrying "found by a runtime re-check while the server was running"; see `ad-version-gate.ts` in the Module Map), and, while the server runs, `persona-unclassified-error`: an unclassified-error alert for a persona no longer in the applied configuration, naming its key and the alert's text ([The unclassified-error episode](#the-unclassified-error-episode-bjg5-srj-313-srj-1009)). The kill-failure alert ([The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007)) writes `persona-kill-failed`, its ordinary version for a persona no longer in the applied configuration, and `persona-kill-survivor`, its survivor version on a route with no Slack destination (such a persona, or a start-sweep kill). Each such entry is `<ref> (<context>): <text>`: `persona=<key> (recovery): …` from the restart path or the collision ladder, `instanceId=<id> (start sweep): …` from the start sweep. A stopped retry of a persona removed during its tries writes one `persona-kill-failed` entry carrying the stop's log line, `persona=<key> (<context>): the kill-failure ordinary alert not raised — its tries were stopped (<cause>)…`, with no alert text (b.jg5 SRJ-702). `persona-teardown-notice` (b.jg5 SRJ-1003, SRJ-1013) is every notice raised for a persona while its teardown's notice window is open ([Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65), "The notice window"), whether or not the persona is still in the applied configuration: the kill's ordinary kill-failure alert, a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME its kill met, an outage onset (and that outage's all-clear, whenever it comes), an unclassified-error alert, the notices of the launch in flight, a stuck-prompt warning; the kill-failure alert's survivor version raised then is a `persona-kill-survivor` entry of the same form. The persona notifier writes each through `recordStartupError`, as `personaTeardownNoticeEntryText` builds it: `persona "<name>" (key=<key>), raised during its teardown: <text>`, or `…, the all-clear of an outage raised during its teardown: <text>` for an all-clear after the window has closed. Every start-sweep kill that did not succeed writes one `orphan-cleanup` entry naming the row, its listed state, its session and the outcome with its class, the row kept (`kill did not succeed for <row> state=<state> tmux_session=<session>: <outcome>; row kept, its session may still be running`; Server-Managed Startup step 4); when its tries call for the ordinary version, its text follows, after `; kill-failure alert: `, unless a shutdown stopped the tries, which the entry says instead, with no alert text. One timestamped line per entry; a typed agent-director error is surfaced as its `errName` plus, when it has a description, `message="…"` (`describeAgentDirectorFailure`), except `ad-template-install`, which keeps the name and description verbatim. Rotation is operator-owned via `docs/logrotate-startup-errors.conf`.

### cron.log (`cron_log_path`)

Append-only plain-text log of every cscb_cron fire outcome, written by `src/cron-log.ts`. Location is the config-resolved `cron_log_path` (default `<config dir>/cron.log`); boot-fixed — the path never hot-reloads. Deliberately plain text, not JSONL, so `grep no-session cron.log` yields human-triageable lines.

Each outcome entry is one physical line of five space-delimited fields: `<ISO-8601 UTC ms timestamp> <identity|-> <target|-> <outcome> <detail>`. The `detail` field leads with key=value tokens (`prompt=`, `status=`, `errno=`, `line=`) then free text. Every value is newline-escaped, so one record is always exactly one physical line. UTC matches server.log so an outage window can be cross-correlated.

The `outcome` field is one of nine classes:

| Outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `delivered` | prompt delivered to the target persona |
| `no-session` | `/interject` answered 503: the target persona is not up (broken or retrying), or has no live connected session — dropped |
| `unknown-persona` | no persona in the applied config has that name or key |
| `prompt-missing` | prompt file did not exist at fire time |
| `prompt-unreadable` | prompt file existed but could not be read |
| `prompt-oversize` | prompt file exceeded the size ceiling |
| `parse-error` | the crontable line could not be parsed |
| `http-error` | localhost POST hit an unexpected HTTP status or a network failure (503→`no-session`, 404→`unknown-persona` are classed separately) |
| `fanout-deferred` | all-bots fire skipped — emitted by the cron dispatcher while fan-out remains deferred to E4; kept so old lines stay interpretable |

A per-fire summary line shares the five-field layout with `summary` in the outcome position (a line kind, not an outcome class): `<ts> <identity> - summary delivered=N failed=M`. An `info` line kind (same layout) carries informational markers, and a `warn` line kind carries operator-actionable conditions — the crontable vanishing or becoming unreadable — with `identity`/`target` defaulting to `-` because they are not fire-scoped. Both tokens are distinct from every outcome class, so `grep warn cron.log` matches exactly the warn lines and neither kind pollutes the outcome triage views.

Append-only: no rotation, no pruning, no read-back (pruning ships in a later Epic). The writer `mkdir`s the log's missing parent directory on first append — deliberately unlike `cron-bootstrap.ts`'s no-mkdir invariant, which is crontable-only (D-Q1), since the log is server-owned output. Write failures never break dispatch — a failed append logs one `[slack] cron-log` line, drops the fd, and self-heals on the next append. This module is a writer other code calls.

### permission-trail.jsonl (~/.claude/channels/slack/permission-trail.jsonl)

Append-only **JSON Lines** event store for the CSCB-side visibility trail of the AD↔CSCB tool-permission relay (SRD `t1.cdb.4g`). One JSON object per newline-terminated line. The file path honors `SLACK_STATE_DIR` — default `~/.claude/channels/slack/permission-trail.jsonl`. Owned by `src/permission-trail.ts`; every emit goes through `emitTrail()` (auto-stamps `ts`) or `emitTrailEvent()` (caller-supplied `ts`).

**Line schema** (enforced at the emitter — SR-V-1 / SR-V-4.5):

| Field | Type | When present | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ts` | string | always | RFC 3339 with ≥ ms precision (SR-V-4.3, SR-V-4.5). Substituted with a `[slack]` warning if missing/invalid. |
| `event` | string | always | Stable hierarchical identifier in the `cscb.*` namespace (e.g. `cscb.chat_post.attempted`, `cscb.click_handler.invoked`, `cscb.chat_update.attempted`, `cscb.decide.attempted`, `cscb.block_actions.received`). |
| `request_token` | string | when AD has minted one | AD-side UUID (SR-V-1.1). Absent for events emitted before token assignment (SR-V-1.2). |
| `claude_instance_id` | string | whenever known | Primary join key when `request_token` is absent (SR-V-1.2). |
| `channel` | string | events touching Slack | Slack channel id (SR-V-1.3). |
| `message_ts` | string | events touching Slack | Slack message `ts` of the prompt or closure (SR-V-1.3). |
| _per-event-class fields_ | any | event-class specific | Passed through verbatim — no truncation (SR-V-3). |

**Example line** (a `chat.postMessage` attempt emitted by the SR-2.1 poller):

```json
{"ts":"2026-06-04T20:39:58.123Z","event":"cscb.chat_post.attempted","claude_instance_id":"cscb_ops_bot","request_token":"6f3a1d2c-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd","channel":"C0B1ZJJLJ9M","text":"*Permission* requested for `Bash`","blocks":[{"type":"section","text":{"type":"mrkdwn","text":"…"}},{"type":"actions","elements":[{"type":"button","action_id":"perm_allow_cscb_ops_bot_6f3a1d2c-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd","text":{"type":"plain_text","text":"Allow"}},{"type":"button","action_id":"perm_deny_cscb_ops_bot_6f3a1d2c-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd","text":{"type":"plain_text","text":"Deny"}}]}],"ok":true,"slack_ts":"1717536002.000100"}
```

**No-truncation guarantee.** The canonical trail line persists every field at full fidelity (SR-V-3.1) — the full `blocks` array including every `action_id`, the full `text`, the full Slack API response. The 300-character `[slack] RAW <event> event persona=<key>: …` summaries the event router (`src/persona-event-router.ts`) logs for each `message` / `app_mention` event, before handing it to `persona-routing.ts`, are a **separate human-readable log** kept truncated intentionally per SR-V-3.2; they do not replace the canonical store and the two coexist.

**`jq` smoke-check** — confirm the file is valid JSONL and pivot by correlation key:

```sh
# Every line parses as JSON
jq -c . ~/.claude/channels/slack/permission-trail.jsonl | head -3

# Every event for one request_token, in time order
jq -c 'select(.request_token=="6f3a1d2c-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd")' \
  ~/.claude/channels/slack/permission-trail.jsonl

# Every event on a Slack channel within a time window (SR-V-5.2)
jq -c 'select(.channel=="C0B1ZJJLJ9M" and .ts>="2026-06-04T20:00:00Z" and .ts<="2026-06-04T21:00:00Z")' \
  ~/.claude/channels/slack/permission-trail.jsonl
```

**Federation.** AD emits a complementary JSONL log on its side (`t1.n4v.14`). The two logs join on `request_token` + `claude_instance_id` per SR-V-4. No shared store; the operator stitches the trail via `jq` or equivalent.

**Retention.** None. The file is append-only and the system does not self-protect against disk pressure (SR-V-5.5). Operators rotate / archive / delete out-of-band.

#### `cscb.poller.row_decision` (SR-V-2.3)

Emitted once per `permission_requests` row per tick (and once per `non_conforming_skipped` spawn per tick) from `src/permission-poller.ts`. Some rows emit no row decision: rows of a spawn skipped for its `persona` label (missing, or naming no applied persona), rows of a spawn whose persona is not up (b.av2 SR-6.4; no `get` is made, so there are no rows to decide), and new rows whose persona has a refused `dm` destination (DMs off or no contact) or no Slack client (logged instead; see [Per-tick flow](#per-tick-flow-sr-2)). The `action` field is one of six stable identifiers; the set is open to extension per SR-V-2.3 — new poller branches may add identifiers without an SRD edit.

| `action` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post_attempted` | New row seen this tick; `chat.postMessage` was issued for this `request_token`. |
| `already_tracked` | Row's composite key already in `livePermissions`; no-op this tick. |
| `reconciled_closed` | Row no longer in the tick's projection; `getPermission` returned a verdict; the closure `chat.update` is sent when the posting persona's client is available, otherwise skipped and logged. The entry is dropped either way. |
| `not_found_generic_deny` | `getPermission` threw `ErrPermissionRequestNotFound`; the generic-deny closure `chat.update` is sent when the posting persona's client is available, otherwise skipped and logged. The entry is dropped either way. |
| `non_conforming_skipped` | The spawn's `permission_requests` was `null`/`undefined`; the row was excluded from the closure sweep this tick. `request_token` is **absent** on this event per SR-V-1.1. |
| `transient_retry` | Transient error on `getPermission`; the entry was left alive for the next tick to retry. |

Fields: `ts`, `event="cscb.poller.row_decision"`, `claude_instance_id`, `action`, and `request_token` (omitted on `non_conforming_skipped`). The envelope `ts` is the only timestamp on the event — there is no per-tick `tick_at` field.

#### `cscb.chat_post.attempted` (SR-V-2.4)

Emitted from `postPermissionPrompt` in `src/permission-poller.ts` for **every** permission-prompt `chat.postMessage` call — success **and** failure — and once for a failed `conversations.open` of a `dm` destination (no post follows it). A refused `dm` destination makes no Slack call and emits nothing. Successes are trail-only; failures land in BOTH the trail (as `ok=false` with a Slack error class string) AND `server.log` via `logViaDeps` (`b.emk` defense-in-depth — the trail is for after-the-fact debugging, `server.log` is for real-time operator visibility). The pre-`b.emk` asymmetry where only failures had a console log is gone — successes are still silent in `server.log`, but failures now appear on both surfaces. For a destination failure (every failed open, and every failed post except a payload error) the `server.log` side is the destination hold's one `persona-destination-failed` line per episode, not a line per attempt (see [Destination hold](#destination-hold-bav2-sr-71-failures)); a failed DM open that returned no conversation ID carries `error` `no_conversation_id`. A payload error (`invalid_blocks`, `msg_too_long`, …) logs `[slack] permission-poller: chat.postMessage failed for <id>[ (reason=<reason>)]: <description>` on each attempt, built with `describeSlackCallFailure` so no raw error object (and no Authorization header) is logged. While the persona is held no attempt is made, so no event is emitted.

Fields:
- `ts`, `event="cscb.chat_post.attempted"`, `claude_instance_id`, `request_token`, `channel` (the conversation posted to: the channel, or the `D…` DM conversation for a `dm` destination; absent on a failed `conversations.open`).
- `text` — the full posted text string, untruncated (SR-V-3.1).
- `blocks` — the full posted Block Kit array, untruncated; both Allow and Deny `action_id`s are present and decodable via `parsePermissionActionId` (SR-V-1.4).
- `ok` — `true` on success, `false` on failure.
- On success: `slack_ts` — the `ts` Slack returned for the posted message (the Slack-side message id, distinct from the envelope `ts`).
- On failure: `error` — the **Slack platform error class string** (e.g. `"channel_not_found"`) from `WebAPIPlatformError.data.error`; falls back to `"network_error"` / `"unknown_error"` for non-platform exceptions. Never the JS `Error.name`.

**Combined example** — a row's first-tick emissions:

```json
{"ts":"2026-06-04T20:39:58.110Z","event":"cscb.poller.row_decision","claude_instance_id":"cscb_ops_bot","action":"post_attempted","request_token":"6f3a1d2c-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd"}
{"ts":"2026-06-04T20:39:58.123Z","event":"cscb.chat_post.attempted","claude_instance_id":"cscb_ops_bot","request_token":"6f3a1d2c-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd","channel":"C0B1ZJJLJ9M","text":"🤖🛠️ permission request: Bash","blocks":[{"type":"section","text":{"type":"mrkdwn","text":"🤖🛠️ *Bash*\n`ls`"}},{"type":"actions","elements":[{"type":"button","text":{"type":"plain_text","text":"Allow"},"style":"primary","action_id":"perm_allow_cscb_ops_bot_6f3a1d2c-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd"},{"type":"button","text":{"type":"plain_text","text":"Deny"},"style":"danger","action_id":"perm_deny_cscb_ops_bot_6f3a1d2c-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd"}]}],"ok":true,"slack_ts":"1780600244.439969"}
```

#### `cscb.chat_update.attempted` (SR-V-2.5)

Emitted for every `chat.update` that closes out a permission prompt. Two surfaces emit: the poller's `renderClosureUpdate` (`src/permission-poller.ts`) and the click handler's verdict-render (`src/permission-click-handler.ts`). Both success and failure emit. Successes are trail-only; failures land in BOTH the trail (as `ok=false` with the Slack platform error class string) AND `server.log` via `logViaDeps`/`logDeps` (`b.emk` defense-in-depth). Successes stay silent in `server.log`, preserving the original SR-V-2.5 asymmetric-behavior fix. The `server.log` lines are `[slack] permission-poller: closure chat.update failed for <id> token=<token> (verdict=<tag>)[ (reason=<reason>)]: <description>` and `[slack] permission-click: decision chat.update failed for <id>[ (reason=<reason>)]: <description>`, both built with `describeSlackCallFailure`.

Fields:
- `ts`, `event="cscb.chat_update.attempted"`, `claude_instance_id`, `request_token`, `channel`, `message_ts` (the prompt `ts` being updated).
- `text` — the new closure text, untruncated.
- `blocks` — the new closure blocks array, untruncated.
- `verdict_tag` — one of the 9 values below.
- `triggered_by` — `"poller"` or `"click_handler"`.
- `ok` — `true` on success, `false` on failure.
- On failure: `error` — Slack platform error class string (e.g. `"message_not_found"`); never JS `Error.name`.

**Verdict tags** — closure rendering identity. The set is open to extension.

| `verdict_tag` | Emitted from | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `operator_allow` | poller | `decision=allow`, `decision_reason=null` — operator allowed via click or TUI. |
| `operator_deny` | poller | `decision=deny`, `decision_reason="operator"`. |
| `timeout` | poller | `decision=deny`, `decision_reason="timeout"`. |
| `find_missing` | poller | `decision=deny`, `decision_reason="find_missing"` — spawn ended before the human responded. |
| `unknown` | poller | Any other `decision`/`decision_reason` pair — fail-closed generic deny per SR-5.2. |
| `not_found` | poller | `getPermission` returned `ErrPermissionRequestNotFound`. |
| `click_handler_allow` | click handler | Allow button click whose `chat.update` rendered the verdict. |
| `click_handler_deny` | click handler | Deny button click whose `chat.update` rendered the verdict. |
| `click_handler_relay_fallen_back` | click handler | b.qi1 — not a verdict. AD refused the click with `ErrRelayFallenBack`; the `chat.update` strips the buttons and redirects the operator to the session's tmux pane. The AD request row stays open, so a later poller closure may still render over the same message. |

**`triggered_by` values** — `"poller"` (SR-2.4 reconciliation) or `"click_handler"` (SR-4.5 verdict render). Open to extension.

**Example** — poller-reconciled `operator_allow` closure:

```json
{"ts":"2026-06-04T20:40:02.456Z","event":"cscb.chat_update.attempted","claude_instance_id":"cscb_ops_bot","request_token":"6f3a1d2c-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd","channel":"C0B1ZJJLJ9M","message_ts":"1780600244.439969","text":"*Permission* — Allowed","blocks":[{"type":"section","text":{"type":"mrkdwn","text":"*Permission* — Allowed"}}],"verdict_tag":"operator_allow","triggered_by":"poller","ok":true}
```

#### `cscb.poller.wedge_detected` (b.fae F4)

Emitted from `postWedgeWarning` in `src/permission-poller.ts` when the wedge detector trips — a spawn seen in `check_permission` with an empty `permission_requests` array for `wedgeTripTicks` consecutive ticks (~90 s). Exactly one **successful** (`ok=true`) event per wedge episode: the `warningFired` latch (set only after a successful post) suppresses further posts until the detector re-arms. A failed post emits an `ok=false` event without latching and the poller retries on a later tick (throttled ~30 s), so an episode with Slack trouble can log several `ok=false` events before the one `ok=true`. Only an attempt that reaches Slack emits the event (a post, or a failed `conversations.open` for a `dm` destination): a refused `dm` destination and an unavailable persona client emit none. The envelope shape mirrors `cscb.chat_post.attempted`: success is trail-only; failure lands in BOTH the trail (`ok=false`) AND `server.log` (`b.emk` convention), where a destination failure appears as the destination hold's one episode line and a payload error as the per-attempt `wedge warning postMessage failed` line. While the persona is held no attempt is made and no event is emitted.

Fields:
- `ts`, `event="cscb.poller.wedge_detected"`, `claude_instance_id`, `channel` (the conversation posted to: the persona's destination channel, or its `D…` DM conversation; absent on a failed `conversations.open`).
- `text` — the full one-shot warning message posted to the destination, prefixed with the persona reference (read-pane + kill/respawn remediation; send-keys explicitly not offered).
- `ok` — `true` on success, `false` on failure.
- On success: `slack_ts` — the Slack `ts` of the posted warning.
- On failure: `error` — the Slack platform error class string.

#### `cscb.block_action.received` (SR-V-2.9)

Emitted once per inbound `block_actions` action by the event router (`src/persona-event-router.ts`) when a persona's connection delivers an `interactive` event, regardless of whether the `action_id` decodes. This is the diagnostically critical surface for **"I clicked Allow and nothing happened"** — decode-failure cases are explicitly in scope. The classification helper lives in `src/permission-click-handler.ts` (`emitBlockActionReceived`) so the server stays a thin wiring layer.

Fields:
- **Always present**: `ts`, `event="cscb.block_action.received"`, `channel`, `message_ts`, `user`, `raw_action_id`.
- **On decode success**: `claude_instance_id`, `request_token`, `decision` (`"allow"` | `"deny"`). `parse_failure_reason` is omitted.
- **On decode failure**: `parse_failure_reason` (table below). Decoded fields are omitted.

**Parse-failure reason set** — open to extension per SR-V-2.9:

| `parse_failure_reason` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `foreign_action_id` | `action_id` does not match the `perm_(allow|deny)_*` prefix — not a CSCB permission button at all. |
| `malformed_token` | `action_id` matches the `perm_(allow|deny)_*` prefix but `parsePermissionActionId` returns `null` (body broken). |

**Not a parse failure: `stale_prompt`.** A click on a closed prompt decodes fine — the `action_id` is still well-formed. Stale clicks surface as `cscb.click_handler.invoked{live_pending: false}` instead.

#### `cscb.click_handler.invoked` (SR-V-2.6)

Emitted from `handlePermissionClick` in `src/permission-click-handler.ts` for every parsed-as-permission click. Emitted exactly once per call, after `parsePermissionActionId` succeeds and before the AD `decide` call. Decode-failure clicks (foreign or malformed action_id) do NOT emit this event — they show up only as `cscb.block_action.received{parse_failure_reason}`.

Fields: `ts`, `event="cscb.click_handler.invoked"`, `claude_instance_id`, `request_token`, `decision`, `channel`, `message_ts`, `user`, `raw_action_id`, `live_pending` (boolean).

`live_pending` is the result of `getLivePermission(claude_instance_id, request_token) !== undefined` at handler entry. `true` means a `LivePermission` entry existed (happy path); `false` means the click decoded fine but the entry had already aged out or been dropped — the operator's "I clicked but the prompt was already closed" diagnostic.

**Example sequence** — happy-path Allow click:

```json
{"ts":"2026-06-04T20:40:01.111Z","event":"cscb.block_action.received","channel":"C0B1ZJJLJ9M","message_ts":"1780600244.439969","user":"U_OPERATOR","raw_action_id":"perm_allow_cscb_ops_bot_6f3a1d2c-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd","claude_instance_id":"cscb_ops_bot","request_token":"6f3a1d2c-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd","decision":"allow"}
{"ts":"2026-06-04T20:40:01.112Z","event":"cscb.click_handler.invoked","claude_instance_id":"cscb_ops_bot","request_token":"6f3a1d2c-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd","channel":"C0B1ZJJLJ9M","message_ts":"1780600244.439969","user":"U_OPERATOR","raw_action_id":"perm_allow_cscb_ops_bot_6f3a1d2c-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd","decision":"allow","live_pending":true}
```

**Note on the `message` / `app_mention` RAW-line truncation (`src/persona-event-router.ts`).** The `[slack] RAW <event> event persona=<key>: …` summaries, cut to 300 characters of the event JSON, are INTENTIONALLY preserved per SR-V-3.2 — they are a separate human-readable log. The canonical store is full-fidelity by construction (no `.slice` in the trail emit path).

#### `cscb.ad_decide.attempted` (SR-V-2.7 call-side)

Emitted from `handlePermissionClick` (`src/permission-click-handler.ts`) once per `decideWithToken` invocation, on success and on every error path. This is the CSCB-side half of SR-V-2.7; AD's complementary SR-A-2.4 emission lives in `t1.n4v.14`. The two halves join on `request_token` for after-the-fact debugging.

Fields:
- `ts`, `event="cscb.ad_decide.attempted"`, `claude_instance_id`, `request_token`, `decision` (submitted — `"allow"` | `"deny"`).
- `result_class` — one of the 6 values below.
- On `result_class="other"`, and on the agent-director/tmux carve-out (`ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`): additionally `raw_error_message`, the original error's `.message` after `redactSlackLogText` (URL-like and token-like text replaced), otherwise untruncated. For the other named classes, `raw_error_message` is OMITTED.
- `submitted_decision_reason` — currently never sent on the wire from CSCB. Documented for future use per SR-V-2.7's "when present" rule.

**Response-class set** — match the AD error identifiers in `src/agent-director-errors.ts` so the trail's classification stays consistent with the rest of the codebase. Open to extension.

| `result_class` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ok` | `decideWithToken` returned without throwing. |
| `ErrAlreadyDecided` | The request was already closed (race with poller reconciliation or peer click). |
| `ErrInvalidFlags` | AD rejected the call shape — typically a missing required field. Should not happen under contract. The event is emitted before the handler's log line, and the handler then starts its immediate version re-check without awaiting it (see [Click handler (SR-4)](#click-handler-sr-4)). |
| `ErrAmbiguousRequest` | AD couldn't uniquely identify the request — defense-in-depth backstop per SR-4.4. |
| `ErrRelayFallenBack` | b.qi1 — the request's relay window elapsed, so Claude re-asked at its own tmux pane and AD will not record the verdict. The click did not land; the session is unaffected. |
| `other` | Any other thrown value (non-AD error, transport, etc.). `raw_error_message` carries the original `.message`, redacted. |

**Example** — happy-path `ad_decide.attempted` after a click:

```json
{"ts":"2026-06-04T20:40:01.130Z","event":"cscb.ad_decide.attempted","claude_instance_id":"cscb_ops_bot","request_token":"6f3a1d2c-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd","decision":"allow","result_class":"ok"}
```

**Operational logging.** The existing `[slack] permission-click: ErrInvalidFlags from decide for ...` / `ErrAmbiguousRequest` / `decide failed for ...` `console.error` lines stay alongside the trail event. They serve a different purpose — live stderr monitoring — and are intentionally not redundant with the canonical after-the-fact debugging surface.

#### Trail file location and query recipes — SR-V-5 / SR-V-6

The file is the surface; `tail`, `grep`, and `jq` are the readers. No running CSCB process is required and nothing is perturbed (SR-V-6.2).

**Path:** `~/.claude/channels/slack/permission-trail.jsonl`
**Directory override:** `SLACK_STATE_DIR` (sets the directory; file name is always `permission-trail.jsonl`)

**Single-side recipes:**

```sh
# Live stream
tail -f ~/.claude/channels/slack/permission-trail.jsonl

# SR-V-5.1: every event for one interaction
jq -c 'select(.request_token=="X")' ~/.claude/channels/slack/permission-trail.jsonl

# SR-V-5.2: events on a channel within a time window
jq -c 'select(.channel=="C..." and .ts >= "T1" and .ts <= "T2")' \
  ~/.claude/channels/slack/permission-trail.jsonl
```

**Cross-side join** (AD trail + CSCB trail, ordered by `ts`, filtered to one interaction):

```sh
cat ~/.agent-director/ad-trail.jsonl ~/.claude/channels/slack/permission-trail.jsonl \
  | jq -sc 'sort_by(.ts) | map(select(.request_token=="X"))[]'
```

**Join keys** for stitching the CSCB trail against the AD trail (SR-V-4):

| Key | Emitted by (CSCB surface) | When |
|---|---|---|
| `request_token` | every CSCB event after AD mints one | primary join key (SR-V-1.1) |
| `claude_instance_id` | every CSCB event when known | join when no token yet (SR-V-1.2) |
| `channel` + `message_ts` | every Slack-touching event (`chat_post.attempted`, `chat_update.attempted`, `block_action.received`, `click_handler.invoked`) | Slack pivot (SR-V-1.3) |

The AD trail (file owned by agent-director — see `t1.n4v.14`) emits the complementary side; the operator joins by `request_token` and orders by `ts`.

**SRD §10 question → answering event class** — CSCB side (questions 2–5; question 1 is AD's):

| SRD §10 question | Answered by |
|---|---|
| Q2: Did CSCB issue a `chat.postMessage` carrying the expected Block Kit blocks? | `cscb.chat_post.attempted` — `text` and `blocks` fields. |
| Q3: What `ts` did Slack return? | `cscb.chat_post.attempted` — `slack_ts` field. |
| Q4: Was a `block_actions` click received against that `ts`? | `cscb.block_action.received` — `message_ts` field equals the post's `slack_ts`. |
| Q5: Did the closure render on the original `ts`? | `cscb.chat_update.attempted` — `message_ts` field equals the post's `slack_ts`. |

### Removed pre-Epic-2 files

The previous tmux-direct architecture wrote `~/.claude/channels/slack/sessions.json` to persist tmux session names and discovered Claude session UUIDs. Both responsibilities have moved to agent-director — `sessions.json` and `sessions.json.last` no longer exist. Operators upgrading from a pre-Epic-2 install can safely delete the stale files; CSCB will not read them.

### server.pid (STATE_DIR/server.pid)

Written at startup with the server's process ID. Used by the CLI `stop` command to send SIGTERM (with SIGKILL escalation after `stop_timeout`) to a running server, and by startup to detect a conflicting already-running instance. Removed on graceful shutdown.

### reply-guard/<key> (STATE_DIR/reply-guard/<key>)

One file per persona, named by its key, in the record directory `reply-guard/` under the state directory (honours `SLACK_STATE_DIR`; `src/reply-guard-record.ts`). It holds the exact text `true` or `false`: the persona's effective `stop_hook_bootstrap`.

- **Written** atomically (`.tmp` + rename) by `preLaunchReplyGuard` immediately before each spawn or resume of that persona (Server-Managed Startup step 5), never on a reconnect and never for another persona's launch. The directory is created on first write.
- **Read** by `stop-hooks/slack-reply-guard.sh`, which takes the record directory as its first argument (from the managed hook's command) and reads `<dir>/<CSCB_PERSONA>`. It reminds only when the record reads `true` (one trailing newline tolerated). The start and launch passes of step 4a-ter also read it: a record reading `true` keeps the managed hook in the persona's directories.
- **Fail-open.** A missing argument, an unset, empty or non-key `CSCB_PERSONA`, or a missing, unreadable or other-valued record means no reminder.
- **Deleted** by `teardownPersonaReplyGuard(stateDir, key)` (a missing record is success), which also forgets the persona's launched-with dir. The persona teardown calls it for a removed persona (see Session Lifecycle, [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65)). A failed write at launch also deletes any stale record.

### Environment Variables

The server (`server.ts`) requires no environment variable and reads no Slack token from the environment: each persona's `bot_token` and `app_token` come only from its credentials file (`credentials_file`, see Persona config), and nothing supplies the bind address or port except the applied configuration (the last-applied record, else `config.json`). The CLI reads no token either: `start` checks only that `config.json` or its last-applied record exists (see [start command](#start-command)). `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` and `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` are read by nothing; setting them has no effect.

Optional:

- `SLACK_STATE_DIR` — the state directory (made absolute; default `~/.claude/channels/slack`). `config.json` and its reload files, the inbox, `server.pid`, the reply-guard records (`reply-guard/`), the logs and the permission trail live under it. `resolveServerStateDir` reads it at call time; `server.ts` computes its paths once at import.
- `SLACK_DRY_RUN` — set to `1`, `true`, or `yes` to enable dry-run mode (`isDryRun()` in `tokens.ts`). No credentials file is read and no Slack call is made: each persona's bring-up runs only the working-directory check, then the connection manager marks it up with a distinct placeholder identity derived from its key (`U000DRY_<key>` / `B000DRY_<key>`), and builds no Slack client. Spawns, the start sweep and the permission poller are skipped. The reload detection tick still runs over `config.json` alone: it reads no credentials file, credentials never count as changed, and the fingerprint covers the configuration file only. All MCP tool calls (`reply`, `react`, `edit_message`, `fetch_messages`, `download_attachment`) are stubbed — each returns a `[dry-run]` placeholder and logs the call to the server log — and persona notices are logged, not posted. The HTTP/MCP server still starts normally so Claude Code sessions can connect and exercise tool calls without a Slack workspace.
- `CSCB_LOG_MAX_BYTES`, `CSCB_LOG_KEEP`, `CSCB_AD_VERBOSE`, `CSCB_HTTP_VERBOSE` — log rotation and verbosity; see [Logging](#logging).
- `CSCB_SLACK_API_URL` — the Slack API base URL override, for the docker integration suite only (Test 10 points a live start at the loopback Slack stub, `tests/integration/fixtures/slack-stub-server.ts`). Never set it on an operator's host; no shipped doc describes it. `main()` in `server.ts` reads it once per start, through `resolveSlackApiUrlOverride(process.env, log)` in `persona-slack-clients.ts`, and passes the result to the connection manager as `slackApiUrl`. It is honoured only for an `http:` URL whose host is one of the literal loopback addresses, `http://127.0.0.1…` or `http://[::1]…` (any port and path, and forms the URL parser normalises to them, such as `127.1` or the long form of `::1`), with no user info, query or fragment. `localhost` is not accepted: it would be the one host resolved by name. When honoured, one `[slack] Slack API base URL override in use: <origin> (CSCB_SLACK_API_URL)` line is logged, naming only the URL's origin (never its path), and all three client call sites in `persona-connections.ts` build their clients with the full normalised URL as `slackApiUrl`: the validation client for `auth.test`, the long-lived Web API client, and the Socket Mode client's `clientOptions`, so `apps.connections.open` goes there and the WebSocket URL it returns is used as given. Any other value is ignored with one `[slack] Warning: CSCB_SLACK_API_URL ignored: …` line that names the accepted forms (`http://127.0.0.1` or `http://[::1]`) and never echoes the value, and the start goes on against the default Slack API. Unset or empty, nothing is logged and every client's options are exactly the SR-3.3 sets. When it is honoured, the persona tokens go only to whatever listens on that loopback port, which is trusted with them.

Optional CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (set at spawn time via SpawnParams.extra_env when configured per persona or top-level) is propagated by agent-director to the spawn's tmux session, enabling per-persona Claude account selection.

CSCB_PERSONA and CLAUDE_MANAGED_CHANNEL are set at spawn time via SpawnParams.extra_env for every managed session, both to the persona key, and are propagated by agent-director to the spawn's tmux session. An instance uses its `CSCB_PERSONA` key to target itself in crontable lines and in `/interject` requests, and the Slack Reply Guard reads it to find the instance's own `reply-guard/<key>` record.

CSCB_CRONTABLE_PATH is set at spawn time via SpawnParams.extra_env for every managed session — unconditionally, for every persona — and is propagated by agent-director to the spawn's tmux session. It carries the resolved tilde-expanded `cron_table_path` (the default `<config dir>/crontab` or the configured override) so bots can self-schedule by locating and appending to the crontable, the single source of truth for scheduled prompts (bots are first-class writers alongside the server).

CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION is set to `false` at spawn time via SpawnParams.extra_env for every managed session (`PROMPT_SUGGESTION_OFF_ENV` in `persona-identity.ts`, spread last so no other entry replaces it; a resume restores it from the row's stored env). Claude Code reads it before its server-side flag and the `promptSuggestionEnabled` setting, so no suggested prompt shows in the session and the end-of-turn suggestion fork never starts. That fork runs the session's PreToolUse hooks and is denied, so agent-director flipped idle personas from `waiting` to `working` (b.svb); the stale-`working` recovery (b.f2b) still covers such rows.

## Logging

### Why console.error/console.log are overridden directly

Bun bypasses `process.stderr.write` overrides — the runtime writes directly to the file descriptor, so patching `process.stderr.write` has no effect. `src/logging.ts` works around this by replacing `console.error` and `console.log` themselves before any logging occurs.

### initLogging()

`initLogging(logFilePath)` in `src/logging.ts` opens the target file in append mode and replaces both `console.error` and `console.log` with wrapper functions that:

1. Format all arguments to a single string (JSON-serializing objects)
2. Prepend an ISO-8601 timestamp: `[2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z] message`
3. Roll the file if it has grown past the threshold (see **Rotation** below)
4. Write the line synchronously via `writeSync` to the open file descriptor
5. Fall back to the original `console.error`/`console.log` if the write fails

The originals are captured at module load time so the fallback always refers to Bun's native output.

### Rotation (b.brv)

Rotation is built into `src/logging.ts` so it applies on every machine that runs CSCB — no per-host logrotate config. `maybeRotate()` runs before each write: it `fstat`s the active fd and, when the size crosses the threshold, closes the fd, shifts `<path>.N-1 → <path>.N` down to `<path>.1`, renames the active file to `<path>.1`, discards the oldest generation beyond `CSCB_LOG_KEEP`, and reopens a fresh active file. It is best-effort — any filesystem error is swallowed rather than thrown into the caller's hot path, and a failed reopen after rotation is recovered on a subsequent write rather than disabling file logging.

| Env var | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `CSCB_LOG_MAX_BYTES` | 10 MiB (`10485760`) | Rotate when the active file reaches N bytes. Values `<= 0` or non-numeric ignored. |
| `CSCB_LOG_KEEP` | 5 | Rotated generations retained. `0` = keep none (the active file is `rm`ed on rotation, i.e. truncate). Values `< 0` or non-numeric ignored. |

Rotated generations are **not** compressed. Applies to both `server.log` and `clean_restart.log` (any file passed to `initLogging`). This is distinct from `startup-errors.log`, whose rotation remains operator-owned via `docs/logrotate-startup-errors.conf`.

### agent-director logger filter (b.brv)

The agent-director `Client` is constructed with a `logger` in `src/agent-director-startup.ts`, and since `initLogging()` patches `console`, everything the Client logs lands in `server.log`. At info level the Client emits a per-poll `SubprocessClient: <verb> ok { … }` success dump for every `list`/`status`/`get`/`decide` call — with CSCB polling continuously, these dumps historically dominated the log (2 GB / 137 MB observed in b.brv). `makeFilteredAdLogger(console)` in `src/agent-director-logger.ts` wraps the console: it drops those routine `SubprocessClient: <verb> ok` records at `log`/`info` level while passing `warn`/`error` through unfiltered. Setting `CSCB_AD_VERBOSE` to a truthy value (`1`/`true`/`yes`/`on`) returns the base logger unwrapped, restoring the full chatter for debugging.

### Slack library output (b.av2 SR-10.3)

Because `console` is patched, anything a Slack library logs lands in `server.log`. The persona clients' library loggers are built in `src/persona-slack-clients.ts` (see Security Model, Slack library logging):

- **Socket Mode** (`socketModeSlackLogger`): only the library's fixed-text connection-health lines get through, each written through the connection manager's log as `[slack] persona Socket Mode: personas[<i>] "<name>" (key=<key>): <text>`. The text is `A ping wasn't received from the server before the timeout of <n>ms!` or `A pong wasn't received from the server before the timeout of <n>ms!` (both warnings), or `Failed to send ping to Slack` (the library's error detail is dropped). After any of the three the library closes the connection and CSCB logs `persona-connection-lost`. Every other line is dropped, including the handshake error that carries the WebSocket URL and its ticket; the server logs its own connection lines instead.
- **Web API** (validation and long-lived, `redactingSlackLogger`): the library's lines are written as its console logger would (`[WARN]  web-api:WebClient …`, default INFO) with URL-like text replaced by `<redacted-url>` and token-like text by `<redacted-token>`. Default-level lines are Slack's response warnings, rate-limit waits and a failed request's message, which on a 429 names the request URL (for `filesUploadV2`, the short-lived upload URL).

### HTTP request access line (b.3k6)

The `/mcp` endpoint's `fetch` handler in `src/server.ts` is hit on every MCP round-trip — client polls, notifications, tool-call responses, and each SSE stream open — so its one-line-per-request access log (`[slack] HTTP <method> <path> session=…`) is the highest-frequency routine success line left in `server.log` after b.brv silenced the `SubprocessClient` dumps. It shares their signal/noise profile: routine and continuous at steady state, useful only when debugging a specific transport/session-routing problem. It is gated behind `isHttpVerbose()`, which reads `CSCB_HTTP_VERBOSE` (truthy: `1`/`true`/`yes`/`on`, case-insensitive) — off by default. Unlike `CSCB_AD_VERBOSE`, the env var is checked per request rather than once at startup, so toggling it takes effect without a restart. Real events (session connect/disconnect, no matching persona, errors) are logged unconditionally elsewhere and are unaffected by this flag.

### Persona bring-up lines (b.av2 SR-10.3)

A persona's bring-up and its retries log to `server.log` only, with the `[slack]` prefix; none goes to `startup-errors.log` or to Slack. Diagnostic lines use `formatPersonaDiagnostic` (`persona-diagnostics.ts`): `[slack] <class>: personas[<i>] "<name>" (key=<key>)`, then ` path="<path>"` when the class has one, then `: <cause>`. The full class list is in the `persona-diagnostics.ts` entry of the Module Map. No line carries a token. The operator-facing catalogue of these classes, with each one's cause and fix, is the shipped debugging skill `skills/debug-slack-channel-bots/SKILL.md`.

| Line | When | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `persona-start: … : bring-up starting` | Once per applied persona as its bring-up starts, before any of its outcome lines | entry, name, key |
| `persona-credentials-missing` / `-unreadable` / `-invalid` | Once, when step 1 fails | entry, name, key, credentials-file path, cause |
| `persona-directory-missing` / `-unusable` | Once, when step 2 fails and its retry starts; later failed re-checks log nothing, even if the class changes | entry, name, key, working directory, cause |
| Same directory class, cause `cleared: working directory is usable again; continuing the bring-up` | Once, when a re-check finds the directory usable; with a credentials cause still open the cause ends `the persona stays broken until its credentials file is fixed and the change confirmed` instead | entry, name, key, working directory |
| `persona-slack-unreachable` / `persona-credentials-refused` | Logged by the connection manager once when the cause starts and once when it clears (cause `cleared: …`), not on every attempt | entry, name, key, credentials-file path, cause; a `persona-slack-unreachable` start line then the thrown value's message, when it had one, as `message="…"` (`describeLogMessage`: redacted, one line, capped at 300 characters; none for the 10 s timeout markers) |
| `persona-credentials-refused` with cause `bot_token refused by a Web API call (<method>): Slack error <code>` (bug b.ujn) | Once, when a Web API call of a running persona is rejected with `invalid_auth`, `token_revoked`, `account_inactive` or `not_authed` and the manager marks it credentials-broken; later calls on that client are refused locally and log nothing. A pending credentials reconnect that swaps in logs the cleared line `cleared: bot_token no longer refused by a Web API call (was Slack error <code>)`; the usual recovery (apply step 6) stops the connection first and so starts a fresh tracker with no cleared line, logging `broken by its credentials and its credentials file changed — bringing it up again` and the new bring-up's lines instead | entry, name, key, credentials-file path, cause |
| `persona-config-dir-unresolvable: … path="<dir>": claude_config_dir cannot be resolved to a real path (<code>[: a symlink on its path points to nothing]); its Slack connection is closed and its launch waits until it resolves` (bug b.g57) | Once, when the controller's check right before step 3, or a launch, finds the persona's effective `claude_config_dir` unresolvable and the hold starts; later failed re-checks log nothing. `<dir>` is the configured directory, tilde-expanded and absolute (`<home>/.claude` when none is configured); `<code>` is the errno code (`unknown` when there is none) | entry, name, key, config directory, errno code |
| Same class, cause `cleared: claude_config_dir resolves to a real path again; continuing the bring-up` (or `…; the persona stays broken until its credentials file is fixed and the change confirmed` for a persona Slack had refused when the hold started) | Once, when a re-check finds the directory resolvable; Slack validation and connection with the held credentials follow | entry, name, key, config directory |
| `persona-connection-lost` / `persona-slack-unreachable` / `persona-credentials-refused`, cause `cleared: the persona's Slack connection was closed while its claude_config_dir cannot be resolved` | Once, when a later launch's hold closes the connection of a persona whose Slack episode of that class is still open (a lost connection still reopening, a Slack retry, a refusal); logged by the manager's `stop` with an end reason, right after the hold's `persona-config-dir-unresolvable` line. The recovery connects on a fresh episode, with no restored line. A teardown or shutdown close logs nothing (b.av2 SR-6.5) | entry, name, key, credentials-file path |
| `[slack] persona "<name>" (key=<key>): up after its claude_config_dir resolved — launching` | After the cleared line, once the persona's Slack step reports `up` | name, key |
| `[slack] persona "<name>" (key=<key>): no longer applied — its claude_config_dir retry stops` | A re-check came due for a persona no longer applied | name, key |
| `[slack] persona "<name>" (key=<key>): claude_config_dir retry failed: <error>` | A re-check attempt threw | name, key, error |
| `[slack] persona "<name>" (key=<key>): closing its Slack connection for its claude_config_dir failed: <error>` | The manager's `stop` threw or rejected when a later hold closed the persona's connection | name, key, error |
| `[slack] persona "<name>" (key=<key>): up after its bring-up retry (directory\|Slack) — launching` | Once, when a retry brings the persona up and the controller launches it | name, key, which retry |
| `[slack] persona "<name>" (key=<key>): launch after its bring-up retry failed: <error>` | That launch threw | name, key, error |
| `persona-credentials-change-failed: … path="<path>": the confirmed credentials change cannot be used: <cause>; the current connection stays in use, and the change stays pending` | Once per failed confirmed credentials change (apply step 4), or when a reconnect left retrying is refused later while the persona is still up. `<cause>` is the credentials check's cause (missing, unreadable, invalid, or the real-path collision naming the other persona) or Slack's refusal (`<key> refused by <check>: Slack error <code>`). For a retrying persona the line ends `it keeps retrying with its current credentials, and the change stays pending`; for an up persona whose own connection was refused while the attempt ran (credentials-broken by then) it ends `it stays broken by its credentials, and the change stays pending`. Logged by the bring-up controller through `formatCredentialsChangeFailed` | entry, name, key, credentials-file path, cause |
| `persona-slack-unreachable` with cause `cleared: the new connection of its confirmed credentials change is no longer retried: a later confirmed credentials change replaced it` (or `…: the persona's connection was stopped`) | Once, when a credentials reconnect left retrying is cancelled, by a later confirmed change or by the persona's connection being stopped, while its unreachable episode is open; so the reconnect's unreachable start line always gets an end | entry, name, key, credentials-file path, cause |
