| `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> set observer failed: <error>`, `… end observer failed: <error>`, `… retry timer stop failed: <error>`, `… alert failed: <error>`, `… ending its hold episode failed: <error>`, `… its retry failed: <error>`, and `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: ending the holds on a version change failed: <error>` | A failing observer or reaction step; the other steps still run |

Thrown values are described by `describeThrownValue`.

### agent-director settings lines (b.jg5 SRJ-209)

The settings reader (`src/ad-settings.ts`) logs through `console.error` (so `server.log`); every line starts with `AD_SETTINGS_LOG_PREFIX`, `[slack] agent-director settings:`. The startup call-timeout check (b.jg5 SRJ-213) writes the last two lines through the log its caller passes, `console.error` in `server.ts`'s start step. An accepted read logs nothing.

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[slack] agent-director settings: the read of "<path>" was refused: <reason>; <kept> stay in effect until a read is accepted (b.jg5 SRJ-209)` | The first refused read after start or after an accepted read (`buildAdSettingsRefusedReadLine`); the rest of that run logs nothing, and the next accepted read ends the run. `<path>` is the file's full path under the server's HOME. `<kept>` is `the defaults` when no read has been accepted since start, else `the values of the last accepted read`. `<reason>` is the first broken rule, e.g. `[tmux] stopping_window_seconds is 10, below its minimum of 30`, `[tmux] query_timeout_ms is not an integer (it is a string)`, `[tmux] action_timeout_ms is too large for agent-director`, `it is not valid TOML (at line <L>, column <C>)`, `it is not valid UTF-8`, `it cannot be read (EISDIR)` or `the home directory cannot be found` (then `<path>` is `~/.agent-director/config.toml`). Never in `startup-errors.log`, never posted to Slack |
| `[slack] agent-director settings: already installed — ignoring the second install` | A programming error: `installAdSettings` called twice |
| `[slack] agent-director settings: agent_director_call_timeout_ms is <value>, at or below its need of <need> ms (the <verb> ceiling plus the 15000 ms margin): a call can time out while its verb still acts; see the README's switch-over runbook, section "Switching over to agent-director Phase 1" (b.jg5 SRJ-213)` | The startup check (`buildAdCallTimeoutWarningLine`, once per start, step 2c) when the setting is at or below the need. `<need>` is exact, in ms; `<verb>` names the row whose ceiling sets it: the `AD_CEILING_VERBS` id, or `resume/spawn-with-reuse/plain-spawn` (`AD_LAUNCH_CEILING_VERBS`) for the launch row those three share, whose `setBy` is `resume` (a tie names the earlier verb); the section title is `PHASE1_RUNBOOK_SECTION_TITLE`. Never in `startup-errors.log`, never posted to Slack; the start continues |
| `[slack] agent-director settings: agent_director_call_timeout_ms is <value>; its need is unknown: [pause] timeout_seconds holds <found>, a value that is not used, so pause's wait is not counted and the need without it is <need> ms; see the README's switch-over runbook, section "Switching over to agent-director Phase 1" (b.jg5 SRJ-213)` | The same check, in place of the line above and whatever the setting, when `[pause] timeout_seconds` is not used. `<found>` is `AdPauseTimeout`'s token-free `found`; `<need>` counts `pause` without its wait |

### Retired-key record lines (b.jg5 SRJ-1013, SRJ-1014)

The start read's refusal is written by `recordStartupError`; the store (`src/retired-keys.ts`) logs one line per change of the record and one per failed write through its `log` (`console.error` from `main()`, so `server.log`), each starting `RETIRED_KEYS_LOG_PREFIX`, `[slack] retired-keys:`. Loading the store logs nothing, and a primitive that writes nothing logs nothing. A running server's store calls are a confirmed apply's step 1 `record` and, after a failed write, its `restore` (b.jg5 SRJ-803, SRJ-804), the start sweep's one `absent-at-start` `record` (b.jg5 SRJ-714), and the session manager's shared own-row reads' `clear`, the start sweep's list rows included (b.jg5 SRJ-807), and the session manager's `mark` when a reuse spawn for a recorded key succeeds and at a later launch decision (b.jg5 SRJ-806), so it logs every line below. No line carries file content, parser text or a token. `<path>` is the file's JSON-quoted path; a key is shown as `persona=<key>`, bare when it is a persona key and JSON-quoted otherwise.

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[<timestamp>] [retired-keys-unreadable] The retired-key record "<path>" <problem>, so the server does not start: it never guesses which persona keys are retired. Moving the file aside (for example, renaming it) lets the server start, at the cost that the keys it held are no longer retired, so a persona whose key it held may resume the conversation of the life that was retired.` | The start read refused the record; also in `startup-errors.log`. `<problem>` is `cannot be read (<code>)` (an errno such as `EISDIR`, or `not a regular file`), `is not valid UTF-8`, `is not valid JSON at line <L>, column <C>`, or `is invalid: …` naming the first rule broken (an entry by its position in `keys`) |
| `[slack] retired-keys: recorded <key list> in <path>[; it carries the changes held only in memory for <keys>] (b.jg5 SRJ-803)` | `record` wrote a batch. Each key is `persona=<key> (cause=<cause>)`, with `, its "new life has begun" mark cleared` for a marked key re-recorded, or `(cause=<cause>, held only in memory)` for a held key it wrote |
| `[slack] retired-keys: persona=<key> marked: its new life has begun, in <path>[; it carries …] (b.jg5 SRJ-806)` | `mark` wrote the mark |
| `[slack] retired-keys: persona=<key> entry cleared from <path>[ on <read>][; it carries …] (b.jg5 SRJ-807)` | `clear` removed an entry. From a row read, `<read>` is `its row read <state> with its mark set (<site>: <what>)`, the state read and the read's site (`persona teardown kill: status read between tries` for the teardown kill's read between its tries, `reconcileOrphans: status read between kill tries` for a start-sweep kill's) |
| `[slack] retired-keys: restored the record held before the apply in <path> (b.jg5 SRJ-804)`; for an empty snapshot `… restored the record held before the apply: it was empty, so <path> was removed (b.jg5 SRJ-804)`, `…, but its directory could not be synced (<errno>), so it may reappear after a crash (b.jg5 SRJ-804)`, or `… it was empty, and removing <path> failed (<errno>), so an empty record was written (b.jg5 SRJ-804)` | `restore` succeeded |
| `[slack] retired-keys: cannot record <key list> in <path><detail>; the record in memory is unchanged (b.jg5 SRJ-803)`, or, when the batch held `absent-at-start` keys, `…; this server holds <keys> as retired in memory for its life, and the next write of the record that succeeds carries them (b.jg5 SRJ-803, SRJ-714)` | A failed `record` |
| `[slack] retired-keys: cannot mark persona=<key> in <path><detail>; this server holds its mark in memory, and its next launch decision writes it again (b.jg5 SRJ-806)` | A failed `mark`; the mark stays set in memory |
| `[slack] retired-keys: cannot clear persona=<key> from <path>[ on <read>]<detail>; the entry stays, and the next qualifying read clears it again (b.jg5 SRJ-807)` | A failed `clear`; the entry stays, in memory and in the file, and the read's answer is unchanged |
| `[slack] retired-keys: the mark query for persona=<key> failed: <failure>; nothing is cleared (b.jg5 SRJ-807)` | Logged by the session manager, not the store: the installed store's `isMarked` threw at an own-row read, which counts the key as unmarked and goes on |
| `[slack] retired-keys: cannot restore the record held before the apply in <path><detail>; the keys it could not remove stay retired (b.jg5 SRJ-804)`, or for an empty snapshot `… cannot restore the record held before the apply: removing <path> failed (<errno>), and writing an empty record failed<detail>; the keys it holds stay retired (b.jg5 SRJ-804)` | A failed `restore`; the record in memory is left as it is |

`<detail>` is ` (<errno>); the file is unchanged` for a write that failed before its rename, or `: the new record was written but its directory could not be synced (<errno>); ` followed by `the previous record was written back`, `the file, absent before, was removed again` (either with `, though its directory could not be synced either`), or `putting the previous state back failed too (<errno>), so the file holds the new record`. An errno is shown only when it is a safe errno code.

### Retired-key launch lines (b.jg5 SRJ-805, SRJ-806)

Logged by the session manager (`src/session-manager.ts`) and the reconnect adapter (`src/server.ts`) when a launch path meets a key the retired-key record holds ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-srj-806)). `<mark words>` is `its new life has begun` or `no new life has begun yet, so any row it has is the old life`.

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[slack] spawnForPersona: <ref>'s key is retired (<mark words>) — its first launch is a reuse spawn of the same id, never a plain spawn or a resume (b.jg5 SRJ-805)` | A recorded key's first launch, before its reuse spawn |
| `[slack] spawnForPersona: the retired key's reuse spawn of <ref> collided — fetching current state; this is the one get-then-act a reuse collision gives (b.jg5 SRJ-805, SRJ-112)` | That reuse met a live row; the reply-guard steps are undone and the collision `get` follows, as the attempt's one re-run of get-then-act: a second reuse collision there arms `reuse-collision` and answers the uncounted refused result |
| `[slack] spawnForPersona: <ref>'s key is retired (<mark words>; last read <state>) — not resuming: a reuse spawn of the same id first; nothing is deleted (b.jg5 SRJ-805)` | `resumeOrFreshSpawn` for a recorded key, in place of a `resume` |
| `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: <ref>'s key is retired and its new life has begun — answering fresh-retired; <mark> (b.jg5 SRJ-806, SRJ-112)` | A reuse spawn succeeded for a recorded key. `<mark>` is `its mark is set in the retired-key record`, `its mark was already set, so nothing is written`, or `writing its mark failed, so this server holds the mark in memory and writes it again at the key's next launch decision`. Only for a key recorded when the launch attempt started and at success with its record generation unchanged |
| `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: <ref>'s key was recorded as retired while this reuse spawn's launch attempt was in flight (<how>) — the launch was decided before that recording, so its life is the old life: no mark is set; answering spawned (b.jg5 SRJ-806, SRJ-805)` | A reuse spawn succeeded for a key recorded during its launch attempt. `<how>` is `it was not recorded when the launch attempt started`, `recorded again while the launch attempt was in flight`, or `its record generation could not be read, so a recording during the launch attempt cannot be ruled out`; no mark is set and the answer is `spawned` |
| `[slack] spawnForPersona: <ref>'s key is retired, so its reuse spawn answered fresh-retired — answering it, not an amnesia result; the lost-transcript diagnosis's persona notice is not posted (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-806)` | The no-transcript step after `ErrJsonlMissing`: the diagnosis held a persona notice, and the reuse answered `fresh-retired`; no amnesia result and no notice |
| `[slack] live-row-sequence: <ref>: its key is retired, so the sequence carries the retired-key flag and ends in a reuse spawn, never a resume (b.jg5 SRJ-805, SRJ-705)` | The start entry set the retired-key flag the starter had not set |
| `[slack] reconnectSession: persona=<key> is <state> and its key is retired with no new life begun — not typing /mcp reconnect into its old life; the live-row sequence replaces it (start answered <answer>); deferring (b.jg5 SRJ-805)` | The reconnect adapter met a retired key's old life; it answers `'transient'` |
| `[slack] retired-keys: the recorded query for persona=<key> failed: <failure>; taken as not recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-805)` | The installed store's `isRecorded` threw at a launch decision; the key launches as one not retired |
| `[slack] retired-keys: the mark query for persona=<key> failed: <failure>; taken as not marked, so its row is the old life (b.jg5 SRJ-805, SRJ-806)` | The store's `isMarked` threw at a launch decision |
| `[slack] retired-keys: writing the held mark of persona=<key> again failed: <failure>; this server still reads it as marked (b.jg5 SRJ-806)` | The store's `mark` threw at a later launch decision |
| `[slack] retired-keys: the record-generation query for persona=<key> failed: <failure>; a recording during the launch attempt cannot be ruled out, so no mark is set (b.jg5 SRJ-806)` | The store's `recordGeneration` threw when a launch attempt started or at a reuse spawn's success; the reuse sets no mark and answers `spawned`, with the in-flight line |

The replace step's line for a retired key carries ` (its key is retired)` (Server-Managed Startup step 5). The store's own mark and clear lines are in [Retired-key record lines](#retired-key-record-lines-bjg5-srj-1013-srj-1014).

### Start sweep list lines (b.jg5 SRJ-116, SRJ-714)

Logged by the session manager's start sweep (`reconcileOrphans`, Server-Managed Startup step 4) between its `list` and its first kill. `<ref>` is `"<name>" (key=<key>)` for a configured persona and `persona=<key>` otherwise; `<keys>` are JSON-quoted and comma-separated.

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: start sweep list for <ref>: its row reads pending with no launch start (state=pending) — <outcome>; nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-114, SRJ-513)` | A configured persona's own listed row latched it with `launch-start-not-recorded`; `<outcome>` is `the persona latched`, `the persona relatched`, `the persona was already latched with this case`, `no latch is installed, so nothing is latched` or `latching the persona failed: <error>`, as at the shared `get` read |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: start sweep list for <ref>: its row carries the liveness note provenance_conflict (state=<state>) — <outcome>; nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-114, SRJ-501)` | A configured persona's own listed row latched it with `conflicting-labels` |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: <ref> latched from its own listed row instanceId=<id> (case=<case>) — its own row and every row labelled with it are left unkilled (b.jg5 SRJ-116, SRJ-502, SRJ-714)` | Once per persona the latch pass latched, after the line above |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: <ref> is latched (case=<case>) — its own row and every row labelled with it are left unkilled (b.jg5 SRJ-502, SRJ-714)` | A configured persona already latched when the sweep ran |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: no retired-key store is installed, so the keys of absent personas' rows are not recorded as retired: <keys> (b.jg5 SRJ-714, SRJ-803)` | Absent personas' keys with no store installed; 0 recorded |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: recording the keys of absent personas' rows as retired failed: <error>; nothing is recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-714, SRJ-803)` | The store's `record` threw; 0 recorded, and the sweep goes on |

The list rows' other own-row lines (a non-latching note, a note not applied, a clear) are the shared read's, headed `[slack] reconcileOrphans: start sweep list for <ref>` ([Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)); the recording's write and its failure are the store's lines ([Retired-key record lines](#retired-key-record-lines-bjg5-srj-1013-srj-1014)), the clear's `<read>` naming `reconcileOrphans: start sweep list`.

### Start sweep kill lines (b.jg5 SRJ-714, SRJ-702, SRJ-205)

Logged by the start sweep (`reconcileOrphans`, Server-Managed Startup step 4) from its kills to its end. `<row>` is `orphan instanceId=<id> persona=<persona>` for a swept row (`<persona>` as in the sweeping line) and `pre-persona row instanceId=<id>` for a row with no `persona` label; `<outcome>` is `describeKillOutcome`'s rendering. The bounded retry's own try, read and stop lines carry the same `[slack] reconcileOrphans` prefix.

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: sweeping row (<reason>) persona=<persona> instanceId=<id> state=<state>[ cwd=<cwd>] — <it is live, so it is killed; the row is kept\|it is finished, so it is not killed (a finished row is never killed); the row is kept> (b.jg5 SRJ-714)` | A labelled row the sweep sweeps (`absent persona`, `wrong instance ID`, `wrong cwd`) |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: killing <row> state=<state> tmux_session=<session>; the row is kept whatever the outcome (b.jg5 SRJ-714)` | Before each kill of a live stray, swept or pre-persona |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: kill succeeded for <row> (<outcome>) — row kept` | The kill's success stands; a `persona-kill-survivor` entry follows when an earlier try named a survivor |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: the status read between kill tries for instanceId=<id> answered CONFIG; the row names no persona of the applied configuration, so no outage is raised — logged only (b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-316)` | A between-try read answered CONFIG for a row of no configured persona |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: kill tries for <row> (start sweep) were stopped: <cause>; its last outcome's class: <class>; no kill-failure alert is raised; <descriptions> (b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-714[, SRJ-205])` | `startSweepStoppedKillLine`: a stop ended a kill's tries before a success stood. `<cause>` is `the server is shutting down` (`START_SWEEP_KILL_STOP_SHUTDOWN`: a shutdown stopped the tries) or `the version re-check decided that the server stops; row kept; the sweep makes no further call` (`START_SWEEP_KILL_STOP_RECHECK`: the kill's `ErrInvalidFlags` re-check stops the server; `SRJ-205` is cited then). `<descriptions>` is `describeKillFailureDescriptions`' rendering (the latest survivor-naming description included, else `no description`); its `orphan-cleanup` entry carries no alert text, and nothing is posted |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: the server began shutting down — the sweep stops: no further kill, status read, findMissing or get, and no further latch, record write or clear; what it did stands, and the rows it left unkilled count as kept (b.jg5 SRJ-714, SRJ-205)` | Once per sweep, the first time its shutdown query answers true (`START_SWEEP_SHUTDOWN_STOP_LINE`), before the summary, also when the findMissing run then failed or the shutdown began during the post-run `get`s; never after a re-check's stop |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: the <class> answer to the <call> for persona=<key> came after the sweep stopped — no outage is raised (b.jg5 SRJ-714)` | `logSweepOutageNotRaised`: an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer to a kill (`<call>` `kill`), or a CONFIG answer to a between-try read (`<call>` `status read between kill tries`), for a configured persona's row arrived after the sweep stopped: no outage is raised |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: post-sweep get for persona=<key>: the get settled after its caller stopped — not acted on: no latch, clear or episode end (b.jg5 SRJ-714)` | A post-run `get` settled after a shutdown began (`OwnRowReadSite.actGoes`): no latch, clear or episode end; the `get`s' line shows `persona=<key> not acted on (its caller stopped)` |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: findMissing sweep for the rows the start sweep killed — count=<n> ids=[…] unverified=<n> unverified_ids=[…]` | The post-kill findMissing run's own line |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: after the findMissing sweep for the rows the start sweep killed — no post-sweep get is made: its caller stopped (b.jg5 SRJ-120, SRJ-714)` | A shutdown began while the run was under way: no post-run `get` |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: findMissing after the kills of <n> row(s): missing=<n> [<ids>] still-live=<n> [<ids>] not-judged=<n> [<ids>] — a row that still reads live is killed again by the next start's sweep when it sweeps it; a not-judged row was pending and not judged by this run (retry later)` | After the run, over every row given a kill (`startSweepPostKillLine`) |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: findMissing after the kills of <n> row(s) failed — each reads as it did, and a live one is killed again by the next start's sweep when it sweeps it` | The run failed, after its failure line (`startSweepPostKillFailedLine`) |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: summary — listed=<n> killed=<n> kept=<n> (kill-failed=<n>) recorded-as-retired=<n> left-unkilled-for-latch=<n> (b.jg5 SRJ-714)` | The last line of every sweep that listed its rows, a stopped one included (`startSweepSummaryLine`) |

The `orphan-cleanup` entry of a kill that did not succeed is `kill did not succeed for <row> state=<state> tmux_session=<session>: <outcome>[; its tries were stopped because the server is shutting down, so no kill-failure alert is raised]; row kept, its session may still be running`, with `; kill-failure alert: instanceId=<id> (start sweep): <text>` appended when the retry decided the ordinary version and no stop ended the tries (`startSweepKillFailedEntry`).

### Log file locations

Both paths are rooted in `SLACK_STATE_DIR` (default: `~/.claude/channels/slack/`).

| Process | Log file |
|---------|----------|
| Server daemon (`server.ts`) | `STATE_DIR/server.log` |
| `clean_restart` subcommand | `STATE_DIR/clean_restart.log` |
| cscb_cron fire log (`cron-log.ts`) | `cron_log_path` (default `<config dir>/cron.log`) |

All three are opened in append mode — multiple restarts accumulate in the same file rather than overwriting it; only the first two are subject to the size-based rotation above.

## Endpoint Inventory

The HTTP server serves `/interject` and `/mcp` only; any other path is a 404. Neither triggers or describes a reload (see Security Model, Reload is file-triggered only), and a new endpoint must not either.

### POST /interject

Injects a message into one persona's live Claude session without going through Slack. Localhost-only. Handler: `handleInterject` in `src/interject.ts`, wired by `server.ts`.

**Request body** (JSON, max 32 KB)

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `persona` | string | yes | Target persona's name or key (exact, case-sensitive match) |
| `message` | string | yes | Message content to inject |
| `sender` | string | no | Display name; defaults to `"interject"` |

**Success response**

`200 OK` — `{ ok: true, persona: <name> }` (the persona's name, even when the request used its key)

**Status codes**

| Status | Condition | Body `error` |
|--------|-----------|--------------|
| 200 | Notification handed to the persona's session | — |
| 400 | Invalid JSON | `Invalid JSON` |
| 400 | Missing, empty or non-string `persona` (including a body with only the old `channel` field) | `Missing or invalid field: persona (string) required` |
| 400 | Missing, empty or non-string `message` | `Missing or invalid field: message (string) required` |
| 403 | Non-localhost origin | `Forbidden` |
| 404 | No applied persona has that name or key, or there is no persona config | `Persona not found in the applied config` |
| 405 | Non-POST method | `Method Not Allowed` |
| 413 | Body exceeds 32 KB | `Request body too large (max 32KB)` |
| 503 | The persona is in the applied config but not up (broken or retrying), even when its instance is running or its session is still registered; the body also carries `persona` (its name) | `Persona is not up` |
| 503 | The persona is up but has no registered, connected session | `No active session for this persona` |

**Behavior**

- Resolves `persona` against the applied persona config (`resolvePersonaTarget`); 404 if absent
- Asks the injected `isPersonaUp` (the server's shared up predicate, `createPersonaUpPredicate`; b.av2 SR-6.4) before any session lookup. A persona that is not up gets 503 and one line, `[slack] /interject: refused for persona "<name>" (key=<key>) — the persona is not up; nothing delivered`; nothing reaches its instance
- Calls `getSessionByPersona()` with the persona's key; 503 if none or not connected
- Logs `[slack] /interject: delivering to persona "<name>" (key=<key>) sender="<label>" message="<first 80 chars>"`
- Sends `notifications/claude/channel` to that session only, with `content: message` and `meta: { user, ts }` — no `chat_id`, `message_id` or `via`. `user` is the `sender` label; `ts` is `String(Date.now() / 1000)`, which has at most three fractional digits. The absence of `via` is what the Slack Reply Guard uses to tell an injected message from a delivered Slack one (see [Slack Reply Guard](#slack-reply-guard-stop-hook)).
- Does not await the notification: a later rejection is logged as `[slack] /interject: notification to persona … failed: …`
- Does not call the Slack API

## Security Model

- **Inbound delivery** (b.av2 SR-4.2): every inbound event goes through the receiving persona's pipeline (`src/persona-routing.ts`), whose delivery rules are in `src/delivery-decision.ts`. A persona receives its configured channels, each by its `delivery` setting, and, with `dm.enabled` on, direct messages to its own app (b.av2 SR-4.3). A group DM (`channel_type` `mpim`) is never delivered; an @mention in a group DM arrives without `channel_type` and is decided by the channel rules, so it is delivered only to a persona that lists that conversation ID. Its own messages are dropped, and that is the only sender filter: any other author, a workspace user who has never posted before included, reaches the persona wherever it receives: there is no sender allowlist and no per-sender approval step
- **Outbound scoping** (b.av2 SR-5.1): every MCP tool resolves the calling session's persona and its client at call time and may target only that persona's configured channels and, while its `dm.enabled` is on, a `D…` DM conversation or (for `reply` only) a user ID, which is opened with `conversations.open` on the persona's client before the post (`checkPersonaTarget`). With `dm.enabled` off, no tool call opens a DM (`conversations.open`) or acts on a `D…` or user-ID target for that persona, including a `chat.postMessage` to a user ID, which Slack would turn into an implicit DM open. A refused target returns a tool error naming the persona and the target, and no Slack call is made. The call posts as the persona, with no username or icon override. The server's own posts to a persona's destination (prompts, the stuck-prompt warning, notices) are held to the same DMs switch, though not through `checkPersonaTarget`: a `dm` destination with DMs off is refused with no Slack call (`persona-destination.ts`); the one exception is an update to a prompt already posted in a DM (see [In-memory state](#in-memory-state-sr-1))
- **File exfiltration guard**: `assertSendable()` (`src/lib.ts`) blocks uploading files from the state directory (outside `inbox/`) and every persona credentials file named by the applied configuration or by the configuration file as it currently stands (b.av2 SR-5.2), compared by real path so a symlink to one is refused too. **State-directory rule:** a file is refused when it is inside the state directory and not inside `inbox/`, by either of two checks: one on the paths as given, and the same check on the real paths of the file and of both directories. So a symlink outside the state directory that points into it (for example at a credentials-holding `.env` there) is refused, and one that points into `inbox/` is allowed. Both checks respect path-component boundaries: `<state dir>/inbox-old/x` is not in the inbox, and `<state dir>2/x` is not in the state directory. A path that does not exist gets only the as-given check. The list is rebuilt per call from the reload controller's `protectedCredentialsFiles()` (`credentialsFilesToProtect` over the applied set, which is the last-applied record's set at a start from the record, plus every `credentials_file` string in `config.json` read tolerantly now), so a credentials file named only by an unapplied edit is protected too. That read of `config.json` is the one read the 64 KiB size cap does not cover (`readPersonaConfigBytes` with `uncapped`): the whole file is read, so a path named only in an oversized unapplied `config.json` is still refused. It is still opened and stat'ed first, so a non-regular file is never read (see Reload files, Size cap). Before `main()` builds the controller there is no applied set, and only `config.json`'s paths are refused. It never opens the file. `reply` checks every file up front and re-checks each one right before its upload
- **Attachment download token scope**: `download_attachment` sends the persona's bot token only to `https://files.slack.com` URLs. External (non-Slack-hosted) files are refused, and a redirect off that origin is never followed with the Authorization header, so the token cannot reach a third-party host
- **Localhost restriction**: `/interject` is the only localhost-restricted endpoint; it accepts requests only from 127.0.0.1/::1/::ffff:127.*
- **Session scope guard**: agent-director enforces session scope via `relay_mode='on'` at spawn time. Permission requests are routed through agent-director's internal relay machinery (SR-2.1 poller), which is scoped to the spawned session. Sessions not spawned by CSCB have no relay route and no `PermissionRequest` or `PreToolUse` hook entries in `settings.json` — the `.sh` hook files are not shipped.
- **Credentials-file secrecy**: each persona's credentials file is the server's only token source (b.av2 SR-1.4, SR-10.2). The persona credentials module (`src/persona-credentials.ts`) and the bring-up checks (`checkPersonaLocalSteps` in `src/persona-start.ts`, run by the bring-up controller) read it once per persona at each bring-up (at start, at apply, and at a recovery bring-up) and once at each confirmed credentials change (apply step 4), and hand the tokens to the connection manager; the controller holds them in the persona's entry for a later directory retry and never logs, returns or re-reads them; beside them it holds only a SHA-256 digest of the bytes read (or a missing/unreadable marker). A persona whose credentials file another applied persona shares (a record-start collision) has its own path read only to be hashed: the bytes are never parsed and no token is taken from them. The reload detection tick reads each referenced credentials file every 5 s outside dry run, through the same stat-first reader, holds the bytes only for that pass (read once per path, hashed into the fingerprint), compares only digests with the held one, and drops the bytes when the pass ends; the server holds no token at module scope, and none of that code reads an environment variable. The CLI reads no token at all: it opens no credentials file. A credentials path that is not a regular file (a directory, FIFO, socket or device) is `persona-credentials-unreadable` and is never read: the file is opened non-blocking, so a FIFO cannot stall the open, and its type is checked through the same descriptor before any read. A file over the size cap is unreadable the same way and never read in full (see Reload files, Size cap). It never writes, copies, caches or persists a credentials file or any value from one; a digest is held in memory only, never written to disk or logged. It does not check or change the file mode. A bad token is described only by its key and the rule it breaks, never by its value, so no diagnostic line or failure result carries a token, and the success value redacts itself if logged.
  - **Who writes the file** (b.av2 SR-1.4, SR-12): the operator, by hand or with the setup wizard's credentials command (`## Credentials command` in `skills/setup-slack-channel-bots/SKILL.md`): one line, `claude-slack-channel-bots credentials <persona>`, which the operator runs in their own terminal once the persona is declared in `config.json` (the line stays short, so a copy from an 80-column terminal keeps it whole). The CLI finds the persona in the configuration file as it stands and runs the packaged `scripts/write-credentials.sh` with `bash` for its `credentials_file` (see the `cli.ts` and `scripts/` entries of the Module Map). That script is the only shipped writer and the only place mode 0600 is guaranteed. It turns tracing and automatic export off (`set +xa`), checks the path and that `curl` is installed before any prompt, reads both tokens without echo, and validates the bot token with `auth.test` and the app token with `apps.connections.open` (each token reaches `curl` only on its standard input, as a `--config -` header, so no token is on any command line or in the process list; a check passes only when the reply's leading field is `"ok":true`). Only then does it write exactly `bot_token` and `app_token` to a temporary file created exclusively with `mktemp` beside the target under `umask 077` and `chmod 600` (removed by a trap on any failure or interrupt), check the file is not empty, and rename it onto the target; if the target appeared, vanished, became or stopped being a symlink, or became a directory while it ran (checked again after the rename, removing the moved temporary file from a directory that appeared at the path), nothing is written. The rename replaces a symlink at the path with a regular file, leaving the old tokens in the file it pointed to. An empty answer at the replace prompt declines, and `curl -q` ignores the operator's `~/.curlrc`. The server never writes the file and never polices its mode, and the CLI process itself reads no token. No shipped skill asks for, accepts or prints a token, or displays a credentials file's content: the wizard never takes a token in chat and checks only that the file exists and its mode, and the debugging skill's shape check (`jq`) reports key names and prefixes only. Rotation is the same command for the persona, then a confirmed credentials change (see Reload).
- **Reload is file-triggered only** (b.av2 SR-8.8): a change is applied only when the operator puts a confirmation at `config.json.apply` beside `config.json`. That rename is the only trigger, made by the operator or by an agent the operator explicitly directs. No HTTP endpoint, MCP tool or CLI subcommand (listed or hidden) triggers, confirms or performs a reload, and no MCP instruction text, tool definition or CLI usage text describes it; a confirmation's content is never logged (the stale line names only its path and the reason). This is deliberate opacity, not a security boundary: the server and the persona instances run as the same OS user, so a bot could make the rename itself.
  - **The surfaces as built.** The CLI accepts only `start`, `stop` (with `--stop-bots`) and `clean_restart`; any other first argument (`reload`, `apply` and the like included) prints the same usage text and exits 1, writing nothing. The HTTP server serves only `/interject` and `/mcp` (see Endpoint Inventory). The MCP server lists five tools (`reply`, `react`, `edit_message`, `fetch_messages`, `download_attachment`), and any other tool name is an `Unknown tool` error. The start, stop and clean_restart sections above describe no reload behaviour: those commands only read the last-applied record through `readAppliedPersonaConfig` and never write a reload file.
  - **Pinned by AC 74 tests.** `tests/cli.test.ts` (`unknown subcommand`) checks the usage text lists exactly the four subcommands and the one flag, carries no reload wording, and that hidden spellings take the unknown-subcommand path with the temp tree unchanged. `tests/registry.test.ts` (`tool list and instructions`) checks every tool definition and the MCP instructions carry no reload wording, and that `reload` and `apply_config` tool calls are refused. The shared term list is in the testing guide's Unadvertised Reload Checks section.
- **Reload output stays local** (b.av2 SR-7.2, SR-8.3): the reload detection tick's output (the pending file, the preview lines, every detection line and every apply line) goes only to `config.json.pending` and the server log, never to Slack; nothing about a pending or applied change is posted or held as a notice. Neither the pending file nor any reload line carries a token, credentials content or a digest: credentials changes are named by persona and path only, the change plan they are rendered from holds no digest, an added persona's can't-come-up cause names keys and rules only (`credentialsReadProblem`), and the pending file's fingerprint is a SHA-256 over the files, from which no content can be read back. An `INVALID` line repeats the loader's error, which echoes no rejected value, no file text and no unknown key name that isn't a plain setting name (`ECHOABLE_KEY_NAME_RE`), so a token pasted into `config.json`, even as a key, never reaches either.
- **Slack validation outcome secrecy** (b.av2 SR-10.3): outcomes from `src/persona-slack-validation.ts` carry only the class, the token key, the check, and the Slack error code or reason kind (plus an HTTP status or `retryAfter` number). The log lines `src/persona-slack-episodes.ts` builds from them carry those fields plus the persona reference (entry position, name and key) and the credentials-file path. Neither ever carries the raw error object, its message, the request, a header or a token value. The connection manager (`src/persona-connections.ts`) uses them. The Web API auth-failure watch (`src/persona-web-api-watch.ts`, bug b.ujn) copies only the Slack error code and the method name (only when it matches `SLACK_METHOD_NAME_RE`) from a rejected call; it never logs, stores or modifies the error, the caller still sees the original rejection, and its local refusal (`WebApiCallRefusedLocallyError`) carries only that code and method name.
- **Persona Slack client error secrecy** (b.av2 SR-3.3): no persona Slack client (`src/persona-slack-clients.ts`) attaches the original request, and so the Authorization header, to its errors. `attachOriginalToWebAPIRequestError: false` is set by every option builder, so on every client the connection manager builds: the short-lived validation client (`validationWebClientOptions`), the Socket Mode client's own Web API client for `apps.connections.open` (its `clientOptions`, from the private `validationRequestLimits()`: the validation client's limits without its logger), and the long-lived Web API client (`longLivedWebClientOptions`). A credentials reconnect builds its validation, Web API and Socket Mode clients through the same factory and option sets, so it adds no token surface; the new tokens are held like the old ones and replace them only at the swap (or at once for a retrying persona). The `persona-credentials-change-failed` line carries only the persona reference, the path and a token-free cause (a credentials-check cause or the Slack classifier's refused cause). The connection manager logs a thrown value only through `describeThrownValue` (constructor name, a short `code`, the message through `redactSlackLogText` as `message="…"`, stack frames), and the exported `unhandledRejection` handler (`src/persona-connection-errors.ts`) logs the same way, so neither writes a token value. `server.ts` installs the handler once in `main()`; the event router, `connectPersonaSlack` and the bring-up controller also log thrown values only through `describeThrownValue`.
- **Slack API endpoint override is loopback only** (E14 Task 4): every persona Slack client talks to the library's default Slack API, except when `CSCB_SLACK_API_URL` holds an `http://127.0.0.1…` or `http://[::1]…` URL (literal addresses; `localhost` is refused) with no user info, query or fragment (the integration suite's Slack stub). Any other value is ignored with a warning that does not echo it. The honoured line logs only the URL's origin. The persona tokens then go only to whatever listens on that loopback port, which is trusted with them. See Environment Variables.
- **Slack library logging** (b.av2 SR-10.3): every persona Socket Mode client is built with `socketModeSlackLogger(persona, log)` (`src/persona-slack-clients.ts`) in place of the library's console logger, which `initLogging()` would route into `server.log`. Under Bun, a failed WebSocket handshake's error text holds the full WebSocket URL, and its `ticket=` query is a short-lived bearer for the app's socket, which the library prints at its default level; "Failed to retrieve a new WSS URL" prints whatever the Web API error says. So the logger is an allowlist, not a filter: only whole lines matching the library's fixed-text ping/pong timeouts are forwarded as they are, and a failed ping is forwarded as `Failed to send ping to Slack` without its runtime error text. The socket client passes the logger on to its own `apps.connections.open` client (whose `clientOptions` carry none) and its WebSocket, so their lines go through the same allowlist. The connection manager logs every connection failure itself, through `describeThrownValue`. The validation and long-lived Web API clients get `redactingSlackLogger()`: the token travels only in the Authorization header and they don't attach the original request, but a failed request's message can hold the request URL (a `filesUploadV2` upload URL is a short-lived bearer), and a runtime's header check could echo a header value, so every argument has URL-like text replaced by `<redacted-url>` and token-like text (a deliberately wide pattern) by `<redacted-token>` before it reaches the console.
- **Persona names and paths are echoed as written** (b.av2 SR-1.2, SR-2.2): a persona's name and its key are shown everywhere a persona is named (log lines, loader errors, previews, Slack notices, tool results, agent-director labels, the instance ID and the tmux session name). A name has no format rule and is neither rejected nor masked: the operator chooses it, and it is not a credential. Persona paths (`credentials_file`, `working_directory`, `claude_config_dir`) and `ack_reaction` are echoed as written in errors and log lines for the same reason. Unknown key names are echoed only when they are plain setting names (`ECHOABLE_KEY_NAME_RE`), since a key could be a pasted token. Message content is archived and debug-logged unfiltered. Redaction covers exactly two things: the Slack libraries' own log output (the allowlist and `redactingSlackLogger` above, and `redactSlackLogText` inside every describer of a thrown value), and CSCB's own credentials, which no loader or credentials error echoes (a bad token is named only by its key and rule).
- **No token in any output** (b.av2 SR-10.3, AC 20): no log line, error, server-written file (`config.json.pending`, `config.json.last-applied`, `reply-guard/<key>`, the permission trail), preview, Slack notice or MCP tool result carries a Slack token value, credentials content or a credentials digest. The last-applied record is a byte copy of a config file that passed the loader, which rejects unknown keys, and credentials live only in the credentials files. What persona, reload and apply output may carry:
  - the persona reference (entry position, JSON-quoted name and key), paths, class labels and fixed wording;
  - Slack error codes that are safe identifiers, and Web API method names only when they match `SLACK_METHOD_NAME_RE` (the `persona-credentials-refused` "Web API call" cause from `src/persona-web-api-watch.ts`, and `WebApiCallRefusedLocallyError`);
  - errno codes, in `persona-config-dir-unresolvable` (its cleared line carries none) and the JSONL check's "transcript not checked" line; the launch's "could not be resolved" line and the restart kill adapter's "not killing" line name only the persona and the setting;
  - thrown values only through `describeThrownValue` or `describeSlackCallFailure` (the teardown's "before its turn failed" line, the connection manager's reconnect failures); `persona-credentials-change-failed` carries a credentials-check or refused cause, never a thrown value; the `template refresh:` failure line carries an agent-director error's `errName` (only when it passes `isSafeIdentifier`) and its description as `message="…"` (`describeLogMessage`), or the `describeThrownValue` description of any other value (a typed error whose `errName` fails the check included).
  - every log line, startup-error record and notice on a Slack or agent-director path (the persona connections, the permission poller and click handler, restart, the UNAVAILABLE retry timer, the health check and its stat route, the outage state, the session manager's launches and orphan cleanup, the JSONL check, the CLI's teardown and `stop --stop-bots`, `isSessionAlive`) renders a thrown value through `describeThrownValue`, never the raw error or its raw message (b.av2 SR-10.3): the message appears only as `message="…"`, through `redactSlackLogText`, on one line and capped at 300 characters (`describeLogMessage`). An agent-director `errName` is printed, by that describer or directly, only when it passes `isSafeIdentifier`; `describeAgentDirectorFailure` (declared once in `src/ad-error-class.ts`, imported by the session manager and the episode tracker, and re-exported by the permission poller for its click handler) renders `<errName> message="<description>"` with the description through `describeLogMessage`, and any other value through `describeThrownValue`. The resume path's `ErrInvalidFlags` line is built from the classifier's answer only (`describeAdErrorClassification`, `ad-error-class.ts`): the name only when it passes `isSafeIdentifier`, the message rendered by `renderLogMessageText`, the same rendering `describeLogMessage` quotes. The session manager's startup-error records (`spawn-failed`, `orphan-cleanup*`, `jsonl-transcript-lost-on-resume`, `jsonl-diagnosis-inconclusive`) carry that description in their message, never the error itself; the JSONL diagnosis's fallback description is redacted the same way. The spawn-failure notice posted to Slack shows the checked label and the redacted description, capped at 300 characters after redaction. The CLI's `stop --stop-bots` initialization-failed and teardown-failed lines print the message of a failure CSCB built (`StartupGateFailedError`, `TeardownIncompleteError`) and describe anything else. The permission trail keeps `raw_error_message` for forensics (SR-V-2.7), redacted by `redactSlackLogText` before it is written;
  - deliberate exceptions, which print an error's own text (the `RAW_ERROR_ALLOWED` list of the source audit in `tests/secrecy-audit.test.ts`, each with its reason): the `[slack] Fatal:` catch-alls (`src/cli.ts`, `src/server.ts`), the only text of an unexpected start failure; the CLI's config-load lines (`stop`, `stop --stop-bots`, `clean_restart`, `credentials`), which carry the loader's token-free message and, for a record, its deletion hint; the `clean_restart` `fatal(...)` lines, which in production receive the CSCB-built errors above; the boot template install's failure, recorded verbatim; the startup gate's message, which may embed agent-director's description or a construct error and is the same text the server writes to `startup-errors.log`; and paths that touch neither Slack nor agent-director (MCP roots and connect, the message archive's open, cron, permission trail and cron log writes, cozempic, the PID read, the Stop-hook and trust patches' catch-alls);
  - MCP tool errors name the persona, the target and at most a Slack platform error code. The lost-message notice carries, in every one of its states, fixed wording (`STATE_WORDING`) and the sender's label only.
  - The latch notices quote agent-director's description only as the latch record holds it: redacted, on one line and capped (`renderLogMessageText`), then escaped once for Slack (`escapeSlackControlCharacters`). This holds for the CONFLICT notice (b.jg5 SRJ-1004) and for the *Held: unusable tmux session name* notice (b.jg5 SRJ-1019, `unusableNameNoticeText` in `src/conflict-latch.ts`), whose description is the classifier's message, rendered the same way. The *Held: launch start not recorded* notice (b.jg5 SRJ-1020, `launchStartNotRecordedNoticeText`) quotes no description; its session name is rendered and escaped the same way. CSCB's own text in them names no session-ending command and no label option.
  - The kill-failure alert (b.jg5 SRJ-704, SRJ-1007; `src/kill-failure-alert.ts`) quotes agent-director's descriptions only through the redactor (`renderLogMessageText`: redacted, one line, capped), escaped once for Slack after that, and takes its pid list only from `survivorPids` (`src/ad-description-phrases.ts`), never from a pattern of its own. The agent-director commands its ordinary version names are a human's next step: the text says no bot, including any persona that sees the post, may run them, and points to agent-director's README "Operator actions" for anything beyond. The survivor version names no command, and nothing in CSCB acts on a pid it lists. Its log-only routes carry the same redacted text, unescaped, to `server.log` and `startup-errors.log`.
  - The *Cannot launch* alert (b.jg5 SRJ-1008; `INVALID_FLAGS_HOLD_ALERT_TEXT` in `src/invalid-flags-hold.ts`) is fixed text: it quotes no agent-director description and no version. The hold's lines show a version agent-director reported only as `describeHoldVersion` renders it (a short version string, else `unknown` or `unreadable`), and a thrown value only through `describeThrownValue`; `src/invalid-flags-hold.ts` is one of the secrecy audit's source surfaces.
